Title: Speech given by Mr. Carlos de Burgo
text: Speech given by Mr. Dr. Carlos de Burgo on the occasion of the inauguration as Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde Mr Minister for Finance and Planning, Representatives of the Diplomatic Corps, Members of the Board of Directors, the Supervisory Board, the Advisory Council and Representatives of Workers of the Bank of Cape Verde, Representatives of the Financial Institutions, Ladies and gentlemen, When I take office as Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde, I am well aware of the responsibility inherent in the position. The proper functioning of this institution is fundamental for the performance of the economy, the development of the country and the improvement of the level of well-being of the Cape Verdean people. This stems from its attributions to the value of the currency, the operation and development of the payment system as well as the stability and development of the financial system. The responsibility is greater because, in this important area, we are in a process of consolidating a new institutional option, following the adoption of the new Organic Law of the Bank of Cape Verde. The new institutional framework clarifies the bcv's main mission  maintaining price stability  and gives it the necessary autonomy to fulfil it. This autonomy essentially contributes to the stability of the mandates of the holders of management and the restriction of monetary financing of the budget deficit. The establishment of a Fiscal Council and an Advisory Board, this timo integrating beyond the former Governors, personalities with competence in the economic and financial areas as well as representatives of financial institutions and the business sector, certainly represents an institutional strengthening of the Bank of Cape Verde. Through accountability mechanisms to the National Assembly and the Government, transparency and the proper functioning of the institution are safeguarded. The courageous decision to promote the autonomy of the Central Bank has led to institutional weakness  the lack of separation between fiscal and monetary policy  which has been responsible in the recent past for the worsening of macro-eco-imbalances, the negative effects of which are still being felt in terms of the pace of growth, employment and the evolution of the living standard of Cape Verdeans. This is because the adjustment  the sanitation of the finances and the elimination of inflationary pressures  is inevitable because it is necessary to function properly in the economy and to restore the confidence of eco-workers as well as credibility with partners, to contain plicate expenditure and to a restrictive monetary policy. The recently released indicators on the level of econic activity, inflation, the budget deficit, the current account deficit, the influx of external resources and monetary reserves well confirm the success of the stabilisation and development policy adopted. In our context, the objective of monetary policy  the defence of fixed parity in relation to the Euro  is set by the Government. This exchange rate regime is best suited for an economy like ours. In a small open economy such as ourforeign price taker, the loss of the exchange rate instrument does not represent a significant additional cost in terms of the loss of degrees of freedom in the conduct of environmental policy. In addition to being transparent and easier to manage, this regime, due to the stability of exchange rate, favours trade and foreign investment. The BCV now has all operational autonomy in pursuit of the monetary policy objective. It is responsible for conducting monetary policy in such a way that, first, it constitutes and maintains a level of foreign exchange reserves necessary for the credibility of the exchange rate regime adopted. Due to the impact of the State's financial operations on global demand and the balance of payments, close cooperation between the Government and the BCV is imposed. The Central Bank must take into account the Government's fiscal policy, without this meaning that monetary policy is located in fiscal policy. On the other hand, state fiscal policy should be based on the sustainability of the plica debt and the search for solutions for long-term budgetary pressures, in particular those arising from social policies and pension responsibilities. In fact, the current eco-system, based on monetary and exchange rate stability, requires a fiscal policy that is in line with it, this is characterised by prudence, discipline and sustainability. In the last instance, however, the feasibility of the current parity of the shield will depend on the evolution of the competitiveness of the Cape Verdean economy. Reducing the cost of business in Cape Verde is an imperative. In fact, our exchange rate regime presupes adjustment mechanisms on the side of the real economy in order to ensure their sustainability, so that the qualitative and structural overcoming of our economy in order to increase the weight of transactionable goods and services is the challenge that arises for us. Good macro-econic management geared towards stability, by reducing risk, increasing the confidence of environmental agents and the good allocation of resources, is an important factor in the competitiveness of the economy, while being a condition of mobilising the resources needed to modernise the country and balance external accounts, precarious in this transitional period. The fragility of our economy in the face of possible external shocks and fluctuations in econic activity due to climate randomness makes good macro-econic management unavoidable. It is clear that, in carrying out its task, the BCV should at no time lose sight of the view that the objective of monetary policy is not an end in itself, but rather aimed at promoting economic growth and the fight against poverty. This is the criterion for astoling the effectiveness of the governance system of the central bank. Because of its role in mobilizing savings, allocating and monitoring the use of resources, the financial system is very relevant for eco-growth. It is now known that an efficient and developed financial system increases the total productivity of factors, that is, resource efficiency. Measured by the relative volume of financial assets, Cape Verde has already achieved a reasonable level of financial development and its banking system is been. However, the financial system consists primarily of the banking system and lacks sophistication. While there are factors such as the small size of the market and the difficulties in circumventing the difficulties arising from information asymmetries, it is urgent to promote innovation with a view to the emergence of the capital market (shares and debt securities) and new financial instruments. The BCV offers itself as a partner to actively contribute to the identification and promotion of certain financial activities for which there are indications that they can contribute to the development of the national financial system. In this vein, it is proposed, in addition to the necessary regulatory framework, to promote the operationalisation of new financial mechanisms and instruments, such as factoring, leasing, venture capital, capital markets as well as new financial products in the insurance area, in particular life insurance. It should be noted that a systemic reform of the so-called system that encourages the establishment of penss funds greatly could contribute to the development of the financial system, providing resources at longer time frames and therefore more suitable for financing investment. At institutional level, in addition to promoting the effective and transparent functioning of the institutions currently building the national financial system, the BCV should actively promote its development. In this situation, actions will be developed with a view to: promoting the competitiveness of the banking and insurance sector; the active engagement of relevant, plyandprivate national partners, including The ILOE (PROMEX/IADE), SDE, Chambers of Commerce, commercial banks, in the design and implementation of agreements aimed at facilitating and reducing the cost of financing; promoting cooperation with specialised international financial institutions; the dissemination and facilitation of access to specialised financial instruments in donor countries; The promotion of micro-finance and the development of individual national capacities in the financial area. Particular attention will be paid to the creation and management of the competitiveness necessary for the location of international financial institutions, considering that the production of financial services is an identified and promising potential for the growth of the Cape Verdean economy. In line with the work that has been carried out, efforts will continue to be made to develop the payment system and liquidation of securities. The payment system should promote the creation of new banking products and services and the development of the capital market and increase the efficiency and liquidity of the banking system in a context of adequate risk management. The national economy will achieve competitiveness gains by this way due to the speeding and lowering of payment costs and Cape Verde will strengthen its advantage in competition for the location of companies, in particular financial institutions. The use of international means of payment will particularly benefit tourism, the sector with the greatest growth potential in the Cape Verdean economy. Due to its characteristics and importance in the economy, the financial sector lacks proper regulation and supervision. Despite the role of the institutions' self-discipline and market discipline to be promoted through the dissemination of information that enables a perception of the risk of the institutions, the Bank of Cape Verde will strengthen and improve its regulatory and supervisory capacity, with a view to ensuring the stability of the financial system. Finally, let me express my gratitude for the work done by the that preceded me in this position. To the workers of the BCV, through their representatives, I wanted to at the moment when I begin the mandate to convey my conviction that the fulfillment of such important functions, as those committed to the central bank must be based on the good performance of the institution and its workers. All are called to contribute to the efficiency of the institution. For this reason, institutional development, through the adequacy of systems and structures as well as the qualification and motivation of workers, will be a central concern of the Governor. Beach, on 6 days of August 2004.
text_original: Discurso proferido pelo Sr. Dr. Carlos de Burgo por ocasio da tomada de posse como Governador do Banco de Cabo Verde Senhor Ministro das Finanas e Planeamento, Senhores Representantes do Corpo Diplomtico, Senhores Membros do Conselho de Administrao, do Conselho Fiscal, do Conselho Consultivo e Representantes dos Trabalhadores do Banco de Cabo Verde, Senhores Representantes das Instituis Financeiras, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Ao tomar posse como Governador do Banco de Cabo Verde, tenho bem presente a responsabilidade inerente ao cargo. O bom funcionamento dessa instituio  fundamental para o desempenho da economia, o desenvolvimento do pas e a melhoria do nvel de bem-estar do povo cabo-verdiano. Isto decorre das suas atribuis na garantia do valor da moeda, do funcionamento e desenvolvimento do sistema de pagamentos bem como da estabilidade e desenvolvimento do sistema financeiro. A responsabilidade  maior porque, neste importante domnio, encontramo-nos num processo de consolidao de uma nova opo institucional, na sequncia da aprovao da nova Lei Orgnica do Banco de Cabo Verde. O novo quadro institucional clarifica a misso principal do BCV  a manuteno da estabilidade dos preos  e confere-lhe a necessria autonomia para o seu cumprimento. Para essa autonomia concorrem fundamentalmente a estabilidade dos mandatos dos titulares dos gos de gesto e a restrio do financiamento monetrio do dfice oramental. A instituio de um Conselho Fiscal e de um Conselho Consultivo, este timo integrando alm dos antigos Governadores, personalidades com competncia nas reas econmica e financeira bem como representantes das instituis financeiras e do sector empresarial, representa certamente um fortalecimento institucional do Banco de Cabo Verde. Atravs dos mecanismos de prestao de contas  Assembleia Nacional e ao Governo, est salvaguardada a transparncia e o bom funcionamento da instituio. A corajosa deciso em promover a autonomia do Banco Central veio p cobro a uma fraqueza institucional  a falta de separao entre a poltica oramental e monetria  responsvel num passado recente pelo agravamento dos desequilbrios macroeconicos cujos efeitos negativos ainda se fazem sentir a nvel do ritmo de crescimento, do emprego e da evoluo do nvel de vida dos cabo-verdianos. Isto porque o ajustamento  o saneamento das finanas plicas e a eliminao das presss inflacionistas  inevitvel porque necessrio ao bom funcionamento da economia e  recuperao da confiana dos agentes econicos bem como da credibilidade junto dos parceiros, imp a conteno das despesas plicas e uma poltica monetria restritiva. Os indicadores recentemente divulgados referentes ao nvel de actividade econica, da inflao, do dfice oramental, do dfice das transaces correntes, do afluxo de recursos externos e das reservas monetrias bem confirmam o sucesso da poltica de estabilizao e de desenvolvimento adoptada. No nosso contexto, o objectivo da poltica monetria  a defesa da paridade fixa em relao ao Euro  encontra-se fixado pelo Governo. Este regime cambial  o mais adequado para uma economia como a nossa. Numa pequena economia aberta como a nossa, tomadora de preos externos, a perda do instrumento cambial no representa um custo adicional significativo em termos de perda de graus de liberdade na conduo da poltica econica. Para alm de ser transparente e de mais fcil gesto, este regime, em virtude da estabilidade cambial, favorece as trocas comerciais e o investimento externo. O BCV tem agora toda a autonomia operacional na prossecuo do objectivo estabelecido para a poltica monetria. Cabe-lhe conduzir a poltica monetria de forma a, em primeiro lugar, constituir e manter um nvel de reservas cambiais necessrio  credibilidade do regime cambial adoptado. Pelo impacto das operas financeiras do Estado na procura global e na balana de pagamentos, imp-se uma estreita cooperao entre o Governo e o BCV. O Banco Central deve ter em considerao a poltica oramental do Governo, sem que isso signifique uma acomodao da poltica monetria  poltica oramental. De outro lado, a poltica oramental do Estado deve ter em vista a sustentabilidade da dvida plica e a procura de solus para as presss oramentais de longo prazo, nomeadamente as decorrentes das polticas sociais e das responsabilidades a nvel das penss de reforma. De facto, o actual regime econico, assente na estabilidade monetria e cambial, requer uma poltica oramental que lhe seja consentnea, isto  caracterizada pela prudncia, pela disciplina e pela sustentabilidade. Em tima instncia, porm, a viabilizao da paridade actual do escudo depender da evoluo da competitividade da economia cabo-verdiana. A reduo dos custos de negios em Cabo Verde  um imperativo. Na realidade, o nosso regime cambial pressupe mecanismos de ajustamento do lado da economia real, por forma a assegurar a sua sustentabilidade pelo que a superao qualitativa e estrutural da nossa economia, no sentido do aumento do peso dos bens e servios transaccionveis  o desafio que se nos coloca. Uma boa gesto macroeconica orientada para a estabilidade, pela via da reduo do risco, do aumento da confiana dos agentes econicos e da boa afectao dos recursos, constitui um importante factor da competitividade da economia, ao mesmo tempo que  uma condio da mobilizao dos recursos necessrios  modernizao do pas e ao equilbrio das contas externas, ainda precrio neste perodo de transio. A fragilidade da nossa economia face a eventuais choques externos e s flutuas da actividade econica em virtude da aleatoriedade climtica faz com que a boa gesto macroeconica seja incontornvel.  evidente que, no cumprimento da misso que lhe est atribuda, o BCV em momento nenhum deve perder de vista que o objectivo da poltica monetria no  um fim em si, mas sim visa favorecer o crescimento econico e a luta contra a pobreza.  este o critrio de aferio da eficcia do sistema de governao de que faz parte o banco central. Pelo seu papel na mobilizao das poupanas, na alocao e monitorizao do uso dos recursos, o sistema financeiro  muito relevante para o crescimento econico. Pesem embora factores como a reduzida dimenso do mercado e as dificuldades em contornar as dificuldades resultantes das assimetrias de informao, urge promover a inovao com vista  emergncia do mercado de capitais (acs e ttulos de dvida) e de novos instrumentos financeiros. O BCV oferece-se como parceiro para contribuir activamente na identificao e promoo de determinadas actividades financeiras para as quais existem indcios de poderem contribuir para o desenvolvimento do sistema financeiro nacional. Nessa ordem de ideias, prop-se, para alm do necessrio quadro regulamentar, favorecer a operacionalizao de novos mecanismos e instrumentos financeiros, designadamente o factoring, o leasing, o capital de risco, o mercado de capitais bem como novos produtos financeiros na rea seguradora, nomeadamente os seguros de vida. Importa referir que uma reforma sistmica do sistema de penss que incentive a constituio de fundos de penss muito poder contribuir para o desenvolvimento do sistema financeiro, disponibilizando recursos a prazos mais longos e por isso mais adequados ao financiamento do investimento. A nvel institucional, para alm de promover o funcionamento eficaz e transparente das instituis que actualmente compm o sistema financeiro nacional, o BCV dever promover activamente o seu desenvolvimento. Nessa tica, sero desenvolvidas acs com vista:   promoo da competitividade do sector bancrio e segurador;  Ao engajamento activo de parceiros nacionais relevantes, plicos e privados, nomeadamente a AITE (PROMEX/IADE), a SDE, as Cmaras de Comrcio, os bancos comerciais, na concepo e implementao de solus visando facilitar e reduzir o custo do financiamento;   promoo da cooperao com instituis financeiras internacionais especializadas;   divulgao e facilitao do acesso a instrumentos financeiros especializados existentes nos pases doadores;   promoo das micro-finanas e  Ao desenvolvimento de capacidades individuais nacionais na rea financeira. Ateno particular ser dispensada  criao e gesto da competitividade necessria  localizao das instituis financeiras internacionais, considerando que a produo de servios financeiros  uma potencialidade identificada e promissora para o crescimento da economia cabo-verdiana. Na linha do trabalho que vem sendo realizado, continuaro a ser envidados esforos em prol do desenvolvimento do sistema de pagamentos e liquidao de ttulos. O sistema de pagamentos deve favorecer a criao de novos produtos e servios bancrios e o desenvolvimento do mercado de capitais bem como aumentar a eficincia e a liquidez do sistema bancrio, num contexto de adequada gesto do risco. A economia nacional realizar por esta via ganhos de competitividade em virtude da agilizao e diminuio dos custos dos pagamentos e Cabo Verde reforar a sua vantagem na competio pela localizao de empresas, nomeadamente as instituis financeiras. A utilizao dos meios internacionais de pagamento beneficiar particularmente o turismo, o sector com maior potencial de crescimento na economia cabo-verdiana. Pelas suas caractersticas e importncia na economia, o sector financeiro, carece de regulao e superviso apropriadas. No obstante o papel da autodisciplina das instituis e da disciplina do mercado a ser promovida pela via da divulgao de informas que possibilitem uma percepo do risco das instituis, o Banco de Cabo Verde reforar e aperfeioar a sua capacidade de regulamentao e superviso, com vista a garantir a estabilidade do sistema financeiro. Para finalizar, permitam-me manifestar o meu reconhecimento pelo trabalho efectuado pelos que me antecederam neste cargo. Aos trabalhadores do BCV, atravs dos seus representantes, queria no momento em que inicio o mandato transmitir a minha convico de que o cumprimento de to importantes funs, como as cometidas ao banco central tem de assentar no bom desempenho da instituio e dos seus trabalhadores. Todos so chamados a contribuir para a eficincia da instituio. Por isso mesmo, o desenvolvimento institucional, pela via da adequao dos sistemas e das estruturas bem como da qualificao e motivao dos trabalhadores constituir preocupao central do Governador. Praia, aos 6 dias de Agosto de 2004.

Title: Speech of the Governor of the BCV
text: Intervention of the Governor of bcv at the inauguration of the Bca Beach Agency Page 1 of 3 Speech given by the Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde in the ceremony of inauguration of the new facilities of the Bca Beach Agency. Beach, September 6, 2004 Mr Minister of Finance and Planning Mr Mayor of Praia Representatives of the Diplomatic Corps Ladies and gentlemen of the Board of Directors and the Executive Committee of the BCA Representatives of financial institutions Mr. President of the Chamber of Commerce and the Trade Association Ladies, gentlemen It is notnote the effort to improve the service that banking institutions provide to their customers, companies and individuals. The nero of agencies and branches grows, increases the use of modern technologies (ATMs, POS and even Internet banking) and improves the qualification of human resources. The Bank of Cape Verde welcomes this development, as it translates into a greater and better supply of financial services, which is an important condition for the country's economic growth and development. As a regulatory and supervisory authority, the BCV's primary mission is to ensure the stability of the financial system. But it is also up to it to promote the improvement of efficiency and to promote the development of the system. With this purpose are ongoing and new partnerships will be developed with financial institutions. In the context of the payment system. We have in our common agenda the acceptance and issuance of VISA carts, which is coming soon, the implementation of interbank electric transfers, telecompensation and the payment of services. The Treasury's involvement in this 15-09-2010 Intervention of the Governor of bcv at the inauguration of the Bca Beach Agency Page 2 of 3 partnership, by the volume and scope of state payments, will bring important efficiency gains to the economy and provide greater convenience to businesses and citizens. The Interbank Payment System Commission will soon begin operating as a strategic driving tool for the payment system. The most significant challenge, however, lies in the level of financial innovation. The powers of the court must modernise and permanently adapt the legal infrastructure, creating the requirements and incentives for the development of the financial system; institutions, the modernisation and sophistication of the supply of financial products with a view to mobilising savings and financing investment projects. It should be noted in this case, the ongoing initiative for the development of the capital market, the promotion of leasing, the assignment of credits (factoring), collective investment undertakings (investment funds and penss) and financial management companies. In these new areas, the BCV is not only preparing to assume its regulatory and supervisory role, but also offers to work together with the Government and financial institutions to create conditions for the realization of trades. In order to improve liquidity management, the BCV will soon change its monetary policy operational framework. A basic assumption in this change will be the reduction of the minimum cash availability coefficient, which will lower bank intermediation costs and therefore favour the reduction of interest rates in loan operations. Loan operations will also be facilitated with the effective online operation of the Risk Centre. The information provided will enable a more qualified assessment of the risk to which banks are subjected and this means fewer barriers to obtaining loans. Another area where we want to work in partnership with the Government, banking institutions and business associations is the access of small and medium-sized enterprises to credit. We believe that it is possible to develop innovative solutions that will reduce the transaction costs and the risk of loans to this category of entrepreneurs and thereby make it more attractive to banks this negio. 15-09-2010 Intervention of the Governor of bcv at the inauguration of the Bca Beach Agency Page 3 of 3 Let me also mention the attention that the BCV has set out to deal with conflicts of interest between financial institutions and their clients, especially individuals, who are the most unprotected because they have the least negotiating power. To meet the complaints, a service is being set up that will be briefly disclosed. With financial institutions, we will continue the partnership in the formation of cadres in the most diverse areas of finance. This is another significant contribution that the central bank can make to the development of the national financial system. Due to the context in which it is located and its importance itself, it is therefore worth noting the refurbishment of this agency, located, by the way, in a building deeply linked to the history of banking activity in Cape Verde. Beach, on September 6, 2004 15-09-2010

Title: Intervention at the Opening of the Workshop
text: Governor's intervention in launching visa page 1 of 3 service Intervention in the Opening of the Workshop for presentation of the Study on the Insurance Sector The current eco-policy of the Government of Cape Verde calls for accelerated eco-growth, in a stable macro-ecological framework. Thus, the private sector is called, much more than in the past, to play a driving role in the creation of national wealth. However, the participation of the private sector is hampered by constraints of various order, among which is the difficulty in accessing and the cost of financing. That is why, among the initiatives to promote private sector participation, actions related to the development of the financial sector should be pontificated. In this regard, and following the restructuring of the financial sector and the opening up of banking and insurance to private enterprise, measures have also been adopted which have enabled a substantial liberalisation of the rules applicable to the financial system, with a view to the liberalisation of interest rates, goods and invisible operations and the simplification of procedures and regulations relating to foreign exchange operations. Despite the measures taken, the financial system remains incipient, uncompetitive and low in character. In particular, banks continue to occupy a prominent position in the financial system, with a strong predominance of the mobilisation of surpluses formed by eco-agents and in the internal financing of the economy. As a result, banking products and services predominate to the detriment of more specialised ones that can better meet the specific needs of national deficit eco-workers. Overall, there is a lack of insufficiency in the mobilisation of savings by financial institutions, of which insurance companies are part. In this context, the promotion of national savings, particularly long-term savings, and its channelling into the productive sector, as well as the strengthening of institutional capacities and intervention of the financial system, are indispensable, thus constituting indispensable requirements for the eco-development that is advocated. Insurance institutions are potentially important partners in the practical efforts to promote the development of the financial sector because, in addition to the role of promoting environmental protection and safety, insurers can also play an important role in straining savings by virtue of the ability of certain indtria products to accumulate financial capital over time. However, national insurers are far from matching the above-mentioned potential. If it is certain that basic activities, with a predominance of insurance obrigatio automel, are already 15-09-2010 Governor's intervention at the launch of visa page 2 of 3 service established and operate regularly, while with regard to specialised services and products the activity also rehearses the first steps. In Cape Verde, in fact, there are several obstacles to the full role of insurers as promoters of savings and their channeling for investment. In addition to the structural constraints arising from the smallness and low income of the national economy, there are also regulatory constraints. In particular, the current legal and regulatory framework needs updating in order to monitor developments in the rest of the sector and thus respond to the new reality that is being envisaged, in particular by introducing new institutions, products and services. Another constraint is the lack of capacity in the country's specialized insurance activity. The Study on the Insurance Sector, the subject of this meeting, is part of the efforts to overcome the constraints with which the insurance activity is debated, thus allowing the development of it and the increase of its contribution to the ecological development. In turn, the promotion of the development of the insurance activity is part of a broader framework of concerted actions aimed at the overall development of the national financial system, and the following aspects should be highlighted: :: affirmation of the supervisory body, by clarifying its mission and strengthening its autonomy; :: improving monetary policy management by improving reserve management and liquidity in general; :: promotion of risk-based management; :: promoting the establishment and development of specialised financial institutions, in particular the capital market; :: systematic reform of Social Security. In the framework of the Study, which is supported by the World Bank, the BCV used internationally renowned experts to analyze the current situation in the sector, identify the potential market and design of measures and policy instruments necessary for the development of the activity. The first results of the Study will be presented here today by the consultants for your appreciation and comments. We have a debate that has been participated in and leads to concrete and detailed recommendations for the conclusion of the Study. We end up thanking you in advance for your contribution in this exercise, and we will continue to count on your collaboration in the following phases of this process. Together we will be able to overcome the challenges that we face, towards the consolidation and development of insurance and financial activity in general. 15-09-2010 Governor's intervention in the launch of the Visa Page 3 of 3 service Beach, April 6, 2005. Carlos Augusto de Burgo -Governor 15-09-2010
text_original: Interveno do governador no lanamento do servio Visa Page 1 of 3 Interveno na Abertura do Workshop para apresentao do Estudo sobre o Sector Segurador A actual poltica econica do Governo de Cabo Verde preconiza um crescimento econico acelerado, num quadro macro econico estvel. Assim, o sector privado  chamado, muito mais do que no passado, a desempenhar um papel motor na criao da riqueza nacional. Porm, a participao do sector privado  dificultada por constrangimentos de vria ordem, de entre os quais se salienta a dificuldade no acesso ao financiamento e o custo deste. Da que, entre as iniciativas plicas de promoo da participao do sector privado, pontifiquem as acs relacionadas com o desenvolvimento do sector financeiro. Nesta tica, e na sequncia da reestruturao do sector financeiro e da abertura da actividade bancria e seguradora  iniciativa privada, foram igualmente adoptadas medidas que permitiram uma substancial liberalizao da regulamentao aplicvel ao sistema financeiro, com realce para a liberalizao das taxas de juro, das operas de mercadorias e de invisveis e para a simplificao dos procedimentos e regulamentos referentes a operas cambiais. No obstante as medidas adoptadas, o sistema financeiro continua incipiente, pouco concorrencial e com baixo nvel de especializao. Em concreto, os bancos continuam a ocupar uma posio de grande destaque no sistema financeiro, sendo muito acentuado o seu predomnio na mobilizao dos excedentes formados pelos agentes econicos e no financiamento interno da economia. Em consequncia, predominam os produtos e servios de cariz bancrio em detrimento de outros mais especializados e que podem melhor corresponder s necessidades especficas dos agentes econicos deficitrios nacionais. No geral, constata-se uma insuficincia notia na mobilizao da poupana por parte das instituis financeiras, das quais as companhias seguradoras fazem parte. Neste contexto, a promoo da poupana nacional, particularmente a poupana de longo prazo, e a sua canalizao para o sector produtivo, assim como o reforo das capacidades institucionais e de interveno do sistema financeiro tornam-se indispensveis, constituindo, dessa forma, requisitos incontornveis para o desenvolvimento econico que se preconiza. As instituis seguradoras constituem potencialmente importantes parceiros no quadro dos esforos plicos em matria de promoo do desenvolvimento do sector financeiro pois, para alm da funo de promover a proteco e segurana econicas, as seguradoras podem tambm desempenhar um papel importante na formao da poupana em virtude da capacidade de certos produtos da indtria para acumular capital financeiro no tempo. Porm, as seguradoras nacionais esto longe de corresponder ao potencial atrs referido. Se  certo que a as actividades bsicas, com predominncia para o seguro obrigatio automel, j esto http://www.bcv.cv/_conteudo/intervencao/governador/2005/ig20050604.htm 15-09-2010 Interveno do governador no lanamento do servio Visa Page 2 of 3 estabelecidas e funcionam regularmente, j no que concerne aos servios e produtos especializados a actividade ensaia ainda os primeiros passos. Em Cabo Verde existem, de facto, diversos entraves  assumpo plena do papel das seguradoras enquanto promotoras da poupana e da sua canalizao para o investimento. Para alm dos constrangimentos estruturais, decorrentes da pequenez e baixo rendimento da economia nacional, existem tambm constrangimentos de ordem regulamentar. Em concreto, o actual quadro jurdicolegal e regulador carece de actualizao em ordem a acompanhar a evoluo no resto do sector e, assim, dar resposta  nova realidade que se projecta, nomeadamente pela via de introduo de novas instituis, produtos e servios. Outro constrangimento prende-se com a falta de capacidade em matria de actividade seguradora especializada no pas. O Estudo sobre o Sector Segurador, objecto do presente encontro, insere-se no quadro dos esforos para ultrapassar os constrangimentos com que se debate a actividade seguradora, permitindo assim o desenvolvimento da mesma e o aumento da sua contribuio para o desenvolvimento econico. Por sua vez, a promoo do desenvolvimento da actividade seguradora insere-se num quadro mais amplo de acs concertadas visando o desenvolvimento global do sistema financeiro nacional, sendo de salientar as seguintes vertentes: :: afirmao da entidade de superviso, pela via da clarificao da sua misso e reforo da sua autonomia; :: melhoria da gesto da poltica monetria, pela via do aperfeioamento da gesto das reservas e da liquidez em geral; :: promoo da gesto baseada no risco; :: promoo do estabelecimento e desenvolvimento de instituis financeiras especializadas, nomeadamente o mercado de capitais; :: reforma sistemtica da Previdncia Social. No quadro do Estudo, que conta com apoio do Banco Mundial, o BCV recorreu a especialistas de renome internacional para anlise da situao actual do sector, identificao do mercado potencial e concepo de medidas e instrumentos de poltica necessrios ao desenvolvimento da actividade. Os primeiros resultados do Estudo sero aqui hoje apresentados pelos consultores para vossa apreciao e comentrios. Contamos com um debate participado e que conduza a recomendas concretas e detalhadas para a concluso do Estudo. Terminamos agradecendo antecipadamente a vossa contribuio neste exerccio, sendo certo que continuaremos a contar com a vossa colaborao nas fases seguintes deste processo. Juntos conseguiremos vencer os desafios que temos pela frente, rumo  consolidao e desenvolvimento da actividade seguradora e financeira em geral. http://www.bcv.cv/_conteudo/intervencao/governador/2005/ig20050604.htm 15-09-2010 Interveno do governador no lanamento do servio Visa Page 3 of 3 Praia, 6 de Abril de 2005. Title: Speech Delivered at the Inauguration of Members
text: Governor's intervention in launching visa page 1 of 2 service SPEECH GIVEN BY THE GOVERNOR OF BANCO DE CABO VERDE, DR. CARLOS AUGUSTO DE BURGO, AT THE INAUGURATION OF THE MEMBERS OF THE GENERAL AUDIT OF THE SECURITIES MARKET We are pleased to be today giving possession to the holders of the General Audit of the Securities Market. This is an important step towards the institutionalization of the capital market, another step in the journey towards the development of the national financial system. This act is part of a broad framework of concerted actions aimed at the overall development of the national financial system, including, inter alia, the following strands:  Diversification of the financial system through the development of the capital market and specialised financial institutions;  strengthening the supervisory authority's capacity and transitionto risk-based supervision to ensure the safety and efficiency of the system;  Improving the management of monetary policy by improving the management of reserves and liquidity in general;  Promotion of long-term savings through the development of penss funds and life insurance. The current eco-policy of the Government of Cape Verde calls for accelerated eco-growth, in a stable macro-ecological framework. In the past few years, with the strengthening of the central bank's autonomy and budgetary discipline, significant progress has been made in ensuring macro-econic stability. In the growth of the economy, the private sector is called, much more than in the past, to play a driving role. However, the participation of the private sector is hampered by constraints of various order, among which is the difficulty in accessing and the cost of financing. This is why, among the initiatives to promote private sector participation, actions related to the development of the financial sector are pontificated. Despite the measures taken, the financial system remains incipient, uncompetitive and low in character. In particular, banks continue to occupy a prominent position in the financial system, with a strong predominance of the mobilisation of surpluses formed by eco-agents and in the internal financing of the economy. As a result, banking products and services predominate to the detriment of more specialised ones that can better meet the specific needs of national deficit eco-workers. Overall, there is a lack of note in the diversification of savings instruments offered by national financial institutions, resulting in discrepancies between the maturities of the funds raised and those of the possibilities of implementation, with negative effects on risk management and interest rates and, therefore, also at the level of investment. In this context, the promotion of national savings, particularly long-term savings, and its channeling to the productive sector, as well as the strengthening of institutional and 15-09-2010 Governor's intervention in the launch of visa page 2 of 2 service intervention of the financial system becomes indispensable, thus constituting indispensable requirements for the ecological development that is advocated. The process of institutionalising the capital market is of particular importance for Cape Verde given that a dynamic, efficient and transparent capital market can contribute to the development and modernisation of the financial system and, therefore, to the growth and competitiveness of the Cape Verdean economy. Because of its attributes in terms of volume, risk, and transparency in price formation, the capital market can contribute to meeting the specific financing needs of the national business community. However, for this to happen, it is necessary to create the appropriate conditions for the functioning of the market, in particular in terms of the efficiency of operations, guarantees to investors and competitive conditions of financing to the business community. The Bank of Cape Verde is actively committed to the creation of these conditions, and among others the following initiatives currently underway:  strengthening internal capacity in the supervision of financial activity, in particular in the banking, capital markets, and international financial institutions;  improving the regulatory framework for the activity of specialised financial institutions;  Development of the payment system in the framework of speed and transparency and through the improvement of the technological infrastructure. As everyone is aware, the process of institutionalization of the capital market has known uncertainties and bumps. However, we are convinced that with the actions underway or planned, the conditions for an effective start of the process are gathered this time. Our conviction is reinforced by the involvement of commercial institutions in this enterprise. To those sworn in, on whom the first responsibility for the supervision of the capital market will be, we wish to succeed in the exercise of the new functions, and they will understand the choice that has fallen on them as proof of the much that is expected of them in this process. We end by thanking you once again for your presence in this act, and making a vow of a fruitful collaboration between the entities in the process of installation and development of the capital market. We count on you for the activities that we want to develop in the aspects of the process that are the responsibility of the BCV, and it is certain that you can count on us as responsible for supervising the activity. Beach, May 11, 2005 Charles Augustus of Burgo -Governor 15-09-2010

CARLOS AUGUSTO DE BURGO, NO ACTO DE TOMADA DE POSSE DOS MEMBROS DA AUDITORIA GERAL DO MERCADO DE VALORES MOBILIRIOS Apraz-nos estar hoje a conferir posse aos titulares da Auditoria Geral do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios. Trata-se de um passo importante rumo  institucionalizao do mercado de capitais, mais uma etapa na caminhada para o desenvolvimento do sistema financeiro nacional. Este acto insere-se num quadro amplo de acs concertadas visando o desenvolvimento global do sistema financeiro nacional, que inclui, nomeadamente, as seguintes vertentes:  Diversificao do sistema financeiro atravs do desenvolvimento do mercado de capitais e de instituis financeiras especializadas;  Reforo da capacidade da autoridade de superviso e transio para uma superviso baseada no risco, com vista a garantir a segurana e a eficincia do sistema;  Melhoria da gesto da poltica monetria, pela via do aperfeioamento da gesto das reservas e da liquidez em geral;  Promoo da poupana de longo prazo, atravs do desenvolvimento de fundos de penss e do seguro de vida. A actual poltica econica do Governo de Cabo Verde preconiza um crescimento econico acelerado, num quadro macro econico estvel. Nos timos anos, com o reforo da autonomia do Banco Central e a disciplina oramental, registaram-se avanos significativos na garantia da estabilidade macroeconica. No crescimento da economia, o sector privado  chamado, muito mais do que no passado, a desempenhar um papel motor. Porm, a participao do sector privado  dificultada por constrangimentos de vria ordem, de entre os quais se salienta a dificuldade no acesso ao financiamento e o custo deste. Da que entre as iniciativas plicas de promoo da participao do sector privado pontifiquem as acs relacionadas com o desenvolvimento do sector financeiro. No obstante as medidas adoptadas, o sistema financeiro continua incipiente, pouco concorrencial e com baixo nvel de especializao. Em concreto, os bancos continuam a ocupar uma posio de grande destaque no sistema financeiro, sendo muito acentuado o seu predomnio na mobilizao dos excedentes formados pelos agentes econicos e no financiamento interno da economia. Em consequncia, predominam os produtos e servios de cariz bancrio em detrimento de outros mais especializados e que podem melhor corresponder s necessidades especficas dos agentes econicos deficitrios nacionais. No geral, constata-se uma insuficincia notia na diversificao dos instrumentos de poupana oferecidos pelas instituis financeiras nacionais, traduzindo-se em discrepncias entre as maturidades dos recursos captados e as das possibilidades de aplicao, com efeitos negativos a nvel da gesto dos riscos e das taxas de juros e, por conseguinte, tambm a nvel do investimento. Neste contexto, a promoo da poupana nacional, particularmente a poupana de longo prazo, e a sua canalizao para o sector produtivo, assim como o reforo das capacidades institucionais e de http://www.bcv.cv/_conteudo/intervencao/governador/2005/ig20051105.htm 15-09-2010 Interveno do governador no lanamento do servio Visa Page 2 of 2 interveno do sistema financeiro tornam-se indispensveis, constituindo, dessa forma, requisitos incontornveis para o desenvolvimento econico que se preconiza. O processo de institucionalizao do mercado de capitais reveste-se de particular importncia para Cabo Verde atendendo ao facto de que um mercado de capitais dinmico, eficiente e transparente pode contribuir para o desenvolvimento e a modernizao do sistema financeiro e, por conseguinte, para o crescimento e a competitividade da economia cabo-verdiana. Pelos seus atributos em termos de volume, risco, e transparncia na formao dos preos, o mercado de capitais pode contribuir para satisfazer as necessidades especficas de financiamento do empresariado nacional. Porm, para que tal acontea torna-se necessrio que sejam criadas as condis adequadas ao funcionamento do mercado, nomeadamente em termos de eficincia das operas, de garantias aos aforradores e investidores e de condis competitivas de financiamento ao empresariado. O Banco de Cabo Verde encontra-se activamente empenhado na criao dessas condis, sendo de salientar, entre outras as seguintes iniciativas actualmente em curso:  Reforo da capacidade interna em matria de superviso da actividade financeira, nomeadamente nas reas bancria, de mercado de capitais, e das instituis financeiras internacionais;  Melhoria do quadro regulamentar aplicvel  actividade das instituis financeiras especializadas;  Desenvolvimento do sistema de pagamentos na tica da celeridade e transparncia e pela via da melhoria da infra-estrutura tecnolica. Como  do conhecimento de todos, o processo de institucionalizao do mercado de capitais tem conhecido incertezas e solavancos. Estamos porm convictos de que com as acs em curso ou previstas, esto desta vez reunidas as condis para um arranque efectivo do processo. Esta nossa convico  reforada pelo envolvimento das instituis comerciais neste empreendimento. Aos empossados, sobre quem recair a responsabilidade primeira pela superviso do mercado de capitais, desejamos sucesso no exerccio das novas funs, sendo certo que entendero a escolha que sobre os mesmos recaiu como prova do muito que deles se espera neste processo. Terminamos agradecendo mais uma vez a vossa presena neste acto, e fazendo votos de uma colaborao frutfera entre as entidades no processo de instalao e desenvolvimento do mercado de capitais. Contamos convosco para as actividades que pretendemos desenvolver nas vertentes do processo que forem da responsabilidade do BCV, sendo certo que podem contar connosco enquanto responsvel pela superviso da actividade. Praia, 11 de Maio de 2005 Carlos Augusto de Burgo -Governador http://www.bcv.cv/_conteudo/intervencao/governador/2005/ig20051105.htm 15-09-2010

text: Index 1 - Cape Verdean economy in 2004................ 3 1.1 - External Framing..................................... 3 1.2 - Economic activity................................... 3 1.3 - Prices......................................... 4 1.4 - Balance of Payments................................................. 4 1.5 - Public Finances.................................................... 5 1.6 - Monetary Policy, Interest Rates and Exchange Rates ................................................ 5 1.6.1 - Monetary situation..................... 5 1.6.2 - Public Debt Market....................... 6 1.6.3 - Exchange Rates ........................ 6 2 - Economic developments in the first half of 2005................................................. 7 2.1 - International Economy................. 7 2.2 - Economic activity................................................................... 7 2.3 - Monetary Policy ........................ 8 2.4 - Evolution of the Main Monetary Aggregates ................................................................... 8 3 - Monetary Policy Forecast for Next Semester ...................................................................... 9 3.1 - Current Monetary Programme ................... 10 Attachments .................................................. 11 1.Cape Verdean Economy in 2004 1.1 - External Framework According to estimates by the International Monetary Fund, the global economic climate in 2004 was characterized by a favorable performance, with the world's product growing at the real rate of 5%, driven to a large extent by the positive developments of industrialized economies (particularly the American one) and the exceptional growth of emerging economies, especially China. International economic activity, however, was conditioned by oil market disruptions, which culminated in oil prices rising above USD 50/barrel in the second half of the year, which reinforced the risks of slowing down global activity. The climate of political and military instability, which is still in force in the Middle East, also restricted developments in global activity in 2004. Regionally, the U.S. economy continued to lead the global economic recovery, growing at 4.4 percent. The analysis of the fundamentals of the Japanese economy points to a more sustainable economic recovery and the dissipation of the deflation situation that the country has faced for some years. The euro area, for its part, has been testing a recovery in its economic activity, which has remained extremely dependent on external demand. Eurozone GDP grew at 2%, compared to the 0.6% rate in 2003. In turn, emerging markets continued a pace of accelerated growth, especially the Chinese economy, mainly based on its external sector. China's economic performance has had positive effects for other Asian countries and raw material export markets overall. Still for developing countries, IMF estimates point to a positive performance, with Africa, in particular, growing at the rate of 4.5% (Subsahriana Africa 4.6%). 1.2 - National economic activity The Bank of Cape Verde estimates growth in the Cape Verdean economy of 4.9% in real terms in 2004, after a slight slowdown in 2003, despite less favourable developments in the price of oil and the government's policy of containing expenditure. For this development, domestic demand has contributed positively, particularly its components private consumption and investment, as the relevance of external demand is still weak, despite the growing importance of tourism revenues in economic activity. Private consumption grew 9.5% in 2004, recovering from the slight slowdown in 2003. The behaviour of private consumption reflected the increase in imports of consumer goods, especially durable goods (12.7% in the whole of the year), while non-durable goods slowed in their pace of growth. In turn, the significant increase in investment (which grew 4.6% in real terms) essentially reflected increased investment in construction, equipment goods and transport materials, to be assessed by the evolution of imports of these types of goods and by the improvements in cement and automobile sales. It should also be noted that in 2004, in particular from the second half of the year on, there was a greater dynamism of economic activity, mainly driven by the services sector, particularly the Trade and Tourism subsectors. 1.3 - Prices In 2004, the inflation rate, measured through the Consumer Price Index (CPI), showed a sharp drop, both in terms of average annual variation and annual variation, maintaining the trend of deceleration of inflation started in August 2003. Despite the increases in fuel prices in June and November, there was, on average annual terms, negative inflation of around 1.9%. Overall, the behavior of the Consumer Price Index essentially reflected the price variations in the food class, whose predominant weight in the basket continues to largely determine the inflation rate in the country, as the evolution of core inflation attests. However, the increase in fuel prices in June clearly marks a trend reversal in the monthly change in the inflation rate, reflecting the average rate of change that decreases less compared to previous months. Indeed, industrial energy goods showed a markedly upward trend (average annual rate of 5.2%), counterbalancing the impact of core inflation, which shows a clearly deflationary trend in the year (-2.1%) and a negative contribution of 1.3%. 1.4 - Balance of Payments The favourable evolution of the balance of payments in the period resulted in a substantial improvement in the structural deficit of the current account, which now represents 6% in the ratio of GDP, remaining, for the second consecutive year, below double digits. The positive developments in the current account resulted mainly from the good performance of the balance of services (especially those related to tourism), which reached 4.5% of GDP, compared to 1.6% of GDP in 2003, and the evolution of private current transfers, especially remittances from emigrants, which grew at the rate of 11%. Unlike the balances of services and current transfers, the balances of goods and incomes have been less favourable, deteriorating by around 4% and 18%, respectively. The performance of the balance of goods was due to the increase in the trade deficit of goods, by 5.4% (although at a lower rate, taking into account the evolution of domestic demand), together with the reduction in fuel reexports (-0.6%), related to the reduction in the flow of aircraft at the international airport, which also led to a decrease in net revenues from services related to air navigation support. 1 Inflation rate discounted the effects of unprocessed food and industrial energy goods In turn, the financial flows between Cape Verde and abroad were resuming by a surplus equivalent to 3.5% of GDP, resulting in a reduction in the financing needs of the Cape Verdean economy compared to the outside world. Indeed, during the year under review, there has been a positive evolution of foreign direct investment (OI) for the country, particularly aimed at the Tourism sub-sector, which will also have contributed decisively to a higher net capital inflow into the country, with an increase in the flow of RdI by 34%. The combined result of the evolution of current and capital accounts made it possible to reduce the financing needs of the economy (from 6% of GDP to 4% of GDP) and favored the accumulation of external reserves that began to cover 2.4 months of import. 1.5 - Public Finances In 2004, the budgetary policy followed, translated into austerity in the application of resources and the expansion of the tax base, resulted in a significant improvement in the overall public deficit (including donations), resulting not only from the increase in revenues which mainly reflects the introduction of VAT but also the increase in donations, coupled with a reduction in current expenditure. Available data point to a global public deficit, including donations, of the order of 1,125 million escudos, representing 1.3% of GDP, against 3,285 million escudos, 4.1% of GDP, recorded in 2003. For the financing of the deficit, the State has mostly used external resources, including disbursements from multilateral bodies and budget support provided by bilateral partners. In turn, the primary deficit as a percentage of GDP, calculated excluding net interest expenses, decreased by 1.9 p.p., reaching 7.6% (9.5% in 2003). 1.6 - Monetary policy, interest rates and exchange rates 1.6.1 - Monetary situation In 2004, monetary policy continued to be geared towards the main objective of maintaining price stability, with a view to ensuring the conditions for long-term growth and strengthening international reserves in a context of parity of the Cape Verdean shield to the euro. Indeed, the positive development of the national economic environment, coupled with the strengthening of the country's credibility, translated into the confidence of external donors, allowed a significant influx of capital during the year, both in the framework of the country's budget aid programmes, contributing to the strengthening of ongoing fiscal consolidation, and in the framework of the policy of attractiveness of external investment, which resulted in the strengthening of the country's net external position. As a result of this evolution, there was a frankly positive behavior of the main monetary aggregates in 2004, particularly the net cash equivalents of or which grew exceptionally at a rate of 31.9%, as a result of the positive evolution of net cash and foreign assets of Commercial Banks, the total external assets of the system and the Net Cash Of The Central Bank (foreign exchange reserves and other foreign assets). In the same period, net domestic credit showed a growth rate of 5.2%, reflecting, fundamentally, the increase observed in the credit to the economy, in 9.3%, reflecting or favourable behaviour of its components in relation to 2003, in particular housing credit (11%), credit to the manufacturing industry (about 26%) and credit to trade, restaurants and hotels (7%). Reflecting the moderation of the use of bank financing by the State, the Credit to the Public Administrative Sector increased by 0.48% compared to 3.1% recorded in 2003. The increase in net cash and cash above, together with the growth in domestic credit, contributed to the increase in the monetary mass of about 10.5%, 2.8 p.p. above the forecast for the year. This favorable performance of monetary aggregates consubstanciouse in meeting the mandatory targets contained in the Growth and Poverty Reduction Program (PRGF), agreed with the IMF. These results, together with the favourable behaviour of the reserves, allowed the monetary authority to relieve monetary conditions in 2004. In this context, in order to reduce the cost of financial intermediation and stimulate the reduction of interest rates by credit institutions, the Central Bank lowered the rate of minimum cash cash and cash flows from 19% to 18%. It should be noted, however, that the system's liquidity surplus did not affect active and passive interest rates, which remained at the same level as in 2003. 1.6.2 - Public debt market In the whole of the year, reflecting a lower need for state indebtedness, the public debt market was characterized by less intensive emissions and use of Treasury Bills, compared to the previous year. As a result of this situation, the emission and placement rates of BT showed progressive decreases over 2004 for all deadlines, with an average of around 5.5%. Contrary to developments in the BT market, the rates of tBs increased successively throughout the year, with the average rate settling at 7.5%, partly reflecting greater investor appetite for the longer-term market segment. Despite this change in the profile of domestic public debt, with increased demand for TUs, the average placement rate decreased by 1 p.p. compared to the previous year, mainly due to decreased state financing needs. 1.6.3 - Exchange Rates The evolution of the Cape Verdean shield, in a context of fixed parity with the euro, essentially reflected the behavior of the dollar in international foreign exchange markets, in the face of investor concerns about the sustainability of the current Us external deficit, estimated at 5.7% of GDP. In this perspective, during 2004, the nominal effective exchange rate index (TEN) showed a slight appreciation of 0.88% compared to 2003, reflecting, fundamentally, the appreciation of the Cape Verdean currency against the US dollar, at 8.5%. For its part, the real effective exchange rate (TER) index revealed a depreciation of 3.1% compared to the previous year, as a result of the favorable behavior of the Cape Verde price index, which resulted in a positive price differential in relation to the main trading partners. 2 - Economic developments in the first half of 2005 2.1 - International economy According to bloombergg, the world economy is growing at lower rates than in 2004, mainly due to tightening monetary conditions (rising interest rates) in the US and the high price of oil. U.S. economic growth is closer to the rate of potential GDP expansion, which lessens concern about inflation, with regard to domestic demand, while that of the EURO zone is and will continue to be low due to the need for structural reforms, a problem that also affects the Japanese economy. Emerging countries, in general, remain well, with China and India standing out. The price of oil continues to benefit Russia. For Portugal, in the summer projections, Banco de Portugal, recognizing the worsening economic situation, revised the growth rate for GDP from 1.6% to 1.5%. The performance of the Portuguese economy in the first three months of the year, the set of fiscal policy measures aimed at rebalancing public accounts, as well as the sharp degradation of external accounts, reflecting not only the rise in the price of oil, but also the loss of competitiveness of exports, are the basis of this review. The biggest concerns for the world economy are:  The evolution of U.S. twin deficits and a possible "bubble" in the real estate market  The disparity of expansion between regions  Volatility and high oil prices  The possibility of political disruption in one of OPEC's major oil producers -Saudi Arabia, Iran or Venezuela 2.2 -National economic activity In the first half of the year, to be assessed by the behaviour of some indicators of gross fixed capital formation and private consumption, economic activity continues to accelerate to levels higher than in 2004, according to the initial forecasts of the BCV, which point to GDP growth in the range of 6 to 6.5%. From the analysis, in the same year, of the balance of payments data for the month of June, it is observed that, for the expansion of economic activity, the dynamic behavior of domestic demand is underlying, judging by the growth of imports of intermediate goods (17.5%) and capital (in the order of 50%), goods considered as main components of the investment, and consumer goods (6%), despite the slowdown in exports of goods. The expansion of economic activity in the period under review is visible in the evolution of the economic climate indicator released by the INE. Since mid-2004, this indicator has maintained an upward trajectory, suggesting further expansion of economic activity for the remaining months of 2005. With regard to sectoral developments and, for the same period, the behaviour of indicators in the sub-sectors of industry, tourism and transport shows increased confidence in entrepreneurs, reflecting their appreciation of production, and the increase in the order book and turnover. 2.3 - Monetary Policy The IMF's assessment in March 2005 confirms that by the end of 2004 the quantitative targets agreed under the PRGF were "all met and with substantial margins", in particular for net external reserves and for the ceilingiling of the evolution of net credit from the banking system to the Central Government. The positive evolution of the main monetary aggregates in the last quarter of 2004, in particular the accumulation of the Bank of Cape Verde's international reserves, an essential condition for the defense of pegg, determined that at the beginning of the year the Bank of Cape Verde would start taking measures to loosen monetary conditions. Thus, after a first intervention of lowering the rate of minimum cash cash availability from 19% to 18% in December 2004, the reduction in the rate of withdrawal from 8.5% to 7.5% is followed in February 2005. In March, the combined impact of these two measures is reflected in the lower average interest rates of commercial banks. In June, the Central Bank further reduced the minimum cash availability rate from 18% to 17%, with no significant impacts on the system's excess liquidity. 2.4 - Evolution of the main Monetary Aggregates In June 2005, and in relation to December 2004, the positive evolution path of the main monetary aggregates continued, highlighting the continuous strengthening of the Bank of Cape Verde's net international reserves, which grow at a rate of 32.3%, translating foreign exchange inflow to the State and for projects, as well as the positive net evolution of the interbank foreign exchange market. In absolute terms, the bcv's net international reserves reached 14,945.6 million escudos (134.5 million euros) at the end of June. In this period, the system's Net External Assets grew 34.1%, reaching 18,164.3 million escudos, contributing to the evolution of this aggregate the behavior of the Liquid External Assets of the Bank of Cape Verde (24.3%) and the External Assets of deposit banks (9.8%). The monetary mass has a growth rate of 5.5%, reflecting the positive behaviour of the main factors of monetary creation. From the analysis of the components of the Monetary Mass, there is a decrease in monetary circulation (6.2%) and an increase of 5.7% in demand deposits in national currency. For its part, almost monetary liabilities grew at a rate of 7.5% compared to December, at 41,335.3 million escudos in June (40,975.1 million escudos in May), which reflects the positive evolution of the generality of its components, with emphasis on emigrant deposits, the most representative in total almost monetary liabilities, growth at a rate of 4.4% compared to December. Internal Credit reached 57,287.8 million escudos in June, growing 1.42% compared to December, as a result of the combined evolution of Net Credit to the Central Government (which decreased 0.6% and Credit to the Economy, which grew 3.04%). For December, the evolution of credit to the economy in the period reflects the predominant weight of home loans (45.3% in total credit2), which grows by 2.7%. Credit to Commerce, Restaurants and Hotels, less representative of total credit (about 11.1%) also shows a positive evolution, with a growth of 7.9%, while credit to the Manufacturing Industry (5%) and Social and Personal Services (14.3%) reports negative variations of 7.1% and 3.5%, respectively. 2 Excluding credit granted by CECV In the first half of 2005 there was a change in the temporal profile of government debt securities, leading to a greater weight of short-term debt. Bt's placement rates, reflecting the moderation of bank lending by the Public Administrative Sector (SPA), maintained a downward trajectory throughout the semester, reaching 4.25% in June in a context marked by a high demand for securities. The cost of financing government bonds, measured by the average interest rates of the last 20 issues placed on the market, fell from 5.0850% to 4.9092%. 3 - Monetary Policy Forecast for next semester For the next six months, monetary policy objectives will continue to be based on price stability and maintaining exchange rate stability. The implementation of monetary policy should, however, be conditioned by the evolution of the main monitoring variables. In the context of growing signs of strengthening economic activity and maintaining core inflation at a fairly low level, the loosening of monetary conditions by the Bank of Cape Verde (reduction in rates of minimum cash and rate of ease of supply), and the resulting liquidity, in the short term, have created favorable conditions to accommodate greater financing needs of the Cape Verdean economy. In this circumstance, the monetary authority's stance will be non-interventionist, embodied in the careful follow-up of market behaviour to the stimulus generated, in particular with regard to the change in rates of passive and active operations, bearing in mind that the interest rates of the privileged instrument of application of banks, BT, are at historically low levels. A possible intervention measure of the BCV would be to reduce the rate of ease of transfer. From a medium-term perspective, the monetary authority should continue to pay attention to possible risks, which may require the revision of its current stance, related in particular to:  loosening of the policy of budgetary restraint, as a result, inter alia, of increased expenditure on public administration salaries, transfers to municipalities, institutes and autonomous services, as well as subsidies to undertakings;  Instability in the oil market and forecast of high price maintenance for the next two years, meaning the economy could face a possible oil shock;  Euro/Dollar price fluctuation due to its impact on reserve management. In the long run, for an open economy such as cape Verde, the performance of the real economy is fundamentally the pace of carrying out a set of structural reforms, including public finances, public administration, pension systems, the labour market (amendment of the Labour Code and Professional Qualification), Economic Infrastructure and the Institutional Framework (formalities, regulation, conflict prevention/resolution), without which it is not possible to lay the foundations for the development of competitiveness. 3.1 Current Monetary Programme Taking into account the macroeconomic developments outlined for 2005, the monetary programming scenario defined by the Bank of Cape Verde boils down to:  The monetary mass will grow about 8%, 1 p.p. above the initially scheduled, in line with the expected growth for nominal GDP, judging by the expected maintenance of the currency's movement speed level of around 1.15.  The system's net reserves are expected to grow at a rate of 9% (8.2% initially scheduled), reflecting developments in economic activity, especially in exports of goods and services, tourism and remittances from emigrants, as well as the disbursement of resources linked to external loans allocated to investment programmes and donations for project financing and food aid. Domestic credit will grow at a rate of 5.7%, reflecting a decrease in the financing needs of the general government (it is expected that in 2005, credit to the general public sector will decrease by 2.1%) and a positive credit behaviour to the economy (12%).
