Title: Speech at the Opening Session
text: Speech at the Release Session of the 500 Note -February 25 Page 1 of 2 Madam Secretary of State for Finance, Excellency Gentlemen Ladies and gentlemen of the Town Halls of Santo Antao Distinguished Guests Excellencies Cape Verde is experiencing a unique moment today, marked by the dynamism of its economy, the accumulation of external reserves, the stability of the currency exchange rate and the great confidence of the eco-agents. It remains, now, to face the challenge of sustainability of growth. In this perspective, it is necessary to continue to create the conditions to expand production capacity, generate jobs and allow the country to grow sustainably. In addition to consistent fiscal and monetary policies, macro-econic stability must continue to be achieved in order to facilitate the mobilisation of investments necessary for the sustained expansion of production capacity, the expansion of which is also directly dependent on the productivity levels achieved. Just as there is no growth without investment, there is also no investment without an effective and secure financial intermediation, capable of enabling the link between the savings of agents and investment opportunities, with positive repercussions on the environmental activity. The creation of conditions for sustained growth is therefore the development of a modern, safe and efficient capital market. The efficiency of financial intermediation also depends on factors such as transparency, which allows the rational allocation of available resources to the most productive investments. As regards the role of the Bank of Cape Verde, transparency and communication are basic instruments for the effectiveness of monetary policy. Believing that the financial system should always be open to interaction with society, the Bank of Cape Verde has been promoting dialogue and the circulation of information, in the understanding that the more transparent a market, the more competitive it will be and the more access to financial services will have the population. Dear Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, It is the role of the Bank of Cape Verde to promote the effective functioning of the financial system in general and the payment system, in particular by ensuring, inter alia, the stock of banknotes and coins and the good quality of fiduciary circulation. It is from this perspective that we continue with the purpose of constituting a new series of banknotes, which began with the emission of two thousand and five thousand escudos, and we now take another step with this five hundred escudos. If this event is relevant in itself, the act to which we are pleased to preside today is also of great symbolism, first and foremost because the Bank of Cape Verde is paying tribute to the figure of a man who, through the universality of his work, has contributed to the recognition of his country of origin. The election of Roberto Duarte Silva is nothing more than the recognition of the invaluable contribution to science, and to Cape Verde, who gave this son of Santo Antao. The island that saw him born also deserved to be highlighted on the back of the same note, through the image of a trapiche, symbol of one of the activities that holds the most weight in the economy of the island. Ladies and gentlemen, 15-09-2010 Speech at the Release Session of the 500 Note -February 25 Page 2 of 2 The symbolism of this act is great, but it becomes even greater, when it happens on this Day 25 February, date of the birthday of Roberto Duarte Silva and the general issue of the note, and in this School that also bears his name. It was therefore not a chance to choose this island, this place and this day to mark the official launch of the new note of five hundred escudos. To complement all this symbolism, we are pleased here to announce that the Bank of Cape Verde should join this School in order, with its Management, to examine concrete forms of collaboration, so that we can continue to dignify the name of its patron. To paraphrase the poet, The Great Men Don't Die! Let me therefore express my full admiration for the remarkable man of science, who was Roberto Duarte Silva, in the person of his relatives in this act represented. A word of appreciation to the Municipality of Ribeira Grande that spared no effort to help to give shine to this simple cerimia with the Bank of Cape Verde. May this note of five hundred escudos, in addition to exercising the functions of means of exchange and payment, also serve to perpetuate and make known to young figures who ennoble and pride Cape Verde. Thank you very much! 15-09-2010

Title: BCV Governor's Speech
text: Intervention of the Governor of the BCV in the Atelier on the Development of the System ... Page 1 of 2 BCV Governor's speech at the Atelier on the Development of the Financial System March 28, 2007 Prime Minister, Minister for Finance and Public Administration, Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, The importance of the financial system relates to the number of important functions it has, including the implementation of payments, the transformation of risk, mobilisation and channeling of savings to investment. It should be noted that the proper functioning of the financial system can greatly boost economic activity, in particular by strengthening confidence in the currency, increasing investment, and consequently accelerating economic activity. Moreover, in the case of Cape Verde, the provision of financial services to non-residents has been identified as an opportunity to develop the economy. The development of the national financial system should be guided by a set of priority objectives, in particular: -efficiency and regularity in the functioning of markets; -risk prevention; -quality control of financial information; -protection of investors, particularly those who have greater difficulty in defending their rights and interests; -prevention and repression of illegal or fraudulent actions; -facilitating access to finance and reducing the financial costs faced by national micro-and small enterprises. In the process of developing the financial system we will have to act in a concerted manner in various respects. In this sense, by way of example: (i) The possibility of conducting trades with Treasury securities, in particular on the secondary market, requires consolidation and deepening of macro-economic stability; (ii) The development of specialised financial activities requires reforms at the tax and tax systems; (iii) The development of the international financial market requires a strengthening of the country's fiscal competitiveness, on the basis of internal non-discrimination, an objective whose materialisation requires the search for a balance with state financing needs; (iv) The realisation of investment and business opportunities requires better organization of the business fabric and greater training of the national business. The proper functioning and development of the financial system should concern all its actors. In particular, their effective regulation and supervision should be central and permanent concerns of the authorities. The regulatory framework should ensure, at all times, in addition to good risk management, that there are adequate incentives for financial innovation and the development of financial services. 15-09-2010 Intervention of the Governor of the BCV in the Atelier on the Development of the System ... Page 2 of 2 At this conference on the development of the financial system, we have as our starting point a study evaluating the legal and institutional framework of the national financial system prepared by international experts. We bring it to your consideration as a vehicle to facilitate discussion in the matter. Feel free to ask the various experts present here and to question their findings and proposals. We have also brought here a group of public and private leaders who play an important role in this process. I ask you to take advantage of this unique opportunity to put the questions and present the proposals that contribute to the important objective to which we have set ourselves. At the end of the day we hope to leave here with a set of proposals to be implemented in the short and medium term, because the time is for action. In a globalized and increasingly competitive world, opportunities do not wait. Welcome to this conference and may it be profitable and pleasant for all of us. Praia City, March 29, 2007 15-09-2010

O bom funcionamento e o desenvolvimento do sistema financeiro devem preocupar todos os seus intervenientes. Em particular, a sua regulao e superviso efectivas devem constituir-se como preocupaes centrais e permanentes das autoridades. O quadro regulatrio deve garantir, a cada momento, alm da boa gesto do risco, a existncia de incentivos adequados  inovao financeira e ao desenvolvimento dos servios financeiros. http://www.bcv.cv/_conteudo/intervencao/governador/2007/ig20070328.htm 15-09-2010 Interveno do Governador do BCV no Atelier sobre o Desenvolvimento do Sistema ... Title: Press Conference to Present the Report to the Government
text: Press Conference for Presentation of the Report to the Government -April 2007 Page 1 of 2 PRESS CONFERENCE BY THE GOVERNOR OF BANCO DE CABO VERDE, DR. CARLOS BURGO,ON THE OCCASION OF THE DELIVERY OF THE REPORT TO THE GOVERNMENT (under Article 18, 3. of the Organic Law of the BCV) 1. In compliance with the provisions of its Organic Law, the Bank of Cape Verde sent to the Government, through the Minister of Finance and Pblica Administration, the Report to the Government, with reference to March 31, 2007. Cpia will also be referred to the President of the National Assembly and to the Specialized Committee on Finance and Budget 2. The monetary situation, in the six months ending in March 2007, was marked by the positive evolution of the external position of the Cape Verdean economy, translated into the accumulation of external reserves of the central bank and foreign assets net of commercial banks, which, in a fixed parity exchange rate regime, ultimately determines the expansion of the monetary mass (M2) which, in the period under analysis, it varies by 3.4%. 3. In a framework for the defense of the exchange rate regime, and with the end of the maintenance of price stability, the conduct of monetary policy by the Central Bank was based on the cautious use of the instruments it has, in order to effectively manage the liquidity existing in the banking system, taking into account the high price pressures in the economy. In this way, the Bank of Cape Verde has resorted, inter alia, to the active issue of Monetary Intervention Securities, intended to absorb part of the excess liquidity in the banking system. 4. In terms of the evolution of the economic environment, the available indicators suggest some slowdown in economic activity, derived mainly from the evolution of national private investment and consumption, the behaviour of which continues to be decisively influenced by less favourable price developments. On the other hand, there is a significant dynamism in net exports of services, especially those related to tourism. 5. As far as inflation is concerned, it remains  if the bullish trend in prices, with the monthly average reaching a 5.6 % change in March. This behaviour of the inflation rate continues to be determined by changes in prices and tariffs administered, but also by the price developments of certain products of the goods component, in particular "energy", "processed food" and "industrial". As for the services component, there is a decrease in prices, in particular international telephone crossings, international telephone communication tariffs and public transport fares. 6. As for Cape Verde's external accounts, information available until March points to positive behaviour, which is particularly reflected in a strengthening of the country's international reserves, despite the worsening trade deficit of goods as a result of the continued increase in imports. The increase in these was, however, offset by the significant growth in net exports of services (particularly services related to travel and air transport). 7. Benefiting from the positive contribution of the external position, the main monetary aggregates presented a positive trajectory in March 2007, with particular emphasis on the System's Net External Assets, which grew at a rate of 11% compared to December of the previous year. Net Internal Credit shows a stable behavior, with a 1.8% change, explained by the evolution of Net Credit to the Pblico Sector, which has been decreasing, and by the positive evolution of credit to the Economy, which grows at a rate of 4.1% compared to December 2006, which reflects the recovery of credit activity with the national banking system. 8. Taking into account the preliminary information available, the BCV projections for 2007 point to a growth of the product in the range of 6 -7 %. This development mirrors the prospects for increased consumption and investment expansion, especially foreign direct investment for the tourism sector. 9. For inflation, the BCV projection points to a slowdown in prices, with the average annual rate in the range of 2.5 to 3.5%. This projection includes the downward trend of CPI, which in March reached 4.2% in terms of the homlog variation, but takes into account the risk of updating the prices of managed goods and effects arising from possible bad agricultural year on unprocessed goods, the most volatile component of CPI. 10. In line with the scenario presented for economic activity for the next six months, the monetary policy orientation, aiming at the ultimate objective of price stability and conditioned by the fulfilment of the criteria set out in the agreement signed with the IMF, the Policy Support Instrument (PSI), will continue to be the monitoring of the evolution of external reserves and the management of the differential between the interest rates of the euro area, in particular those of Euribor, and the rates of bcv intervention operations, in a context of rising rates on international markets. 15-09-2010 Press Conference for Presentation of the Report to the Government -April 2007 Page 2 of 2 15-09-2010

CARLOS BURGO,POR OCASIO DA ENTREGA DO RELATRIO AO GOVERNO (ao abrigo do art. 18., 3. da Lei Orgnica do BCV) 1. Em cumprimento do estipulado na sua Lei Orgnica, o Banco de Cabo Verde remeteu ao Governo, atravs da Senhora Ministra das Finanas e Administrao Pblica, o Relatrio ao Governo, com referncia a 31 de Maro de 2007. Cpia do mesmo ser igualmente remetida ao Senhor Presidente da Assembleia Nacional e  Comisso Especializada de Finanas e Oramento 2. A situao monetria, nos seis meses terminados em Maro de 2007, foi marcada pela evoluo positiva da posio externa da economia cabo-verdiana, traduzida na acumulao de reservas externas do banco central e de activos externos lquidos dos bancos comerciais, o que, num regime cambial de paridade fixa, acaba por determinar a expanso da massa monetria (M2) que, no perodo em anlise, apresenta a variao de 3.4%. 3. Num quadro de defesa do regime cambial, e tendo como fim ltimo a manuteno da estabilidade de preos, a conduo da poltica monetria por parte do Banco Central pautou-se pelo recurso cauteloso aos instrumentos que possui, no sentido de uma gesto eficaz da liquidez existente no sistema bancrio, tendo em conta as presses altistas dos preos na economia. Deste modo, o Banco de Cabo Verde tem recorrido, nomeadamente,  emisso activa de Ttulos de Interveno Monetria, destinados  absoro de uma parte do excesso de liquidez existente no sistema bancrio. 4. Em termos de evoluo da conjuntura econmica, os indicadores disponveis sugerem algum abrandamento da actividade econmica, derivado essencialmente da evoluo do investimento privado nacional e do consumo, cujo comportamento continua a ser decisivamente influenciado pela evoluo menos favorvel dos preos. Em contrapartida, regista-se um dinamismo expressivo das exportaes lquidas de servios, especialmente dos ligados ao turismo. 5. No que diz respeito  inflao, mantm  se a tendncia altista dos preos, com a mdia mensal a atingir em Maro uma variao de 5,6 %. Este comportamento da taxa de inflao continua a ser determinado pelas alteraes dos preos e tarifas administrados, mas tambm pela evoluo de preos de determinados produtos da componente bens, em especial os energticos, os alimentares transformados e os industriais. Quanto  componente servios, regista-se um decrscimo dos preos, designadamente das passagens reas internacionais, das tarifas de comunicao telefnica internacional e das tarifas de transporte pblico. 6. Quanto s contas externas de Cabo Verde, informaes disponveis at Maro apontam para um comportamento positivo, que se traduz, particularmente, num reforo das reservas internacionais do pas, apesar de se verificar agravamento do dfice comercial de bens, em resultado do aumento contnuo das importaes. O aumento destas foi, no entanto, compensado, pelo crescimento expressivo das exportaes lquidas de servios (particularmente dos servios ligados a viagens por motivo de turismo e aos transportes areos). 7. Beneficiando do contributo positivo da posio externa, os principais agregados monetrios apresentam uma trajectria positiva em Maro de 2007, com particular destaque para os Activos Externos Lquidos do Sistema, que cresceram a uma taxa de 11%, relativamente a Dezembro do ano anterior. Tendo em conta as informaes preliminares disponveis, as projeces do BCV para 2007 apontam para um crescimento do produto no intervalo de 6 -7 %. Esta evoluo espelha as perspectivas de aumento do consumo e de expanso do investimento, sobretudo, o investimento directo estrangeiro para o sector do turismo. 9. Title: Speech by Administrator Manuel Costa, Seminar for Journalists
text: BANCO DE CABO VERDE - 31 YEARS OF EXISTENCE I. CREATION OF THE CAPE VERDE BANK (1975/76) To speak of the history of the Bank of Cape Verde is also to speak of the economic history of Cape Verde Independent by the similarity existing in these two routes. It is consensual the idea that the power to issue currency (in the broad sense) constitutes one of the main attributes of a sovereign state, "un droit regalien" as the French said at the time of the monarchy. With the signing of the agreements signed with Portugal in 1974 and which led to the constitution of a transitional government and later in the Independence of Cape Verde, a process began, aiming in the long term, the creation of a central bank in our country. How to achieve this goal? We must go back three decades, in order to be able to imagine the situation of the moment and to be situated in the surrounding context. We are in 1974/75 in a small island country of the Sahel, in the process of gaining independence, and over which the threat of drought is constantly hanging over, reducing dryland subsistence agriculture to a high-risk activity. It is a country without known natural resources, with a population valued at less than three hundred and a half thousand inhabitants spread over 9 islands, with very few resident staff and virtually no quality infrastructure (excluding Sal airport and Porto Grande de S. Vicente), nor means of transport, without an industrial base, condemned, many think, to survive eternally thanks to foreign aid. The product per inhabitant of the country, at the time, did not reach 150 dollars, place Cape Verde among the poorest countries in the world. Foreign debt was already relatively high, due to some investments made by Portugal in the first half of the 1970s. If I am not mistaken, the amount of foreign exchange reserves in July 1975 was only to guarantee a few days of import. Among the elements that were part of the Finance Department of the Transitional Government, a responsible person was appointed at the beginning of 1975 to set up a team in charge of conducting the whole process of setting up that bank. This process had 3 main strands: 1. Negotiation with Banco Nacional Ultramarino-BNU (and with Banco de Fomento Nacional  BFN); 2. Preparation of the legal instruments necessary for the establishment and entry into operation of the future Central Bank; 3. Looking for partnerships for qualified technical support and training of the staff who would head this Bank. Negotiation with The National Overseas Bank BNU For 111 years, that is, from 1864 to 1975, BNU was the issuing Bank in Cape Verde, also functioning as a commercial bank, with two establishments, one in Praia and the other in S. Vicente, a small agency/counter in Sal and a network of correspondents in the other islands and municipalities of the country (mainly merchants). The National Development Bank, which had a small unit recently opened in Mindelo City, was rehearsing the first steps in financing the construction (housing), fisheries and small industry sectors. The Cape Verdean financial system also included two small institutions, Caixa Economica Postal and Caixa de Credito Agricola, which in 1975 were already in a periclitive financial situation. The negotiations with BNU focused mainly on the conditions for the transfer of BNU's activities to the Bank of Cape Verde, in the process of being set up, with emphasis on the following actions: - transition of bnu branch staff into CVs to the future bank; - acquisition of BNU's assets and liabilities in Cv, including installations; - transfer of monetary instruments to the future central bank. The technical part of the negotiations of these items was conducted without any problem, and on 1 July 1976 the transfer to the BCV of the liabilities and assets of BNU and BFN was carried out without any problems and the activities of the BCV began. If there has been any difficulty in this process, we have no evidence to say so, but it will certainly have been in the part related to the transition of staff, and a small number of BNU employees have chosen to continue in their home frame, that is, not to move to the framework of the future Bank of Cape Verde. Legal Instruments Decree Law No. 25/75 of 29/09 Banco de Cabo Verde was formally created by DL No. 25/75 of 29 September, and on the same date was appointed its first Governor, a young board of 29 years, graduated in Public Finance in Portugal and with only 5 or 6 years of professional experience at the time. From September 75 to June 76, a major boost will be given in the preparation of the effective structuring and implementation of the BCV, first ly thanks to the recruitment of a small "hard core" of senior technicians (4, including the Governor) who, with the valuable support of some Cape Verdean bnu staff, will launch, in a relatively short time, the foundations of the future central bank. These 4 senior technicians are assigned specific responsibilities in the preparation of important processes: - First Organic Law of the Bank; - foreign exchange management and exchange control; - relations with international financial institutions; - organisation and management of credit to the economy; - statistics and economic studies. Under the control of the Governor, bnu's most experienced staff were entrusted with the aspects related to: - management of the commercial banking strand; - preparation of the first issue of banknotes and coins; - organisation of treasury and accounting; - organization and management of administration and personnel. Decision under Law No. 13/76 of 26 June In addition to the above-mentioned DL, the main legal instrument of the Bank's creation process is undoubtedly Decision with force of Law No. 13/76 of 26 June approving the 1st Organic Law of the Bank of Cape Verde. Let me quote four articles from this L.O. that give a small idea of the important powers that the first Government of the Republic of Cape Verde understood to be right to attribute to the Bank of Cape Verde. Art. 4. The Bank's purpose is to exercise the functions of central bank, sole issuer, in the national territory, of banknotes and coins, treasury and commercial bank. Art. 5. The Bank's general mission, in accordance with the Government's economic policy, is to establish in the field of currency, credit and foreign exchange, the most favorable conditions for the balanced development of the national economy, contributing to the use of all the productive resources of the country and ensuring the internal and external stability of the currency. Art. 6. The Bank shall have the following resources: a) The assets and values of the Cape Verde departments of banco Nacional Ultramarino and Banco de Fomento Nacional that may be transferred to and integrated into the bank under and under the agreements concluded between the Republic of Cape Verde and the Portuguese Republic on 15 April 1976; Art. 11. As central bank, the bank will be the state banker, government advisor in the financial field, advisor and controller of monetary and credit policy, manager of the country's external availities and intermediary in international monetary relations. Technical assistance for the development of this project The development of such a complex project, with the limited means available, could have been much more difficult and time-consuming without the collaboration of the central banks of some neighbouring countries. In this sense, and it should be recognized here, the greatest assistance obtained in the creation of the Bank of Cape Verde was provided, without a doubt, by the Central Bank of Algeria through: - technical support to bcv leaders in negotiations with BNU; - short- or long-term training of the bank's first technicians in all aspects of the competence of a central bank; - support in the preparation, ordering and monitoring of the production of the first banknotes issued by the BCV; - assistance in the organisation of certain services. II. EVOLUTION OF BANCO DE CABO VERDE AS BANCO UNIVERSAL (1976/1993) Created a year earlier, the BCV will fully develop its actions from September 1976, with the cessation of BNU's activities in Cape Verde. It started the BCV with a small capital of 100 million escudos and with a staff (after integration of BNU workers) of less than 150 elements, including only 4 senior technicians. For about 16 years the bank will experience an interesting evolution and rapid growth of its activities. On 1 July 1977 there was the launch of the first BCV banknotes and, consequently, the collection of the last BNU issue. It was a complex but very well conducted operation that benefited from the enthusiastic support of many civil service actors, especially in the interior of Santiago and the larger islands. The contribution of BCV workers in this process was admirable. The notes issued by the BCV were still made with a parity identical to that of the Portuguese. A short time later, this parity ceased to exist, due to the strong devaluation of the Portuguese currency, not accompanied by that of the Cape Verde shield, which came to be worth more than the Portuguese shield, with some undesired implications for our emigration in Portugal, which thus reduced the value of its shipments to Cape Verde. In the early years of independence, Cape Verde, through the BCV, will negotiate and achieve its support for the African Development Bank (ADB) in 1976, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank group (IBRD/SFI) in 1978, benefiting the BCV from this quality technical assistance, provided mainly by the Bretton Woods institutions (IMF and World Bank). In the BCV, the 1980s was marked by the following events: - Strengthening the staff with the accelerated recruitment of senior technicians; - increase in bcv capital in 1981 from 100 million escudos to 400 million escudos; - approval of staff status, which was a major demand for workers, especially those who have moved from BNU; - large investments in the construction of BCV agencies in all municipalities of the country and in the construction of special facilities on Sal Island; - computerization of the Bank's main services; - the creation of special accounts of emigrants, with subsidized interest rates, to encourage remittances from cape verdeans of the diaspora and their application in the country in the form of savings and investment; - the establishment of an investment department to boost the financing of medium and long-term loans in key sectors of the economy. In 1990, the Organic Law of the BCV was amended by DL No. 52-D/90, which highlights the "central bank" function, preparing the Government, with this amendment, for the future dislocation of the BCV, from the commercial aspect. At the end of the year preceding the separation (Dec. 1992) the BCV had accumulated in its balance sheet, in capital and reserves, a value of 1,156 million escudos, that is, 10 times more than it had in these headings in 1976. The number of workers was then around 500 elements (about 10% of senior technicians), distributed between headquarters and a dozen and a half agencies spread throughout the municipalities of the country. By December 1992, through its own efforts combined with the support of the international community, Cape Verde had already managed to overcome the most serious initial constraints and had a nominal GDP of 31 billion escudos, which divided by a population of 450,000 inhabitants, gave a per capita product of more than 800 Usd, that is, about 6 times more than it had in 1975. III. BANCO DE CABO VERDE AS CENTRAL BANK (1993/2007) The dislocation came to fruition through a further amendment of the L.O., introduced by DL No. 42/93 of 16 July. From now on, the attributions of the BCV are limited to those of a central bank, with Article 3 of this DL: "The Bank of Cape Verde is the central bank of the Republic of Cape Verde, and in this capacity must ensure the internal monetary balance and the external stability of the national currency". As a consequence of this change in the L.O., there is the creation of banco Comercial do Atlantico (BCA), which will receive, at the same time, the previous commercial tasks of the BCV, a large part of its assets and facilities, but also the majority of its staff (more than 300 active workers, with the BCV having about 100 assets and 100 pensioners). Four years later, the BCA would be privatized. The main advantage of the separation of functions was a clear definition of the role and responsibilities of each institution operating in the financial system, while safeguarding compliance with the defined rules. It is therefore up to the Central Bank to fully carry out the functions contained in its L.O., including the supervision of all institutions operating in the Cape Verdean financial system. Law No. 10/VI/2002 of 15 July introduces a final amendment to the BCV L.O. to: - Clarify the role of the Bank, which now has as its main attribution the "maintenance of price stability"; - and strengthen the autonomy (independence) of the Bank in relation to political power, by prohibiting state financing, and inamobility, except in exceptional cases, of the Governor and the Administrators. I will dispense with talking about today's BCV, leaving this task to the next players. I will end my speech by saying that bcv remains a small institution, the size of our country, but an institution with great ambition and a great desire to serve, which has contributed to its efforts so that our financial system can, from now on, be up to a Country of Medium Development, a group in which, with a lot of sacrifice, we all managed to put Cape Verde. Thank you very much. Beach 3 Apr 2007
text_original: BANCO DE CABO VERDE  31 ANOS DE EXISTNCIA I. CRIAO DO BANCO DE CABO VERDE (1975/76) Falar da histria do Banco de Cabo Verde  falar tambm da histria econmica de Cabo Verde Independente pela semelhana existente nestes dois percursos.  consensual a ideia de que o poder de emitir moeda (no sentido amplo) constitui um dos principais atributos de um Estado soberano, un droit rgalien como diziam os franceses no tempo da monarquia. Com a assinatura dos acordos firmados com Portugal em 1974 e que desembocaram na constituio de um governo de transio e posteriormente na Independncia de Cabo Verde, teve incio um processo, visando a prazo, a criao de um banco central no nosso pas. Como concretizar este objectivo? Convm voltarmos trs dcadas atrs, para poder imaginar a situao do momento e situarmo-nos no contexto envolvente. Estamos em 1974/75 num pequeno pas insular do Sahel, em vias de aceder  independncia, e sobre o qual paira em permanncia a ameaa da seca, reduzindo a agricultura de subsistncia de sequeiro a uma actividade de alto risco. Trata-se de um pas sem recursos naturais conhecidos, com uma populao avaliada em menos de trs centenas e meia de milhares de habitantes espalhados por 9 ilhas, com pouqussimos quadros residentes e praticamente sem infra-estruturas de qualidade (excluindo o aeroporto do Sal e o Porto Grande de S. Vicente), nem meios de transporte, sem uma base industrial, condenado, pensam muitos, a sobreviver eternamente graas  ajuda externa. O produto por habitante do pas, na altura, nem chegava a 150 dlares, situando Cabo Verde entre os pases mais pobres do mundo. A dvida externa j se apresentava relativamente elevada, devido a alguns investimentos realizados por Portugal na primeira metade da dcada de 70. Se no me engano, o montante das reservas em divisas dava, em Julho de 1975, apenas para garantir escassos dias de importao. De entre os elementos que integravam o departamento das Finanas do Governo de transio, foi indigitado, no incio de 1975, um responsvel para constituir uma equipa encarregue da conduo de todo o processo de criao do referido banco. Este processo teve 3 vertentes principais: 1. Negociao com o Banco Nacional Ultramarino-BNU (e com o Banco de Fomento Nacional  BFN); 2. Preparao dos instrumentos legais necessrios  constituio e entrada em funcionamento do futuro Banco Central; 3. Procura de parcerias para um apoio tcnico qualificado e formao dos quadros que iriam dirigir esse Banco. Negociao com o Banco Nacional Ultramarino BNU Durante 111 anos, ou seja, de 1864 at 1975, o BNU foi o Banco emissor em Cabo Verde, funcionando tambm como banco comercial, com dois estabelecimentos, um na Praia e outro em S. Vicente, uma pequena agncia/balco no Sal e uma rede de correspondentes nas restantes ilhas e concelhos do pas (sobretudo comerciantes). O Banco de Fomento Nacional, que dispunha de uma pequena unidade recentemente aberta na Cidade do Mindelo, ensaiava os primeiros passos no financiamento dos sectores da construo civil (habitao), da pesca e da pequena indstria. O sistema financeiro cabo-verdiano integrava ainda duas pequenas instituies, a Caixa Econmica Postal e a Caixa de Crdito Agrcola que, em 1975, j se encontravam numa situao financeira periclitante. As negociaes com o BNU incidiram, principalmente, sobre as condies de transferncia das actividades do BNU para o Banco de Cabo Verde, em processo de constituio, com destaque para as seguintes aces: - transio do pessoal das agncias do BNU em CV para o futuro banco; - aquisio do activo e do passivo do BNU em CV, incluindo as instalaes; - transferncia dos instrumentos monetrios para o futuro banco central. A parte tcnica das negociaes destas rubricas foi conduzida sem qualquer problema, tendo-se, a 1 de Julho de 1976, realizado, sem sobressaltos, a transferncia para o BCV do passivo e do activo do BNU e do BFN e dado incio s actividades do BCV. Se houve alguma dificuldade neste processo, no temos elementos para o afirmar, mas ter sido de certeza na parte relacionada com a transio do pessoal, tendo um pequeno nmero de empregados do BNU optado por continuar no seu quadro de origem, ou seja, no transitar para o quadro do futuro Banco de Cabo Verde. Instrumentos Legais Decreto Lei n. 25/75 de 29/09 O Banco de Cabo Verde foi criado, formalmente, pelo DL n. 25/75 de 29 de Setembro, tendo sido nomeado na mesma data o seu primeiro Governador, um jovem quadro de 29 anos, formado em Finanas Pblicas em Portugal e com apenas 5 ou 6 anos de experincia profissional na altura. De Setembro de 75 a Junho de 76, vai ser dado um grande impulso na preparao da estruturao e implementao efectiva do BCV, em primeiro lugar graas ao Recrutamento de um pequeno ncleo duro, de tcnicos superiores (4, incluindo o Governador) que, com o apoio valioso de alguns quadros cabo-verdianos do BNU, vo lanar, num prazo relativamente curto, os alicerces do futuro banco central. A estes 4 tcnicos superiores so atribudas responsabilidades especficas na preparao de importantes processos: - Primeira Lei Orgnica do Banco; - gesto das divisas e controlo de cmbios; - relaes com instituies financeiras internacionais; - organizao e gesto do crdito  economia; - estatsticas e estudos econmicos. Sob o controlo do Governador, foram incumbidos os quadros mais experientes do BNU dos aspectos ligados a: - gesto da vertente banco comercial; - preparao da primeira emisso de notas e moedas; - organizao da tesouraria e da contabilidade; - organizao e gesto da administrao e pessoal. Deciso com fora de Lei n. 13/76 de 26 de Junho A par do DL acima referido, o principal instrumento jurdico do processo de criao do Banco , sem dvida, a Deciso com fora de Lei n. 13/76 de 26 de Junho que aprova a 1. Lei Orgnica do Banco de Cabo Verde. Permitam-me citar 4 artigos desta L.O. que do uma pequena ideia dos importantes poderes que o primeiro Governo da Repblica de Cabo Verde entendeu por bem atribuir ao Banco de Cabo Verde. Art. 4. O Banco tem por objecto o exerccio das funes de banco central, de exclusivo emissor, no territrio nacional, de notas e moedas, de caixa do tesouro e banco comercial. Art. 5. O Banco tem por misso geral, em conformidade com a poltica econmica do Governo, estabelecer no domnio da moeda, do crdito e dos cmbios, as condies mais favorveis para o desenvolvimento equilibrado da economia nacional, contribuindo para o aproveitamento de todos os recursos produtivos do Pais e assegurar a estabilidade interna e externa da moeda. Art. 6. O Banco dispor dos seguintes recursos: a) O patrimnio e os valores dos departamentos de Cabo Verde do Banco Nacional Ultramarino e do Banco de Fomento Nacional que vierem a ser transferidos para o banco e nele integrados ao abrigo e por fora dos acordos celebrados entre a Repblica de Cabo Verde e a Repblica Portuguesa em 15 de Abril de 1976; Art. 11. Como banco central, o banco ser o banqueiro do Estado, consultor do governo no domnio financeiro, orientador e controlador da poltica monetria e de crdito, gestor das disponibilidades externas do pas e intermedirio nas relaes monetrias internacionais. Assistncia Tcnica para o desenvolvimento deste projecto O desenvolvimento de um projecto to complexo, com os parcos meios de que se dispunha, poderia ter sido muito mais difcil e moroso, sem a colaborao dos bancos centrais de alguns pases amigos. Neste sentido, e convm que seja aqui reconhecido, a maior assistncia obtida, na criao do Banco de Cabo Verde, foi proporcionada, sem margem para dvida, pelo Banco Central da Arglia atravs de: - apoio tcnico aos responsveis do BCV nas negociaes com o BNU; - formao de curta ou longa durao dos primeiros tcnicos do banco em todas as vertentes da competncia de um banco central; - apoio na elaborao, encomenda e acompanhamento da produo das primeiras notas emitidas pelo BCV; - assistncia na organizao de determinados servios. II. EVOLUO DO BANCO DE CABO VERDE ENQUANTO BANCO UNIVERSAL (1976/1993) Criado um ano antes, o BCV vai desenvolver as suas aces, de forma plena, a partir de Setembro de 1976, com a cessao das actividades do BNU em Cabo Verde. Arrancou o BCV com um pequeno capital de 100 milhes de escudos e com um quadro de pessoal (aps integrao dos trabalhadores do BNU) de menos de 150 elementos, entre os quais apenas 4 tcnicos superiores. Durante cerca de 16 anos o banco vai registar uma interessante evoluo e um rpido crescimento das suas actividades. A 1 de Julho de 1977 regista-se o lanamento das primeiras notas do BCV e, consequentemente, a recolha da ltima emisso do BNU. Foi uma operao complexa mas muito bem conduzida e que beneficiou do apoio entusistico de boa parte dos agentes da funo pblica, sobretudo no interior de Santiago e das ilhas maiores. O contributo dos trabalhadores do BCV neste processo foi admirvel. As notas emitidas pelo BCV foram feitas ainda com uma paridade idntica  do escudo portugus. Pouco tempo depois deixou de existir esta paridade, devido  forte desvalorizao da moeda portuguesa, no acompanhada pela do escudo de Cabo Verde, que passou a valer mais do que o escudo portugus, com algumas implicaes no desejadas junto  nossa emigrao em Portugal, que via reduzir assim o valor das suas remessas para Cabo Verde. Nos primeiros anos da independncia, Cabo Verde, pelo intermdio do BCV, vai negociar e conseguir a sua adeso ao Banco Africano de Desenvolvimento (BAD), em 1976, ao Fundo Monetrio Internacional (FMI) e ao grupo do Banco Mundial (BIRD/IDA/SFI), em 1978, beneficiando o BCV a partir da duma assistncia tcnica de qualidade, proporcionada sobretudo pelas instituies de Bretton Woods (FMI e Banco Mundial). No BCV, a dcada de 80 foi marcada pelos seguintes acontecimentos: - Reforo do quadro de pessoal com o recrutamento acelerado de tcnicos superiores; - aumento do capital do BCV, em 1981, de 100 milhes de escudos para 400 milhes de escudos; - aprovao do estatuto de pessoal, o que constitua uma grande reivindicao dos trabalhadores, sobretudo aqueles que transitaram do BNU; - realizao de avultados investimentos na construo de agncias do BCV em todos os Concelhos do pas e na construo de instalaes especiais na Ilha do Sal; - informatizao dos principais servios do Banco; - criao das contas especiais de emigrantes, com taxas de juro bonificadas, para incentivar as remessas dos cabo-verdianos da dispora e aplicao das mesmas no pas sob forma de poupana e investimento; - constituio de um departamento de investimentos para dinamizar o financiamento de emprstimos de mdio e longo prazos nos principais sectores da economia. Em 1990  alterada a Lei Orgnica do BCV pelo DL n. 52-D/90, que vem dar maior destaque  funo banco central, preparando o Governo, com esta alterao, a futura desafectao do BCV, da vertente comercial. No final do exerccio que precedeu a separao (Dez. 1992) o BCV tinha acumulado no seu balano, em capital e reservas, um valor de 1.156 milhes de escudos, ou seja, 10 vezes mais do que dispunha nestas rubricas em 1976. O nmero de trabalhadores rondava ento os 500 elementos (cerca de 10% de tcnicos superiores), distribudos entre a Sede e uma dezena e meia de agncias espalhadas por todos os Concelhos do pas. Em Dezembro de 1992, mediante esforos prprios conjugados com o apoio da comunidade internacional, Cabo Verde j tinha conseguido ultrapassar os constrangimentos iniciais mais graves e apresentava um PIB nominal de 31 mil milhes de escudos, o que dividido por uma populao de 450 mil habitantes, dava um produto per capita de mais de 800 Usd, ou seja, cerca de 6 vezes mais do que possua em 1975. III. O BANCO DE CABO VERDE ENQUANTO BANCO CENTRAL (1993/2007) A desafectao veio a concretizar-se mediante uma nova alterao da L.O., introduzida pelo DL n. 42/93 de 16 de Julho. Doravante, limitam-se as atribuies do BCV s de um banco central, dispondo o art. 3. deste DL o seguinte: O Banco de Cabo Verde  o banco central da Repblica de Cabo Verde, devendo nessa qualidade assegurar o equilbrio monetrio interno e a estabilidade externa da moeda nacional. Como consequncia desta alterao da L.O., assiste-se  criao do Banco Comercial do Atlntico (BCA) que vai receber, em simultneo, as atribuies comerciais anteriores do BCV, uma grande parte do seu patrimnio e instalaes, mas tambm a maioria do seu pessoal (mais de 300 trabalhadores no activo, tendo o BCV ficado com cerca de 100 activos e 100 reformados). Quatro anos depois viria o BCA a ser privatizado. A separao das funes teve por vantagem principal uma clara definio do papel e das responsabilidades de cada instituio que opera no sistema financeiro, salvaguardando o respeito das regras definidas. Cabe assim ao Banco Central exercer plenamente as funes constantes da sua L.O., entre as quais se insere a superviso de todas as instituies que operam no sistema financeiro cabo-verdiano. A Lei n. 10/VI/2002 de 15 de Julho vem introduzir uma derradeira alterao  L.O. do BCV no sentido de: - Clarificar o papel do Banco que passa a ter como atribuio principal a manuteno da estabilidade dos preos; - e reforar a autonomia (independncia) do Banco em relao ao poder poltico, mediante interdio do financiamento do Estado, e inamobilidade, salvo casos excepcionais, do Governador e dos Administradores. Dispensarei falar do BCV de hoje, deixando esta tarefa para os prximos intervenientes. Terminarei a minha interveno dizendo que continua sendo o BCV uma pequena instituio, da dimenso do nosso pas, mas uma instituio com muita ambio e uma grande vontade de servir, que tem contribudo com os seus esforos para que o nosso sistema financeiro possa, desde j, estar  altura de um Pas de Desenvolvimento Mdio, grupo no qual, com muito sacrifcio, conseguimos todos colocar Cabo Verde. Muito obrigado. Praia 3 Abr. 2007

Title: SPEECH GOV Opening IX Forum SITI
text: INTERVENTION OF THE GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF CAPE VERDE, DR. CARLOS BURGO, AT THE OPENING SESSION OF THE IX FORUM OF INFORMATION SYSTEMS AND TECHNOLOGIES Mindelo, May 16, 2007 Dear Participants to the IX Frum of Information Systems and Technologies, Ladies and gentlemen, As is already becoming traditional, the realization of this Frum represents a high moment for the exchange of information and experience among central banks, faced with all the challenges posed by the increasing use of new information technologies and consequent need for reconfiguration of financial systems. Given that technology is also a determining factor in accelerating the globalisation of markets and systems, increased cooperation will bring, without due life, benefits. Information technologies are considered one of the main drivers of changes in banking activity, enabling wider access to financial services, the quality of which must necessarily increase. If, on the one hand, technological developments give banks immense advantages, ranging from reducing transaction costs, expanding information processing and improving risk management tools, on the other hand, it poses the same enormous strategic challenges arising from the need to make appropriate decisions in the long term. The extension of new technologies to banking clearly increases the complexity of the internal control function and the need to services with a high level of safety and quality. The security objectives will have to take into account the full reliability and technical safety of the systems and the necessary confidence of the agents in those systems. The choice of new technologies also has implications for banking supervision, as the speed and complexity of technological developments require banking supervisors to face the need to improve their knowledge and technical skills and improve the tools used in this specific area. The central bank's perspective should be to support the banking sector in particular, but also the economy as a whole, creating a condition for a functional and stable payment system. It is clear, then, that it is responsible for adopting the most modern information technologies, under penalty of the competitiveness of the sector being called into question, with negative consequences for the efficiency of monetary policy itself and financial stability. Central banks should maintain an interbank payment system that provides the most efficient services using new technologies. This will be one of the main reasons why it is necessary to strengthen the areas of information systems and technologies in central banks. Their responsibility extends, in fact, beyond the mere technological support to the systems, in order also to cover the conical functions that these systems perform. If, on the one hand, the impacts of technological changes on the structure of the real economy influence the conduct of monetary policy, on the other hand, its implications in terms of payment systems will affect the efficiency of that policy without due knowledge. More practical questions also arise, related to the routine market operations carried out by central banks. For all this, the great importance of the progress that takes place in the field of information technologies is unquestionable for our institutions. Ladies and gentlemen, Technological innovations increase the weight in the economic activity of intangible goods and services - knowledge and information - which are variables difficult to measure in statistical terms. As a result, central banks, which rely on indicators to outline their monetary policy, will face greater difficulties in selecting and interpreting these types of economic indicators from this point of view. The implications of this are much deeper, since it is not easy to deform and transform the value of this type of goods in terms of prices, it will be difficult to define what is now the primary objective of central banks  price stability. For these and other reasons, rapid technological progress will increase uncertainties about the assessment of the economic situation and price changes and, as a result, the implementation of monetary policy. In this respect, theories have diverged as to the best solution to be adopted in such a context  if more conservative players advise that monetary authorities take a prudent, wait-and-see stance, making, for example, minor changes in interest rates, others suggest, on the contrary, a more aggressive stance of central banks in times of uncertainty. But the challenges are not only of an economic and financial nature. They also come from the purely technical aspect, considering that payment systems increasingly rely on physical information media, such as networks and communication systems. Any failure, caused by purely technical problems (problems with hardware, software, or the telecommunications network), may trigger a chain reaction of payment system failures and cause serious financial problems. Central banks will therefore have to be properly prepared to take appropriate measures to deal with such situations and prevent a simple technical problem from causing disruption throughout the financial system. It is in this sense that the precautions that have been taken by central banks are included, which have been preparing back-up and replication systems. Having the responsibility to assess the risks that the banking sector is taking on, central banks should be familiar with new technologies in order to take advantage of the benefits they provide in terms of cost reduction and the time required to collect information. Given that financial markets are increasingly integrated and globalised, the issues that arise with technological progress are increasingly global and not sas of a country taken individually. I believe, therefore, that in this frum, and in others that will certainly follow, as well as in the actions that are developing, our institutions will continue, in a shared way, to focus on the exploitation of information technology resources, in order to obtain additional improvements, in particular in the process of managing internal information. The adoption of common priests must also be addressed, as the emergence of a safe and efficient technological infrastructure entails enormous challenges that partnerships can help overcome. A fruitful work and an excellent stay in Cape Verde is as much as everyone wishes. Thank you very much!

Neste aspecto, as teorias tm divergido quanto  melhor soluo a adoptar num tal contexto  se tericos mais conservadores aconselham a que as autoridades monetrias tenham uma postura prudente, do tipo esperar para ver, fazendo, por exemplo, pequenas alteraes nas taxas de juro, outros h que, pelo contrrio, sugerem uma postura mais agressiva dos bancos centrais em tempos de incerteza. Mas os desafios no so apenas de natureza econmica e financeira. Vm tambm da vertente puramente tcnica, considerando que os sistemas de pagamento dependem cada vez mais de suportes de informao fsicos, como as redes e os sistemas de comunicao. Qualquer falha, causada por problemas meramente tcnicos (problemas com o hardware, com o software ou com a rede de telecomunicaes), poder despoletar uma reaco em cadeia de falhas no sistema de pagamentos e provocar srios problemas financeiros. Assim, os bancos centrais tero de estar convenientemente preparados para tomar as medidas adequadas para fazer face a esse tipo de situaes e evitar que um simples problema tcnico provoque perturbaes em todo o sistema financeiro.  neste sentido que se inserem as precaues que vm sendo tomadas pelos bancos centrais, que vm nomeadamente preparando sistemas de back-up e de replicao. Tendo a responsabilidade de avaliar os riscos que o sector bancrio vai assumindo, os bancos centrais devem estar familiarizados com as novas tecnologias, de modo a tirar proveito das vantagens que elas proporcionam em termos de reduo de custos e do tempo necessrio  recolha de informao. Tendo em conta que os mercados financeiros se encontram cada vez mais integrados e globalizados, as questes que se levantam com o progresso tecnolgico so cada vez mais questes globais e no sas de um pas tomado individualmente. Acredito, pois, que neste frum, e em outros que certamente se seguiro, bem como nas aces que se vo desenvolvendo, as nossas Instituies continuaro, de forma partilhada, a apostar na explorao dos recursos das tecnologias de informao, visando obter melhorias adicionais, nomeadamente no processo de gesto da informao interna. Title: Speech of the Governor of the BCV
text: Intervention of the Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde at the Opening of the Hearing by the Commission Permanent Specialist in Finance and Budget of the National Assembly May 17, 2007 1. First of all, I would like to point out that I am very pleased to hold this hearing, which is part of the good practices that are now cultivated for accountability to society, by public institutions which, like the Bank of Cape Verde, enjoy autonomy, but therefore must guide all their action on principles of transparency and credibility. 2. On the national economic activity, it should be noted that it has evolved positively in the last six months, to attest by the different quantitative indicators of conjuncture that measure the evolution of the main components of expenditure. This is corroborated by the feeling of the economic agents of the main sectors of economic activity, measured by the economic climate indicator, which has shown an ever-increasing evolution. There was, however, a slight slowdown in the first quarter of the year. 3. A significant external demand, which is certainly not foreign to the economic stability in the country, has contributed to an increasing volume of foreign direct investment and a significant growth in net exports of services (particularly services related to travel and air transport). This resulted in a good balance of payments performance and a significant strengthening of the country's international reserves, which in March exceeded EUR 200 million. 4. As far as inflation is concerned, it remains  if the bullish trend in prices, with the average change reaching 5.3 % in April. This behaviour of the inflation rate continues to be determined by changes in prices and tariffs administered, but also by the price developments of certain products of the goods component, in particular "processed food" and "industrial". As for the services component, there is a decrease in prices, in particular international telephone crossings, international telephone communication tariffs and public transport fares. 5. The monetary situation, in the six months ending in March 2007, was determined by the positive evolution of the external position of the Cape Verdean economy, translated into the accumulation of external reserves of the central bank, which, in a fixed parity exchange rate regime, ultimately determines the expansion of the monetary mass. 6. In a framework for the defense of the fixed parity exchange regime, and with the end of the maintenance of price stability, the conduct of monetary policy by the Central Bank was based on the use of the instruments it has, in order to effectively manage the liquidity existing in the banking system, taking into account the high price pressures in the economy. In this way, the Bank of Cape Verde has resorted, inter alia, to the active issue of Monetary Intervention Securities, intended to absorb part of the excess liquidity in the banking system. 7. With regard to the main monetary aggregates, there is also a stable behavior of Net Internal Credit, explained, on the one hand, by the evolution of Net Credit to the Pblico Sector, which has been decreasing, and, on the other hand, by the resumption of credit activity with the national banking system. 8. For 2007, bcv projections for the pace of economic activity, taking into account recent information, point to a growth of the product in the range of 6 -7 %. This projection of the BCV reflects the prospects for increased consumption and expansion of investment, especially foreign direct investment directed to the tourism sector, but also to public investment in infrastructure. 9. For inflation, the BCV projection points to a slowdown in prices, with the average annual rate in the range of 2.5 to 3.5%. This projection includes the downward trend of CPI, which in April reached 3.5% in terms of the homlog variation, but takes into account the risk of updating the prices of managed goods and effects arising from any bad agricultural year on unprocessed goods, the most volatile component of CPI. 10. In the monetary field, in the near future, policy orientation will continue to be the monitoring of developments in external reserves and the management of the gap between euro area interest rates, in particular those of euribor, and rates of BCV intervention operations, in a context of rising rates on international markets. 11. The Financial System, as a fundamental pillar of the national economic financial fabric, will continue to deserve full attention, with a view to strengthening its operating structure and ensuring its stability. Thus, the BCV will continue to develop initiatives aimed at establishing institutional regulatory and supervisory conditions, in particular the emergency securities market and international financial institutions, in accordance with international best practices. Recent developments in IFIs institutions in Cape Verde recommend that mechanisms be put in use to protect the system against the potential use of national institutions in illegal financial practices which can contribute to denigrating the reputation of the Cape Verdean jurisdiction and thus its integration into the international financial system. 12. In the long term, the acceleration of the pace of economic growth poses major challenges for Cape Verdean society. At first, we can greatly increase the positive impact of tourism, in terms of jobs and wealth creation, through the diversification and improvement of our offer of goods and services to the growing number of tourists who flock to our country. Secondly, and with a view to reducing the vulnerability of the economy and ensuring the sustainability of growth, we must aim to create standards for the provision of services in other areas. 13. In addition to improving infrastructure and modernising the legal and institutional framework, achieving these objectives also requires a broad and targeted effort to train human resources. In an economic regime based on fixed parity with the euro, this is the only way to ensure the competitiveness necessary for successful integration into the international economy. 14. The effort to consolidate the pblicas finances, an indispensable condition of macro-economic stability, should be continued. Risks arising from the rapid growth of expenditure on the functioning of the State, both centrally and locally, of responsibilities with think systems or management of public enterprises cannot be ignored. 15. Finally, I would like to mention, among the challenges facing us, the very development of the financial system. In order to be able to grow faster, the economy requires more financial intermediation, with new financial institutions and services more sophisticated and appropriate to needs. Moreover, the provision of financial services to non-residents is a way to continue in the search for diversification of the economy.
text_original: Interveno do Governador do Banco de Cabo Verde na Abertura da Audio pela Comisso Especializada Permanente de Finanas e Oramento da Assembleia Nacional 17 de Maio de 2007 1. Antes de mais gostaria de realar que muito me apraz a realizao desta audio, que se enquadra nas boas prticas hoje cultivadas de prestao de contas  sociedade, por parte de instituies pblicas que, como o Banco de Cabo Verde, gozam de autonomia, mas, por isso mesmo, devem pautar toda a sua actuao por princpios de transparncia e credibilidade. 2. Sobre a actividade econmica nacional, de referir que evoluiu positivamente nos ltimos seis meses, a atestar pelos diferentes indicadores quantitativos de conjuntura que medem a evoluo das principais componentes da despesa. Este facto  corroborado pelo sentimento dos agentes econmicos dos principais sectores de actividade econmica, medido pelo indicador de clima econmico, que tem apresentado uma evoluo sempre crescente. Registou-se, no entanto, um ligeiro abrandamento neste 1 trimestre do ano. 3. Uma assinalvel procura externa, a que no  certamente estranha a estabilidade econmica que se vive no pas, tem contribudo para um volume crescente de investimento directo estrangeiro e um crescimento expressivo das exportaes lquidas de servios (particularmente dos servios ligados a viagens por motivo de turismo e aos transportes areos). Disso resultou um bom desempenho da balana de pagamentos e um reforo significativo das reservas internacionais do pas que, em Maro, ultrapassaram os 200 milhes de euros. 4. No que diz respeito  inflao, mantm  se a tendncia altista dos preos, com a variao mdia a atingir em Abril 5,3 %. Este comportamento da taxa de inflao continua a ser determinado pelas alteraes dos preos e tarifas administrados, mas tambm pela evoluo de preos de determinados produtos da componente bens, em especial os alimentares transformados e os industriais. Quanto  componente servios, registase um decrscimo dos preos, designadamente das passagens reas internacionais, das tarifas de comunicao telefnica internacional e das tarifas de transporte pblico. 5. A situao monetria, nos seis meses terminados em Maro de 2007, foi determinada pela evoluo positiva da posio externa da economia caboverdiana, traduzida na acumulao de reservas externas do banco central, o que, num regime cambial de paridade fixa, acaba por determinar a expanso da massa monetria. 6. Num quadro de defesa do regime cambial de paridade fixa, e tendo como fim ltimo a manuteno da estabilidade de preos, a conduo da poltica monetria por parte do Banco Central pautou-se pelo recurso aos instrumentos que possui, no sentido de uma gesto eficaz da liquidez existente no sistema bancrio, tendo em conta as presses altistas dos preos na economia. Deste modo, o Banco de Cabo Verde tem recorrido, nomeadamente,  emisso activa de Ttulos de Interveno Monetria, destinados  absoro de uma parte do excesso de liquidez existente no sistema bancrio. 7. No que tange aos principais agregados monetrios destaca-se ainda um comportamento estvel do Crdito Interno Lquido, explicado, por um lado, pela evoluo do Crdito Lquido ao Sector Pblico, que vem diminuindo, e, por outro, pela retoma da actividade creditcia junto do sistema bancrio nacional. 8. Para 2007, as projeces do BCV para o ritmo de actividade econmica, tendo em conta as informaes recentes, apontam para um crescimento do produto no intervalo de 6 -7 %. Esta projeco do BCV espelha as perspectivas de aumento do consumo e de expanso do investimento, sobretudo, o investimento directo estrangeiro direccionado para o sector do turismo, mas tambm do investimento pblico em infra-estruturas. 9. Para a inflao, a projeco do BCV aponta para uma desacelerao dos preos, situando a taxa mdia anual no intervalo de 2.5 a 3.5%. Esta projeco contempla a tendncia descendente do IPC que, em Abril, atingiu os 3.5% em termos de variao homloga, mas leva em conta o risco de actualizao dos preos dos bens administrados e efeitos decorrentes de eventual mau ano agrcola sobre os bens no transformados, componente mais voltil do IPC. 10. No campo monetrio, no futuro prximo, a orientao da poltica continuar a ser a monitorizao da evoluo das reservas externas e a gesto do diferencial entre as taxas de juro da zona euro, em particular as do Euribor, e as taxas das operaes de interveno do BCV, num contexto de subida das taxas nos mercados internacionais. 11. O Sistema Financeiro, enquanto pilar fundamental do tecido econmicofinanceiro nacional, continuar a merecer toda a ateno, com vista a se fortalecer a sua estrutura de funcionamento e garantir a sua estabilidade. Assim, o BCV continuar a desenvolver iniciativas orientadas para a criao de condies de regulao e superviso institucional, em particular do mercado de valores mobilirios em emergncia e das Instituies Financeiras Internacionais, de acordo com as melhores prticas internacionais. A evoluo recente das instituies IFIs em Cabo Verde recomenda que sejam criados mecanismos que protejam o sistema contra potencial utilizao de instituies nacionais em prticas financeiras ilegais que possam contribuir para denegrir a reputao da jurisdio caboverdiana e assim pr em causa a sua integrao no sistema financeiro internacional. 12. A prazo, a acelerao do ritmo de crescimento da economia coloca  sociedade cabo-verdiana desafios de monta. Num primeiro momento, podemos aumentar grandemente o impacto positivo do turismo, em termos de empregos e de criao de riqueza, atravs da diversificao e melhoria da nossa oferta de bens e servios ao nmero crescente de turistas que afluem ao nosso pas. Num segundo momento, e com vista a reduzir a vulnerabilidade da economia e garantir a sustentabilidade do crescimento, devemos ter como objectivo a criao de condies para a prestao de servios noutras reas. 13. Alm da melhoria das infra-estruturas e da modernizao do quadro legal e institucional, a realizao destes objectivos requer ainda um esforo amplo e orientado de formao dos recursos humanos. Num regime econmico assente na paridade fixa com o euro, essa  a nica via para a garantia da competitividade necessria  insero com sucesso na economia internacional. 14. Deve ser prosseguido o esforo de consolidao das finanas pblicas, condio indispensvel da estabilidade macro-econmica. text: Intervencao do Governador Page 1 of 2 Speech by S.E. The Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde, Dr. Carlos Augusto de Burgo, in the Act Fortheenoting of the Training Workshop on Operational Techniques in the field of Asset Recovery, Combating Money Laundering and Corruption Beach, May 23, 2007 Mr. Minister of Justice Distinguished Guests My Ladies and Gentlemen I am pleased to be here today to participate in the closing of this Atelier on Operational Techniques of Asset Recovery, Fight against Money Laundering and Corruption. For the BCV this is an important and topical issue, considering the negative impact of such practices on the proper functioning and development of the financial system. The proper functioning of the financial system, in particular its effective regulation and supervision, is guided by a number of priority objectives, namely: -Protection of investors, particularly those who have greater difficulty in defend their rights and interests; -Efficiency and regularity in the functioning of markets; -Quality control of financial information; -Risk prevention; -Prevention and repression of illegal or fraudulent acts. It is in this context that the Central Bank's concern is with the problem of money laundering and the resulting actions. Money laundering is likely to seriously damage the financial system as it largely affects the credibility of the financial system  its most precious asset, given the fact that it handles other people's money. Therefore, money laundering can undermine our country's aspirations to become an international financial market as large investors and legitimate operators tend to move away from centres of dubious reputation, fearing that, by association, their reputation will be adversely affected. Hence the need to avoid the attraction of "dirty money" that can immediately propel the start-up of our international financial centre but in the long run to scare away the flow of lawful capital that contributeto sustained long-term growth. Being responsible for the supervision of all institutions covered by the Law on money laundering, except the Cape Verde Post Office, the BCV has been since the first hour in the first line of combating the practice of money laundering. In this context, the BCV supervises compliance with that Law by those institutions, in particular through remote supervision and on-the-spot inspections. To this end, the Bank has provided and continues to provide training opportunities for the area's staff, in particular with regard to the supervision of international financial institutions and specialised financial instruments, which, by their nature and financial dimension, are more easily provided to the activity of money laundering. In addition, the Bank has been collaborating in the evaluation of the national anti-money laundering system, including the recent evaluation mission carried out by experts from the International Monetary Fund. The preliminary recommendations of that mission, in particular 15-09-2010 Intervencao do Governador Page 2 of 2 with regard to the revision of the law on money laundering and the creation of a Financial Information Unit (FIU) auspicious the continued role of the BCV in the process of improving this system. At the same time, various ongoing and/or scheduled structuring activities in other core areas of bcv's activity  the development of the payment system, the development of supervision of financial institutions, improved liquidity management and even the monitoring of the economy as a whole  will certainly contribute to strengthening the Bank's overall action and thus to the development and credibility of the national financial system; therefore the design of these actions will necessarily have to take into account the problem of money laundering, which is unavoidable today because of their size and impact on the financial system. The fight against corruption is another area in which the BCV also collaborates, albeit less directly. By promoting good practices in financial reporting and the conduct of business in general, the Bank has been collaborating to root an eco-financial culture in line with internationally accepted best practices. We highlight here, for example, the process of adoption of the International Financial Reporting Standards, a project budgeted at about 60,000 contos and which aims to adapt the Central Bank and the supervised institutions to international standards in this area, thus contributing to greater clarity and reliability of the financial information produced in the system. Another illustrative action is a Seminar on Ethics and Transparency in financial and business systems, to be held in the first month of June. It is a privilege for us to have had among n experts representing the most advanced and credible systems in the areas dealt with during this seminar. We believe that the approach used, in particular the analysis of emblematic illustrative cases of these practices, has greatly contributed to the awareness and empowerment of our institutions and our staff who face these scourges more directly, in particular that of money laundering. We count on your support to continue to meet this challenge that affects all our countries, peoples and economies. On the part of the Central Bank, we reiterate our full openness and willingness to continue collaborating in the areas treated in this Atelier, whether by providing the use of our staff, our systems and our instruments, or also contributing to the financing of the activities that are necessary for the strengthening and development of the system. We end by congratulating and thanking S.E. the Minister of Justice for the political conduct of this important and timely event and to all the participants who made it possible in practice. I fervently hope for success in your steamy tasks. To those who have had to travel from abroad or from other islands to be here with us, I hope you will have a safe and pleasant journey home. 15-09-2010

text: Speech by S.E. The Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde, Dr. Carlos Augusto de B... Page 1 of 2 Speech by S.E. The Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde, Dr. Carlos Augusto de Burgo, in the release of the new 1000 notes Mindelo, 25 September 2007 Distinguished Guests My Ladies and Gentlemen It is a privilege and an honor for me to preside over this act of launching the new banknotes of a thousand escudos, on the eve of an important milestone in the histia of the Bank of Cape Verde  the passage of the thirty-second anniversary of its creation. With the responsibility of ensuring the necessary conditions for the development of the financial sector, the Bank of Cape Verde is committed to deepening the reforms already initiated, in particular towards the modernization of the Cape Verdean payment system, an important element of the financial context and the implementation of monetary policy. The aim is to build a safe and efficient INFRASTRUCTURE that facilitates monetary circulation and safely manage the risks inherent in the financial framework. The ability to make payments efficiently and securely is therefore indispensable to the proper functioning of the financial sector and to the efficiency in transactions and resource allocation, facilitating growth and improving overall well-being. Considering its systemic importance, the reform of the payment system therefore aims to maintain its stability, promote its efficiency and mitigate risks in the financial system and, consequently, in the economy. This is how, in accordance with its statutory responsibility to ensure the proper functioning of the overall financial framework and aware of the relevance of the issue, the Board of Directors of the Bank of Cape Verde has just adopted a set of regulations which, by adjusting existing standards and practices to international standards and standards in the field of interbank clearing and settlement automation, as well as in the telecompensation of cheques, it represents an advance towards the establishment of a safe and efficient framework. However, we are aware that the challenges to the emergence of a secure and efficient payment system remain great. Dear Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, Despite the growing importance that alternative means of payment to paper money have been taken, this remains a fundamental instrument in the ecological life of our country, considering its function of allowing the exchange of goods and services to be done more efficiently. The wide use of this instrument requires that it be reviewed with characteristics such as quality, safety, availability, in a framework of stability and confidence in the system. As a continuation of a process of renewal of banknotes initiated in 1999, the entry into circulation of this new 1000 banknote will enable the objective of the development of this instrument to be addressed, in order to increase its effectiveness and safety, with the incorporation of modern graphic and technolic elements, which facilitate the identification of its authenticity and hinder its counterfeiting, referred to herein by the Director of the Department of Payment Systems. We wanted, with the realization of this cerimia on this island and on this date, to pay another tribute to this eminent writer, who today would be one hundred and six years old. In fact, this is not the first time that the Bank of Cape Verde has been recognizing such an illustrious personality.
