Title: Speech at the Opening Ceremony of the ASEL Meeting
text: BCV Governor's speech at the ASEL Meeting 1 of 2 Opening Ceremony Madam Minister of Finance and Administration Pblica Exmos Lords Administrators of the Bank of Cape Verde Ladies and Gentlemen Distinguished Guests Of ASEL Ladies and Gentlemen Let me first of all welcome all present and, in particular, to the members of ASEL  Association of Lusfonos Insurance Supervisors  and to the representative of the International Association of Insurance Supervisors, and to say that it was with great pleasure and high honor that the Bank of Cape Verde took responsibility for organizing the XI Conference and the IV General Assembly of ASEL. The changes that are being made in the financial system and, in particular, in the insurance sector in Cape Verde, but also globally, will certainly entail a profound reformulation of the way in which the insurance business is managed and supervised. In addition to the establishment of appropriate incentives, appropriate prudential and supervisory systems are an indispensable condition for the development of the insurance business in a framework of financial stability. The great challenge of today's insurance management, mainly oriented towards risk management, requires the restructuring of the system and the adoption of more competitive and transparent practices, aiming at promoting operational efficiency. Consistent, secure and transparent methodologies are an important element in ensuring financial stability and increasing market confidence in the insurance sector. As a regulatory and supervisory authority, the Bank of Cape Verde must be able to assume its responsibilities and adapt to the developments that are taking place, and it should continue to contribute to the development of new opportunities for the insurance market in the context of creating a stable and healthy financial environment, confidence to consumers and the economy. Within a framework of internationalization of the financial system, with challenges and opportunities emerging for the insurance sector, the reformulation of the legal and regulatory environment is imposed, aiming to adopt international best practices, in the interest of all those involved  policyholders, beneficiaries and other participants. It is therefore, in view of the imperative of the soundness of the financial system, and in view of the environment of changes and increased demands faced by the insurance sector, with the need for efficient supervisory and regulatory practices, that a new legislative package is proposed today, which will be presented here today. Increasing competitiveness and dynamism is vital for the survival of a sector facing enormous challenges in the face of the increasing globalisation of the financial system. Its growing vitality and the role it plays in the development of the whole system calls for supervision with greater rationality, dynamism and flexibility, thus being able to adapt to market developments and respond effectively to the requirements of the insurance business. In this context, and finally, I would like to express my wish that this event will serve to stimulate the debate on the issues that are emerging for the future of the insurance market  globalisation, economic uncertainty, development of new markets and financial innovation, among others. All this requires that we seek to find the best solutions, to develop new and consistent priests, in the framework of greater openness, greater dialogue and collaboration. This requires the new reality and the new challenges, which therefore call for greater articulation and cooperation between the authorities of 15-09-2010 Speech of the Governor of the BCV at the Opening Ceremony of the ASEL Meeting Page 2 of 2 supervision, in a context of increasing integration of financial markets. May this be another opportunity for exchange and exchange of knowledge and experience. With these brief words, I am honoured to give the floor to His Excellency the Minister of Finance and The Pblica Administration, who will deliver the opening speech of this event. Thank you very much! 15-09-2010

Title: Prospects for the National Financial System
text: Prospects for the National Financial System 2008 (Communication by Governor Carlos Burgo to the Financial Square Program) January 9, 2008 In a context marked by growing opportunities and challenges at international level, particularly those related to tourism, foreign investment and international financial transactions, and the resulting momentum and optimism about the growth prospects of the national economy, in 2008 the financial system will be called upon to play an increasingly important role in the "service-oriented" economy that is imposed on Cape Verde. The year 2008 presents with important and good prospects with regard to the development of the national financial system. As a result of the growing macro-economic stability in recent years and more recent initiatives in the definition of the main lines of development of the system, there are now conditions that allow a quantitative and qualitative leap of the system as a mobilising of savings and its channeling for investment. As a result of several relevant factors and the implementation of ongoing or portfolio initiatives, in the course of 2008 Cape Verde will have a more competitive financial system; better integrated into the international financial system; and more accessible to disadvantaged sectors of the economy and society. (i) A more competitive financial system In the process of improvements already made in the re-structuring of the financial system, and with a view to contributing to its diversification and deepening, the framework of financial activity will undergo a review process in order to facilitate the exercise of certain specialised financial activities and facilitate the introduction of certain new institutional typologies and specific activities more appropriate to our reality current. In the field of new institutional typologies, the legal conditions necessary for the emergence of holding companies and managers of social holding stakes (SGPS) and variable capital investment companies (SICAV), a relatively informal collective investment vehicle but capable of international investment operations, will be created. Another innovation will be the introduction of the Regime of Financial Credit Institutions (IFIC), allowing the practice of all operations allowed to banks, with the exception of the reception of depsitos of the pblico. On the other hand, the Collective Investment Organisations (ICO) scheme should become more competitive in terms of requirements for constitution and management, as well as the introduction of new categories of OICs. Another area that is already and will continue to make significant advances is the insurance activity. As a result of the current review effort in the sector, the main areas of this field of activity will be adequately regulated and the activity as a whole will be better tuned to the other components of the financial system. The process includes the review, updating and creation of legislation in the most diverse areas related to insurance activity, with a view to improving the capacity of all market participants, increasing the quality of services provided and adapting the regulation and supervision of the sector to the effort of opening up and modernising undertaken across the market in the Cape Verdean economy. (ii) Better integration into the international financial system In line with the increasing cross-border mobility of capital and the opportunities and challenges arising from a small, open country devoid of natural resources such as Cape Verde, the Cape Verdean international financial market will see a phase of marked consolidation and modernisation during 2008. In addition to the effort to raise funds and develop more and better financial services targeted at non-residents, considerable progress is also expected to strengthen the soundness, integrity and stability of credit institutions and national parabanking institutions, thus contributing to increasing confidence in the national financial system as a whole. The prevention and combating of money laundering and terrorist financing will be particularly well received by national authorities, in line with recommendations and practices from relevant international entities such as the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the European Union and the International Financial Action Group (FATF), and with their support. Among the expected advances for the Cape Verdean international financial market are the following:  Improvement of the national system for the prevention and combating of money laundering and terrorist financing, through the adequacy of the applicable regulations (Law 17/VI/2002) to international requirements;  Operationalization of the newly created Financial Information Unit (FIU), specialized service responsible for the collection, processing, forwarding and follow-up of information related to suspicious financial operations;  Approval of a new foreign exchange law, completely liberalizing operations and simplifying procedures in financial relations with abroad, in line with the structural transformations recorded by the national economy. Another important aspect of development to be recorded at the level of the international financial market has to do with the tax measures to be developed and implemented in order to minimise reputational risks and increase Cape Verde's fiscal competitiveness as an international financial centre. In this situation, the special legislation establishing the International Financial Institutions will be repealed and the system of tax benefits granted to the financial sector will be revised, in particular for the international business of financial institutions and income of non-residents in foreign currency. Similarly, the tax system will be adapted to international or cross-border corporate transactions, through the principle of fiscal neutrality, exempting from taxation some of these operations, in particular those related to royalties, undercapitalisation, dividend distribution, sharing resulting from dissolution of companies and intra-group loans. Another area where the national financial market is expected to make a significant advance has to do with capital market operations. In particular, (i) the pblica debt system will be modernised, reducing the cost of financing for the State and expanding the participation by small policymakers, including non-residents; (ii) The Securities Market Code will be thoroughly revised to incorporate recent advances in prospectuses, services and financial products, as well as to reflect international practices on corporate governance and investor protection; (iii) the development of the bond market will be developed through the concession of tax exemptions, thus enabling the commonization of this important instrument of democratization of the financial system, with evident and considerable gains, either for companies or for the aphorizers. Another important aspect has to do with the introduction of international financial reporting standards. The mandatory application of these standards to entities subject to the supervision of the Central Bank, as of this January, will contribute to increasing the comparability and reliability of the financial information provided by these entities, an important gain that, in the medium term, should spill over to the rest of the business sector. (iii) Greater financial inclusion An important challenge currently facing the national financial system is access by those for which it is intended. In fact, it is of little use to have a system with adequate size, stability and profitability if the services offered by that system are not accessible to businesses and households. Cape Verde already sees a considerable advance in this area, as indicated by the growing number of bank branches, the improvement of the quality of service, and the availability of new means of payment (ATMs, POS, credit cards, ...). The penetration rate of financial services, whether geographically or demographicly, is an indicator of the positive developments that the system has recorded in recent years. During 2008, these indicators of financial inclusion improve, in line with the demands of a middle-developing country. This development will particularly benefit the most disadvantaged sectors of the economy and society. As a result of the current dynamic of expanding the network of branches and other financial services, led by commercial banks, micro-enterprises and the most deprived populations will have better access to financial services. The State will also contribute to increasing financial inclusion by supporting the microfinance sector. In particular, the:  Regulation of the recently approved Microfinance Framework Law (Law 15/VII/2007 of 10 September), creating objective conditions for the exercise of the activity in a transparent and sustainable manner;  creation of operating standards and prudential rules specific to microfinance activities;  Creation of capacity for supervision of institutions that practice micro-finance. In conclusion, considerable improvements are expected for the national financial system in 2008: a system experiencing continued gains in competitiveness, taking greater advantage of international markets and practices, but also more attuned to national needs. This is the challenge ahead and that, with the commitment of all stakeholders, we will certainly be able to win.
text_original: Perspectivas para o Sistema Financeiro Nacional 2008 (Comunicao do Governador Carlos Burgo ao Programa Praa Financeira) 9 de Janeiro de 2008 Num contexto marcado por crescentes oportunidades e desafios a nvel internacional, particularmente os relacionados com o turismo, o investimento externo e as transaces financeiras internacionais, e da resultante dinmica e optimismo quanto s perspectivas de crescimento da economia nacional, em 2008 o sistema financeiro ser chamado a desempenhar um papel cada vez mais importante na economia servio-orientada que se impe para Cabo Verde. O ano de 2008 apresenta-se com importantes e boas perspectivas no que respeita ao desenvolvimento do sistema financeiro nacional. Fruto da crescente estabilidade macroeconmica registada nos ltimos anos e de iniciativas mais recentes em matria de definio das grandes linhas de desenvolvimento do sistema, existem hoje condies que permitem um salto quantitativo e qualitativo do sistema enquanto mobilizador da poupana e sua canalizao para o investimento. Em resultado de diversos factores relevantes e da concretizao de mltiplas iniciativas em curso ou em carteira, no decorrer de 2008 Cabo Verde passar a ter um sistema financeiro mais competitivo; melhor integrado no sistema financeiro internacional; e mais acessvel aos sectores desfavorecidos da economia e da sociedade. (i) Um sistema financeiro mais competitivo Na senda das melhorias j introduzidas em matria de re-estruturao do sistema financeiro, e visando contribuir para a sua diversificao e aprofundamento, o enquadramento da actividade financeira passar por um processo de reviso, de modo a facilitar o exerccio de determinadas actividades financeiras especializadas e facilitar a introduo de determinadas novas tipologias institucionais e actividades especficas mais adequadas  nossa realidade actual. Em matria de novas tipologias institucionais sero criadas as condies legais necessrias ao surgimento de sociedades detentoras e gestoras de participaes sociais (SGPS) e de sociedades de investimentos de capital varivel (SICAV), um veculo de investimento colectivo relativamente informal mas apto s operaes internacionais de investimento. Outra inovao ser a introduo do regime das Instituies Financeiras de Crdito (IFIC), permitindo a prtica de todas as operaes permitidas aos bancos, com excepo da recepo de depsitos do pblico. Por outro lado, o regime dos Organismos de Investimento Colectivo (OIC), dever tornar-se mais competitivo em matria de exigncias para constituio e gesto, bem como de introduo de novas categorias de OICs. Outra rea que j est e continuar a registar importantes avanos  a actividade seguradora. Em resultado do actual esforo de reviso no sector, as principais reas desse ramo de actividade ficaro adequadamente reguladas e a actividade no seu todo ficar melhor sintonizada com as demais componentes do sistema financeiro. O processo inclui a reviso, a actualizao e a criao de legislao nas mais diversas reas relacionadas com a actividade seguradora, perspectivando uma melhoria na capacidade de todos os intervenientes no mercado, o incremento na qualidade dos servios prestados e a adaptao da regulao e superviso do sector ao esforo de abertura e modernizao empreendido transversalmente na economia cabo-verdiana. (ii) Uma melhor integrao no sistema financeiro internacional Em linha com a crescente mobilidade transfronteiria de capitais e das oportunidades e desafios da decorrentes para um pas pequeno, aberto e desprovido de recursos naturais como Cabo Verde, a praa financeira internacional cabo-verdiana conhecer durante o ano de 2008 uma fase de acentuada consolidao e modernizao. A par do esforo no sentido de captar fundos e de desenvolver mais e melhores servios financeiros orientados para no residentes, esperam-se tambm avanos considerveis no sentido do reforo da solidez, da integridade e da estabilidade das instituies de crdito e das instituies parabancrias nacionais, contribuindo assim para aumentar a confiana no sistema financeiro nacional no seu conjunto. A preveno e o combate ao branqueamento de capitais e ao financiamento do terrorismo merecero uma particular ateno das autoridades nacionais, em linha com recomendaes e prticas de entidades internacionais relevantes tais como o Fundo Monetrio Internacional (FMI), a Unio Europeia e o Grupo de Aco Financeira Internacional (GAFI), e com apoio destas. Entre os avanos esperados para a praa financeira internacional cabo-verdiana salientam-se os seguintes:  Melhoria do sistema nacional de preveno e combate ao branqueamento de capitais e ao financiamento do terrorismo, pela via da adequao do normativo aplicvel (Lei 17/VI/2002) s exigncias internacionais;  Operacionalizao da recm-criada Unidade de Informao Financeira (UIF), servio especializado responsvel pela recolha, processamento, encaminhamento e seguimento de informaes relativas a operaes financeiras suspeitas;  Aprovao de uma nova lei cambial, liberalizando completamente as operaes e simplificando os procedimentos nas relaes financeiras com o exterior, em linha com as transformaes estruturais registadas pela economia nacional. Um outro aspecto importante do desenvolvimento a registar a nvel da praa financeira internacional tem a ver com as medidas fiscais a serem desenvolvidas e implementadas de modo a minimizar os riscos reputacionais e aumentar a competitividade fiscal de Cabo Verde como um centro financeiro internacional. Nesta ptica, ser revogada a legislao especial que cria as Instituies Financeiras Internacionais e revisto o sistema de benefcios fiscais concedidos ao sector financeiro, nomeadamente para os negcios internacionais das instituies financeiras e rendimentos de no residentes em moeda estrangeira. De igual modo, proceder-se-  adequao do sistema fiscal s operaes societrias internacionais ou transfronteirias, atravs do princpio da neutralidade fiscal, isentando de tributao algumas dessas operaes, nomeadamente as relacionadas com royalties, subcapitalizao, distribuio de dividendos, partilha resultante de dissoluo de sociedades e emprstimos intra-grupo. Uma outra rea em que a praa financeira nacional dever registar um avano significativo tem a ver com as operaes do mercado de capitais. Em concreto, (i) o sistema de leiles da dvida pblica ser modernizado, reduzindo o custo de financiamento para o Estado e ampliando a participao por parte dos pequenos aforradores, nomeadamente os no residentes; (ii) O Cdigo do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios ser objecto de uma profunda reviso de modo a incorporar os recentes avanos em matria de prospectos, dos servios e dos produtos financeiros, bem como a reflectir prticas internacionais em matria de governana empresarial e proteco dos investidores; (iii) proceder-se- ao desenvolvimento do mercado obrigacionista pela via de concesso de isenes fiscais, viabilizando assim a vulgarizao desse importante instrumento de democratizao do sistema financeiro, com ganhos evidentes e considerveis, seja para as empresas, seja para os aforradores. Outro aspecto importante tem a ver com a introduo das normas internacionais de relato financeiro. A obrigatoriedade da aplicao dessas normas s entidades sujeitas  superviso do Banco Central, j a partir do corrente ms de Janeiro, contribuir para aumentar a comparabilidade e fiabilidade da informao financeira prestada por essas entidades, um ganho importante que, a mdio prazo, dever transbordar para o resto do sector empresarial. (iii) Maior incluso financeira Um importante desafio que se coloca actualmente ao sistema financeiro nacional  o do acesso por parte daqueles a que se destina. De facto, de pouco vale ter um sistema com dimenso, estabilidade e rentabilidade adequados se os servios oferecidos por esse sistema no forem acessveis s empresas e s famlias. Cabo Verde regista j um avano considervel nessa matria, conforme indica o nmero crescente de agncias bancrias, a melhoria da qualidade do atendimento, e a disponibilidade de novos meios de pagamento (ATMs, POS, cartes de crdito, ). O ndice de penetrao dos servios financeiros, seja em termos geogrficos, seja em termos demogrficos,  indicador da evoluo positiva registada pelo sistema nos ltimos anos. No decorrer do ano de 2008, esses indicadores de incluso financeira continuaro a melhorar, em linha com as exigncias de um pas de desenvolvimento mdio. Esta evoluo beneficiar particularmente os sectores mais desfavorecidos da economia e da sociedade. Fruto da dinmica actual de alargamento da rede de agncias e outros servios financeiros, protagonizada pelos bancos comerciais, as micro-empresas e as populaes mais carenciadas passaro a ter melhor acesso a servios financeiros. O Estado tambm contribuir para aumentar a incluso financeira pela via do apoio ao sector das micro-finanas. Em concreto, proceder-se- :  Regulamentao da recm aprovada Lei de Enquadramento das Micro-finanas (Lei 15/VII/2007, de 10 de Setembro), criando condies objectivas para o exerccio da actividade de forma transparente e sustentvel;  Criao de normas de funcionamento e regras prudenciais especficas para as actividades de micro-finanas;  Criao de capacidade para superviso das instituies que praticam micro-finanas. Em concluso, esperam-se melhorias considerveis para o sistema financeiro nacional em 2008: um sistema a registar ganhos contnuos de competitividade, tirando maior vantagem de mercados e prticas internacionais, mas tambm mais sintonizado com as necessidades nacionais. Este  o desafio que temos pela frente e que, com o empenho de todas as partes interessadas, saberemos certamente vencer.

Title: Speech at the Press Conference
text: Speech by The Governor of the BCV, Dr. Carlos Burgo, at the opening of the Seminar on "Credit Information Bureau" Chamber of Commerce, Industry and Services of Sotavento Beach, July 16, 2009 Ladies and gentlemen On behalf of the Bank of Cape Verde, I am now able to share with you some initial reflections on the theme of credit information, in the tics of a private service. The BCV promptly responded to the invitation made by the organization of the event, given the important contribution that credit information can make to the process of building a financial system that is read, efficient and accessible, an important aspect of the Central Bank's mission. The importance of credit information to the financial system stems from contributing to a more comprehensive and transparent distribution of credit. It helps to avoid or mitigate information asymmetry problems that typically hinder the lending process, resulting in unnecessary costs for consumers, businesses, financial institutions and the economy. The expansion of credit, on a transparent basis, means in turn less undocumented credit, greater profitability for financial intermediaries and, in the last instance, a more developed and stable financial system, therefore with better capacity to fulfill its functions in the process of developing the economy. The participation of the national private sector in the management of the credit information problem  as may be decided  will be an important complement to the efforts already made by the State, through the BCV, with a view to ensuring credit information that reflects the interests and responsibilities of the competent parties. In particular, it will be welcomed as a complement to the Credit Risk Central (CRC), an instrument developed and managed by the BCV in compliance with the prudential responsibilities of the Central Bank as responsible for supervising the national financial system. The synergies that will become possible within the framework of a system with these two valences will translate into no better and less costly information for the financial system. Allow me here a parenthesis to share with you some current bcv initiatives aimed at improving the context of credit activity in Cape Verde:  Improving monetary policy and supervising financial activity, elements with strong influence on credit activity;  Assessment of the financial system, detecting the vulnerabilities and risks that condition financial activity;  review of the framework of banking and parabanking activity, currently almost thirteen years old, in order to promote the emergence of specialised institutions and financial instruments best suited to the needs of national eco-operators;  Participation in the review of a set of regulations, such as the Code of Commercial Enterprises, in order to create an environment of Office of the Governor and the Councils Avenida Amilcar Cabral  Caixa Postal 101  Phone (238) 2607000  Fax (238) 2614447  Praia - Cabo Verde Mod.Not.02 investment and businesses conducive to opportunities needs existing in the country; Strengthening and improving the national credit reporting system is a current priority for the BCV. The rapid growth of (formal) credit to the economy  26% in 2008  in a context of international crisis and slowing in the pace of national econational growth, calls on us to strengthen capacity and monitoring measures for credit activity taking into account the possible harmful effects it may have on the monetary mass, the country's balance of payments and international reserves. It is important that there is credit to the private sector but in a sustainability environment, with adequate risk management and attention to the possible effects on the financial system and the economy as a whole. While there is no detailed and reliable data on the development of informal credit in Cape Verde, some indications, including the dynamics of micro-credit activity and the behaviour of some larger commercial operators, lead us to believe that such activity is expanding. Credit information in private statistics can help the central bank in fulfilling its responsibilities for monitoring credit developments, similar to what has already been happening in many developing countries, particularly some with credit activity and econic reality comparable to those of Cape Verde. In the past few years, several emerging countries have experienced high rates of credit growth  in some cases above 50% Office of the Governor and the Councils Avenida Amilcar Cabral  Caixa Postal 101  Phone (238) 2607000  Fax (238) 2614447  Praia - Cabo Verde Mod.Not.02 by year  leading authorities to recommend greater accountability in lending, particularly in a context of widespread financial crisis. The provision of credit information, in particular through the establishment of private agencies, is an important part of this new responsibility. Several low-middle income countries  therefore comparable to Cape Verde  have participated in this dynamic, resulting in better credit information produced and reported at lower costs. We hope that Cape Verde can also be associated with this dynamic, with advantages for the financial sector and for all its participants. The Bank of Cape Verde is available to collaborate in this effort in a way that is defined and agreed. I therefore hope that you will have a good working session, enjoying the knowledge of the international specialist present here, with the rear of the International Financial Society, an international institution of reference in the panorama of the development of private activity. I also ask the distinguished participants to share their concerns and contributions with the promoters and the entities present here, with a view to the appropriate involvement of the private sector in addressing this important and current problem. Where interventions of the responsibility of the plica sphere are justified, the Bank of Cape Verde undertakes here to intercede through the main channels with a view to assuming the responsibilities of the State in this matter. text_original: Discurso do Sr. Governador do BCV, Dr. Carlos Burgo, no acto de abertura do Seminrio sobre Bureau de Informao de Crdito Cmara do Comrcio, Industria e Servios de Sotavento Praia, 16 de Julho de 2009 Minhas senhoras e meus senhores Em nome do Banco de Cabo Verde, cumpre-me hoje partilhar convosco algumas reflexs iniciais sobre a temtica da informao de crdito, na tica de um servio privado. O BCV atendeu prontamente ao convite formulado pela organizao do evento atendendo ao importante contributo que a informao de crdito pode trazer para o processo de edificao de um sistema financeiro slido, eficiente e acessvel, uma vertente importante da misso do Banco Central. A importncia da informao de crdito para o sistema financeiro decorre do facto de contribuir para uma distribuio mais abrangente e transparente do crdito. Ajuda a evitar ou mitigar os problemas de assimetria de informao que normalmente dificultam o processo de concesso de crdito, resultando em custos desnecessrios para os consumidores, as empresas, as instituies financeiras e para a economia. A expanso do crdito, numa base transparente, significa por sua vez menos crdito em situao irregular, maior rendibilidade para os intermedirios financeiros e, em tima instncia, um sistema financeiro mais desenvolvido e estvel, portanto com melhor capacidade para cumprir as suas funs no processo de desenvolvimento da economia. A participao do sector privado nacional na gesto da problemtica da informao de crdito  nos moldes que eventualmente vierem a ser decididos  ser um importante complemento aos esforos j desenvolvidos pelo Estado, atravs do BCV, com vista a garantir uma informao de crdito que traduza os interesses e as responsabilidades das partes competentes. Em concreto, ser bem-vindo como um complemento  Central de Risco de Crdito (CRC), um instrumento desenvolvido e gerido pelo BCV em cumprimento das responsabilidades prudenciais do Banco Central enquanto responsvel pela superviso do sistema financeiro nacional. As sinergias que se tornaro possveis no quadro de um sistema com essas duas valncias traduzir-se-o sem dida em melhor e menos custosa informao para o sistema financeiro. O rpido crescimento do crdito (formal)  economia  26% em 2008  num contexto de crise internacional e abrandamento no ritmo de crescimento econico nacional, interpela-nos para a necessidade de reforar a capacidade e as medidas de acompanhamento da actividade creditcia tendo em conta os possveis efeitos nocivos que a mesma pode ter sobre a massa monetria, a balana de pagamentos e as reservas internacionais do pas. Importa sim que haja crdito ao sector privado mas numa tica de sustentabilidade, com gesto adequada do risco e ateno aos possveis efeitos sobre o sistema financeiro e a economia no seu todo. Se bem que no existem dados detalhados e fiveis sobre a evoluo do crdito informal em Cabo Verde, alguns indcios, nomeadamente a dinmica a nvel da actividade de micro-crdito e o comportamento de alguns operadores comerciais de maior dimenso, levam-nos a acreditar que tal actividade est a expandir-se. A informao de crdito, na tica privada pode ajudar o banco central no cumprimento das suas responsabilidades de acompanhamento da evoluo do crdito,  semelhana do que j vem acontecendo em muitos pases em desenvolvimento, em particular alguns com actividade creditcia e realidade econica comparveis s de Cabo Verde. A prestao de informao sobre o crdito, nomeadamente pela via de estabelecimento de agncias privadas, constitui uma vertente importante desta nova responsabilidade. Vrios pases de rendimento mdio-baixo  portanto comparveis a Cabo Verde  tm participado desta dinmica, resultando em melhor informao de crdito produzida e reportada com menores custos. Esperamos que Cabo Verde possa tambm associar-se a esta dinmica, com vantagens vias para o sector financeiro e para todos os seus participantes. Espero pois que tenham uma boa sesso de trabalho, desfrutando dos conhecimentos do especialista internacional aqui presente, com a retaguarda da Sociedade Financeira Internacional, instituio internacional de referncia no panorama do desenvolvimento da actividade privada. Peo igualmente aos ilustres participantes que partilhem com os promotores e com as entidades plicas aqui presentes as suas preocupas e contribuis, visando uma participao adequada do sector privado na abordagem a esta importante e actual problemtica. Title: 13th Meeting of Jurists of the Central Banks of the CPLP
text: 13th Meeting of Jurists of the Central Banks of the CPLP - Praia - September 2010 - Opening Speech of the Exmo. Mr. Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde Exmos. Mr. Administrators of the Bank of Cape Verde Exma. Madam Auditor General of the Securities Market Exmos. Directors, Consultants and Staff of the Bank of Cape Verde Guest gentlemen Ladies and gentlemen It is with great satisfaction that, on behalf of the Bank of Cape Verde and on my own behalf, I greet the participants of the thirteenth meeting of Jurists of the Central Banks of the Countries that have the Portuguese as their official language, warmly greeting the representatives of the Central Banks of Angola, Brazil, Mozambique, Portugal, Sao Tome and Principe and the Monetary and Payment authority of East Timor, gathered here. Welcome to Cape Verde and wishes for a pleasant stay. I hope that this meeting will be another opportunity for the strengthening of the friendship that unites us, of debate on issues that are today and an opportunity to enjoy creole morabeza as well. At an important and historic moment in the life of our institution - the Bank of Cape Verde - which will be 35 years old on 29 September this year, and at a time when the world is still experiencing, to a lesser extent, the effects of the financial crisis triggered in mid-2007, the topics chosen for debate on these two days of the meeting are of unquestionable timeliness and importance. Topics such as "legislative responses to the recent economic and financial crisis"; "banking secrecy - flexibility versus tax law"; "consumer protection of financial services and products"; "deposit guarantee fund", among others that will be discussed at this meeting, are matters that will certainly arouse the interest of the central bank staff represented here, to the extent that they have gained relevance with the financial crisis that has been left naked by some weaknesses in the financial system at the level of the globe, namely as to the capacity of supervision to monitor the activity of financial institutions. Following this crisis, the international community quickly sought the means to stop it and at the same time prevent or mitigate its future consequences. This is how, for example, at European level, the European Parliament has called for measures to be taken to improve financial control. In addition, it reiterated its call for legislative measures to strengthen the regulatory and supervisory framework and crisis management in the European Union, namely: regulation and supervision of banks, role of credit rating agencies, securitisation and control, speculative funds and other types of new structures, role of indebtedness, transparency obligations; settlement rules, clearing markets for non-listed derivatives and crisis prevention mechanisms. At the G20 meeting, a common approach was called for to improve financial sector regulation and financial supervision on the basis of greater coherence and systematic cooperation between countries; the adoption of a framework governing the adequacy of Basel II own funds and efforts to strengthen prudential regulatory standards. Similarly, countries have been asked to promote the integrity and transparency of financial markets as well as greater accountability of financial actors, among others. At a time when the consumer of financial products and services is increasingly in the spotlight, behavioural supervision has not been forgotten and appears as a complement to the regulation of financial markets. The issue of bank secrecy was once again on the agenda, with those who vaticinasse their end or at least its reanalysis or profound reconfiguration. All this to say that the scheduled topics will certainly deserve heated discussions. Let me point out that, at the request of the monetary authorities of Cape Verde and in the context of the Bank of Cape Verde's mission to promote the stability of the financial system took place in Cape Verde between the end of 2008 and mid-2009, the financial assessment exercise, commonly referred to as the Financial Sector Assessement Program (FSAP). This exercise concluded by a comprehensively positive assessment of the Cape Verdean financial system and produced, among others, the following conclusions: The national financial system has been supporting the objectives of growth and development; Monetary policy is overall adequate, but there is room for improvement through simplification of procedures and introduction of new instruments and practices; The offshore financial sector carries prudential and reputational risks arising from less stringent regulation and supervision in relation to the onshore sector, which is why there is a need for a reform of that sector; It was recommended to continue and deepen the efforts of the Bank of Cape Verde to strengthen the supervisory capacity of financial activity; Continuation and deepening of the reform of the legal infrastructure of the financial and judicial system in order to allow the increase and improvement of the contribution of the financial system. It should be noted here that, on the impulse of the Bank of Cape Verde, virtually all insurance legislation has been revised, and in the conclusion phase a new General Regime of Credit Institutions has been revised, as well as the revision of the Securities Market Code. It should be noted that already in 2009 the national banking sector was marked by the adoption of the International Financial Reporting Standards (IAS/IFRS or NIRF). Now, this is to give a brief overview of what the Bank of Cape Verde has been doing, with regard to the adoption of measures to strengthen the national financial system, in order to continue to grow with Cape Verde, as is the motto of the celebrations of the 35th year of its existence. Ladies and gentlemen, This is an important moment of sharing knowledge, experiences and advice, so that each of those present can be more enriched from this 13th meeting, bringing to each of the Central Banks and the Monetary Authority important subsidies for the improvement of their financial systems. It is time, therefore, to begin, without further ado, the purpose that brought us here today and, thus, I declare open the thirteenth meeting of jurists of the Central Banks of the Portuguese Official Language Countries. I hope for a good job and thank you very much. Beach, September 23, 2010
