Title: International conference on "Mobilising post-crisis opportunities"
text: Celebrations of the 35th Anniversary of the Bank of Cape Verde International conference on "Mobilising opportunities in the post-crisis" Madam Minister of Finance, Diplomatic Representatives, Governors and Representatives of the Central Banks of the CPLP Countries Gentlemen Lecturers Distinguished Guests Ladies and gentlemen, On behalf of the Bank of Cape Verde, I would like to welcome you to this international conference on "The mobilisation of opportunities in the post-crisis". The fact that the financial system was the area of economic activity where the crisis first manifested itself, and where it had its most visible effects, justified the choice of the theme for this event which is carried out in the framework of the Bank's mission to ensure the stability of the financial system and in the context of its 35th Anniversary celebrations, under the motto "35 years growing with Cape Verde" Due to the great importance of the financial system for economic and social life, the financial crisis has led to an economic crisis that has shaken the foundations of modern society. For the same reason, the Bank of Cape Verde believes that the financial system should take a prominent position in the post-crisis management debate, signalling that financial activity can and should take the lead in creating conditions that allow the resumption of normality in economic activity and in the functioning of society. In Cape Verde, fortunately, the financial system has not been directly affected by the international crisis. Dominated by the banking sector, financial activity in the country remains stable and profitable, adequately serving the needs of the economy and society. However, of course, the indirect effects of the crisis have been and continue to be felt. The evolution of the level of bad-stop credit indicates the existence of emerging challenges with regard to credit risk. On the other hand, the nature of the business fabric puts us at considerable levels of concentration risk. Last but not least, in times of crisis, the national financial system tends to renote the uncertainties in the evolution of external flows that underpin our economy, namely tourism revenues, foreign investment, emigrant deposits and export revenues. In this context, the BCV has been developing and implementing a set of measures to manage the identified challenges and strengthen the resilience and competitiveness of the system. The aim is to ensure that the financial system enables and facilitates economic activity by enabling our service-oriented economy to take advantage of opportunities in this post-crisis time. In this process we benefit greatly from the recommendations of the recent evaluation of the financial system under the FSAP programme of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank and, with the lessons we are all learning from the current crisis. Later in this event I will have the opportunity and pleasure to share with you more details about the behaviour of the Cape Verdean economy, the performance of the financial system and the lessons learned from the crisis in both macroeconomic management and the regulation and supervision of the financial system. I begin, however, by bringing to your attention some of the measures that the Bank of Cape Verde has been developing and implementing in the framework of its mission as responsible for the stability and development of the national financial system, with the specific objective of ensuring that the financial system can fulfil its role as a signaler and facilitator of recovery in this post-crisis period. Among these measures we highlight: i. the introduction of macro-prudential supervision, promoting a targeted approach and specific tools, such as stress tests, to prevent systemic risk; (ii) the turning point for risk-based supervision in order to reduce existing vulnerabilities and to ensure the timely and systematic identification and treatment of the main risks to which the banking sector is exposed; iii. strengthening prudential supervision by empowering the Bank and its employees to meet the growing needs of the activity, in particular with regard to specialised financial activities; iv. The reform of the legal infrastructure of the financial system to enable the expansion of activity in line with national potential and international standards and practices. In this chapter, it is worth mentioning the ongoing process of revision of the law regulating financial activity and the Securities Market Code, and also the reform of the off-shore sector, the latter with the aim of ensuring the provision of financial services to non-residents, but in line with internationally accepted standards, thus reducing the inherent reputational risk. The Bank of Cape Verde is aware that financial activity does not take place in a void. First of all, in a successful way, it needs a global environment that is appropriate for investment and economic activity in general. This is why, in addition to the above actions, the Bank of Cape Verde is also deepening the field of non-financial issues and has been and will continue to work in partnership with other national public and private entities in identifying and solving problems in other sectors that may affect the health and effectiveness of the financial system. Among these extra-system initiatives we refer here to measures related to the strengthening of the stability of public finances, essential for the success of the private sector, and measures aimed at improving the investment and business environment. In addition to two speakers, renowned economists who will share with us their analysis and their suggestions on the national economy and the Eurozone, we have representatives of various central banks of countries who are friends and relevant to our reality, to share with us their experiences and their vision for this crucial moment. We also count on the active participation of the invited guests, so that we are attuned to the concerns and aspirations of our economy and our society. Together we will come out of this event more enlightened about the challenges and opportunities that exist, but also about the responsibilities of each and every one at this decisive moment. I am therefore able to give the floor to the Minister of Finance for the opening of the event, presenting her communication. Beach, September 24, 2010
text_original: Comemoraes do 35 Aniversrio do Banco de Cabo Verde Conferncia internacional sobre A mobilizao de oportunidades no ps-crise Senhora Ministra das Finanas, Senhores Representantes Diplomticos, Senhores Governadores e Representantes dos Bancos Centrais dos Pases da CPLP Senhores Conferencistas Distintos Convidados Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Em nome do Banco de Cabo Verde, quero dar-vos as boas vindas a esta conferncia internacional sobre A mobilizao de oportunidades no ps-crise. O facto de o sistema financeiro ter sido a rea de actividade econmica onde a crise primeiro se manifestou, e onde teve os seus efeitos mais visveis, justificou a escolha do tema para este evento que  realizado no quadro da misso do Banco de velar pela estabilidade do sistema financeiro e no mbito das comemoraes do seu 35 Aniversrio, sob o lema 35 anos a crescer com Cabo Verde Devido  grande importncia do sistema financeiro para a vida econmica e social, a crise financeira conduziu a uma crise econmica que abalou os alicerces da sociedade moderna. Pela mesma razo, entende o Banco de Cabo Verde que o sistema financeiro deve assumir uma posio de destaque no debate sobre a gesto do ps-crise, sinalizando que a actividade financeira pode e deve assumir a dianteira na criao de condies que permitam a retoma da normalidade na actividade econmica e no funcionamento da sociedade. Em Cabo-Verde, felizmente, o sistema financeiro no foi afectado directamente pela crise internacional. Dominada pelo sector bancrio, a actividade financeira no pas mantm-se estvel e rentvel, servindo adequadamente as necessidades da economia e da sociedade. Porm, como  natural, os efeitos indirectos da crise se fizeram e continuam a fazer-se sentir. A evoluo do nvel de crdito mal-parado indicia a existncia de desafios emergentes no que concerne ao risco de crdito. Por outro lado, a natureza do tecido empresarial coloca-nos perante nveis considerveis de risco de concentrao. Por ltimo, mas no menos importante, em tempo de crise o sistema financeiro nacional tende a ressentir-se das incertezas na evoluo dos fluxos externos que sustentam a nossa economia, designadamente as receitas tursticas, o investimento externo, os depsitos de emigrantes e as receitas de exportao. Neste contexto, o BCV tem vindo a desenvolver e a implementar um conjunto de medidas visando gerir os desafios identificados e reforar a resilincia e a competitividade do sistema. O objectivo  garantir que o sistema financeiro viabilize e facilite a actividade econmica, permitindo  nossa economia servio-orientada tirar partido das oportunidades neste momento de ps-crise. Neste processo beneficiamos grandemente das recomendaes da recente avaliao do sistema financeiro no mbito do programa FSAP do Fundo Monetrio Internacional e do Banco Mundial e, com as lies que estamos todos aprendendo com a actual crise. Terei mais tarde neste evento a oportunidade e o prazer de partilhar convosco mais detalhes sobre o comportamento da economia cabo-verdiana, o desempenho do sistema financeiro e as lies aprendidas com a crise tanto a nvel da gesto macro-econmica como da regulao e superviso do sistema financeiro. Comeo, todavia, por trazer ao vosso conhecimento algumas das medidas que o Banco de Cabo Verde tem vindo a desenvolver e a implementar no quadro da sua misso de responsvel pela estabilidade e desenvolvimento do sistema financeiro nacional, com o objectivo especfico de garantir que o sistema financeiro possa cumprir o seu papel de sinalizador e de facilitador da retoma neste momento de ps-crise. De entre estas medidas salientamos: i. A introduo da superviso macro-prudencial, promovendo uma abordagem orientada nesse sentido e ferramentas especficas, tais como os stress tests, visando prevenir o risco sistmico; ii. A viragem para a superviso baseada no risco, de modo a diminuir as vulnerabilidades existentes e a garantir a identificao e o tratamento atempado e sistemtico dos principais riscos a que se encontra exposto o sector bancrio; iii. O reforo da superviso prudencial, capacitando o Banco e o os seus colaboradores com vista a atender s necessidades crescentes da actividade, em particular no que respeita s actividades financeiras especializadas; iv. A reforma da infra-estrutura legal do sistema financeiro, de modo a permitir a expanso da actividade em linha com o potencial nacional e com os padres e prticas internacionais. Neste captulo, merece realce o processo em curso de reviso da lei reguladora da actividade financeira e do Cdigo do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios, e ainda a reforma do sector off-shore, este ltimo com o objectivo de garantir a prestao de servios financeiros a no residentes, mas em linha com padres internacionalmente aceites, reduzindo assim o risco reputacional inerente. O Banco de Cabo Verde est consciente de que a actividade financeira no ocorre num vazio. Antes porm, para ter sucesso precisa de um ambiente global adequado ao investimento e  actividade econmica em geral. Da que, em complemento s aces atrs referidas, o Banco de Cabo Verde est tambm a aprofundar o domnio de questes no financeiras e tem estado e vai continuar a trabalhar em parceria com outras entidades pblicas e privadas nacionais na identificao e resoluo de problemas em outros sectores que possam afectar a sade e a eficcia do sistema financeiro. Entre essas iniciativas extra-sistema referimos aqui as medidas relacionadas com o reforo da estabilidade das finanas pblicas, imprescindvel para o sucesso da iniciativa privada, e as medidas orientadas para a melhoria do ambiente de investimento e de negcios. Para alm de dois palestrantes, conceituados economistas que iro partilhar connosco a sua anlise e as suas sugestes na matria para a economia nacional e para a zona Euro, temos connosco representantes de vrios bancos centrais de pases amigos e relevantes para a nossa realidade, para partilhar connosco as suas experincias e a sua viso para este momento crucial. Contamos tambm com a participao activa dos senhores convidados, de modo a ficarmos sintonizados com as preocupaes e as aspiraes da nossa economia e da nossa sociedade. Juntos sairemos deste evento mais esclarecidos sobre os desafios e as oportunidades existentes, mas tambm sobre as responsabilidades de todos e de cada um neste momento decisivo. Cumpre-me assim passar a palavra a S.E. a Senhora Ministra das Finanas para a abertura do evento, apresentando a sua comunicao. Praia, 24 de Setembro de 2010

Title: International seminar on "Efficient supervision and capital market development"
text: International seminar on "Efficient supervision and capital market development" Opening speech On behalf of the Bank of Cape Verde, I am pleased to open this international seminar on "Efficient supervision and the development of the capital market". A life-long theme of international financial status and closely linked to the Bank of Cape Verde's mission to ensure the stability of the national financial system. In fact, supervision  i.e. the process of monitoring financial institutions in order to ensure adequate compliance with applicable standards and standards  has been one of the most common aspects in connection with the recent economic and financial crisis. Today it is agreed that the action  or inaction in many cases  of supervisors has contributed to expanding and accelerating the impact of the fundamental causes of the crisis, namely excess liquidity, excessively low interest rates and excesses by financial intermediaries and consumers. That is why, of course, in the post-crisis period, special attention has been paid to the problem of supervision and the twin issue of regulation. Guided by the De Larosiere Report, the whole of Europe has reorganised and/or is reorganising the supervisory architecture, introducing or strengthening Community mechanisms, while rethinking the national systems in force in the Member States. In the USA, at the same time the epicentre of the crisis and the leader of the recovery process among developed countries, responses to modernise the rules and, above all, to improve compliance with them are multiplied: the Volcker Rule and the Dodd-Frank Act have become frequent expressions of American financial daily life. Going a little further, in some circles there is a possibility of a return of the Glass-Steagall Act, an authentic firewall between commercial banking and investment banking introduced in the Franklim Roosevelt era and in force until just over a decade ago. In short, we are experiencing new times in the supervision of financial activity. A new context marked by increased responsibilities for entities responsible for ensuring the stability and efficiency of the system and defending the rights and interests of all its actors. A recent study by the International Monetary Fund shows that as a rule existing supervisory systems do not comply with recommended international principles and standards. Also according to the same study, this widespread problem of "non-compliance" conditions the performance of financial institutions and is related, at least in part, to the level of economic development of the country concerned. The quality of supervision and the impact on the performance of financial institutions is an important issue if it is considered that, because of increasing financial globalisation, differences in the quality of supervision can have rapid and significant cross-border effects. A matter of great importance, particularly for small countries, dependent on external flows and committed to developing a service economy. Here in Cape Verde, although the financial system has not been directly affected by the crisis, we have been working to address and progressively manage the emerging risks resulting indirectly from the crisis. In fact, if on the one hand the system has not been directly affected, it is certain that the decline in growth resulting from the decrease in external flows on which the national economy depends tends to contribute to the deterioration of the quality of the assets in the banks' portfolio. Among the actions that Banco de Cabo Verde has already implemented or has in its portfolio to safeguard emerging risks in the financial system, we highlight: i. the introduction of macro-prudential supervision, promoting the careful monitoring of the system as a whole as a way of preventing systemic risk; ii. The turning point for risk-based supervision to reduce existing vulnerabilities and identify and manage the main risks to the banking sector; iii. strengthening prudential supervision by empowering the institution and its staff to meet the growing needs of the activity, in particular with regard to specialised financial activities; iv. The reform of the legal infrastructure of the financial system, with an enhancement to the ongoing process of revision of the Financial Activity Framework Act and the Securities Market Code. The Bank of Cape Verde is still actively committed to introducing behavioural supervision, promoting consumer protection, in particular those who, for financial, cultural or other reasons, are less empowered to defend themselves. The draft revision of the Financial Activity Framework Act, referred to above, expressly introduces behavioural supervision as one of its main innovations. The capital market has received a very special attention from the Bank of Cape Verde. In line with the potential and growing dynamics in our country in this field of financial activity in recent years, the Bank of Cape Verde has been and will continue to invest in the development of the supervisory capacity of this market, with special attention to the secondary market, a real barometer of the health of the financial system and the economy in general. As part of these development efforts, laws and regulations are being modernised, with emphasis on the securities market code, as mentioned above, the working conditions of the General Audit are being improved, and its staff is benefiting from training actions. We are also making efforts to raise awareness, capacity building and engage the other market participants, an effort of which this international seminar is the most recent example. All this action by the Bank of Cape Verde on capital market regulation and supervision aims to modernise the regulatory environment and strengthen the supervisory capacity of the activity, in line with market dynamics and international best principles and practices. My lords and gentlemen, This Seminar represents an important milestone in the history of international relations of the Bank of Cape Verde. As a result of contacts that the Bank of Cape Verde and the General Securities Market Audit have been developing with u.S. Securities and Exchange Commission officials, the SEC is currently conducting a regional training action in our country co-organized by this accredited supervisory body. We thank the SEC for the preference and we have a dwelled that more of these and similar shares may take place in our country, for the benefit of participants in the Cape Verdean market and countries in our sub-region. As a result of collaboration with the SEC, we will have today and in the coming days the privilege of receiving information and clarification directly from frontline supervisors and researchers on how to do proper oversight and on the development and implementation of corrective and punitive measures to be implemented when pedagogy and prevention are not enough to solve the problem. We will learn about strategies and tactics developed over decades of hard work in monitoring and action, including investigation and prosecution in court, in the face of the biggest predators that the market has known to date. Let's know the details and impacts of the most striking frauds, from enron cases to Worldcom, from Ponzi to Madoff. We therefore thank the SEC experts for this unique opportunity. Extensive thanks to the experts of the Brazilian Securities and Exchange Commission, who through the SEC are also here with us in this Seminar, also allowing us to know the experiences of this important Portuguese-speaking market. To the distinguished participants, in particular those who came from other jurisdictions, we ask that you help enrich this event with your active participation and then use the knowledge acquired here in formatting and making your contribution to building the capital market that we all want and are building. I end with words of gratitude to the staff of the Bank of Cape Verde who worked on the organization of this unique event in the history of international relations of the Bank of Cape Verde. If we are gathered here today, it is because the Bank of Cape Verde, through these leaders and staff, has managed the complex logistics inherent in such an activity. With the hope of a fruitful exchange of ideas, I declare open the work of this international seminar. Praia City, Cape Verde, on October 25, 2010
text_original: Seminrio internacional sobre A superviso eficiente e o desenvolvimento do mercado de capitais Discurso de abertura Em representao do Banco de Cabo Verde, apraz-me proceder  abertura deste seminrio internacional sobre A Superviso eficiente e o desenvolvimento do mercado de capitais. Um tema candente da actualidade financeira internacional e intimamente ligado  misso do Banco de Cabo Verde de velar pela estabilidade do sistema financeiro nacional. De facto, a superviso  ou seja o processo de acompanhamento das instituies financeiras de modo a garantir o adequado cumprimento dos padres e das normas aplicveis  tem sido um dos aspectos mais aflorados em conexo com a recente crise econmica e financeira. Hoje  consensual que a aco  ou inaco em muitos casos  dos supervisores contribuiu para ampliar e acelerar o impacto das causas fundamentais da crise, designadamente o excesso de liquidez, as taxas de juros exageradamente baixas e os excessos praticados pelos intermedirios financeiros e pelos consumidores. Da que, naturalmente, no perodo ps-crise uma ateno especial tem sido dada  problemtica da superviso e  questo gmea da regulao. Orientando-se pelo Relatrio de Larosire, a Europa toda reorganizou e/ou est a reorganizar a arquitectura de superviso, introduzindo ou reforando os mecanismos comunitrios, ao mesmo tempo que se repensam os sistemas nacionais em vigor nos estados membros. Nos EUA, simultaneamente epicentro da crise e lder, entre os pases desenvolvidos, do processo de recuperao, multiplicam-se as respostas no sentido de modernizar as regras e, sobretudo, de melhorar o cumprimento das mesmas: a Regra de Volcker e a Lei Dodd-Frank transformaram-se em expresses frequentes do quotidiano financeiro americano. Indo um pouco mais longe, em alguns crculos cogita-se a possibilidade de um regresso da Lei Glass-Steagall, autntico firewall entre a banca comercial e a banca de investimento introduzido na era de Franklim Roosevelt e em vigor at h pouco mais de uma dcada. Em suma, vivemos novos tempos em matria de superviso da actividade financeira. Um novo contexto marcado por responsabilidades acrescidas para entidades que tm a seu cargo a misso de garantir a estabilidade e a eficincia do sistema e de defender os direitos e os interesses de todos os seus intervenientes. Um estudo recente realizado pelo Fundo Monetrio Internacional demonstra que em regra os sistemas de superviso actualmente existentes no esto em conformidade com os princpios e padres internacionais recomendados. Ainda de acordo com o mesmo estudo, este problema generalizado de no conformidade condiciona o desempenho das instituies financeiras e est relacionado, pelo menos em parte, com o nvel de desenvolvimento econmico do pas em causa. A qualidade da superviso e o impacto sobre o desempenho das instituies financeiras  uma questo importante se se considerar que, por causa da crescente globalizao financeira, diferenas na qualidade da superviso podem ter rpidos e significantes efeitos transfronteirios. Uma questo de grande importncia, particularmente para pases pequenos, dependentes de fluxos externos e apostados em desenvolver uma economia de prestao de servios. Aqui em Cabo Verde, apesar de o sistema financeiro no ter sido afectado directamente pela crise, temos vindo a trabalhar no sentido de equacionar e progressivamente gerir os riscos emergentes resultantes indirectamente da crise. De facto, se por um lado o sistema no foi directamente afectado, o certo  que a quebra no crescimento resultante da diminuio dos fluxos externos de que depende a economia nacional tende a contribuir para a deteriorao da qualidade dos activos da carteira dos bancos. De entre as aces que o Banco de Cabo Verde j implementou ou tem em carteira com vista a acautelar os riscos emergentes no sistema financeiro, destacamos: i. A introduo da superviso macro-prudencial, promovendo o acompanhamento criterioso do sistema no seu todo como forma de prevenir o risco sistmico; ii. A viragem para a superviso baseada no risco, visando diminuir as vulnerabilidades existentes e identificar e gerir os principais riscos a que se encontra exposto o sector bancrio; iii. O reforo da superviso prudencial, capacitando a instituio e os seus quadros para atender s necessidades crescentes da actividade, em particular no que respeita s actividades financeiras especializadas; iv. A reforma da infra-estrutura legal do sistema financeiro, com realce para o processo em curso de reviso da Lei de enquadramento da actividade financeira e do Cdigo do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios. O Banco de Cabo Verde est ainda activamente empenhado em introduzir a superviso comportamental, promovendo a defesa dos consumidores, em particular aqueles que, por razes de ordem financeira, cultural ou outra, esto menos habilitados para se defenderem a si prprios. O projecto de reviso da Lei de enquadramento da actividade financeira, anteriormente referido, introduz expressamente a superviso comportamental como uma das suas principais inovaes. O mercado de capitais tem merecido uma ateno muito especial do Banco de Cabo Verde. Em linha com o potencial e com a dinmica crescente registada no nosso pas nesse ramo de actividade financeira nos ltimos anos, o Banco de Cabo Verde tem vindo e vai continuar a investir no desenvolvimento da capacidade de superviso desse mercado, com especial ateno para o mercado secundrio, um verdadeiro barmetro da sade do sistema financeiro e da economia em geral. No mbito desses esforos de desenvolvimento, as Leis e os regulamentos esto sendo modernizados, com destaque para o Cdigo do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios, anteriormente referido, as condies de trabalho da Auditoria Geral esto sendo melhoradas, e o seu pessoal est a beneficiar de aces de capacitao. Estamos tambm envidando esforos no sentido da sensibilizao, capacitao e engajamento activo dos demais participantes no mercado, um esforo do qual este seminrio internacional  o exemplo mais recente. Toda esta aco do Banco de Cabo Verde em matria de regulao e de superviso do mercado de capitais tem como objectivo modernizar o ambiente regulatrio e reforar a capacidade de superviso da actividade, em linha com a dinmica do mercado e com os melhores princpios e prticas internacionais. Minhas senhores e meus senhores, Este Seminrio representa um marco importante na histria das relaes internacionais do Banco de Cabo Verde. Fruto de contactos que o Banco de Cabo Verde e a Auditoria Geral do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios tm vindo a desenvolver com responsveis da Comisso de Valores Mobilirios dos EUA, a SEC, concretiza-se hoje uma aco de formao regional no nosso pas co-organizada por esta credenciada entidade supervisora. Agradecemos  SEC pela preferncia e auguramos votos de que mais aces destas e similares possam ter lugar no nosso pas, para benefcio dos participantes no mercado cabo-verdiano e de pases da nossa sub-regio. Em resultado da colaborao com a SEC, teremos hoje e nos prximos dias o privilgio de receber informaes e esclarecimentos directamente da parte de supervisores e investigadores de primeira linha sobre como fazer uma adequada superviso e sobre o desenvolvimento e a implementao de medidas correctivas e punitivas a aplicar quando a pedagogia e a preveno no bastarem para resolver o problema. Vamos ficar a conhecer estratgias e tcticas desenvolvidas ao longo de dcadas de rduo trabalho em matria de acompanhamento e aco, incluindo investigao e acusao em tribunal, frente aos maiores prevaricadores que o mercado conheceu at hoje. Vamos conhecer detalhes e impactos das fraudes mais marcantes, dos casos da Enron  Worldcom, de Ponzi a Madoff. Agradecemos pois aos especialistas da SEC por esta oportunidade mpar. Agradecimentos extensivos aos especialistas da Comisso de Valores Mobilirios do Brasil, que pela via da SEC tambm esto aqui connosco neste Seminrio, permitindo-nos tambm conhecer as experincias deste importante mercado lusfono. Aos ilustres participantes, em particular aos que vieram de outras jurisdies, pedimos que ajudem a enriquecer este evento com a sua participao activa e que depois utilizem os conhecimentos aqui adquiridos na formatao e efectivao da sua contribuio para a edificao do mercado de capitais que todos queremos e estamos construindo. Termino com palavras de reconhecimento ao pessoal do Banco de Cabo Verde que trabalhou na organizao deste evento mpar na histria das relaes internacionais do Banco de Cabo Verde. Se aqui estamos hoje reunidos  porque o Banco de Cabo Verde, pela via desses dirigentes e quadros, soube gerir a complexa logstica inerente a uma actividade deste tipo. Com votos de um frutfero intercmbio de ideias, declaro aberto os trabalhos deste Seminrio internacional. Cidade da Praia, Cabo Verde, aos 25 de Outubro de 2010

Title: Speech at the Conference on the revision of the Regime of Collective Investment Undertakings
text: Conference on the revision of the Collective Investment Bodies scheme - 24 November 2011  This event is guided by the need to revise the regime of collective investment organizations, approved in 2005, in line with the developments in the meantime, whether internationally or in the Cape Verdean economy and society;  The revision of the regime is part of the broader process of promoting the stability and development of the national financial system, the statutory responsibility of the BCV;  An important set of initiatives aimed at strengthening the credibility and competitiveness of the national financial system are underway, which is already making considerable progress, but there are still several constraints, in particular as regards (i) alternatives for implementation with attractive but moderate risk-based remuneration and (ii) financing to SMEs.  Reform and innovation initiatives include both strengthening regulation and supervision, and also raising awareness and training of the various financial actors;  These initiatives are based on the best relevant international principles and practices and are supported by important external partners, including the World Bank, the International Monetary Fund, and the central banks of Portugal, Luxembourg and Brazil;  Collective Investment Organizations can play an important role in the process of consolidating and deepening the national financial system, as, by their characteristics, in particular the broad fundraising base, they can help overcome the financial and cultural constraints that characterize our market;  Despite the fact that the regime of Collective Investment Organizations has existed in our country for almost seven years, the practical results achieved are incipient, limited to two offshore investment funds with a low turnover. It is therefore important to make efforts to affirm and develop the scheme;  In addition to the revision of the regime, a process that brings us together today, the BCV advocates other solutions to help overcome the current situation. In this context, we are already working on other relevant aspects of the issue, namely the allocation of tax incentives for the various agents dedicated to the activity of collective investment bodies;  Other solutions are under development, and in due course they will be presented to the consideration of those present and other partners, for consideration, appropriation and collaboration with a view to their implementation;  Immediately, we count on receiving contributions to improve the draft review already available and currently in public consultation, as well as to framing and resolving other aspects that contribute to the affirmation of the regime of Collective Investment Organizations in Cape Verde.
text_original: Conferncia sobre a reviso do regime dos Organismos de Investimento Colectivo  24 de Novembro de 2011  Este evento orienta-se pela necessidade de reviso do regime dos Organismos de Investimento Colectivo, aprovado em 2005, em linha com a evoluo entretanto registada, seja no plano internacional, seja na economia e na sociedade cabo-verdianas;  A reviso do regime insere-se no processo mais amplo de promoo da estabilidade e desenvolvimento do sistema financeiro nacional, responsabilidade estatutria do BCV;  No mbito deste processo encontram-se em curso um conjunto importante de iniciativas orientadas para o reforo da credibilidade e da competitividade do sistema financeiro nacional, o qual j regista avanos considerveis, porm continua a debater-se com constrangimentos vrios, designadamente no que respeita a (i) alternativas de aplicao com remunerao atractiva mas de risco moderado e (ii) financiamento s PMEs.  As iniciativas de reforma e inovao incluem seja o reforo da regulao e da superviso, seja tambm a sensibilizao e a capacitao dos diversos agentes financeiros;  Estas iniciativas sustentam-se nos melhores princpios e prticas internacionais relevantes e so apoiadas por importantes parceiros externos, designadamente o Banco Mundial, o Fundo Monetrio Internacional, e os bancos centrais de Portugal, do Luxemburgo e do Brasil;  Os Organismos de Investimento Colectivo podem desempenhar um papel importante no processo de consolidao e aprofundamento do sistema financeiro nacional, j que, pelas suas caractersticas, designadamente a alargada base de captao de recursos, podem ajudar a ultrapassar as limitaes financeiras e culturais que caracterizam o nosso mercado;  Pese embora o facto de o regime dos Organismos de Investimento Colectivo j existir no nosso pas h quase sete anos, os resultados prticos conseguidos so incipientes, limitando-se a dois fundos de investimento off-shore com um reduzido volume de negcios. Da que importa envidar esforos com vista  afirmao e ao desenvolvimento do regime;  Para alm da reviso do regime, processo que hoje aqui nos congrega, o BCV preconiza outras solues para ajudar a ultrapassar a situao actual. Nesse mbito, estamos j trabalhando outros aspectos pertinentes da questo, designadamente a atribuio de incentivos fiscais para os diversos agentes que se dediquem  actividade dos Organismos de Investimento Colectivo;  Outras solues esto em vias de desenvolvimento, sendo que oportunamente sero apresentados  considerao dos presentes e dos demais parceiros, para apreciao, apropriao e colaborao com vista  sua implementao;  De imediato, contamos receber contribuies para melhorar o projecto de reviso j disponvel e actualmente em consulta pblica, bem como para enquadramento e resoluo de outros aspectos que concorram para a afirmao do regime dos Organismos de Investimento Colectivo em cabo Verde.

Title: Governor's speech at adeco workshop on consumer protection of financial services in Cape Verde
text: Speech of the Governor at the Workshop of ADECO on Consumer Protection of Financial Services in Cape Verde Praia, 2 December 2011 Mr. Chairman of the Board of directors of the Association for Consumer Protection, Exmos representatives and members of ADECO, Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, 1. I am happy to participate in this workshop, focusing on the concern for consumer protection of financial services, a complementary perspective to that of financial stability, the main focus of the Activity of the Bank of Cape Verde, as regulator and supervisor of the national financial system. 2. The Bank of Cape Verde is of interest to the sustainability and stability of this system as a necessary condition for sustained development. However, in order to achieve this great objective, it contributes to the awareness and training of citizens, who must be prepared to take financial decisions and to have responsible conduct, especially with regard to the use of credit. 3. In to ensure that its interests can be protected, the consumer of financial services must first of all be a conscious, well-informed consumer, as the decisions taken by him have impacts not only on an individual level, but also on macroeconomic and financial stability. 4. In order to avoid too much asymmetry in relations between market players, it is for the Bank, on the one hand, to impose clear and transparent information standards and appropriate commercial practices on financial institutions, but also to support the financial consumer to achieve higher levels of information and training so that they are able to make the best decisions, for you and the system. 5. The international financial crisis has shown that, for the proper functioning of the financial system, there needs to be a balance between the interests of financial institutions, whose principles of action must be transparent, and those of bank customers, who must act responsibly, and it is desirable to establish a genuine relationship of trust between them. 6. The prudential supervision exercised by the Bank of Cape Verde shall monitor the activity and financial situation of the institutions that are part of the national system, verifying the conformity of their actions to the standards in force and assessing systemic risks. Following developments at international level in financial systems, the Bank has been creating capacity in the area of behavioral supervision, a strand that has assumed great relevance and relevance following the international financial crisis. 7. In fact, the complexity that characterizes financial products and services today requires a consumer with a high degree of knowledge and information, capable of correctly assessing the options that the market makes available to him and knowingly making his decisions, according to his needs and financial capacity, with advantages either for himself or for his financial institution, while preserving the integrity of the financial system. 8. The promotion of financial literacy in the field of behavioural supervision, complementary to prudential supervision, is therefore in order to better prepare consumers to act in an informed manner, which is essential to increase their ability to assess the nature of financial products and services and to a healthier relationship with the market. 9. The Bank of Cape Verde wishes to see improved not only the standard of quality of services provided to citizens, but also the transparency of market rules and the accuracy of information and, at the same time, consumer protection in relation to abusive practices harmful to their interests and those of the system as a whole. 10. Increasing the level of financial knowledge of the citizen will undoubtedly encourage the adoption of appropriate financial behaviour, which will be a benefit to the consumer and to the efficiency of the financial system. 11. In this perspective, banco de Cabo Verde will always be a partner of consumer associations, as it shares with them the same objective of ensuring a good provision of services by financial institutions, promoting the improvement of the quality of their relationships with their customers and ensuring greater capacity for understanding the rights and duties, enhancing the adequate financial inclusion of the Cape Verdean citizen. 12. I therefore hold this workshop of great importance, for certainly providing the analysis and debate of issues of great relevance for the stability of the financial system and the sustained development of the country. I therefore have a fruitful job this morning.
text_original: Interveno do Governador no workshop da ADECO sobre Proteco dos Consumidores dos Servios Financeiros em Cabo Verde Praia, 2 de Dezembro de 2011 Exmo. Sr. Presidente do Conselho da Direco da Associao para a Defesa do Consumidor, Exmos Senhores representantes e membros da ADECO, Distintos Convidados, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, 1.  com muito gosto que participo nesse workshop, centrado na preocupao de proteco ao consumidor de servios financeiros, perspectiva complementar  da estabilidade financeira, foco principal da actividade do Banco de Cabo Verde, enquanto regulador e supervisor do sistema financeiro nacional. 2. Com efeito, interessa ao Banco de Cabo Verde a sustentabilidade e estabilidade desse sistema, como condio necessria a um desenvolvimento sustentado. Todavia, para que este objectivo seja alcanado muito contribui a sensibilizao e a formao dos cidados, que devem estar preparados a tomar decises financeiras e a terem condutas responsveis, sobretudo no que respeita ao recurso ao crdito. 3. Para que os seus interesses possam ser protegidos, o consumidor de servios financeiros deve, antes de mais, ser um consumidor consciente, bem informado, j que as decises por ele tomadas tm impactos no s a nvel individual, mas tambm na estabilidade macroeconmica e financeira. 4. Procurando evitar demasiada assimetria nas relaes entre os agentes do mercado, cabe ao Banco, por um lado, impor s instituies financeiras normas de informao claras e transparentes e prticas comerciais adequadas, mas tambm apoiar o consumidor financeiro a atingir nveis mais elevados de informao e formao, para que sejam capazes de tomar as melhores decises, para si e para o sistema. 5. A crise financeira internacional veio demonstrar que, para um bom funcionamento do sistema financeiro,  necessrio haver um equilbrio entre os interesses das instituies financeiras, cujos princpios de actuao devem ser transparentes, e os dos clientes bancrios, que devem actuar de forma responsvel, sendo desejvel que se estabelea entre ambos uma verdadeira relao de confiana. 6. A superviso prudencial exercida pelo Banco de Cabo Verde acompanha a actividade e a situao financeira das instituies que integram o sistema nacional, verificando a conformidade das suas actuaes s normas em vigor e avaliando os riscos sistmicos. Acompanhando a evoluo a nvel internacional nos sistemas financeiros, o Banco vem criando capacidade na rea da superviso comportamental, vertente que tem assumido grande actualidade e relevncia na sequncia da crise financeira internacional. 7. De facto, a complexidade que caracteriza hoje os produtos e servios financeiros exige um consumidor com elevado grau de conhecimento e informao, capaz de avaliar correctamente as opes que o mercado lhe disponibiliza e tomar conscientemente as suas decises, de acordo com as suas necessidades e capacidade financeira, com vantagens seja para si prprio, seja para a sua instituio financeira, preservando ao mesmo tempo a integridade do sistema financeiro. 8. A promoo da literacia financeira no mbito da superviso comportamental, complementar  superviso prudencial, enquadra-se, pois, no propsito de melhor preparar o consumidor a actuar de maneira informada, o que  fundamental para aumentar a sua capacidade de avaliar a natureza dos produtos e servios financeiros e para uma relao mais saudvel com o mercado. 9. O Banco de Cabo Verde pretende ver melhorados no s o padro da qualidade de servios prestados aos cidados, como tambm a transparncia das regras do mercado e o rigor na informao e, concomitantemente, a proteco do consumidor em relao a prticas abusivas e lesivas dos seus interesses e dos do sistema no seu todo. 10. O aumento do nvel de conhecimentos financeiros do cidado favorecer, sem dvida, a adopo de comportamentos financeiros adequados, o que ser um benefcio para o consumidor e para a eficincia do sistema financeiro. 11. Nesta perspectiva, o Banco de Cabo Verde ser sempre um parceiro das associaes de consumidores, na medida em que partilha com elas o mesmo objectivo de assegurar uma boa prestao de servios por parte das instituies financeiras, promover a melhoria da qualidade das relaes destas com os seus clientes e garantir maior capacidade de compreenso do consumidor dos seus direitos e deveres, potenciando uma adequada incluso financeira do cidado cabo-verdiano. 12. Por isso, reputo este workshop de muita importncia, por certamente propiciar a anlise e o debate de questes de grande relevncia para a estabilidade do sistema financeiro e o desenvolvimento sustentado do pas. Auguro, pois, um trabalho profcuo durante esta manh.

Title: Message on the occasion of the 20th Anniversary of The Odd
text: Excellency Prime Minister Excellency Mr Mayor of Praia Members of the Board of Directors of iMPAR Dear Guests 1. I am very honored to participate in this dinner commemorating the 20th anniversary of impar and I would like to begin by congratulating all the promoters of this initiative to create the first Cape Verdean private insurer and all its employees, for the effort that has been made for its affirmation and growth. 2. As head of the supervisory and regulatory authority of the Cape Verdean insurance sector, allow me to take the opportunity to highlight the fundamental role of insurance in the economy and the prospects of that sector in Cape Verde. 3. It is important, first of all, to highlight the fundamental role of the insurance business as a mechanism for promoting economic activity, opening up the possibility of transferring risks from economic agents to entities better prepared and dedicated to managing them in aggregate. 4. Despite its shortness - it accounts for less than 2% of GDP - the Cape Verdean insurance market has been growing gradually, with growth rates well above those of the national economy in the period 2005 to 2008 - close to 13% on average. However, it should be noted that 2009 and 2010 had a significant slowdown in growth, which did not exceed 4%. 5. It should be noted that a substantial proportion of the insurance premiums issued (more than one billion escudos in 2010) were returned to policyholders and other beneficiaries, through disability and death compensation payments, disability pensions, property and personal injury, or by making provisions for future payments related to the same eventualities. 6. Prudential guarantees involving the business and requiring companies in the sector to provision (and represent in investment assets) the responsibilities they assume contribute decisively to the financing of the economy, not least because a large part of the asset portfolio focuses on private debt securities, such as corporate bonds. 7. At the end of 2010, the total volume of technical provisions  Life and Non-Life  amounted to close to 2 million contos and the volume of investment assets exceeded 2 million contos (about 2% of GDP), figures that place this sector among the large institutional investors in Cape Verde. 8. In addition, and accounting for neither the VAT incurred with goods and services, nor the IUR withheld in the income from the savings and salaries of its employees, the sector has handed over to the State or to institutions under its supervision (such as the Automobile Guarantee Fund and the Bank of Cape Verde) more than 30 million shields corresponding to income taxes, tax rates payed by insurers and taxes and parafiscal fees payof the insured. 9. Not yet having the final data for 2011, the outlook is for greater growth compared to the previous year. However, one of the main difficulties for which the sector should be prepared is the possible slowdown in economic activity and continued uncertainty in international financial markets, despite the fact that Cape Verde is a country that has been in great stability in recent years in terms of the main macroeconomic indicators and its institutions. 10. In practical terms, the development prospects of the sector should mainly be greater boosting long-term capitalisation insurance, in order to provide for the creation of a robust savings mechanism and to encourage greater preparedness to address risks and uncertainties. 11. It is also essential that operators diversify their products and enhance the efficiency and quality of the service provided, seeking to show their characteristics to consumers. Likewise, they should insurers increasingly invest in new technologies, enabling consumers to offer a range of diversified products tailored to their needs. 12. In performing its role as a regulatory and supervisory body, the Bank of Cape Verde has been making efforts to update and revise industry legislation. Thus, in addition to diplomas such as the law of the insurance contract, the law of access and exercise of the insurance activity, it is worth highlighting the entry into force, in 2010, of the legal regime that regulates the Savings Plans, which, in addition to possible attributions of tax incentives, may contribute to the greater success of these capitalization products. 13. This is all the more relevant if it is taken into account that the structure of insurance production in Cape Verde is essentially based on the Non-Life business, which accounts for about 96 per cent of total production, leaving only 4 per cent to the Vida business. 14. It should also be noted that the new Account Plan based on international financial reporting standards is already in force, which is an essential factor of international competitiveness. 15. I conclude, not without first renewing my congratulations to the Administration of impar and all its employees, who have certainly made an invaluable contribution to the fact that in these 20 years of existence this insurer has proved to be a recognized solid company and has made an important contribution to the growth of the financial market in Cape Verde and the national economy. Thank you very much!
text_original: Excelncia Senhor Primeiro Ministro Excelncia Senhor Presidente da Cmara Municipal da Praia Senhores Membros do Conselho de Administrao da MPAR Caros Convidados 1. Sinto-me muito honrado por participar neste jantar comemorativo do 20. aniversrio da mpar e gostaria de comear por felicitar a todos os promotores desta iniciativa de criao da primeira seguradora privada cabo-verdiana e a todos os seus colaboradores, pelo esforo que tem sido empreendido para a sua afirmao e crescimento. 2. Como responsvel pela autoridade de superviso e regulao do sector segurador cabo-verdiano, permitam-me aproveitar a oportunidade para realar o papel fundamental dos seguros na economia e as perspectivas desse sector em Cabo Verde. 3. Importa, antes de mais, salientar o papel fundamental da actividade seguradora, enquanto mecanismo de promoo da actividade econmica, abrindo a possibilidade de transferir riscos dos agentes econmicos para entidades melhor preparadas e vocacionadas para os gerir de forma agregada. 4. Apesar da sua exiguidade - representa menos de 2% do PIB -, o mercado segurador cabo-verdiano tem vindo a crescer de forma paulatina, apresentando taxas de crescimento bastante superiores s da economia nacional, no perodo de 2005 a 2008 - perto de 13%, em mdia. Ressalve-se, no entanto, que os anos de 2009 e 2010 registaram um abrandamento significativo do crescimento, o qual no ultrapassou os 4%. 5. De realar que uma parte substancial dos prmios de seguro emitidos (mais de um bilio de escudos, em 2010) foi devolvida aos segurados e a outros beneficirios, atravs de pagamentos de indemnizaes por incapacidade e morte, penses por invalidez, danos materiais e corporais, ou atravs da constituio de provises para pagamentos futuros relacionados com as mesmas eventualidades. 6. As garantias prudenciais que envolvem o negcio e que obrigam as empresas do sector a aprovisionar (e representar em activos de investimento) as responsabilidades que assumem, contribuem decisivamente para o financiamento da economia, at porque uma boa parte da carteira de activos se concentra em ttulos de dvida privada, como seja, as obrigaes de empresas. 7. No final de 2010, o volume total das provises tcnicas  Vida e No Vida  ascendia a perto de 2 milhes de contos e o volume de activos de investimento ultrapassava os 2 milhes de contos (cerca de 2% do PIB), nmeros que colocam este sector entre os grandes investidores institucionais em Cabo Verde. 8. Adicionalmente, e no contabilizando nem o IVA suportado com bens e servios, nem o IUR retido nos rendimentos das poupanas e nos salrios dos seus empregados, o sector entregou ao Estado ou a instituies sob sua tutela (como, por exemplo, ao Fundo de Garantia Automvel e ao Banco de Cabo Verde) mais de 30 milhes de escudos correspondentes a impostos sobre o rendimento, taxas parafiscais a cargo das seguradoras e impostos e taxas parafiscais a cargo do segurado. 9. No tendo ainda os dados definitivos de 2011, a perspectiva  de um maior crescimento em relao ao ano anterior. Porm, uma das principais dificuldades para as quais o sector dever estar preparado  o eventual abrandamento da actividade econmica e a continuada incerteza a nvel dos mercados financeiros internacionais, no obstante o facto de Cabo Verde ser um pas que tem vindo a apresentar nos ltimos anos uma grande estabilidade ao nvel dos principais indicadores macro-econmicos e das suas instituies. 10. Em termos prticos, as perspectivas de desenvolvimento do sector devero passar sobretudo por uma maior dinamizao dos seguros de capitalizao de longo prazo, de forma a proporcionar a criao de um mecanismo de poupana robusto e a favorecer maior preparao para enfrentar os riscos e as incertezas. 11.  tambm indispensvel que os operadores diversifiquem os seus produtos e reforcem a eficincia e a qualidade do servio prestado, procurando evidenciar, junto dos consumidores, as caractersticas dos mesmos. Do mesmo modo, devero as seguradoras investir cada vez mais nas novas tecnologias, permitindo oferecer aos consumidores uma gama de produtos diversificados e adaptados s suas necessidades. 12. Desempenhando o seu papel de entidade de regulao e superviso, o Banco de Cabo Verde vem envidando esforos no sentido da actualizao e reviso da legislao do sector. Assim, para alm de diplomas como a lei do contrato de seguro, o de acesso e exerccio da actividade seguradora,  de realar a entrada em vigor, em 2010, do regime jurdico que regula os Planos de Poupana, o que, acrescido a eventuais atribuies de incentivos fiscais, poder contribuir para o maior sucesso desses produtos de capitalizao. 13. Este aspecto  tanto mais relevante se se tiver em conta que a estrutura da produo seguradora em Cabo Verde assenta essencialmente no ramo No vida, que representa cerca de 96 por cento da produo total, deixando apenas 4 por cento ao ramo Vida. 14. De referir ainda que est j em vigor o novo Plano de Contas baseado nas Normas Internacionais do Relato Financeiro, o que constitui um factor essencial de competitividade a nvel internacional. 15. Finalizo, no sem antes renovar as minhas felicitaes  Administrao da mpar e a todos os seus colaboradores, que tm certamente dado um contributo inestimvel para que nesses 20 anos de existncia esta seguradora se tenha revelado uma empresa reconhecidamente slida e tenha dado um contributo importante para o crescimento do mercado financeiro em Cabo Verde e da economia nacional. Muito Obrigado!

Title: Presentation at the Forum organised by the Monetary Authority of Macao
text: Cape Verde: an alternative destination for foreign investment and commercial and financial relations Cape Verde is a small archipelagic country, located about five hundred quiletros from the West African coast. With a population of about half a million, Cape Verde still has an important diaspora residing in Europe and the United States, which greatly contributes to the development of the country. For several years now, the country has been at the level of average income, and is currently experiencing considerable development in terms of education, health and social conditions. It is an economy open to the outside world, with a predominance for the tourism sector, which already accounts for about 21% of gross domestic product. The country enjoys important relations with the outside world, especially the euro zone, its main trading and financial partner, and with important international entities such as the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund. Cape Verde also benefits from a foreign exchange cooperation agreement with Portugal, which ensures the convertibility of the national currency and ensures the adoption of appropriate and credible environmental policies. As a result of these policies, even today, in times of global crisis, Cape Verde enjoys ecological stability, based on an adequate management of external flows, namely tourism, external investment, aid and remittances of emigrants. With regard to the financial system, Cape Verde has a strong and automation monetary authority and is also responsible for supervising all financial activity in the country. The financial system is composed of just over thirty entities, namely banks, insurance companies, stock exchanges, penss fund, among others, structured in an on shore and another offshore. The system offers broad coverage in terms of financial regimes and sectoral instruments and a geographical and demographic penetration of financial services and the degree of banking comparable to or higher than that of countries of the same level of income. In the meantime, there are still some constraints, namely the small size, low competitiveness and diversification, and a strong institutional and sectoral concentration. It is a stable system in terms of activity, solvency and profitability, and assets and credits are growing at 10% per year, the solvency ratio reaches 13.9%, and the profitability of assets and capital sums reach 0.6% and 7.1%, respectively. However, it notes some emerging risks, such as non-stop credit, which reaches 6.9% of the portfolio, as well as concentration and sectoral dependence, in particular in relation to the tourism real estate sector. It also faces other challenges arising from uncertainty regarding flows of resources from abroad. As part of the construction of an externally intensive service economy, the national authorities' vision for the development of the financial system is based on five basic principles: i. Improved regulation and enhanced supervision, in line with international principles and practices, in particular the European Union, the country's main trading and financial partner; ii. Greater competitiveness of the system; iii. Greater financial inclusion; iv. improving funding for the private sector, in particular microand small and medium-sized enterprises; in. Improvements in other areas relevant to the system, namely those related to the investment and business environment. On the basis of these principles, the development of the system is based on a strategy with structuring interventions in three areas, namely: a. Promoting the credibility and competitiveness of the system, essential attributes sought by eco-workers, in particular non-residents; b. Development of Cape Verde as an international business center, capitalizing on the advantages offered by the country (location, climate, governance, political and ecological stability, human resources, ...); c. Improving access to finance and reducing the financial costs faced by microand small enterprises, allowing the national business community to participate in investment and increase employment. In the framework of this strategy, a number of measures and activities have been implemented, including: reform of financial legislation, introducing modern principles and practices in insurance, capital markets, preventing and combating money laundering and terrorist financing; adoption of modern practices, such as macroprudential supervision and risk-based supervision, as well as strengthening the central bank's authority to ensure the stability of the system and protect depositors; Review of taxation for certain specialised financial activities such as investment funds, venture capital and asset management; Consolidation and institutional strengthening for the promotion of micro and small business. In line with the measures already implemented, others are being developed and will be implemented in a future prime, among which is the regulation of the superintendence of the payment system, the introduction of a system of guarantee of depitos, the improvement of the regulation of the non-banking financial sector, and the operationalization of the credit guarantee system through the installation of plicas entities recently created in this area. In addition to the measures referred to, related to the financial system itself, initiatives are underway in other areas with influence on financial activity. These initiatives include: ii. Review and regulation of trade legislation, adopting international standards and specific solutions appropriate to the national reality; iii. Reduction of administrative barriers to investment: simplification of procedures in the constitution and operation of companies, international transactions, conflict resolution; iv. Improving the promotion of the country as an international center of businesses (strengthening of regulation, introduction of a legal framework with international acceptance, new corporate models, expansion of incentives, institutional reinforcement for the care of external investors, among others. In conclusion, Cape Verde makes available to potential external partners an attractive destination for investments and businesses, based on the following attributes: i. Openness abroad, with good governance and a development strategy based on private initiative and the internationalization of the economy; ii. a dynamic financial system geared to national development needs and demand from non-residents; iii. Ample opportunities for foreign investment and trade and financial relations, a credible alternative to the crisis in Europe. In other words, Cape Verde offers good prospects for financial cooperation with Macao and China, with potential advantages for both parties.

Title: The protection of consumers of financial services in a context of international financial crisis in the light of bcv performance
text: Lecture on "Protection of consumers of financial services in a context of international crisis: Cape Verdean experience with enhancement to the role of the Bank of Cape Verde" Beach, March 15, 2013 Mr. Governor's Speech 0. Congratulations to the Foundation "Law and Justice" for the initiative of the event and thanks for the opportunity to participate as speaker 1. Consumer law: Origins and evolution  "The consumer, by definition, we are all n," John Kennedy solemnly proclaimed in a speech delivered to the U.S. Congress on March 15, 1962. And he went on to present his vision of what consumer rights should be. For the first time a politician has drawn attention to the issue of consumer rights  Over the years, Kennedy's vision has helped shape the eight consumer rights that guide us today: meeting basic needs, safety, information, choice, hearing, compensation, education, and a healthy environment  March 15  International Consumer Day: celebrated from 1983 worldwide. Guided by a central theme for each year, various activities are carried out on that day to raise awareness and promote consumer rights  1980s: a marked evolution in the paradigm, with the eight rights being complemented by five consumer responsibilities: critical awareness, involvement, social responsibility, eco-responsibility and solidarity. The idea that consumers should not be passive persons of the dynamics affecting them has thus been introduced, but they must also play an active role in this same reality 2. Consumer protection of financial services in a context of international financial crisis  The international financial crisis that plagued the world between 2008 and 2010, and whose effects on the ecological and social sphere are still felt with great intensity, had three main causes: (i) failures in the regulation and supervision of financial activity, (ii) inappropriate behavior on the part of customers and (iii) inadequate risk management by banks and other financial intermediaries o Example: sub-prime credit, a poor financial product (high risk) marketed to misinformed consumers and using inadequate techniques (unqualified agents, teaser interest rates, deferral of capital, ...). With the bursting of the housing bubble, the widespread and consequent failure of many credit institutions was to burst, with tax consequences and in terms of the availability of financial services, which in turn affect consumers  Reflecting this reality, in the last three years, the central theme of the celebrations of International Consumer Day has been dominated by the financial dimension, reflecting concern about the impacts of the international financial crisis on people's well-being  The international financial crisis has led to the questioning of the market efficiency hipesis and the rationality of the agents, underlying most econic models  As a result of this awareness, more attention is now paid to Behavioral Economics, i.e., the analysis of consumer behavior based on psychological or emotional factors, thus admitting the possibility of cognitive errors and limitations and, in this way, better understanding the current reality  According to the EC, consumer behavior can depart from "normal", e.g. unconventional preferences, distorted perception of reality or an inefficient decision-making process, resulting in exaggerated optimism and misperception of risk, which in turn lead to insufficient savings and excessive indebtedness  These conclusions justify and enable a more intrusive regulation, promoting products with appropriate incentives or rules aimed at guiding consumers to more appropriate behaviors. Examples of this turning point: or USA: a real revolution in regulation and supervision, aiming to bring the financial sector closer to the real economy and protect consumers. Examples:  Approval of wall street reform law Consumer Protection  Creation of the Federal Agency for the Protection of Consumers of Financial Services  Conctpetous measures: regulation of Hedge Funds or European Union: the harmonisation of practices in retail banking markets is ongoing, promoting market integration in the EU and consumer protection. Specific initiatives:  Creation of Community-wide supervisory entities (EBA, ESMA, EIOPA)  Mortgage Credit Directive  Regulation of complex financial products  Review of taeg calculation methodology  Introduction of minimum banking services or Portugal: intensive legislative action underway to strengthen the protection of consumer rights, including, for example:  Marketing of complex financial products  Maximum interest rates on consumer credit  best practices to be observed by banks in the context of optional associated sales (bundling) 3. The role of the Bank of Cape Verde  In addition to preventing systemic risk and promoting efficient and transparent markets, the protection of consumer rights is one of the three basic principles of financial regulation  As the international financial crisis has been bitterly taught, these three principles are closely related to each other, so concerted action on these three strands has successful hipsis  That is why the BCV, as responsible for the stability of the financial system, is also obliged to actively engage in promoting the rights of consumers of financial services  In line with this concern, the BCV has actively participated directly or indirectly in promoting and defending consumer rights in financial services  Indirect intervention: participation in the development, approval and implementation of various regulations related to the problem, including, in particular: or Regulatory Decree on Interest (1993) or Legal regime for consumer protection and protection (1998); or Standard on Consumer Credit, currently in the forge, under the initiative and leadership of ADECO: The BCV is available to continue to participate in this process, namely integrating a Working Group for the drafting of the proposed Law  Direct intervention: or Notice regulating the system of the authorities to be charged by credit institutions (1994) or Notice regulating the information to be provided by institutions to customers (1999) or Creation of a Financial Services Consumer Support Office - GAP or Action against collection of unjustified expenses by banks (2011) or Notice on the pricing of credit institutions (in the forge)  Modernises important aspects of the relationship between credit institutions and their customers, in particular the committees and the provision of information, aspects currently regulated by regulations approved in 1994 and 1999, respectively  It determines the free banking services to be provided by credit institutions, in particular: Opening depito accounts Providing one account statement per month Updating customer data Intra-bank transfers Account closure Online account query by customer Payment operations through POS or Notice of information relating to interest rates and costs of credit operations (in forge)  It aims to ensure market transparency by providing a set of comparable and standardized information that must be ensured by credit institutions, allowing comparative judgments by customers  It defines the minimum information to be included in credit agreements, in particular: Amount and purpose of financing Terms and method of reimbursement Nero and periodicity of benefits Operation guarantees TAN, TAE e TAEG Criterion for determining the interest rate in case of late payment  Rules to be observed in credit offer advertising, including the indication of TAE and TAEG  Information to be provided by CI during the term of the contract, namely amount of outstanding capital and modification of contractual conditions  The Bank has also been actively participating in the debate on the issue of consumer protection in the international institutions, in particular at the level of central banks of CPLP countries 4. BCV action in practice  GAP's action: gap's main task is to respond to customer complaints and act to resolve them. In 2012, 241 complaints were answered, resulting in the return of about 2,700 contos to consumers by banks as a result of complaints handled by the Cabinet  In addition, GAP has been actively contributing to consumer awareness and training, and it is important to highlight the dissemination of a Consumer Guide and a Brochure on o Housing Credit, the treatment of frequently asked questions through the BCV website, among other  However, the BCV does not merely address complaints about unacceptable practices on the part of banks and the awareness-raising actions referred to herein. The essence of the Bank's action on the promotion and protection of consumer rights takes on a strategic and preventive character and includes: or Monitoring of national ecological and financial developments, in particular with regard to the situation of phasing finances, and action accordingly, in particular by issuing recommendations on plyo indebtedness. This is because in a small country with a strong state weight in the economy, fiscal sustainability is one of the main conditioning factors for the stability of the financial system and, in this way, a decisive element with regard to consumer rights  Example: about 10 years ago, as a result of the slippage in the finances, the state was indebted to the banks at an interest rate of 12%, thus making it difficult for private clients to access financing. Credit to the private sector was very difficult and much more expensive, for example, interest rates on home loans were approaching 14%. Today, as a result of better management of finances, the state is less indebted, and at an interest rate of around 4%. As a result of this state downtime in the credit market, access to finance by private clients becomes easier and less expensive. Returning to the example of housing credit, today credit is achieved at rates below 10%. More funding and lower cost represents an important advance in customer rights. or Improving monetary policy by promoting appropriate behaviour on the part of financial institutions, with clear impacts on the quality and prices of services offered by them  In this way, the BCV dispenses considerable efforts and resources so that banks have liquidity in quantity and at attractive costs to private clients  Similarly, through the Minimum Cash Availability scheme  unpaid requirements that commercial banks are obliged to keep with the BCV and which are currently represent 18% of customer complaints to banks  bcv also ends up ensuring that a part of these pits is always safely stored with the central bank or Effective oversight of the payment system, either through regular and inspective action or through investments in modern payment infrastructures, through SISP, in order to ensure payment services appropriate to the needs of a modern economy and society  Thanks to this action and investments, we can all have access today to a set of payment services that facilitate our daily lives and allow us to free up time and effort for activities we desire; without dida another important achievement for the consumer of financial services or Improving regulation and strengthening supervision of financial activity, in line with the principles of efficient and transparent markets, systemic risk prevention and consumer protection  As regards improving regulation and strengthening supervision, and always on the basis of relevant international standards and practices, the BCV has been very active, and actions should be highlighted to: or Recent modernisation of insurance legislation or Securities Market Cigo Review o Revision of the Banking Law: currently in the forge, and two draft laws were recently completed by the BCV and submitted to the Government for approval; or Permanent training of supervisory staff; or Improvement of systems and creation of other working conditions in the area of supervision  Among the innovations that are part of the preliminary draft revision of the Banking Law mentioned above, the introduction of Behavioral Supervision should be highlighted  Without neglecting the importance of Prudential Supervision, oriented to the soundness and solvency of credit institutions, bcv has been, in parallel and in line with the requirements of the current situation, to promote the introduction of Behavioral Supervision, which focuses on the conduct of institutions and the relationships of these institutions with their customers, in order to avoid the rights of consumers to be harmed  Under this new approach, with the adoption of the new legislation, the BCV will explicitly exercise specific powers in behavioral supervision, including in particular: or Issue specific instructions and determinations regarding advertising and general contractual clauses that do not comply with the law, instruct their ordination proceedings, apply their sanctions, order the suspension of illegal advertising actions, and other related powers or Issue instructions on the conduct cigos to be adopted by credit institutions in their relationship with the customers, and to set, by notice, guidelines for this purpose or Analyze the conduct cigos submitted by the institutions to the BCV or Require the introduction of changes to the conduct cigos submitted as it deems necessary to ensure the proper fulfilment of the objectives underlying them  Another issue on the agenda that is currently being examined in depth by the BCV is the possibility of introducing an explicit system for guaranteeing the 5. Final considerations  General gifts quests  Comments on ongoing measures or forge  Availability of the BCV to continue to share with the various stakholders the initiatives in charge of the institution;  BCV relies on stakeholders to help form and execute its action in this area;  The BCV will be available to continue to participate in the debate as part of its mission with a view to increasingly improving the situation of consumer rights in Cape Verde.

Parabns  Fundao Direito e Justia pela iniciativa do evento e agradecimentos pela oportunidade para participar como orador 1. Direito dos consumidores: Origens e evoluo  O consumidor, por definio, somos todos n, proclamou solenemente John Kennedy num discurso proferido no Congresso americano no dia 15 de Maro de 1962. E prosseguiu apresentando a sua viso do que devem ser os direitos dos consumidores. Pela primeira vez um poltico chamou ateno para a problemtica dos direitos do consumidor  Ao longo dos anos, a viso de Kennedy contribuiu para enformar os oito direitos do consumidor que hoje nos orientam: satisfao das necessidades bsicas, segurana, informao, opo, audio, compensao, educao e ambiente saudvel  15 de Maro  Dia Internacional do Consumidor: celebrado a partir de 1983 em todo o mundo. Orientando-se por um tema central para cada ano, so nesse dia realizadas actividades diversas de sensibilizao e promoo dos direitos dos consumidores  Dcada de 80: uma evoluo marcante no paradigma, com os oito direitos passando a ser complementados por cinco responsabilidades dos consumidores: conscincia crtica, envolvimento, responsabilidade social, responsabilidade ecolica e solidariedade. Introduziu-se assim a ideia de que os consumidores no devem ser sujeitos passivos da dinmica que os afecta mas tambm devem ter um papel activo nesta mesma realidade 2. Proteco dos consumidores de servios financeiros num contexto de crise financeira internacional  A crise financeira internacional que flagelou o mundo entre 2008 e 2010, e cujos efeitos na esfera econica e social ainda se fazem sentir com forte intensidade, teve na sua origem trs causas principais: (i) falhas na regulao e superviso da actividade financeira, (ii) comportamento inadequado por parte dos clientes e (iii) inadequada gesto do risco por parte dos bancos e outros intermedirios financeiros o Exemplo: o crdito sub-prime, produto financeiro de m qualidade (alto risco) comercializado junto de consumidores mal informados e utilizando tcnicas inadequadas (agentes no qualificados, teaser interest rates, diferimento do capital, ).
