Title: Intervention at the inauguration as Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde
text: Intervention in the inauguration act as Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde, 29 December 2014 Madam Minister for Finance and Planning, Representatives of the Diplomatic Corps, Members of the Board of Directors, the Supervisory Board and the Advisory Board, Representatives of bcv workers, Representatives of financial institutions, Guest Gentlemen, Ladies and gentlemen, Let us first express our confidence in us by the Government for the exercise of such high functions as Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde, which we thank. We are well aware of the delicacy and challenges of the international and Cape Verdean economic, financial and banking environment. Thus, we feel even more honored and motivated by the confidence that this appointment reveals, so much more we will engage in the service of the country, the institution for which we have been appointed, as well as the solidity and deepening of the financial sector. Developments in the Cape Verdean economy are strongly conditioned by the conjuncture and framework of international economic and financial policies, especially in the European Union, from which markets derive about 90% of capital inflows for investment and a large part of emigrant remittances and official development assistance. In this context, the international economic and financial crisis and the euro area sovereign debt crisis that followed it contributed to the slowdown in growth, at the same time, which made it undeferred to urgently overcome the great structural constraints existing in the national economy. It is now agreed that inflation and uncertainty about future inflation impose costs on society, particularly by the puncture exerted on the purchasing power of citizens, particularly for the most disadvantaged, in addition to its harmful effects on the competitiveness of the country's economy. Under the Organic Law, the main attribution of the BCV is to maintain price stability. Secondary allocation means promoting liquidity, solvency and the proper functioning of a financial system based on market stability. The proper functioning of the financial market lacks proper regulation and supervision as a necessary condition for the proper allocation of financial resources in the economy. In Cape Verde, the BCV is also responsible for supervising the financial system, having powers to approve directives for the action of supervised entities, to carry out inspections and investigations, to establish and investigate cases concerning the infringements verified and the application of penalties corresponding to them, where they do not constitute crimes. It is also up to the BCV to participate in the definition of monetary and exchange rate policies, which are executed with full autonomy, that is, without external interference, using only and exclusively appropriate policy instruments, namely interest rates, cash reserves, securities purchase and sale operations. The proper functioning of the BCV is thus fundamental for the performance of the economy, the development of the country and the improvement of the level of well-being of Cape Verdeans. The Government has established the defence of the fixed parity of the national currency against the Euro as an objective of monetary policy. We believe that this exchange rate regime is the most appropriate for an economy like ours, because it is a small open economy and an external price taker, the loss of the exchange rate instrument does not represent a significant additional cost in terms of the loss of degrees of freedom in the conduct of economic policy. Moreover, this regime, due to exchange rate stability, favours trade and foreign investment, in addition to being transparent and easier to manage. In this context, it is for the BCV to conduct monetary policy in such a way that, first, it constitutes and maintains a level of foreign exchange reserves necessary for the credibility of the exchange rate regime adopted. The economic regime in force in the country, based on monetary and exchange rate stability, requires a fiscal policy that is in accordanfront, this is characterized by rigor, discipline and sustainability. Thus, in view of the weight of the State's financial operations in overall demand and the balance of payments, close cooperation between the Government and the BCV is required. On the one hand, the BCV must take into account the Government's fiscal policy, without this meaning that monetary policy is to be in place for fiscal policy. In turn, state fiscal policy should be on the sustainability of public debt and the search for solutions to long-term budgetary pressures, in particular those arising from social policies and pension responsibilities. In addition, our exchange rate regime presupposes adjustment mechanisms on the real economy side in order to ensure its sustainability, so that the country is challenged to overcome the qualitative structural constraints to its economic growth, in order to increase the weight of tradable goods and services. However, the maintenance of the current parity of the shield against the euro will ultimately depend on the positive development of the competitiveness of the national economy. Therefore, it is imperative to reduce the costs of context to conduct business in Cape Verde, and the increase in trend productivity. This will only be possible by correcting the still existing imbalances and re-structuring sectors and enterprises. Improving the quality of institutions is also decisive in attracting the much-desired and necessary foreign direct investment as a way to accelerate the growth process. The BCV, as a central bank and part of the public governance system, should always keep in mind that the objective of monetary policy is not an end in itself, but rather aimed at promoting economic growth and poverty reduction. In this particular, it should be noted that if inflation devours purchasing power and creates uncertainty, deflation, in turn, is no less pernicious, because it discourages productive investments so necessary for economic development. We therefore believe that monetary policy should ensure price stability without, however, inhibiting the conduct of business. The financial system is very relevant to economic growth given its role in mobilising savings, allocating and monitoring resource use. Today it is no longer a secret to anyone that an efficient and developed financial system increases the total productivity of factors, that is, resource efficiency. With reference to the relative volume of financial assets, it can be said that Cape Verde has already achieved a reasonable level of financial development. However, the financial system consists fundamentally of the banking system and lacks dynamic and sophistication, as required by this sector, the ongoing process of transformation of the country. In fact, enormous difficulties in accessing credit persist. Interest rates remain high, even in a context of very low inflation as is currently the case and an accommodative monetary policy, which leads us to question the effectiveness of monetary transmission policies. It is therefore important to promote greater openness and diversification of the financial system to other operators in order to make the sector more competitive and competitive. In this way, we will also be creating conditions for investors' access to long-term capital, as well as access to the international capital market. The dynamic of the financial system requires the existence of investment instruments alternative to traditional and complementary ones. At present, many of these instruments have already been legally created, namely securities and real estate funds, factoring, leasing. However, it is important to operationalize and dynamic, as well as venture capital, pension funds and new financial products in the insurance area. The operationalisation and promotion of these financial products seems to us to be an important factor in promoting a diversified securities market, and the bcv is now available to actively contribute to this process as a partner of the Government. At international level, the financial sector is rapidly changing and is facing increasingly complex challenges, particularly in the field of supervision. The BCV will pay special attention to supervision by strengthening and improving the means and instruments of intervention and monitoring of supervised institutions, with a view to ensuring the stability and solvency of the financial system, as well as the protection of deposits. In this context, it is important, on the one hand, to develop and operationalise the rules on the banking crisis resolution scheme, as well as the deposit guarantee scheme, as provided for in the Basic Law of the Financial System recently adopted by the National Assembly last April. The BCV as the Government's Financial Advisor will not fail to develop technical studies related to deposit guarantee and the financing of resolution measures to be proposed to the Government. On the other hand, we must closely monitor the adequacy of the corporate governance of financial institutions, as well as the capacities and motivations of the people who lead it. It is necessary to constantly assess the risks that exist in the balance sheet or, where appropriate, if they are appropriate and what management we make of them. It is important to create and verify the internal rules and their compliance. It is urgent to fully inform customers and counterparts. These must be permanent tasks and today more than ever are an essential condition of financial activity. And above all, we must act according to irreprehensible ethical principles. There is a need to make a demanding diagnosis of the capacities of each institution and, from it, put into practice with determination the necessary measures. In addition, as Governor, I will try to contribute to strengthening bcv supervision in three important qualities, including: Dialogue, that is, ability to establish and maintain quality communication with institutions and with the market, to know people, strategies and business, in order to better adapt reporting mechanisms and better monitor risks, minimizing bureaucratic burdens. Humility, to know who develops the financial activity, without losing critical capacity and the necessary exemption in the analysis. Rigor, that is, maximum prudence in setting the targets, in the requirement of compliance, in the evaluation of behaviors and, when necessary, in the sanction. BCV workers are a key asset of the institution. I would like to convey to you my deep conviction that the Bank has never needed its employees so much to fulfil its high functions in an increasingly complex and demanding context. All are called and motivated, to contribute their performance to the efficiency of the institution. In addition to the recognized external challenges, the BCV faces important internal challenges. We would highlight the structuring of its pension fund in the perspective of ensuring its future sustainability, the improvement of the financial situation of the institution, the permanent and relevant training of employees and the improvement of the work climate. I am convinced that, with rigour and firmness in the management, dialogue and involvement of all in the life of the institution, we will together overcome these challenges. Certain that we can count on the support of the Government, the other members of the Board of Directors, all the Bank's employees and the committed cooperation of the financial system and the other entities with which the BCV relates we are committed to working with total commitment, loyalty and dedication to the service of the public interest and the country. Finally, let me express my gratitude for the work done by the outgoing Governor, Dr. Carlos Burgo, as well as for the other Governors who preceded me in this position. Thank you for your attention! Beach, December 29, 2014
text_original: Interveno no ato de tomada de posse como Governador do Banco de Cabo Verde, 29 de Dezembro de 2014 Senhora Ministra das Finanas e do Planeamento, Senhores Representantes do Corpo Diplomtico, Senhores Membros do Conselho de Administrao, do Conselho Fiscal e do Conselho Consultivo, Senhores Representantes dos trabalhadores do BCV, Senhores Representantes das Instituies Financeiras, Senhores Convidados, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Permitam-nos, antes de mais, exprimir a confiana em ns depositada pelo Governo, para o exerccio de to elevadas funes de Governador do Banco de Cabo Verde, que agradecemos. Estamos bem cientes da delicadeza e dos desafios da conjuntura econmica, financeira e bancria internacional e cabo-verdiana. Assim, sentimo-nos ainda mais honrados e motivados com a confiana que esta nomeao revela, pelo que tanto mais nos empenharemos ao servio do Pas, da instituio para a qual fomos nomeados, bem como da solidez e aprofundamento do sector financeiro. A evoluo da economia cabo-verdiana  fortemente condicionada pela conjuntura e pelo enquadramento das polticas econmicas e financeiras internacionais, sobretudo na Unio Europeia, de cujos mercados provm cerca de 90% dos influxos de capitais para investimento e grande parte de remessas dos emigrantes e de ajuda pblica ao desenvolvimento. Neste contexto, a crise econmica e financeira internacional e a crise da dvida soberana na rea do euro que lhe sucedeu contriburam para o abrandamento do crescimento, ao mesmo tempo, que tornaram inadivel a superao urgente dos grandes constrangimentos estruturais existentes na economia nacional.  hoje consensual que a inflao e a incerteza em relao  inflao futura impem custos  sociedade, nomeadamente pela puno exercida sobre o poder de compra dos cidados, particularmente para os mais desfavorecidos, para alm dos seus efeitos nefastos sobre a competitividade da economia do Pas. Nos termos da Lei Orgnica, a principal atribuio do BCV consiste na manuteno da estabilidade dos preos. A atribuio secundria traduz-se em promover a liquidez, a solvncia e o funcionamento adequado de um sistema financeiro assente na estabilidade do mercado. O adequado funcionamento do mercado financeiro carece de regulao e superviso apropriadas como condio necessria para uma correcta afectao dos recursos financeiros na economia. Em Cabo Verde, ao BCV compete tambm a superviso do sistema financeiro, dispondo para o efeito de poderes de aprovao de directivas para a actuao das entidades supervisionadas, de realizao de inspeces e averiguaes, de instaurao e instruo dos processos respeitantes s infraces verificadas e de aplicao de sanes correspondentes s mesmas, quando no constituem crimes. Cabe ainda ao BCV participar na definio das polticas monetria e cambial, as quais so executadas com total autonomia, ou seja, sem interferncias externas, recorrendo nica e exclusivamente a instrumentos de poltica adequados, designadamente as taxas de juro, as reservas de caixa, as operaes de compra e venda de ttulos. O bom funcionamento do BCV , assim, fundamental para o desempenho da economia, o desenvolvimento do Pas e a melhoria do nvel de bem-estar dos cabo-verdianos. O Governo fixou a defesa da paridade fixa da moeda nacional em relao ao Euro como objectivo da poltica monetria. Julgamos ser este regime cambial o mais adequado para uma economia como a nossa, porquanto sendo uma pequena economia aberta e tomadora de preos externos, a perda do instrumento cambial no representa um custo adicional significativo em termos de perda de graus de liberdade na conduo da poltica econmica. Outrossim, este regime, em virtude da estabilidade cambial, favorece as trocas comerciais e o investimento externo, para alm de ser transparente e de mais fcil gesto. Nesse quadro, compete ao BCV conduzir a poltica monetria de forma a, em primeiro lugar, constituir e manter um nvel de reservas cambiais necessrio  credibilidade do regime cambial adoptado. O regime econmico vigente no Pas, assente na estabilidade monetria e cambial, requer uma poltica oramental que lhe seja consentnea, isto  caracterizada pelo rigor, disciplina e sustentabilidade. Assim, tendo ainda em conta o peso das operaes financeiras do Estado na procura global e na balana de pagamentos, impe-se uma estreita cooperao entre o Governo e o BCV. Por um lado, o BCV deve ter em considerao a poltica oramental do Governo, sem que isso signifique uma acomodao da poltica monetria  poltica oramental. Por sua vez, a poltica oramental do Estado deve ter em vista a sustentabilidade da dvida pblica e a procura de solues para as presses oramentais de longo prazo, nomeadamente as decorrentes das polticas sociais e das responsabilidades a nvel das penses de reforma. Para alm disso, o nosso regime cambial pressupe mecanismos de ajustamento do lado da economia real, por forma a assegurar a sua sustentabilidade, pelo que se coloca ao Pas o desafio da superao qualitativa dos constrangimentos estruturais ao seu crescimento econmico, no sentido do aumento do peso dos bens e servios transacionveis. Porm, a manuteno da paridade actual do escudo face ao euro depender, em ltima instncia, da evoluo positiva da competitividade da economia nacional. Assim sendo, constituem um imperativo a reduo dos custos de contexto  realizao de negcios em Cabo Verde, e o aumento da produtividade tendencial. Isso s ser possvel com a correco dos desequilbrios ainda existentes e a re-estruturao de sectores e empresas. A melhoria da qualidade das instituies  tambm decisiva para atrair o to almejado e necessrio investimento directo estrangeiro, como forma de acelerar o processo de crescimento. O BCV, enquanto banco central e parte do sistema de governao pblica, dever ter sempre presente que o objectivo da poltica monetria no  um fim em si, mas sim visa favorecer o crescimento econmico e a reduo da pobreza. Neste particular convm referir que se a inflao devora o poder de compra e cria incertezas, a deflao, por seu turno, no  menos perniciosa, por desencorajar investimentos produtivos to necessrios ao desenvolvimento econmico. Entendemos pois que a poltica monetria dever garantir a estabilidade dos preos sem, no entanto, inibir a realizao de negcios. O sistema financeiro  muito relevante para o crescimento econmico dado o seu papel na mobilizao das poupanas, na alocao e monitorizao do uso dos recursos. Hoje j no  segredo para ningum que um sistema financeiro eficiente e desenvolvido aumenta a produtividade total dos factores, isto , a eficincia na utilizao dos recursos. Tendo como referncia o volume relativo dos activos financeiros, pode-se dizer que Cabo Verde alcanou j um nvel razovel de desenvolvimento financeiro. Porm, o sistema financeiro consiste fundamentalmente no sistema bancrio e carece de dinamizao e de sofisticao, tal qual exige, desse sector, o processo em curso de transformao do Pas. Com efeito, persistem enormes dificuldades de acesso ao crdito. As taxas de juro continuam elevadas, mesmo num contexto de muito baixa inflao como se verifica actualmente e de uma poltica monetria acomodatcia, o que nos leva a questionar a eficcia das polticas de transmisso monetria. Importa, assim, promover uma maior abertura e diversificao do sistema financeiro a outros operadores para tornar o sector mais competitivo e concorrencial. Por essa via, estaremos tambm a criar condies de acesso dos investidores a capitais de longo prazo, assim como de acesso ao mercado internacional de capitais. A dinamizao do sistema financeiro requer a existncia de instrumentos de investimento alternativos aos tradicionais e complementares destes. Actualmente, muitos desses instrumentos j foram legalmente criados, nomeadamente os fundos mobilirios e imobilirios, o factoring, o leasing. Porm, importa a sua operacionalizao e dinamizao, bem como o capital de risco, o fundo de penses e novos produtos financeiros na rea seguradora. A operacionalizao e dinamizao desses produtos financeiros afigura-se-nos como um importante factor de promoo de um mercado diversificado de valores mobilirios, pelo que fica, desde j, manifesta a disponibilidade do BCV para, enquanto parceiro do Governo, contribuir activamente nesse processo. A nvel internacional, o sector financeiro encontra-se em rpida mutao e atravessa desafios cada vez mais complexos, particularmente no domnio de superviso. O BCV dar uma ateno muito especial  superviso, reforando e aperfeioando os meios e instrumentos de interveno e de acompanhamento das instituies supervisionadas, com vista a garantir a estabilidade e solvncia do sistema financeiro, assim como a proteco dos depsitos. Neste quadro, importa, por um lado, desenvolver e operacionalizar as normas relativas ao regime de resoluo de crises bancrias, bem como ao regime de garantia de depsitos, alis tal qual previsto na Lei de Bases do Sistema Financeiro aprovado recentemente pela Assembleia nacional, no passado ms de Abril. O BCV enquanto Conselheiro Financeiro do Governo no deixar de desenvolver estudos tcnicos relacionados com a garantia de depsitos e com o financiamento de medidas de resoluo a serem propostos ao Governo. Por outro lado, deve-se acompanhar de perto a adequao do governo societrio das instituies financeiras, bem como das capacidades e motivaes das pessoas que o protagonizam.  necessrio avaliar permanentemente os riscos que existem no balano ou, eventualmente, fora dele, se so apropriados e qual  a gesto que deles fazemos. Importa criar e verificar as regras internas e o seu cumprimento. Urge informar cabalmente clientes e contrapartes. Estas tm de ser tarefas permanentes e hoje mais do que nunca so condio essencial da actividade financeira. E, acima de tudo, temos de actuar de acordo com princpios ticos irrepreensveis. H necessidade de se fazer um diagnstico exigente das capacidades de cada instituio e, a partir dele, pr em prtica com determinao as medidas necessrias. Para alm disso, enquanto Governador, tentarei contribuir para o reforo da superviso do BCV em trs importantes qualidades, a saber: Dilogo, isto , capacidade de estabelecer e manter comunicao de qualidade com as instituies e com o mercado, para conhecer as pessoas, as estratgias e os negcios, a fim de melhor adaptar os mecanismos de reporte e melhor acompanhar riscos, minimizando cargas burocrticas. Humildade, para saber ouvir quem desenvolve a actividade financeira, sem perder capacidade crtica e a iseno necessria na anlise. Rigor, ou seja, mxima prudncia na fixao das metas, na exigncia do seu cumprimento, na avaliao dos comportamentos e, quando necessrio, na sano. Os trabalhadores do BCV so um activo fundamental da instituio. Queria transmitir-lhes a minha profunda convico de que nunca como hoje, o Banco precisou tanto dos seus colaboradores para cumprir com as suas elevadas funes, num contexto cada vez mais complexo e exigente. Todos so chamados e motivados, a contribuir com o seu desempenho para a eficincia da instituio. Para alm dos reconhecidos desafios externos, o BCV tem pela frente desafios internos importantes. Destacaramos a estruturao do seu fundo de penses na perspectiva de garantia da sua sustentabilidade futura, a melhoria da situao financeira da instituio, a capacitao permanente e pertinente dos colaboradores e a melhoria do clima laboral. Estou convencido que, com rigor e firmeza na gesto, dilogo e envolvimento de todos na vida da instituio iremos, em conjunto, ultrapassar esses desafios. Certos de que podemos contar com o apoio do Governo, dos restantes membros do Conselho de Administrao, de todos os colaboradores do Banco e com a cooperao empenhada do sistema financeiro e das demais entidades com que o BCV se relaciona assumimos o compromisso de trabalhar com empenho, lealdade e dedicao totais ao servio do interesse pblico e do Pas. Para finalizar, permitam-me manifestar o meu reconhecimento pelo trabalho efectuado pelo Governador cessante, Dr. Carlos Burgo, bem como pelos demais Governadores que me antecederam neste cargo. Obrigado pela vossa ateno! Praia, 29 de Dezembro de 2014

Title: Speech at the Press Conference on monetary loosening measures
text: COMMUNIQUe SUBJECT: MONETARY LOOSENING MEASURES 1. The Cape Verdean economy is strongly influenced by the dynamics of the international economy, most nomore in the Eurozone. 2. In this context, the persistent economic and financial crisis in the Euro Area has contributed to the slowdown in growth in the national economy, while at the same time the urgent overcoming of existing constraints is indeferred. 3. Despite some progress, Cape Verde continues to face major challenges in its development process in the face of declining public and private investment and, consequently, the weak dynamism of economic activity. 4. Thus, in order to ensure more robust internal growth in the near future, it is imperative, among other situations, that active and effective policy measures for the use of available resources be adopted. 5. With the support of benign developments in inflation and external accounts, the BCV has been implementing, since May 2013, a moderate policy of monetary loosening. It has used permanent deposit and lending facilities, as well as the issuance of own securities, as essential instruments to influence the decision of commercial banks and manage liquidity in the banking system. 6. However, the transmission of monetary policy measures to the real economy has not been desirable, due to both structural constraints and the unfavorable macro-financial environment. 7. The insufficient development of the financial system, the cost of funding banks and the incipient stage of development of the interbank market and the secondary market for short-term public debt significantly reduce the effectiveness of monetary policy interventions. 8. In turn, the current macro-financial environment, conducive to worsening credit and macroeconomic risks and the maintenance of the surplus liquidity of the banking system, hinders the process of financial intermediation. This results in worsening effects on the dynamics of economic activity, together with the persistence of high operational and context costs for the financial sector. 9. Under the current exchange rate regime, the Bank of Cape Verde assigns, in its monetary rule, a necessarily high weighting to the inflation deviation component, bringing the country's inflation expectations closer to the euro area's expectations. 10. After a period of relatively high rates in 2011 and 2012, average annual inflation began, from the second quarter of 2013, a downward trajectory, with a downward trend in December 2014, at -0.2 per cent. The updated projections point to the persistence of deflation in 2015, determined by the reduction in oil prices in international markets and consumer prices of Cape Verde's main supplier - the Eurozone. 11. Consumer price deflation, if aggravated by a slowdown in demand, could exacerbate the inefficiency of money transmission and affect the dynamics of economic activity very negatively. 12. Deflation influences the expectations of economic operators, and they may prefer to postpone consumption and investment in the hope that prices will continue to fall in the future. 13. In the case of Cape Verde, however, there is no evidence that consumers will be able to postpone consumption in the expectation that prices will continue to fall, as the representative basket of national consumption consists mainly of essential goods, goods which are difficult to replace. Many of them are imported, it is expected that the purchasing power and disposable income of households will suffer some increase due to the reduction in imported inflation, offsetting, to some extent, the adverse shock of the bad agricultural year in 2014. 14. Conversely, given that State revenues are strongly linked to the prices of goods and services, a persistent fall in the same would tend to reduce revenue and, consequently, public expenditure. This could lead the government to incur more debt, relegating monetary policy to an even lonelier role of stimulating short-term growth. 15. In this context, the possible benefits of imported deflation could be countered by the deterioration of the government's budgetary position and the combination of these effects may or may not favour economic activity and, therefore, may or may not facilitate the implementation of monetary policy measures. 16. The scope of the country's monetary policy is also limited by the necessary condition of ensuring the credibility of the euro's fixed peg exchange rate regime. 17. The internal environment, where deflation stands out, an unsatisfactory evolution of credit to the economy and a relatively comfortable level of foreign exchange reserves, calls us towards the weighting of complementary measures at the level of monetary policy. These are part of accommodative monetary policy measures, with a view to improving monetary transmission and stimulating credit to the economy and economic growth through the channel of expectations and confidence. 18. In this context, the need to stimulate the financing of productive investments with feasibility to sustain the strengthening of the national economy presupposes the assessment of the impact of an additional monetary loosening, also using the change in the rate of mandatory reserves. 19. Mandatory reserves currently comprise 18 per cent of deposits in the national banking system with maturity up to two years. Although they are considered economically inefficient, from the perspective of some experts in the field, they are the most effective instrument of Cape Verdean monetary policy and to some extent assume the lack of a deposit security scheme in Cape Verde. 20. As we know, banks receive real estate as collateral for the credits granted. With the international financial crisis and the subsequent increase in overdue credit, especially in the real estate-tourism sector, banking institutions were forced to implement some mortgage guarantees, resulting in the increase in real estate on their balance sheet. 21. In view of their liquidity and the need to focus on their core business, the legislation provides that banks have two years to dispose of those properties. Otherwise, their value is deducted from own funds, with an impact on the solvency ratio  one of the main indicators of banks' soundness. 22. In the context of the meeting held on 06 of the current with the commercial banks, the possibility of bcv extending the period referred to above was mentioned. It is recognised that its extension could create a cushion for the release of resources by the bank, with beneficial effects on banking activity. 23. For the foregoing, Aiming to stimulate credit to the economy and promote the economic growth of the country, in a context of deflation and significant increase in foreign exchange reserves; and Taking into account the international context and the evolution of international interest rates, with emphasis on the Euro Area, the Board of Directors, meeting on 12 February, decided on the following monetary policy and prudential measures to enter into force from the 16th of this month: Reduction of the rate of minimum cash reserves by 3 percentage points, from the current 18% to 15% (a decrease in the order of 16.7%); Reduction of the key rate by 25 basis points, from the current 3.75% to 3.50%. As a result, the indexed rates now present the following amendment: Permanent Liquidity-Of-Liquidity Facility Rate - from 6.75% to 6.50%; Liquidity Absorption Facility Rate - from 0.5% to 0.25%. Framework (New Rate Structure) Rates Previous Structure New Structure Minimum Cash Availability 18,0% 15,0% Director Fee 3,75% 3,50% Liquidity Nce rate 6,75% 6,50% Liquidity Absorption Rate 0,50% 0,25% Rediscount 7,75% 7,50% Extension of the deadline for the disposal of the properties received by the banks in dacao, from 2 to a maximum of 5 years, with staggered slaughter to own funds. 24. With the implementation of these measures, the BCV expects an increase in credit to the economy and a reduction in active interest rates, taking into account the gap created by reducing operating costs. Increasing credit to the economy, in turn, will lead to an additional boost to real GDP growth. Likewise, it is expected with these measures, contributing to the rise of the Consumer Price Index, fighting the scenario of deflation. 25. The BCV also expects its efforts to be monitored by banking in the same sense, and it is important to stimulate credit to the economy as a basis for productive investments, indispensable for economic growth. In other words, it is anticipated that the banking sector will take a consequent action as a driving force for monetary transmission as well as economic growth. The expectation of the BCV is that there will therefore be greater proactivity in the selection of projects for credit, imposition of greater confidence in the market, greater innovation and competitiveness. 26. Moreover, the impact of the reduction of minimum cash reserves, like any other monetary stimulus measure, will only be enhanced, in a sustainable way, with the efficient implementation of measures aimed at strengthening the balance sheet of banks and reducing the risks that threaten the financial stability of the country. These measures complemented with: (i) deepening structural reforms enabling infrastructure improvement and diversification of investment products in the financial sector; (ii) Strengthening corporate governance; and (iii) Reducing the risks of the economy and increasing its competitiveness, which also involves increasing the financial literacy of the Cape Verdean population and significantly reducing informality in the economy. 27. At the level of the financial system, the challenges naturally focus on improving and strengthening Banking Supervision combined with the modernization of Payment Systems, ultimately aiming at creating conditions to address any vulnerabilities that one or another financial institution may experience. 28. Finally, it should be noted that the challenges faced with regard to the effectiveness of monetary policy in its final impact on the real economy are not, however, an apanagio of the Cape Verde an economy. This is because this effectiveness presupposes compliance with favourable conditions in other sectors. At the international level, a paradigmatic case is that of the Euro Area, an economic region with which Cape Verde shows a strong synchronization, where unconventional measures have been tested. BCV, 13 February 2015

Title: Intervention at the Seminar Regulatory Reform in the Financial System and corporate governance in Cape Verde
text: Intervention of the Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde, Dr. Joao Serra, in the opening of the Seminar Regulatory Reform in the Financial System and in the Government of Companies in Cape Verde Beach,July 16, 2015 Madam Auditor General of the Securities Market, Members of the Board of Directors and the Advisory Board of the BCV, Representatives of financial institutions, Lecturer Professor Dr. Paulo Camara, Guest Gentlemen, Ladies and Gentlemen The international financial crisis showed the existence of several vulnerabilities and regulatory failures, affecting the very foundations of the global financial system. In particular, it made visible the misalignment between the globalisation of markets and the institutional and regulatory framework of regulation and supervision, as well as the impacting role of an unregulated sector. Increased volatility and increased uncertainty make it difficult to finance the real economy, negatively affecting investment, long-term economic prospects and the well-being of citizens in general. In view of this, the need to rethink regulation and supervision of markets, and even to think about a new governance of the international economic and financial system has returned to the agenda in the discussions of international economic policy. In fact, following the crisis that began in 2007, a number of initiatives have been triggered to resothe the models of regulation, supervision and governance of the financial system. We highlight the supervisory models that have been undergoing significant changes, becoming more intrusive and, in parallel, starting to have a more transversal and prospective approach. Financial stability is an extremely important public good, a key factor in ensuring the confidence of economic operators, ensuring adequate allocation of savings in the economy and promoting sustainable economic growth. Safeguarding financial stability and efficient functioning of markets require robust and effective rules and institutions to support economic activity. The existence of a properly regulated and supervised, sound financial system capable of facing adverse situations, with adequate solvency and liquidity levels, with an appropriate incentive system, with appropriate governance and management models is essential for the proper functioning of any economy. No country is the same as another and each is the bearer of its own culture that is reflected in the models of governance and the quality of its financial institutions, as well as in the values that animate them. These factors are critical to ensure their financial soundness and ensure the relationship of trust with their counterparts. However, it is extremely important that the regulatory and supervisory regimes of the various countries pursue the objective of alignment with the international regulatory framework for the regulation and supervision of the financial system. Particularly interesting for Cape Verde is the specific context of the European Union, where the fulfilment of conditions allowing the recognition of the equivalence of supervisory regimes in third countries induces potential benefits. The promotion of convergence between these schemes influences the determination of capital requirements related to the activities of the subsidiaries of the European institutions and thus the volume and cost of financing local economies. The adequacy of credit institutions' corporate governance models is a support for their soundness and, consequently, of safeguarding financial stability. It is essential that governance models ensure the segregation of functions, as well as the autonomy and independence of internal audit, compliance and risk management functions. On the other hand, it is essential that the interests of stakeholders and the general interest of the institution be properly guarded. As has been happening a little by all latitudes, Cape Verde has embarked on a broad programme of reforms of its financial sector, with a view to creating a solid and efficient institutional framework, by incorporating into the internal standards and regulations the best principles and practices recommended by international reference institutions. With the approval and publication in April 2014 of the Law that defines the Basic Principles and the Guiding Normative Framework of the Financial System", as well as the Law that regulates the activities of financial institutions", Cape Verde has taken a decisive step towards the reform of the frame of reference for its Financial System. These diplomas are part of the key findings of the discussions held in the various national and international for a on the direction of financial regulation and supervision, with emphasis on the recommendations of the Basel Committee. Thus, the ongoing reform is based on the pillars of promoting confidence, soundness and stability of the financial system, in order to promote the efficient collection of savings and the promotion of economic development. To this end, an adequate level of capitalisation of financial institutions, effective supervision by competent authorities, both prudential and behavioural level, and free and sound competition in markets, based on disclosure by financial institutions, timely, accurate, comparable and credible information, must be ensured. The above-mentioned diplomas are based on an integrated view of the financial system. Indeed, the activities carried out by financial institutions and the products they trade are increasingly complex in nature and allow for varied interconnections between the banking, financial and insurance sectors, which recommends integrated regulation and supervision of the various markets. These diplomas sought a better definition and achievement of the powers of the authorities for regulating and supervising the financial system, especially the Bank of Cape Verde, which has strengthened its power. It was ensured that the competent authorities are given the necessary tasks for the performance of regulatory and supervisory functions, which are essential to maintaining high levels of confidence in the financial system. Financial stability mechanisms have been strengthened, in particular with regard to the possibility of the Bank of Cape Verde acting in the context of the prevention and management of banking crises, together with the creation of guarantee systems covering all or part of the losses suffered by financial service acquirers. In addition to the publication of the two diplomas mentioned above, still in the context of the reform of the financial system, the "Cape Verde Securities Market Code" was published through legislative decree no. 1/2012, which also reformed the regulatory framework of the securities market, adopting solutions that follow international best practices and recommendations. The same thing happened to the insurance sector. Defined is the normative framework of reference within which the Cape Verdean financial system will evolve in the near future, it must be implemented through its interpretation and production of standards, regulations and instructions that allow its authentic observance on a day-to-day by the various entities involved in the sector. The Bank of Cape Verde attaches particular importance to the joint reflection on issues relating to the regulation and supervision of financial institutions and the safeguarding of financial stability. In this context, we are gathered here today to seek, in a shared way, to seek a better interpretation and understanding of the principles and practices advocated in the regulatory reform of the current financial system, as well as to seek the best ways for its materialization, in order to develop that system and strengthen its soundness and stability. In this context, a shared approach is crucial, considering the different lines of defence of the stability of the financial system, where the administration of a financial institution, its Supervisory Board and the auditors constitute the first, second and third lines respectively, with the regulator and supervisor, contrary to what was previously thought, the fourth line. The theme to be discussed in this Seminar is therefore of great use and opportunity for the moment we are going through. His presentation is in charge of Dr. Paulo Camara, a prominent university professor and legal adviser, with extensive experience in the field and numerous reflections and written works related to the functioning of the financial system, with emphasis on the governance of financial corporations Thank you very much and good work. Beach, 16 July 2015 John Serra /Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde/
text_original: Interveno do Governador do Banco de Cabo Verde, Dr. Joo Serra, na abertura do Seminrio A Reforma Regulatria no Sistema Financeiro e no Governo das Sociedades em Cabo Verde Praia,16 de Julho de 2015 Senhora Auditora Geral do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios, Senhores Membros do Conselho de Administrao e do Conselho Consultivo do BCV, Senhores Representantes das Instituies Financeiras, Senhor Conferencista Professor Dr. Paulo Cmara, Senhores Convidados, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores A crise financeira internacional veio mostrar a existncia de diversas vulnerabilidades e falhas regulamentares, atingindo as prprias fundaes do sistema financeiro global. Em especial, tornou visvel o desalinhamento entre a globalizao dos mercados e o quadro institucional e normativo de regulao e superviso, bem como o impactante papel de um sector no regulamentado. Maior volatilidade e acrescida incerteza dificultam o financiamento da economia real, afectando negativamente o investimento, as perspectivas econmicas de longo prazo e o bemestar dos cidados em geral. Em face disso, a necessidade de se repensar a regulao e a superviso dos mercados, e at mesmo de se pensar uma nova governana do sistema econmico-financeiro internacional voltou  agenda nas discusses da poltica econmica internacional. Com efeito, na sequncia da crise iniciada em 2007, foi desencadeado um conjunto de iniciativas tendentes  reconfigurao dos modelos de regulao, superviso e de governana do sistema financeiro. Destacam-se os modelos de superviso que tm vindo a sofrer alteraes significativas, tornandose mais intrusivos e, em paralelo, passando a ter um enfoque mais transversal e mais prospectivo. A estabilidade financeira  um bem pblico de extrema importncia, um factorchave para garantir a confiana dos agentes econmicos, assegurar uma adequada afectao da poupana na economia e promover o crescimento econmico sustentvel. A salvaguarda da estabilidade financeira, bem como o funcionamento eficiente dos mercados exigem regras e instituies robustas e eficazes que apoiem a actividade econmica. A existncia de um sistema financeiro devidamente regulado e supervisionado, slido, capaz de enfrentar situaes adversas, com nveis de solvabilidade e de liquidez adequados, com um sistema de incentivos apropriado, com modelos de governao e de gesto adequados  essencial para o bom funcionamento de qualquer economia. Nenhum pas  igual a outro e cada um  portador de uma cultura prpria que se reflecte nos modelos de governao e na qualidade das suas instituies financeiras, bem como nos valores que as animam. Estes factores so crticos para garantir a sua solidez financeira e assegurar a relao de confiana com as suas contrapartes. Todavia,  de extrema importncia que os regimes de regulao e superviso dos vrios pases prossigam o objectivo de alinhamento com o enquadramento normativo internacional em matria de regulao e superviso do sistema financeiro. Particularmente interessante para Cabo Verde  o contexto especfico da Unio Europeia, onde o preenchimento de condies que permitam o reconhecimento da equivalncia dos regimes de superviso em pases terceiros induz potenciais benefcios. Com efeito, a promoo da convergncia entre estes regimes influencia a determinao dos requisitos de fundos prprios relacionados com a actividade das filiais das instituies europeias e, dessa forma, o volume e o custo de financiamento s economias locais. A adequao dos modelos de governao corporativa das instituies de crdito  um sustentculo da sua solidez e, consequentemente, da salvaguarda da estabilidade financeira.  fundamental que os modelos de governao garantam a segregao de funes, bem como a autonomia e independncia das funes de auditoria interna, de compliance e de gesto de riscos. Por outro,  essencial que os interesses dos stakeholders e o interesse geral da instituio sejam devidamente acautelados.  semelhana do que vem acontecendo um pouco por todas as latitudes, Cabo Verde embarcou num amplo programa de reformas do seu sector financeiro, tendo em vista a criao de um quadro institucional slido e eficiente, atravs da incorporao nas normas e regulamentos internos dos melhores princpios e prticas recomendados por instituies internacionais de referncia. Com a aprovao e publicao em Abril de 2014, da Lei que Define os Princpios Bsicos e o Quadro Normativo Orientador do Sistema Financeiro, bem como da Lei que Regula as Actividades das Instituies Financeiras, Cabo Verde deu um passo decisivo no sentido da reforma do quadro de referncia para o seu Sistema Financeiro. Estes diplomas integram o essencial das concluses dos debates que se tem realizado nas diversas instncias nacionais e internacionais sobre o rumo da regulao e superviso financeiras, com destaque para as recomendaes do Comit de Basileia. Assim, a reforma em curso assenta sobre os pilares da promoo da confiana, solidez e estabilidade do sistema financeiro, de modo a favorecer a eficiente captao das poupanas e a promoo do desenvolvimento econmico. Para tanto, h que assegurar um nvel adequado de capitalizao das instituies financeiras, uma superviso eficaz pelas autoridades competentes, tanto ao nvel prudencial como comportamental, e uma livre e s concorrncia nos mercados, baseada na divulgao pelas instituies financeiras, de informao tempestiva, exacta, comparvel e credvel. Os diplomas atrs mencionados assentam numa viso integrada do sistema financeiro. Efectivamente, as actividades desenvolvidas pelas instituies financeiras e os produtos que transaccionam so de natureza cada vez mais complexa e permitem interconexes variadas entre os sectores bancrio, financeiro e dos seguros, o que recomenda uma regulao e superviso integrada dos diversos mercados. Procurou-se com estes diplomas uma melhor definio e concretizao das competncias das autoridades de regulao e superviso do sistema financeiro, com destaque para o Banco de Cabo Verde, que viu reforado o seu poder. Assegurou-se que as autoridades competentes sejam dotadas das atribuies necessrias ao exerccio das funes regulatrias e de superviso, essenciais  manuteno de nveis elevados de confiana no sistema financeiro. Reforaram-se os mecanismos de estabilidade financeira, designadamente no concernente  possibilidade do Banco de Cabo Verde actuar no mbito da preveno e gesto de crises bancrias, a par com a criao de sistemas de garantias que cubram a totalidade ou partes das perdas sofridas pelos adquirentes de servios financeiros. Para alm da publicao dos dois diplomas atrs mencionados, ainda no quadro da reforma do sistema financeiro, foi publicado atravs do decreto-legislativo n1/2012 o Cdigo do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios de Cabo Verde, que tambm veio reformar o quadro regulatrio do mercado de valores mobilirios, adoptando solues que acompanham as melhores prticas e recomendaes internacionais. O mesmo aconteceu com o sector segurador. Definido que est o quadro normativo de referncia dentro qual o sistema financeiro cabo-verdiano ir evoluir nos prximos tempos, h que implement-lo atravs da sua interpretao e produo de normas, regulamentos e instrues que permitam a sua observncia autntica no dia-a-dia pelas diversas entidades envolvidas no sector. O Banco de Cabo Verde atribui particular relevncia  reflexo conjunta sobre as questes relativas  regulao e superviso das instituies financeiras e  salvaguarda da estabilidade financeira. Neste quadro, encontramo-nos hoje aqui reunidos para, de forma partilhada, buscarmos a melhor interpretao e compreenso dos princpios e prticas preconizados na reforma regulatria do sistema financeiro em curso, bem como procurarmos os melhores caminhos para a sua materializao, no sentido do desenvolvimento do referido sistema e do reforo da sua solidez e estabilidade. Neste mbito uma abordagem partilhada  crucial, considerando as diferentes linhas de defesa da estabilidade do sistema financeiro, em que a administrao de uma instituio financeira, o seu Conselho Fiscal e os auditores constituem a primeira, segunda e terceira linhas respectivamente, cabendo ao regulador e supervisor, ao contrrio do que se pensava at recentemente, a quarta linha. O tema a ser debatido neste Seminrio reveste-se, assim, de grande utilidade e oportunidade para o momento que atravessamos. A sua apresentao est a cargo do Dr. Paulo Cmara, um proeminente professor universitrio e consultor jurdico, com vasta experincia na matria e inmeras reflexes e obras escritas relacionadas com o funcionamento do sistema financeiro, com destaque para o governo das sociedades financeiras Muito obrigado e bom trabalho. Praia, 16 de Julho de 2015 Joo Serra /Governador do Banco de Cabo Verde/

Title: Speech at the Acts of Launching the 500 and 5000 banknotes and the History of The Coin Book
text: Speech by the Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde, Dr. Joao Serra, at the launch of the new 500 and 5000 escudo banknotes and the History of Coin Book in Cape Verde, Banquet Hall of the National Assembly, September 10, 2015. Minister for Higher Education, Science and Innovation, Excellence, Family members of the President of the Republic Aristides Maria Pereira, Family lords of the poet Jorge Barbosa, Senhor Professor Joao Estevao, Members of the Board of Directors and the Advisory Board of the BCV, Representatives of financial institutions, Gentlemen bcv collaborators, Guest Gentlemen, Ladies and gentlemen, At a time when Cape Verde celebrates its 40th anniversary as an independent country, the Bank of Cape Verde is preparing to mark the 40th Anniversary of its creation under the motto "BCV: 40 years Committed to Development." With the advent of National Independence, it was important that Cape Verde fully assumed all the attributes of its sovereignty, namely the exercise of its inalienable right to issue the currency. Thus, by Decision with Force of Law No. 25/75 of September 29, the Bank of Cape Verde was created, assigning to it, on an exclusive basis, the functions of central bank and issuer, foreign exchange authority, Treasury and commercial bank. Today, about four decades later, the BCV has been positively following and influencing the development of Cape Verde. Indeed, the widely recognized success of our country's development effort is also due to a large extent to the strong performance that the BCV has had in these 40 years of its existence, ensuring the value of the national currency, the stability and development of the financial system, as well as developing and making the payment system work. With the main task of maintaining price stability, bcv's monetary policy objectives have been oriented over the last 15 years towards the defence of the fixed parity of the Cape Verdean shield against the euro, ensuring exchange rate stability, a key factor in the development of trade and increased external investment. 40 years of existence have a very special meaning for us, are four decades of growth and extraordinary results, which can only be proud of all those who have given and continue to make their contribution to the proper functioning of the Central Bank, as a fundamental institution for the performance of the economy, the development of the country and the improvement of the level of well-being of Cape Verdeans. This is a remarkable date in the history of our institution, which is why we intend to commend it in a special way, with the realization of several important activities. Because Cape Verde also celebrates 40 years of Independence, among the various activities alusive to date we wanted to highlight and perpetuate through bcv fiduciary notes, two unique figures of politics and culture of Cape Verde's history as a country and as a nation. In this context, the note of 5,000 escudos honors one of the most respected Cape Verdean politicians, Aristides Maria Pereira, a figure who distinguished himself, alongside Amilcar Cabral, in the struggle for the liberation of the Cape Verde islands from colonial domination and the first President of the Republic. He was one of the main workers of the Independence of Cape Verde and the construction of the Cape Verdean State. The note also pays homage to Boa Vista, the home island of Aristides Pereira, represented in its verse through the perspective of a landscape of the island, having in the foreground the image of the chimney of a pottery factory buried by the sands coming from the Sahara desert. It is also that it was President Aristides Pereira who signed the diploma that created the Bank of Cape Verde on September 29, 1975. For its part, the note of 500 escudos honors one of the most prestigious figures of modern Cape Verdean poetry, Jorge Barbosa, and his home island, Santiago. Jorge Barbosa was one of the founders of the eventually most important Cape Verdean literary movement. I refer to the Clarity that marks a phase of the aesthetic and linguistic contemporaneity of Cape Verde, based on the cultural, social and political emancipation of Cape Verdean society, more attentive to the realities of its daily lives. Because Jorge Barbosa's poetry seeks to translate the problems of the archipelago and the social drama of Cape Verdean man, such as drought, hunger, emigration, isolation and insularity, the representation of the island of Santiago is symbolized through the first dam of the country  the Poilao dam. To contrast with the symbolic meaning of this hydraulic work, they were applied on she excerpts from the poem "Hovebre", a poem that tries to assertively portray the aforementioned social drama of cape verdean man, namely drought and hunger. Despite the challenges facing the BCV in terms of payment systems, especially in a context where electronic payments are increasingly important, fiat currency remains an essential tool in our country's daily lives, given its function of enabling the exchange of goods and services to be done efficiently. The acceptance and use of this means of payment by all economic agents require that the national currency be covered with some characteristics, such as availability, quality and safety, thus ensuring high confidence and credibility in the use of the shield. In this context, the issue of the new series of banknotes is imposed by the need to restock, as well as by the obligation to safeguard the integrity of banknotes issued by introducing efficiency improvements and preventing counterfeit risks. The new notes thus include security features that take into account recent progress in this area. On the other hand, they aim to be more resilient and, consequently, with lower replacement and impact costs for the environment. Like the other notes issued in 2014, the new 5,000 and 500 escudo banknotes also fulfil a social inclusion function by allowing their identification by the visually impaired. The design of the notes is the company De La Rue in partnership with the Architect Erico Verissimo and the production is from the same company. With the launch of the notes of 500 and 5,000 escudos, the process of issuing the new series of banknotes approved by Decree-Law No. 64/2014 of November 17th is completed. The Bank of Cape Verde, as part of its fortieth anniversary celebrations, also wanted to make its contribution to a better knowledge of the evolution of the monetary system in Cape Verde and the phenomena underlying it. It is a theme, moreover, which falls within the scope of the BCV's mandate and, consequently, the main subject-matter of its activity. As a central element of all economic and financial transactions, knowledge of the currency and its evolution in its most diverse valences, such as unit of value, means of exchange or reserve of value, contributes to a better understanding of companies and their evolution. There is a very strong direct relationship between economic development and the level of monetisation of societies. One of the characteristics of modern societies is the extent and depth with which money plays the central role of economic relations, namely the level of development of its financial system. To know and understand the evolution and role of currency in Cape Verdean society, is to understand one of the fundamental aspects of our life, history and the vicissitudes that the country has faced over the centuries. It is in this context that the Bank of Cape Verde understood to be involved in the project entitled "History of Currency in Cape Verde  From the beginning of the settlement to the present", having to this end requested the ISEG - Higher Institute of Economics and Management of the University of Lisbon the work that will be presented in the following act. The project took place under the direction of Joao Estevao, Professor of ISEG, benefiting from diverse collaboration. The book covers the different periods of monetary history in Cape Verde, from the beginning of the settlement of the islands to the day to this day, through the binding of the Cape Verdean shield, first, to the Portuguese shield and, later, to the euro. It provides us with a set of important information, facts and statistical data on the evolution of the currency and the monetary system in Cape Verde. We hope that with the publication of this work we will be making way and pointing out clues to the emergence and development of projects in this area of knowledge, which will certainly contribute to the enrichment of our collection in this particular area. We ended by expressing our thanks to the Minister and distinguished Historian, who was kind enough to accept our invitation to preside over the acts of releases of the new banknotes, as well as the History of Coin book in Cape Verde, to Professor Joao Estevao, who wrote this book, as well as to family members mr. Aristides Pereira and Jorge Barbosa, who greatly honor us with his presence. To the Architect erico Verissimo our special thanks for having designed all the notes of the BCV, from its creation to this date, seeking, in all of them, to bring remarkable aspects of our life, politics, culture, history and cape verdeanity in general. Thank you so much for your attention!

Por que tambm Cabo Verde comemora 40 anos de Independncia, de entre as vrias actividades alusivas  data quisemos destacar e perenizar atravs de notas fiducirias do BCV, duas figuras mpares da poltica e da cultura da histria de Cabo Verde enquanto Pas e enquanto Nao. O Banco de Cabo Verde, no mbito das comemoraes do seu quadragsimo aniversrio, quis, tambm, dar o seu contributo para um melhor conhecimento da evoluo do sistema monetrio em Cabo Verde e dos fenmenos que lhe so subjacentes. Conhecer e compreender a evoluo e o papel da moeda na sociedade cabo-verdiana,  compreender um dos aspectos fundamentais da nossa vida, histria e das vicissitudes que o Pas vem enfrentando ao longo dos sculos.  neste contexto, que o Banco de Cabo Verde entendeu envolver-se no projecto intitulado de Histria da Moeda em Cabo Verde  Do incio do povoamento  actualidade, tendo para o efeito solicitado ao ISEG  Instituto Superior de Economia e Gesto da Universidade de Lisboa a obra que ser apresentada no acto seguinte.
