Title: Speech at the International Conference New approaches to Regulation and Supervision in Risk Mitigation
text: Speech by the Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde, Dr. Joao Serra, at the International Conference New Approaches to Regulation and Supervision in Risk Mitigation, in the Banquet Hall of the National Assembly, September 22, 2015. Madam Minister for Tourism, Investment and Business Development, Madam Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs, Representatives of the Diplomatic Corps, Mr. Lecturer, Dr. Carlos Costa, Governor of Banco de Portugal, Governor of the Central Bank of Central African States, Vice Governors and other Representatives of the CENTRAL BANKS OF THE CPLP, Members of the Board of Directors, the Supervisory Board and the Advisory Board of the BCV, Madam Auditor General of the Securities Market, Representatives of financial institutions, Mr. BCV Collaborators, Guest Gentlemen, Ladies and gentlemen, I am pleased to greet you and welcome you at this event that marks the highlight of the activities commemorating the 40th anniversary of the Bank of Cape Verde. Let me begin by expressing the thanks of the Board of Directors to all those who have accepted our invitation to be with us on this very special day for our institution. As is well known, macroeconomic stability is fundamental to sustainable economic growth. Now, in the four decades of our country's life, the BCV has been one of the main guarantors of this necessary condition for the proper functioning of the economy. Indeed, the widely recognised success of Cape Verde's development effort is also due to a large extent to the strong performance that the BCV has had in the 40 years of its existence, ensuring the value of the national currency, the stability and modernisation of the monetary and financial system, as well as developing and running the payment system. With the main task of maintaining price stability, bcv's monetary policy objectives have been oriented over the last 15 years towards the defence of the fixed parity of the Cape Verdean shield against the euro, ensuring exchange rate stability, a key factor in the development of trade and increased external investment. Thus, it is not by chance that the Bank of Cape Verde is celebrating its fortieth anniversary under the motto "BCV: 40 years committed to development". As since September 29, 1975, banco de Cabo Verde, with the support of all its employees and institutional partners, will continue to fulfil its role as guarantor of price stability and the proper functioning of the monetary and financial system. It will continue to support the country's economic development, creating conditions for deepening financial intermediation, reducing risk and increasing the confidence of economic agents in the national currency and our financial institutions. Meanwhile, ensuring financial stability, efficient functioning of markets, as well as the continued development of the financial system pose increased challenges for the BCV as a central bank and authority for regulating and supervising financial activity in Cape Verde. Ladies and gentlemen, The international financial economic crisis that began at the end of 2007 demonstrated the need to adopt decisive reforms in the field of financial regulation and supervision in order to restore the confidence of economic operators and overcome the crisis with a more robust, better regulated and better supervised financial system. In fact, this crisis, with the systemic nature and its great power of dissemination and contagion, has called into question the almost absolute belief in the power of self-regulation of markets. In view of this, the need to rethink regulation and supervision of markets, and even to think about a new governance of the economic and financial system has returned to the agenda in the discussions of world economic policy. There have been several international initiatives at this level, with the aim of the measures adopted by the G20, the Financial Stability Board of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, and the European Banking Authority. As a result of these initiatives, the organisation and functioning of banking supervision has been adapting to the needs and requirements arising from the new conditions of financial activity, with a view to enhancing the efficiency and effectiveness of the regulatory and supervisory function. It is important to highlight, within the scope of these initiatives, the call for a review of the supervisory approach, which is based on tighter, more effective, more intensive supervision, I would even say, "more suspicious" in view of the perception of the risks inherent to markets and financial institutions. For that, it has become imperative to change culture in the exercise of banking supervision. In other words, supervision could no longer be carried out almost exclusively from a distance, i.e. in a passive manner and confined practically to an ex-post check of management reports and external auditors. The exercise of supervision has definitely gone on the ground, repeatedly carrying out on-the-spot inspections and using instruments that the law already provides it with, in order to achieve a more direct and deeper knowledge of the supervised entity and its risk profile. In addition to this reform required in the inspective aspect, we must also stress, for the sake of financial stability, the importance attached to the following lines of defence: The role of the administrative bodies of financial institutions in the process of approval, implementation and adequacy of internal control systems; The role of internal auditors exercised independently in the important process of evaluation and validation of the processes, structures, models and metrics of the company's government; as well as The role of external auditors, providing credibility to accounts and enhancing the confidence of all market players. Another area called for by international initiatives is the need for more and better regulation, which is based, inter alia, at the level of the following: Strengthening banks' capital ratios for certain exposures; correct measurement and possible limitation of liquidity risks; the need for increased liquidity risk management by credit institutions, and in particular with regard to the implementation of contingency plans for liquidity; Combating the pro-cyclical effects of financial regulation; Increased transparency of financial products and institutions; and finally, the provision of more information to supervisors on what is happening on the markets, in particular in the interbank money market, the capital market and the derivatives market. Ladies and gentlemen, Our financial system needs, in the sense, a new paradigm, based on trust and credibility, and having efficiency as a cornerstone. This is the right time to undertake the changes that are justified in the face of each of the national realities. We are looking at a unique opportunity to implement crucial reforms in the material and institutional framework governing the national financial system, taking advantage of the momentum of the changes ahead following international guidelines. Cape Verde, like what has been happening a little by all latitudes, has embarked on a broad programme of reforms of its financial sector, with a view to creating a sound and efficient institutional framework, by incorporating into the internal standards and regulations the best principles and practices recommended by international reference institutions. Thus, with the approval and publication in April 2014 of the law that "Defines the Basic Principles and the Guiding Normative Framework of the Financial System", as well as the law that regulates the Activities of Financial Institutions", our country has taken the decisive step towards the reform of the frame of reference for its financial system. These diplomas are based on a holistic view of the financial system and are part of the essential conclusions of the discussions that have taken place in the various national and international for a on the direction of financial regulation and supervision, with emphasis on the recommendations of the Basel Committee. In this context, The main recommendations contained in Pillar 2, i.e. Supervisory Processes and Pillar 3, i.e. Transparency and Market Discipline, have been absorbed into the national legal order, strengthening the powers of supervision at the level of compliance with Basel II. The perimeter of regulation and supervision has been extended to all products, institutions and markets with systemic relevance. Institutionalized and materialized the function of behavioral supervision and macro-prudential supervision. Financial stability mechanisms have been strengthened, in particular the powers of the Bank of Cape Verde to intervene in the prevention and management of banking crises, along side the creation of guarantee systems covering all or part of the losses suffered by financial service purchasers. In addition to the publication of the two above-mentioned diplomas, still in the context of the reform of the financial system, the "Cape Verde Securities Market Code" was published in 2012, which also reformed the regulatory framework of the capital market, adopting solutions that follow international best practices and recommendations. The same has happened with the insurance sector, which has also been reformed. Ladies and gentlemen, Defined is the normative framework of reference within which the Cape Verdean financial system, as a whole, will evolve in the near future, present ing two major challenges. First, to seek a better interpretation and understanding of the principles and practices recommended in the current regulatory reform, a reform that is mainly oriented towards risk management. Secondly, to seek the best ways for its materialization vis-a-vis the development of the financial system, as well as to the strengthening of its solidity and stability. No country is the same as another and each is the bearer of its own culture that is reflected in the models of governance and the quality of its financial institutions, as well as in the values that animate them. These factors are critical to ensuring their financial soundness and preserving the relationship of trust with their counterparts. However, it is extremely important that the regulatory and supervisory regimes of the various countries pursue the objective of alignment with the international regulatory framework for the regulation and supervision of the financial system. In this context, the Bank of Cape Verde attaches particular importance to the joint reflection on issues relating to the regulation and supervision of financial institutions and the safeguarding of their stability, and it is, of course, the responsibility of the national competent authorities to find the solutions that best fit the reality of the country, in the framework of approximation to the international legal and regulatory framework. Hence the reason for the choice of the International Conference under the song "New Approaches to Regulation and Supervision in Risk Mitigation", as a central act of activities commemorating the 40th anniversary of the creation of the Bank of Cape Verde. The Conference, which is now starting, is therefore a unique opportunity that is offered to us for the exchange of experiences and concerns, sharing of lessons and proposals for solutions with regard to the adoption of new supervisory and regulatory approaches aimed at mitigating financial risks. The presentation will be in charge of His Excellency, the Governor of Banco de Portugal, an internationally recognized personality with extensive experience in the field and numerous reflections related to banking supervision and regulation. Our special thanks to Dr. Carlos Costa for being here with us. I want you to know that your presence greatly honors us. Thank you very much and good work! Beach, September 22, 2015 John Serra /Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde/
text_original: Discurso do Governador do Banco de Cabo Verde, Doutor Joo Serra, na Conferncia Internacional Novas Abordagens da Regulao e da Superviso na Mitigao de Riscos, no Salo de Banquetes da Assembleia Nacional, 22 de Setembro de 2015. Senhora Ministra do Turismo, Investimentos e Desenvolvimento Empresarial, Senhora Secretria de Estado dos Negcios Estrangeiros, Senhores Representantes do Corpo Diplomtico, Senhor Conferencista, Dr. Carlos Costa, Governador do Banco de Portugal, Senhor Governador do Banco Central dos Estados da frica Central, Senhores Vice Governadores e demais Representantes dos Bancos Centrais da CPLP, Senhores Membros do Conselho de Administrao, do Conselho Fiscal e do Conselho Consultivo do BCV, Senhora Auditora Geral do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios, Senhores Representantes das Instituies Financeiras, Senhores Colaboradores do BCV, Senhores Convidados, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores,  com prazer que vos cumprimento e vos dou as boas vindas neste evento que marca o ponto alto das actividades comemorativas do quadragsimo aniversrio do Banco de Cabo Verde. Permitam-me comear por expressar o agradecimento do Conselho de Administrao a todos os que aceitaram o nosso convite, para estarem connosco neste dia to especial para a nossa instituio. Como  sabido, a estabilidade macroeconmica  fundamental para o crescimento econmico sustentvel. Ora, nas quatro dcadas de vida do nosso pas, o BCV tem sido um dos principais garantes dessa condio necessria para o bom funcionamento da economia. Com efeito, o sucesso, amplamente reconhecido, do esforo de desenvolvimento de Cabo Verde deve-se, tambm, em boa medida, ao forte desempenho que o BCV tem tido nestes 40 anos da sua existncia, garantindo o valor da moeda nacional, a estabilidade e a modernizao do sistema monetrio e financeiro, bem como desenvolvendo e fazendo funcionar o sistema de pagamentos. Tendo como atribuio principal a manuteno da estabilidade dos preos, os objectivos de poltica monetria do BCV tm-se orientado, nos ltimos 15 anos, para a defesa da paridade fixa do escudo cabo-verdiano em relao ao euro, garantindo a estabilidade cambial, factor essencial ao desenvolvimento das trocas comerciais e ao aumento do investimento externo. Assim, no  por acaso que o Banco de Cabo Verde est a comemorar o seu quadragsimo aniversrio sob o lema BCV: 40 anos comprometido com o desenvolvimento. Como desde 29 de Setembro de 1975, o Banco de Cabo Verde, com o apoio de todos os seus colaboradores e parceiros institucionais, continuar a cumprir o seu papel de garante da estabilidade dos preos e de bom funcionamento do sistema monetrio e financeiro. Continuar a apoiar o desenvolvimento econmico do pas, criando condies para o aprofundamento da intermediao financeira, a reduo do risco e o aumento da confiana dos agentes econmicos na moeda nacional e nas nossas instituies financeiras. Entretanto, a garantia da estabilidade financeira, o funcionamento eficiente dos mercados, bem como o contnuo desenvolvimento do sistema financeiro colocam desafios acrescidos ao BCV enquanto banco central e autoridade de regulao e superviso da actividade financeira em Cabo Verde. Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, A crise econmica financeira internacional iniciada no final do ano de 2007 veio demonstrar a necessidade de adoptar reformas decisivas no domnio da regulao e superviso financeiras, de forma a restabelecer a confiana dos agentes econmicos e ultrapassar a crise com um sistema financeiro mais robusto, melhor regulado e melhor supervisionado. Na verdade, esta crise, com a natureza sistmica e seu grande poder de disseminao e contgio, ps em cheque a crena quase que absoluta no poder de auto-regulao dos mercados. Em face disso, a necessidade de se repensar a regulao e a superviso dos mercados, e at mesmo de se pensar uma nova governana do sistema econmico-financeiro voltou  agenda nas discusses da poltica econmica mundial. Tm sido vrias as iniciativas internacionais a este nvel, destacando-se as medidas adoptadas pelo G20, pelo Conselho de Estabilidade Financeira do Comit de Basileia de Superviso Bancria, e pela Autoridade Bancria Europeia. Na sequncia dessas iniciativas, a organizao e o funcionamento da superviso bancria tm vindo a adaptar-se s necessidades e exigncias decorrentes das novas condies do exerccio da actividade financeira, visando reforar a eficincia e a eficcia da funo de regulao e de superviso. Importa destacar, no mbito do rol destas iniciativas, o apelo  reviso da abordagem da superviso, que se consubstancia numa superviso mais apertada, mais efectiva, mais intensa, diria mesmo, mais desconfiada perante a percepo dos riscos inerentes aos mercados e instituies financeiras. Pelo que, tornou-se imperativa a mudana da cultura no exerccio da superviso bancria. Ou seja, a superviso no podia continuar a ser executada quase que exclusivamente  distncia, isto , de uma forma passiva e confinando-se praticamente a um controlo ex post dos relatrios de administrao e dos auditores externos. Definitivamente, o exerccio da superviso passou a ir para o terreno, a realizar repetidamente inspeces in loco e a recorrer a instrumentos que a lei j lhe faculta, de modo a alcanar um conhecimento mais directo e mais profundo da entidade supervisionada e do respectivo perfil de risco. A par desta reforma exigida na vertente inspectiva, no podemos deixar igualmente de realar, em prol da estabilidade financeira, a importncia que  atribuda s seguintes linhas de defesa:  O papel dos rgos de administrao das instituies financeiras no processo de aprovao, implementao e adequao dos sistemas de controlo interno;  O papel dos auditores internos exercido de forma independente no importante processo de avaliao e validao dos processos, estruturas, modelos e mtricas do governo da sociedade; bem como  O papel dos auditores externos, proporcionando credibilidade s contas e reforando a confiana de todos os intervenientes do mercado. Um outro domnio clamado pelas iniciativas internacionais  a necessidade de mais e melhor regulao que se consubstancia, nomeadamente, ao nvel do seguinte:  Do reforo dos rcios de fundos prprios dos bancos para determinadas exposies;  De uma correcta medio e eventual limitao dos riscos de liquidez;  Da necessidade de reforo da gesto do risco de liquidez por parte das instituies de crdito, e em particular no que se refere  implementao de planos de contingncia para a liquidez;  Do combate aos efeitos pro-cclicos da regulao financeira;  Do aumento da transparncia dos produtos e instituies financeiras; e, por fim,  Da disponibilizao de mais informao para os supervisores relativamente ao que se passa nos mercados, designadamente no mercado monetrio interbancrio, no mercado de capitais e no mercado de derivados. Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, O nosso sistema financeiro precisa, em suma, de um novo paradigma, assente na confiana e credibilidade, e tendo como pedra angular a eficincia. Este  o momento adequado para se empreender as mudanas que se justifiquem em face de cada uma das realidades nacionais. Estamos perante uma oportunidade nica de implementar reformas cruciais no quadro material e institucional que rege o sistema financeiro nacional, aproveitando o impulso das alteraes que se avizinham na sequncia das orientaes internacionais. Cabo Verde,  semelhana do que vem acontecendo um pouco por todas as latitudes, embarcou num amplo programa de reformas do seu sector financeiro, tendo em vista a criao de um quadro institucional slido e eficiente, atravs da incorporao nas normas e regulamentos internos dos melhores princpios e prticas recomendados por instituies de referncia internacional. Assim, com a aprovao e publicao em Abril de 2014 da lei que Define os Princpios Bsicos e o Quadro Normativo Orientador do Sistema Financeiro, bem como da lei que Regula as Actividades das Instituies Financeiras, o nosso pas deu o passo decisivo no sentido da reforma do quadro de referncia para o seu sistema financeiro. Estes diplomas assentam numa viso holstica do sistema financeiro e integram o essencial das concluses dos debates que se tm realizado nas diversas instncias nacionais e internacionais sobre o rumo da regulao e superviso financeiras, com destaque para as recomendaes do Comit de Basileia. Neste quadro,  Foram absorvidas na ordem jurdica nacional as principais recomendaes contidas no pilar 2, ou seja, Processos de Superviso e no pilar 3, isto , Transparncia e Disciplina de Mercado, reforando os poderes da superviso ao nvel de cumprimento de Basileia II.  Alargou-se o permetro da regulao e superviso a todos os produtos, instituies e mercados com relevncia sistmica.  Institucionalizou-se e materializou-se a funo da superviso comportamental e da superviso macro-prudencial.  Reforaram-se os mecanismos de estabilidade financeira, designadamente os poderes de interveno do Banco de Cabo Verde no mbito da preveno e gesto de crises bancrias, a par com a criao de sistemas de garantias que cubram a totalidade ou partes das perdas sofridas pelos adquirentes de servios financeiros. Para alm da publicao dos dois diplomas atrs mencionados, ainda no quadro da reforma do sistema financeiro, foi publicado em 2012 o Cdigo do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios de Cabo Verde, que tambm veio reformar o quadro regulatrio do mercado de capitais, adoptando solues que acompanham as melhores prticas e recomendaes internacionais. O mesmo aconteceu com o sector segurador que, tambm, foi alvo de reforma. Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, Definido que est o quadro normativo de referncia dentro qual o sistema financeiro cabo-verdiano, no seu todo, ir evoluir nos prximos tempos, apresentam-se-nos dois grandes desafios. Primeiro, buscar a melhor interpretao e compreenso dos princpios e prticas preconizados na reforma regulatria em curso, reforma essa orientada sobretudo para a gesto de riscos. Segundo, procurar os melhores caminhos para a sua materializao vis--vis ao desenvolvimento do sistema financeiro, bem como ao reforo da sua solidez e estabilidade. Nenhum pas  igual a outro e cada um  portador de uma cultura prpria que se reflecte nos modelos de governao e na qualidade das suas instituies financeiras, bem como nos valores que as animam. Estes factores so crticos para garantir a sua solidez financeira e preservar a relao de confiana com as suas contrapartes. Todavia,  de extrema importncia que os regimes de regulao e superviso dos vrios pases prossigam o objectivo de alinhamento com o enquadramento normativo internacional em matria de regulao e superviso do sistema financeiro. Neste quadro, o Banco de Cabo Verde atribui particular relevncia  reflexo conjunta sobre as questes relativas  regulao e superviso das instituies financeiras e  salvaguarda da sua estabilidade, cabendo, como  natural, s autoridades competentes nacionais a responsabilidade de encontrarem as solues que melhor se adaptem  realidade do pas, no quadro de aproximao ao enquadramento legal e regulatrio internacional. Da a razo da escolha da Conferncia Internacional sob o tema candente Novas Abordagens da Regulao e da Superviso na Mitigao de Riscos, como acto central das actividades comemorativas dos 40 anos da criao do Banco de Cabo Verde. A Conferncia, que ora se inicia,  pois uma oportunidade mpar que se nos oferece para a troca de experincias e preocupaes, partilha de ensinamentos e propostas de soluo no que toca  adopo de novas abordagens de superviso e de regulao voltadas para a mitigao de riscos financeiros. A apresentao estar a cargo de sua Excelncia, o Governador do Banco de Portugal, uma personalidade internacionalmente reconhecida, com vasta experincia na matria e inmeras reflexes relacionadas com a superviso e regulao bancrias. Os nossos especiais agradecimentos ao Dr. Carlos Costa, por estar aqui connosco. Quero que saiba que a sua presena muito nos honra. Muito obrigado e bom trabalho! Praia, 22 de Setembro de 2015 Joo Serra /Governador do Banco de Cabo Verde/

Title: Intervention at the closing of the VII Institutional Forum of Microfinancas
text: Speech by the Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde, Dr. Joao Serra, at the closing of the VII Institutional Forum of Microfinancas, November 11, 2015. Mr Marc de Bourcy, Representative of Luxembourg Cooperation in Cape Verde, Mr. Jacinto Abreu dos Santos, President of the Federation of Cape Verdean Associations operating in the Area of Micro-Finance, Expensive participants Ladies and gentlemen, Let me first thank you for your kind invitation by the President of the Federation of Cape Verdean Associations operating in the MicroFinance Area to preside over the closing of the VII Institutional Forum on Micro-Tuning. It is with great satisfaction that I accepted the invitation taking into account the personal affection I have for the Micro enterprise sector, having worked in this area for some time in my professional life and contributed with some reflections to a better understanding of its enormous importance in the development process of our country. In fact, according to data obtained by INE in the 4th Business Census, in 2012 there were 7,902 companies in Cape Verde that can be considered microenterprises, because they have between 0 and 5 employees. They accounted for 86 percent of all active companies. They employed 28.8 percent of workers, a total of 51,411. Its turnover amounted to 36.4 million contos, which represented 14.5 percent of the country's total turnover, worth 250.8 million contos. In the same year of 2012, the turnover of microenterprises amounted to 24 percent of GDP. Although microfinance is not limited only to microcredit, it is to be recognized, however, that so far microcredit is the most known and perceptible aspect of microfinance. However, available data show that the level of funding for micro-enterprises through microcredit and much more can be done in this area. However, extraordinary advances are to be made in a sector that began about two and a half decades ago with small credits, and which, from 2009 to 2014, carried out 52,000 credit operations, mobilized about three million contos, benefiting about 9,000 people in Cape Verde. Ladies and gentlemen, In the framework of successful development strategies at the level of different continents and countries, microcredit has increasingly been occupying a major role, with emphasis on policies focused on the empowerment of the most disadvantaged sections of the population. It is unnecessary to mention here the importance of microfinance, with an emphasis on financial and social inclusion, in a country such as Cape Verde, where, despite the remarkable progress made since independence to date, both in the economic and social field, poverty still affects a significant portion of our population, about 26% according to available data. In addition to the lack of opportunities combined with weak levels of income and consumption, poverty is closely associated with limitations in terms of human capital, resulting from unfavorable situations in terms of health, education, security and access to public institutions and services in general. While the potential of microcredit far outsof the problem of poverty reduction, it should be recognised that access to credit represents one of the main barriers for the most disadvantaged layers of the population. As Mr. Muhammad Yunus writes, "Microcredit is much more than lending money and getting it back. This is only part of it. Microcredit is also social change." In this way, I cannot fail to congratulate the organizers of this Forum on the opportunity of the Forum, as it comes at the very moment when several actions are being developed to place more emphasis on financial inclusion policies. Ladies and gentlemen, Let me recall a study in which I paricipei, prepared at the International Symposium on Microfinance and Promotion of Micro and Small Enterprises, in 2000 in Cape Verde. This study, from 15 years ago, concluded that, despite the development so far as it was made, the microfinance system was in many constraints at the level of the institutional and legal framework. In the list of these constraints, we highlighted the lack of concrete and explicit policies and measures, framed by a coherent strategy and translated into a legal and regulatory framework, aimed at the microfinance sector. Instead, one-off interventions and/or operational measures predominated without the consequent legal translation. At the level of stakeholders on the ground, the study in question had concluded that NGOs were by far the biggest driver of microfinance's main product, microcredit, for the following reasons: Had the highest number of credits granted; They were many more beneficiaries; Had the most significant human resources structure allocated to the micro-credit sector; and They were the main entrepreneurs of training. However, the fundamental problem that in 2000 was the microcredit system in Cape Verde was its sustainability. Indeed, although many of the players in the microcredit sector were already aware of the non-eternity of the funds they were managing, which in most cases came from external sources, there were few those with a revolving fund, that is, a self-feeding fund. In this particular, one of the recommendations of this study had to do with the issue of ensuring sustainability. In other words, in the event that the micro-credit sector improves performance and lasts, it is absolutely necessary for its actors to set up revolving and profitable funds, so that they do not remain in eternal dependence on lost fund financing. Today, a decade and a half later I note with satisfaction that an important path has already been taken and that the panorama is something different from then, although some of the bigger problems still remain. However, if in 2000 there was talk of the urgent need for coordination between the various institutions with intervention in the area of microfinance and the lack of intermediaries specialized in financing operations, today the main concern has to do with the materialisation of institutional, legal and regulatory conditions for the coherent implementation of policies for the promotion, growth and professionalisation of the microfinance sector, as a privileged instrument for promoting economic citizenship, as well as social and financial inclusion. Proof of this are the subjects contained in the program of activities of the IV National Week of Microfinance, whose central theme is "the Transformation Process", among others that I believe of great importance and timeliness, in the context of the paradigm shift of development of the microfinance system. As President Jacinto Santos said, with the debate around this central theme, it is intended to collect as many subsidies as possible, to allow some provisions of the laws to be adequate before their effective implementation, thus contributing to the whole process of transformation being a coherent product. He stressed that the Federation he chairs will insist on the fact that a specific transformation plan is needed for a period of five years. This "transformation plan", also according to President Jacinto Santos, implies training, technical assistance, information, preparation on the ground and financial and technical resources, technological innovation, information systems and management, in addition to banking supervision to promote and leverage these institutions, so that they can fulfill their social purpose. In other cases, the transformation in question relates, fundamentally, to the process of converting micro-financ institutions into institutions that carry out a regulated commercial activity, duly authorised and supervised by the Bank of Cape Verde. I can assure you, Mr President, that I essentially share your views on the gradual, balanced and adjusted process of transformation. Ladies and gentlemen, I believe that at the institutional and legal level the decisive step for transformation was taken with the approval of Law No. 83/VIII/2015 of 16 January, which establishes the legal regime for the activity of microfinance and its institutions. In general, the publication of this law has brought new challenges to the BCV, while bringing several benefits in terms of discipline of microfinance institutions, long underway by institutions of this existing nature. Therefore, the microfinance sector is now being supervised and regulated by an autonomous institution, in this case the Central Bank, in line with the recommendations of international institutions, namely the World Bank. The expected result at the macro level is that it will ensure the financial stability and inclusion of the clients of these institutions, protect depositors, increase the allocation of resources and accelerate the development of the sector. At the micro level, it is intended that these institutions will have a more professional management, respecting good governance practices, in terms of accountability, transparency, as well as risk management with more responsibility. But before that had already been taken another important step. I am referring to the government's approval of the Strategic Plan for the Development of the MicroFinance Sector for the period 2014-2019, with the aim of facilitating the development of a solid, diversified, competitive and inclusive microfinance sector. In order to be able to assume their mission responsibly and durablely, microfinance institutions must guide their practices in order to ensure operational and financial sustainability and, this time, provide their clients with a viable and diversified offer of financial services and products tailored to their real needs. On the other hand, it is recognised that, in addition to their financial intermediation function, microfinance institutions also play a decisive role in the process of social intermediation, creating employment and income opportunities for the most vulnerable sections of the population, which contributes to economic development and sustained poverty reduction. As far as the sustainability of the microcredit system is concerned, as it was 15 years ago, I think it is extremely important to reflect in depth on two fundamental issues. The first relates to the cost of the credit and the second relates to reimbursement, more precisely the guarantee of reimbursement. It is not my intention to want to look at the depth and complexity required at this time on these two issues of major importance for the sustainability of microcredit. However, from what we have seen from the analysis of the micro-credit system actors in the 2000 study, there is a great diversity of interest rates applied, as well as guarantee schemes. Likely, without wanting to get into the controversy surrounding the character, nature and function of microcredit, I believe, however, that from the point of view of the sustainability of the system, the interest rate should generally be that which guarantees the payment of the costs of the operation of the credit activity and the maintenance of the real value of the revolving fund. Indeed, as has been demonstrated in the above mentioned study, the central question is not so much the cost of credit as access to it, although efficiency is obviously a fundamental requirement for the better functioning of the activity. Similarly, that, also within the perspective of the system's perperability, all credit granted must be linked to effective guarantee mechanisms ensuring, with reasonable probality, their recovery. This issue has also not been peaceful, as it appears to involve the exclusion of large fringes of disadvantaged population stooes. I think that the multiplicity of guarantee schemes applied by the different actors contacted in the context of carrying out this study excludes the existence of such a relationship. In fact, by requiring as diverse guarantees as possible, our stakeholders were able to guarantee a repayment rate that can be considered reasonable for the nature of this type of financial transaction. Ladies and gentlemen, The aforementioned Law establishing the legal regime of the activity of microfinance and its institutions establishes that for NGOs that take deposits from the public and turn them into credit, supervision is exercised by the Bank of Cape Verde. Basically, this supervision consists of monitoring and monitoring compliance with prudential rules, including the solvency ratio, the establishment of minimum reserves and risk limits, in order to protect the financial system in general and the security of depositors in particular. I believe that microfinance institutions only have to gain from the supervision of the Central Bank, as it provides guarantees of transparency, security and credibility, which facilitates the attraction of financial resources, including international bodies, development banks and investors, to the financing of their operations. Thus, as part of the Project for the Development of Inclusive Finance in Cape Verde financed by Luxembourg Cooperation, a set of prudential regulations such as own funds, solvency ratio, limits and concentration of risks, provisions, internal control and economic and financial performance indicators, adjusted to the specific nature of microfinance institutions, is in the final stages of the evaluation for subsequent approval by the BCV. In other words, the Central Bank's approach to so-called microbanks must necessarily be different from that adopted for traditional banking, without, however, neglecting the rigour that should always be required of those who manage other people's funds. The dynamics of transformation require changes in behaviors and processes, in institutions, legislation and regulation. However, it carries risks, creates resistance and challenges at various levels, notably in the structure, capitalization, legal structure and governance model. However, it is important to recognize that the fundamental factor, in most of the institutional transformations that have occurred in many stops, was the need to have access to larger and more flexible sources of fundraising. I end by reiterating the bcv's interest and commitment in the implementation and creation of institutional and regulatory conditions for the sustainable and inclusive development of microfinance institutions. Thank you so much for your attention! Beach, November 11, 2015 John Serra /Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde/

Entretanto, dados disponveis demonstram que ainda  relativamente modesto o nvel do financiamento das microempresas atravs do microcrdito e que muito mais se poder fazer nesta rea. Todavia,  de se registar avanos extraordinrios num sector que comeou h cerca de duas dcadas e meia com pequenos crditos, e que, de 2009 a 2014, realizou 52 mil operaes de crdito, mobilizou cerca de trs milhes de contos, beneficiando cerca de nove mil pessoas em Cabo Verde. Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, No quadro das estratgias bem sucedidas de desenvolvimento ao nvel dos diferentes continentes e pases, o microcrdito vem ocupando de forma crescente um papel de relevo, com destaque para as polticas focalizadas na capacitao das camadas mais desfavorecidas da populao. Desnecessrio ser referir, aqui, a importncia da microfinana, com nfase no mbito da incluso financeira e social, num pas como Cabo Verde, onde, apesar dos progressos notveis registados desde a Independncia  presente data, tanto no domnio econmico como no social, a pobreza ainda afecta uma parcela significativa da nossa populao, cerca de 26% segundo dados disponveis. Para alm da falta de oportunidades aliada a nveis de rendimento e de consumo fracos, a pobreza est intimamente associada a limitaes em termos de capital humano, decorrentes de situaes desfavorveis ao nvel da sade, da educao, da segurana e acesso s instituies e aos servios pblicos de um modo geral. Sendo certo que as potencialidades do microcrdito extravasam amplamente a problemtica da reduo da pobreza, importa reconhecer que o acesso ao crdito representa umas das principais barreiras para as camadas mais desfavorecidas da populao. Como escreve o Sr. Muhammad Yunus "Microcrdito  muito mais que emprestar dinheiro e receb-lo de volta. Esta  apenas uma parte. Microcrdito  tambm mudana social". Desse modo, no posso deixar de felicitar os organizadores deste Frum pela oportunidade do mesmo, na medida em que ele vem no preciso momento em que vrias aces esto a ser desenvolvidas para dar mais nfase s polticas de incluso financeira. Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, Permitam-me recordar um estudo em que paricipei, elaborado aquando da realizao do Simpsio Internacional sobre Microfinanciamento e Promoo de Micro e Pequenas Empresas, no ano de 2000 em Cabo Verde. Este estudo, de h 15 anos atrs, concluiu que, no obstante o desenvolvimento verificado at  data da sua realizao, o sistema de microfinana deparava-se com inmeros constrangimentos ao nvel do quadro institucional e legal. No rol desses constrangimentos, destacava-se a inexistncia de polticas e medidas concretas e explicitadas, enquadradas por uma estratgia coerente e traduzidas num quadro legal e regulamentar, dirigidas ao sector da microfinana. Em vez disso, predominavam as intervenes pontuais e/ou medidas operacionais sem a consequente traduo legal. Ao nvel dos intervenientes no terreno, o estudo em questo tinha concludo que as ONGs eram de longe o maior impulsionador do principal produto da microfinana, o microcrdito, pelas seguintes razes:  Tinham o maior nmero de crditos concedidos;  Abrangiam muito mais beneficirios;  Tinham a mais significativa estrutura de recursos humanos afectos ao sector de micro-crdito; e  Eram os principais empreendedores das aces de formao. Todavia, o problema de fundo que em 2000 se colocava ao sistema de microcrdito em Cabo Verde era a sua sustentabilidade. Com efeito, apesar de muitos dos intervenientes no sector do microcrdito terem j na altura a conscincia da no eternidade dos fundos que estavam a gerir, que na maioria dos casos provinham de fontes externas, raros eram aqueles que dispunham de um fundo rotativo, ou seja, de um fundo que se auto alimentava. Neste particular, uma das recomendaes desse estudo tinha a ver com a questo da garantia de sustentabilidade. Ou seja, para que o sector de micro-crdito melhore a performance e perdure,  absolutamente necessrio que os seus intervenientes constituam fundos rotativos e lucrativos, para que no fiquem na dependncia eterna de financiamentos a fundo perdido. Hoje, uma dcada e meia depois constato com satisfao que um importante caminho j foi percorrido e que o panorama  algo diferente do de ento, embora ainda permaneam alguns dos problemas maiores. Ora, se em 2000 se falava da necessidade premente de coordenao entre as diversas instituies com interveno na rea de microfinana e a inexistncia de intermedirios especializados nas operaes de financiamento, hoje a preocupao maior tem a ver com a materializao das condies institucionais, legais e regulamentares para uma implementao coerente das polticas de promoo, crescimento e profissionalizao do sector das microfinanas, enquanto instrumento privilegiado de promoo da cidadania econmica, bem como de incluso social e financeira. Prova disso so as matrias que constam do programa de actividades da IV Semana Nacional de Microfinanas, cujo tema central  o Processo de Transformao, entre outros que reputo de muita importncia e actualidade, no mbito da mudana de paradigma de desenvolvimento do sistema microfinanceiro. Segundo avanou o Senhor Presidente Jacinto Santos, com o debate  volta desse tema central, pretende-se recolher mximos subsdios possveis, para permitir que alguns dispositivos das leis possam ser adequados antes da sua implementao efectiva, contribuindo, assim, para que todo o processo de transformao seja um produto coerente. Sublinhou que a Federao que preside vai insistir no facto de que  necessrio um plano de transformao especfico para um perodo de cinco anos. Este plano de transformao, ainda segundo o Presidente Jacinto Santos, implica formao, assistncia tcnica, informao, preparao no terreno e recursos financeiros e tcnicos, inovao tecnolgica, sistemas de informaes e gesto, para alm de uma superviso bancria para promover e alavancar essas instituies, para que possam cumprir a sua finalidade social. Dito doutra forma, a transformao em causa refere-se, fundamentalmente, ao processo de converso das instituies de microfinancas em instituies que exeram uma actividade comercial regulamentada, devidamente autorizada e supervisionada pelo Banco de Cabo Verde. Posso assegurar-lhe, Senhor Presidente, que partilho, no essencial, das suas opinies relativamente ao processo gradual, equilibrado e ajustado de transformao. Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, Considero que ao nvel institucional e legal o passo decisivo para a Transformao foi dado com a aprovao da Lei n 83/VIII/2015, de 16 de Janeiro, que estabelece o regime jurdico da actividade das microfinanas e respectivas instituies. De forma geral, a publicao dessa lei veio trazer desafios novos ao BCV, ao mesmo tempo que traz benefcios vrios em termos de disciplina das instituies de microfinanas, h muito acalentada pelas instituies desta natureza j existentes. Pois, o sector das microfinanas passa, doravante, a ser supervisionado e regulamentado por uma instituio autnoma, no caso o Banco Central, na linha das recomendaes de instituies internacionais, nomeadamente o Banco Mundial. O resultado esperado ao nvel macro  que venha a garantir a estabilidade e incluso financeiras dos clientes dessas instituies, proteger os depositantes, uma maior alocao de recursos e a acelerao do desenvolvimento do sector. Ao nvel micro pretende-se que estas instituies venham a ter uma gesto mais profissional, respeitando as boas prticas de governao, em termos de prestao de contas, de transparncia, bem como de uma gesto de riscos com mais responsabilidade. Mas antes disso j tinha sido dado um outro importante passo. Refiro-me  aprovao pelo Governo, do Plano Estratgico para o Desenvolvimento do Sector de Micro-Finanas, para o perodo de 2014-2019, com o objectivo de facilitar o desenvolvimento de um sector microfinanceiro slido, diversificado, competitivo e inclusivo. Para que possa assumir de forma responsvel e durvel a sua misso, as instituies de microfinanas devem orientar as suas prticas de maneira a garantir a sustentabilidade operacional e financeira e, desta feita, proporcionar aos seus clientes, uma oferta vivel e diversificada de servios e produtos financeiros adaptados s suas reais necessidades. Por outro lado, reconhece-se que, alm da sua funo de intermediao financeira, as instituies de microfinanas tambm exercem um papel determinante no processo de intermediao social, criando oportunidades de emprego e rendimento s camadas mais vulnerveis da populao, o que contribui para o desenvolvimento econmico e para a reduo sustentada da pobreza. No que  sustentabilidade do sistema de microcrdito diz respeito, tal qual h 15 anos atrs, julgo de extrema importncia uma reflexo aprofundada sobre duas questes fundamentais. A primeira tem a ver com o custo do crdito e a segunda refere-se ao reembolso, mais precisamente  garantia do reembolso. No  minha inteno pretender debruar-se, neste momento, com a profundidade e a complexidade requeridas, sobre essas duas questes de capital importncia para a sustentabilidade do microcrdito. Todavia, pelo que pudemos constatar da anlise dos intervenientes do sistema de micro-crdito que constam do estudo feito no ano de 2000, existe uma grande diversidade de taxas de juro aplicadas, bem como de sistemas de garantia. Igualmente, sem querer entrar na polmica  volta do carcter, da natureza e da funo do microcrdito, julgo, no entanto, que na ptica da sustentabilidade do sistema, a taxa de juro geralmente deve ser aquela que garanta o pagamento dos custos do funcionamento da actividade creditcia e da manuteno do valor real do fundo rotativo. Com efeito, como ficou demonstrado ao longo do j referido estudo, a questo central que se pe no  tanto o custo do crdito, mas sim o acesso a ele, embora obviamente a eficincia seja um requisito fundamental ao melhor funcionamento da actividade. Do mesmo modo, que, tambm dentro da ptica da perenidade do sistema, todo o crdito concedido deve estar associado a mecanismos de garantia eficazes que garantam, com uma probalidade razovel, a sua recuperao. Tambm esta questo no tem sido pacfica, por, aparentemente implicar a excluso de grandes franjas de camadas da populao desfavorecidas. Penso que a multiplicidade de sistemas de garantia aplicados pelos diferentes intervenientes contactados, no mbito da realizao desse estudo, exclui a existncia de uma tal relao. Na verdade, exigindo garantias as mais diversas possveis, os nossos intervenientes puderam garantir uma taxa de reembolso que pode ser considerada de razovel, para a natureza deste tipo de operao financeira. Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, A j referida Lei que institui o regime jurdico da actividade das microfinanas e respectivas instituies estabelece que para as ONGs que captam depsitos do pblico e transformam-nos em crdito, a superviso  exercida pelo Banco de Cabo Verde. Basicamente, esta superviso consiste no acompanhamento e controlo do cumprimento das regras prudenciais, nomeadamente o rcio de solvabilidade, a constituio de reservas mnimas e os limites de riscos, a fim de proteger o sistema financeiro em geral e a segurana dos depositantes, em particular. Julgo que as instituies de microfinanas s tm a ganhar com a superviso do Banco Central, na medida em que d garantias de transparncia, segurana e credibilidade, o que facilita a atraco de recursos financeiros, mormente de organismos internacionais, de bancos de desenvolvimento e de investidores, para o funding das suas operaes. Assim, no mbito do Projecto de Apoio ao Desenvolvimento da Finana Inclusiva em Cabo Verde financiado pela Cooperao Luxemburguesa, encontra-se na fase final de apreciao para subsequente aprovao pelo BCV um conjunto de regulamentos prudenciais tais como fundos prprios, rcio de solvabilidade, limites e concentrao de riscos, provises, controlo interno e indicadores de performance econmico-financeiros, ajustados  natureza especfica das instituies de microfinanas. Ou seja, a abordagem do Banco Central relativamente aos chamados microbancos tem que ser necessariamente diferente da adoptada para a banca tradicional, sem, no entanto, descurar o rigor que dever ser sempre exigido a quem gere fundos alheios. A dinmica de transformao exige mudanas de comportamentos e de processos, nas instituies, na legislao e na regulamentao. Todavia, comporta riscos, cria resistncia e desafios a vrios nveis, nomeadamente na estrutura de propriedade, na capitalizao, na estrutura legal e no modelo de governana. Todavia,  importante reconhecer que o factor fundamental, na maior parte das transformaes institucionais ocorridas em muitas paragens, foi a necessidade de ter acesso a maiores e mais flexveis fontes de captao de recursos. Termino reiterando todo o interesse e empenhamento do BCV na implementao e criao das condies institucionais e regulatrias, para o desenvolvimento sustentvel e inclusivo das instituies de microfinanas. Muito obrigado pela vossa ateno! Praia, 11 de Novembro de 2015 Joo Serra /Governador do Banco de Cabo Verde/

Title: Intervention in the presentation of the book BCV 40 years of History and tribute to 25 personalities who played roles of great relevance to the BCV
text: Intervention of the Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde, Dr. Joao Serra, in the acts of public presentation of the book Banco de Cabo Verde - 40 years of history and tribute to personalities who played roles of great relevance and marked indelible the BCV, April 14, 2016. Mr. Ex. President of the Republic and former Prime Minister, Commander Pedro Verona Pires, Mr. Former Prime Minister, Dr. Carlos Whanon Veiga Madam Deputy Secretary of State for the Minister of Finance and Plan, Dr Esana Carvalho, Gentlemen, ex. Finance Ministers, Drs. Amaro da Luz and Jose Tomas Veiga, Gentlemen, ex. Governors of the Bank of Cape Verde, Drs. Corentino Santos, Amaro da Luz, Osvaldo Sequeira, Olavo Correia and Carlos Burgo, Members of the Board of Directors, the Supervisory Board and the Advisory Board of the BCV, Gentlemen, ex. Members of the Board of Directors of the BCV, Madam Representative of BCV Employees, Dr. Raquel Fortes Horta, Honored Gentlemen, Mr. BCV Employees, in assets and retirement, Guest Gentlemen, Ladies and gentlemen, I am pleased to greet you and welcome you to this event that marks the culmination of the activities commemorating the 40th anniversary of the Bank of Cape Verde. Let me begin by expressing the thanks of the Board of Directors to all those who have accepted our invitation to be with us on this very special day for our institution. On September 29, 2015, banco de Cabo Verde celebrated the 40th Anniversary of its creation. Over these years, the BCV has grown, developed and consolidated, following the transformations of various nature that have been happening in the country. The Bank of Cape Verde was present in many remarkable moments of our collective history, walking side by side with the other institutions of the republic and responding affirmatively to all calls. In benefit of the truth, the history of bcv is confused with the history of Cape Verde itself as an independent country. Indeed, the widely recognized success of Cape Verde's development effort is also due to a large extent to the strong performance that the Bank of Cape Verde has had in the 40 years of its existence, ensuring the value of the national currency, stability and modernization of the monetary and financial system, as well as developing and running the payment system. With the main focus on maintaining price stability, bcv's monetary policy objectives have been directed over the past 18 years towards the defence of the fixed parity of the Cape Verdean shield against the euro, ensuring exchange rate stability, a key factor in the development of trade and increased external investment. Thus, it is not by chance that the Bank of Cape Verde has been celebrating its fortieth anniversary under the motto "BCV: 40 years committed to development". It is, in fact, a remarkable ephemeris in the history of the institution, which is why it has been celebrated in a special way, with the realization of an extensive set of activities alusive to date in 2015. The Bank of Cape Verde to continue to build its present and, consequently, its future, necessarily has to know its past. Is based on this premise that is born the work entitled "Banco de Cabo Verde - 40 years of history", also framed in the activities commemorating the fortieth anniversary of the institution. With this book it is intended to register and make known in a synthetic way, through a brief historical review, the evolution of the Cape Verdean banking system, from the formal appearance of the first banking institution in Cape Verde  the National Overseas Bank  to the day to this day. The institutional approach was given priority, leaving for another opportunity other approaches of information and analysis that are also legitimate and are part of our institutional heritage. Institutions are the reflection of men who at every moment give them body, despite the current notion that people pass and institutions become. But it must not be forgotten that it is the people who make the institutions and they are worth what they devote to them. Put another way, an institution is not made by its infrastructure, or just by its history, it is made fundamentally by the people who built this story. In this sense, we took advantage of the moment of elaboration of the above-mentioned book to, in an attitude that we deem fair and commendable, remember and record in the collective memory many of those who were relevant figures of the BCV, on condition that these men and women who are outstanding to the institution are only a sample of a wide and varied range of competent professionals and with feelings of service to the cause of the Bank of Cape Verde. Thus, we sought, throughout the work, to tell the most remarkable moments in the history of the BCV through research, interviews, looks and testimonies of many of those who formed such an important institution of regulation, supervision and promoting the smooth functioning of the monetary and financial system of 40 years ago to this part. The testimonies are told in the first person, because there is no better way to perpetuate the institutional memory, than to give voice to those who have directly experienced the institution, and/or those who, in the most diverse qualities, were protagonists of the moments that marked the life of the institution. Unfortunately, for reasons that go beyond us and which we deeply regret, we have not been able to collect testimonies from some people who have also played roles of great relevance, with decisive contributions to what the BCV is today. Despite this setback, which does not affect the essence of the project that guided the preparation of this book, we believe that we are making an important contribution to the recording of the history of the institution. In this context, it is with great satisfaction that, in the context of the activities commemorating the fortieth anniversary of the BCV, I have the honour of launching this work, which seeks to highlight and share the moments and facts that have indeliblely marked the institution. A word of appreciation and thanks to all those who in one way or another contributed so that this project could become a reality. A special mention to all those who with their testimonies and testimonies gave life to this book. We are sure that your contribution has only greatly endeaved this work. In the context of the activities commemorating the 40th anniversary of its creation, a relevant date full of symbolism, the Bank of Cape Verde wants to thank deeply and pay a fair and simple tribute to all the men and women who contributed, in a relevant way, to the creation, growth and maturation of this institution which is one of the pillars of the Cape Verdean monetary and financial system. Unfortunately, it is not possible to have here with us, in this solemn act, many others who also deserve this recognition and distinction. With the reservation of this embarrassment, we think that the personalities now honored, for their valuable personal and professional contribution to the institution, represent only one symbol, not forgetting all the others who also stood out in the meritorious and resilient action at the service of the Bank of Cape Verde. Reasons to justify the merits of our honorees are not lacking and are exhaustive. However, in order not to extend myself in this brief speech of homage, I turn to one of the greatest exponents of classical Greek philosophy, Aristotle, when he recalled, in the lucidity that marked his acts and discourses, that "honor is not to receive titles, but to deserve them". I am deeply convinced that the Bank of Cape Verde in honoring these men and women no longer does not recognize a debt of gratitude to these people, for the intensity with which they made things happen in favor of the institution. A very special word of appreciation goes to my predecessors, the former Governors Corentino Santos, Amaro da Luz, Oswaldo Sequeira, Olavo Correia and Carlos Burgo who were at the head of this institution and who marked and dictated what is now the Bank of Cape Verde. As in the past, the BCV is currently facing new challenges and is determined to overcome them successfully. In fact, since the outbreak of the recent international economic and financial crisis that began in 2008, central banks, regulators and supervisors in the financial system have been faced with completely new situations. These situations have required innovative and often unconventional responses. In fact, these are new times that require new positions, behaviours and attitudes from the various actors in the economic, monetary and financial system. As since September 29, 1975, banco de Cabo Verde, with the support of all its employees and institutional partners, will continue to fulfil its role as guarantor of price stability and the proper functioning of the monetary and financial system. It will continue to support the country's economic and financial development, creating conditions for deepening financial intermediation, reducing risk and increasing the confidence of economic actors in the national currency and our financial institutions. The Governor and the Board of Directors of the BCV express their strong commitment to continue to fully fulfill their duties, with the commitment and professionalism of all its Employees. I end by addressing the honorees a sincere thanks for their dedication to this House. Thank you all for your attention!

Senhor ex. Presidente da Repblica e ex. Primeiro Ministro, Comandante Pedro Verona Pires, Senhor ex. Primeiro Ministro, Dr. Carlos Whanon Veiga Senhora Secretria de Estado Adjunta da Ministra das Finanas e do Plano, Dr. Esana Carvalho, Senhores ex. Ministros das Finanas, Drs. Amaro da Luz e Jos Toms Veiga, Senhores ex. Governadores do Banco de Cabo Verde, Drs. Corentino Santos, Amaro da Luz, Osvaldo Sequeira, Olavo Correia e Carlos Burgo, Senhores Membros do Conselho de Administrao, do Conselho Fiscal e do Conselho Consultivo do BCV, Senhores ex. Membros do Conselho de Administrao do BCV, Senhora Representante dos Colaboradores do BCV, Dr. Raquel Fortes Horta, Senhores Homenageados, Senhores Colaboradores do BCV, no activo e na reforma, Senhores Convidados, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores,  com prazer que vos cumprimento e vos dou as boas vindas neste evento que marca o culminar das actividades comemorativas do quadragsimo aniversrio do Banco de Cabo Verde. Permitam-me comear por expressar o agradecimento do Conselho de Administrao a todos os que aceitaram o nosso convite, para estarem connosco neste dia to especial para a nossa instituio. O Banco de Cabo Verde comemorou, no dia 29 de Setembro de 2015, o Quadragsimo Aniversrio da sua criao. Ao longo destes anos, o BCV cresceu, desenvolveu-se e consolidou-se, acompanhando as transformaes de diversa natureza que foram acontecendo no pas. O Banco de Cabo Verde esteve presente em muitos momentos marcantes da nossa histria colectiva, caminhando lado a lado com as demais instituies da repblica e respondendo de forma afirmativa a todos os chamamentos. Em abono da verdade, a histria do BCV confunde-se com a prpria histria de Cabo Verde como pas independente. Com efeito, o sucesso, amplamente reconhecido, do esforo de desenvolvimento de Cabo Verde deve-se, tambm, em boa medida, ao forte desempenho que o Banco de Cabo Verde tem tido nestes 40 anos da sua existncia, garantindo o valor da moeda nacional, a estabilidade e a modernizao do sistema monetrio e financeiro, bem como desenvolvendo e fazendo funcionar o sistema de pagamentos. Tendo como atribuio principal a manuteno da estabilidade dos preos, os objectivos de poltica monetria do BCV tm-se orientado, nos ltimos 18 anos, para a defesa da paridade fixa do escudo cabo-verdiano em relao ao euro, garantindo a estabilidade cambial, factor essencial ao desenvolvimento das trocas comerciais e ao aumento do investimento externo. Assim, no  por acaso que o Banco de Cabo Verde vem comemorando o seu quadragsimo aniversrio sob o lema BCV: 40 anos comprometido com o desenvolvimento. Trata-se, efectivamente, de uma efemride marcante na histria da instituio, razo pela qual vem sendo comemorada de uma forma especial, com a realizao de um conjunto extenso de actividades alusivas  data, em 2015. O Banco de Cabo Verde para continuar a construir com solidez o seu presente e, consequentemente, o seu futuro, tem, necessariamente, que conhecer o seu passado.  partindo desta premissa que nasce a obra intitulada Banco de Cabo Verde  40 anos de Histria, tambm enquadrada nas actividades comemorativas do quadragsimo aniversrio da instituio. Com este livro pretende-se registar e dar a conhecer de forma sinttica, atravs de uma breve resenha histrica, a evoluo do sistema bancrio cabo-verdiano, desde o aparecimento formal da primeira instituio bancria em Cabo Verde  o Banco Nacional Ultramarino  at aos dias de hoje. Privilegiou-se a abordagem institucional, deixando para uma outra oportunidade outras abordagens de informaes e anlises que tambm so legtimas e fazem parte do nosso patrimnio institucional. As instituies so o reflexo dos homens que em cada momento as do corpo, apesar da noo corrente de que as pessoas passam e as instituies ficam. Mas no se pode esquecer que so as pessoas que fazem as instituies e estas valem aquilo que aquelas as devotarem. Dito doutro modo, uma instituio no  feita por sua infraestrutura, ou apenas por sua histria, ela  feita fundamentalmente pelas pessoas que construram essa histria. Neste sentido, aproveitou-se o momento de elaborao do livro acima referido para, numa atitude que julgamos justa e louvvel, lembrar e registar na memria colectiva muitos daqueles que foram figuras relevantes do BCV, na condio de que estes homens e mulheres marcantes para a instituio sejam somente uma amostra de um leque vasto e variado de profissionais competentes e com sentimentos de servio  causa do Banco de Cabo Verde. Assim, procurou-se, ao longo da obra, contar os momentos mais marcantes da histria do BCV atravs de investigao, entrevistas, olhares e testemunhos de grande parte daqueles que enformaram to importante instituio de regulao, superviso e promoo do bom funcionamento do sistema monetrio e financeiro de h 40 anos a esta parte. Os testemunhos so contados na primeira pessoa, pois, no h melhor forma de perpetuar a memria institucional, do que dar voz aos que vivenciaram de forma directa a instituio, e/ou aqueles que, nas mais diversas qualidades, foram protagonistas dos momentos que marcaram a vida da mesma. Infelizmente, por razes que nos ultrapassam e que lamentamos profundamente, no se pde recolher testemunhos de algumas pessoas que tambm protagonizaram papis de grande relevncia, com contribuies decisivas para o que o BCV  hoje. Apesar deste contratempo, que no afecta o essencial do projecto que norteou a elaborao deste livro, pensamos estar a dar um contributo importante para o registo da histria da instituio. Neste contexto,  com grande satisfao que, no quadro das actividades comemorativas do quadragsimo aniversrio do BCV, tenho a honra de proceder ao lanamento desta obra, que procura realar e partilhar os momentos e factos que marcaram de forma indelvel a instituio. Uma palavra de apreo e de agradecimento a todos aqueles que de uma forma ou de outra contriburam para que este projecto pudesse se tornar realidade. Uma meno especial a todos aqueles que com o seu testemunho e depoimentos deram vida ao presente livro. Estamos certos que o vosso contributo s engrandeceu esta obra. No mbito das actividades comemorativas dos 40 anos da sua criao, uma data relevante e repleta de simbolismo, o Banco de Cabo Verde quer agradecer profundamente e render uma justa e singela homenagem a todos os homens e mulheres que contriburam, de forma relevante, para a criao, crescimento e amadurecimento desta instituio que  um dos pilares do sistema monetrio e financeiro cabo-verdiano. Lamentavelmente no  possvel ter aqui connosco, neste acto solene, muitos outros tambm merecedores deste reconhecimento e distino. Com a ressalva deste constrangimento, pensamos que as personalidades ora homenageadas, pelo seu valioso contributo pessoal e profissional em prol da instituio, representam apenas um smbolo, no esquecendo todos os outros que tambm se destacaram na aco meritria e resiliente ao servio do Banco de Cabo Verde. Razes para justificar os mritos dos nossos homenageados no faltam e so exaustivas. Todavia, para no me alongar neste breve discurso de homenagem, recorro a um dos expoentes mximos da filosofia clssica grega, Aristteles, quando lembrou, na lucidez que marcava os seus actos e discursos, que "a honra no consiste em receber ttulos, mas em merec-los". Estou profundamente convicto de que o Banco de Cabo Verde ao homenagear esses homens e mulheres mais no faz que reconhecer uma dvida de gratido que tem para com estas pessoas, pela intensidade com que fizeram as coisas acontecer a favor da instituio. Uma palavra de apreo muito especial vai para os meus antecessores, os ex. Governadores Corentino Santos, Amaro da Luz, Oswaldo Sequeira, Olavo Correia e Carlos Burgo que estiveram  frente desta instituio e que marcaram e ditaram o que  hoje o Banco de Cabo Verde. Tal como no passado, o BCV enfrenta, neste momento, novos desafios e est determinado a ultrapass-los com sucesso. Como efeito, desde o eclodir da recente crise econmica e financeira internacional que teve incio em 2008, os bancos centrais, os reguladores e supervisores do sistema financeiro vm sendo confrontados com situaes completamente novas. Estas situaes tm exigido respostas inovadoras e muitas vezes pouco convencionais. Na verdade, so novos tempos que exigem dos diversos intervenientes do sistema econmico, monetrio e financeiro novos posicionamentos, comportamentos e atitudes. Como desde 29 de Setembro de 1975, o Banco de Cabo Verde, com o apoio de todos os seus colaboradores e parceiros institucionais, continuar a cumprir o seu papel de garante da estabilidade dos preos e de bom funcionamento do sistema monetrio e financeiro. Continuar a apoiar o desenvolvimento econmico e financeiro do pas, criando condies para o aprofundamento da intermediao financeira, a reduo do risco e o aumento da confiana dos agentes econmicos na moeda nacional e nas nossas instituies financeiras. O Governador e o Conselho de Administrao do BCV expressam o seu forte compromisso em continuar a cumprir na plenitude as suas atribuies, com o empenho e profissionalismo de todos os seus Colaboradores. Termino endereando aos homenageados um agradecimento sincero pela sua dedicao a esta Casa. A todos, um obrigado pela vossa ateno!

Title: Speech at the Meeting between the Bank of Cape Verde and the Credit Institutions
text: Speech by the Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde, Dr. Joao Serra, at the Meeting between the Bank of Cape Verde and the Credit Institutions, 20 July 2016 Representatives of banking institutions, Members of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Cape Verde, Madam Auditor General of the Securities Market, Dear BCV Employees, Ladies and gentlemen, I am pleased to greet you and welcome you at this II Meeting of the Management of the Bank of Cape Verde with the Administrations of the National Banking. The banking crisis that has shaken the world since 2008 is proving to be a very complex and costly budgetary, economic and social problem for an increasing number of countries. Indeed, the resolution of banking crises has almost always been through bail out, i.e. a massive injection of public funds into the sector and an increase in the public debt of the countries concerned, which is becoming political, economic and socially increasingly unsustainable. In the face of this poignant reality, one of the major challenges facing the public authorities is to know what to do to prevent a banking crisis and, in the case of this, limit its effects at the lowest possible cost to the economy, taxpayers and aerators. The problem has been attacked on several fronts, notably by strengthening regulation and supervision, as well as establishing strategies for crisis management and bank resolution. From the outend, one can question the reasons for the authorities' so much concern about the banking sector. For the dominant economic and legal chain, in market economies the creation, development, restructuring, closure and bankruptcy of undertakings are normal facts of business life. In a functional market, with adequate regulation, competition is the seed of efficiency and the mechanism for selecting the most capable. The answer to the particular institutional concern with banking is that, unlike so-called normal companies where the effects of bankruptcy are restricted to their shareholders and direct stakeholders, the spill over effects of crises in the financial sector or the closure of banks spread over the entire economy, especially when the institutions concerned are systemic in size. In the case of banks, these are linked to a set of contracts that have to be fulfilled, and often renewed on a permanent basis, in order for the economy to function harmoniously and efficiently. The interruption of the normal functioning of a bank can cause serious constraints to individuals and companies, because they may suddenly be deprived of access to their availability, make their payments or access credit lines. Thus, subjecting banks to the classic procedures of restructuring or liquidation of companies would lead to the ipending of their clients being able to stay months or even years without being able to access their funds, with all the constraints that this brings to the entities involved and to the economy. The recent global financial crisis has given bare the enormous shortcomings of regulatory and supervisory mechanisms based on the conviction that the maturity and efficiency of modern markets, as well as corporate governance and bank risk management would be sufficient to safeguard or immunize the banking sector from crises that had periodically beset it in the past. It was then questioned about the current architecture of the international financial system and its regulatory and supervisory mechanisms. Indeed, the system in force so far, based on Basel II, proved incapable of meeting the objectives for which it was established, so that a process of its modernization and reform, embodied in the Basel III initiative, began. It is in this new context that, in the framework of a preventive and proactive approach, the Cape Verdean authorities have been taking a set of initiatives to ensure the soundness of the national banking system, as well as to provide an adequate response to crisis situations if these occur. The publication in April 2014 of the Basic Law of the Financial System and the Financial Institutions Activities Act was the first step towards creating an institutional framework better suited to the challenges facing the national banking system today. In addition to the strengthening and modernization of the mechanisms for regulating and supervising the banking system, this new regulatory framework for the activities of financial institutions presents as a novelty the establishment of mechanisms for the prevention and management of banking crises and the creation of deposit and investment guarantee systems. Since the publication of the laws mentioned above, the Bank of Cape Verde has been developing a set of initiatives aimed at embodying the directives emanating from them, having already published a considerable number of regulatory notices, in a process still in progress. The BCV has been prioritizing actions aimed at strengthening the mechanisms for preventing banking crises, either by publishing new regulations or by strengthening the central bank's supervisory capacity. In the chapter of monitoring and supervision of banking, the actions of the Bank of Cape Verde have been guided by the demand for greater transparency and strengthening of the balance sheet of banks. In this context, it has been making as exhaustive a survey as possible of the quality of the banks' credit portfolio, identifying their problems and demanding the therapies that are required. In fact, the high level of uneven credits, the near stagnation of activity and low profitability have been the main problems facing Cape Verdean banks at the moment. Compared to countries with the same characteristics and size, Cape Verde has higher levels of non-parade credit and lower levels of credit activity and return on assets and equity. Solving the larger problem, i.e. uneven claims, requires concerted efforts between the Government, the BCV and the bank administrations to make it work, without unnecessary disruption to the banking system and compromising the stability of the bank system. Another issue that has been the subject of the Bank of Cape Verde's concerns is the strengthening of the capital base of Cape Verdean banks. The high level of default in the system and the high sectoral concentration of credit point to the risk of material potential losses. Thus, solvency risks remain very as stress tests attest. On the other hand, although above the regulatory limit (10%), Cape Verde has solvency ratio levels below similar island economies. There is therefore a need to strengthen the level of the minimum regulatory solvency ratio, as well as the creation of additional buffers, i.e. complementary financial cushions, to mitigate the potential impact of a risk accumulation, as recommended by international best practice. In the chapter of crisis management, the current law imposes on banks the requirement to prepare and submit to the BCV for the purpose of assessment and approval, the Recovery Plans and their developments embodied in the Resolution Plans. The purpose of these plans is to identify the measures that could be taken to correct in due course a situation that compromises or could compromise a bank's financial balance. Recovery and resolution plans are new and very complex instruments, which has created some difficulties for banks with their preparation. Hence the need for precision, on the one hand, of some of its fundamental concepts, and, on the other hand, in the use of indicators that allow credit institutions to more easily point out when recovery measures can be activated. There is also concern about the increasing materialisation of some operational risks, such as the risks associated with the electronic payment system. It is urgent to know and discuss this issue in a way that together we can find the best solutions. The Bank of Cape Verde is legally responsible, among other functions, for the regulation and supervision of the financial system, having broad powers to approve directives for the performance of supervised entities. The BCV Administration considers that these powers should be exercised with great responsibility and in a framework of dialogue and consultation. That is, in a thoughtful, balanced and always in the interest of the public good, the economy and population of the country, depositors and investors. It is with this purpose and the intention of analyzing the above mentioned issues and seeking consensus on the same ones that we are gathered here today, with the strong conviction that this Meeting will leave important subsidies and an enhanced commitment so that we can have in Cape Verde a strong banking sector, resilient and prepared to face possible systemic shocks of different nature. Thank you for your attention!
