Title: Speech at the 4th Meeting of Supervision of the Central Banks of Portuguese-speaking Countries
text: Speech of the Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde, Dr. Joao Serra, at the 4th Meeting of Supervision of the Central Banks of Portuguese-speaking Countries, 21 to 23 September 2016. Representatives of the Central Banks of portuguese-speaking countries, Madam Auditor General of the Securities Market, Mr. Administrator of the Bank of Cape Verde, Madam Director of the Department of Supervision of Financial Institutions, Mr. BCV Collaborators, Ladies and gentlemen, I am pleased to greet and welcome you to Cape Verde and the 4th Banking Supervision Meeting of the Central Banks of Portuguese-speaking Countries. Let me begin by expressing the sincere thanks of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Cape Verde to all those who have accepted our invitation to be with us at this very important event. It is important because it allows us to share good supervisory practices and deepen possible mechanisms for communication, integration and cooperation between participating central banks. In this context, the recent institutional and regulatory changes emanating from the BIS - Bank for International Payments, through the Committees based there, the most important being the Basel Banking Supervision, as an unavoidable international reference in the framework of banking supervision. Moreover, it is essential that there is close institutional collaboration and cooperation between our supervisory authorities and other relevant entities. In an increasingly globalised world, the supervision of the financial system, the latest in the banking sector, has become increasingly complex, requiring global solutions whose are not confined to a single country. That is why this sharing of experiences, knowledge, procedures, concerns and challenges among the central banks of portuguese-speaking countries is extremely pertinst. Ladies and gentlemen, The subprime crisis has brought about a financial crisis of size and complexity that has not happened since the great depression. It brought down institutions that until then were considered strongholds such as Lehman Brothers, devastated economies, caused suffering to the population and, above all, brought about the weaknesses and failures of central bank supervision. In fact, the supervisors were unable to predict the harmful effects of the risks associated with subprime and were also unable to properly assess the extent of the exposure of banks to this category of assets in its most diverse modalities. By the time they realised the complexity and scale of the problem, the crisis had already infected Europe. As a result of this situation, regulators and supervisors in the affected countries have made a thorough reflection and assessment on the weaknesses of the supervisory process. They have also worked on the reform and modernization of the institutional structure, as well as policies and processes, with a view to preventing new crises. In the case of Cape Verde, the financial system has not been directly affected by the international financial crisis, due to its weak integration into the foreign market and its low level of sophistication. However, it has taken advantage of the lessons of recent events to strengthen the protection and process of regulation and supervision of the national financial sector. The Bank of Cape Verde, as the central bank of the Republic, has the responsibility of supervising the entire national financial system. To this end, the approach adopted has been a combination of on-site inspections and indirect monitoring through data provided by supervised institutions, according to a pre-established timetable. This process of inspection and monitoring of financial institutions is intended not only to assess their ability to honour the commitments made to their depositors and aphores, but also to comply with rules and regulations associated with the exercise of the activity. The evaluation of these institutions has been based on the well-known CAMELS* parameters. Although this approach has served the Cape Verdean financial system so far, we should not be satisfied. For, one of the lessons of the recent international financial crisis is that many of the institutions that collapsed were apparently well capitalized, at least to believe the data they presented. Moreover, these same institutions had been evaluated as adequately capitalized and net also by the supervisors. This indicates that there has been an inappropriate assessment of the risks both present and those that subsequently emerged, either by the institutions themselves and by regulators and supervisors. ____________________________________________________________ *Capital Adequacy, Asset Quality, Management, Earnings, Liquidity and Sistems and Controls There is therefore a need for regulators and supervisors to make a more realistic assessment of the risks that banks face and be more likely to make decisions and act quickly whenever situations are detected that could pose a risk to the institution and/or the financial system. It is in this context that the principle of risk-based supervision emerges, which we believe to be the most adjusted paradigm in the face of the new context of the financial system. The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision defines risk-based supervision as a forward-looking approach. Through this approach, the supervisor assesses the various lines of business of a financial institution, as well as the quality of management and internal control systems that is dedicated to the business concerned. Once this is done, it begins to identify the areas of greatest risk and concern, in order to direct the attention of supervisors to them. For its part, the 14th International Conference of Banking Supervisors has held risk-based supervision as the essence of risk-based supervision that the supervisor's focus is risk and available resources are allocated where they are most needed. In addition, risk-based supervision has the advantage of enabling supervisors to better understand the risks incurred in a banking institution and its lines of business. It helps to assess the systemic risk that a bank contains, as well as the likelihood of contagion. It allows a prospective assessment, indicating the sense of risk and provides the supervisor with the necessary inputs to take action that is required. Ladies and gentlemen, In recent years, supervisors have been confronted, with a continued increase in responsibilities. This is without their levels of training and the resources available, following, to a desired level, this increase in attributions. This situation is particularly noticeable in developing countries where human and material resources are scarcer. Furthermore, there is also a context in which the international community has not sufficiently developed the guidelines for effective supervision. In fact, regulators and supervisors who until recently had only the prudential supervision of some banks to take care of the sustainability of the financial system. In addition, they also began to supervise e-money issuing institutions, so-called microbanks, as well as a growing number of Financial Technology companies. All this, along with the concern with the protection of consumers of financial services and financial education, which has been called behavioral supervision. In this context, risk-based supervision helps supervisors allocate and use their scarce resources from a strategic perspective, as well as to prioritize and adjust their interventions according to identified and assessed risks. In recent years, Cape Verde has taken significant steps towards reforming and modernizing the regulatory framework and the supervisory process of financial institutions, with the support of various entities, including Banco de Portugal, the Central Bank of Brazil and bretton woods institutions. In this context, a number of actions and activities have already been developed, of which: The publication in 2014 of the Law Defining the Guiding Principles and the Normative Framework of Reference for the Financial System; The publication, also in 2014, of the Law regulating the Activities of Financial Institutions; The restructuring of the Department of the Bank of Cape Verde with the responsibility of supervising financial institutions, adapting its structure to the current responsibilities and needs of its activity; The strengthening and training of human resources allocated to this Department; and The regulation by the Central Bank of the various directives contained in the two above-mentioned diplomas, and the process is still ongoing. Ladies and gentlemen, In 2015, banco de Cabo Verde adopted the risk-based supervision modality, which was applied throughout that year in supervisory procedures, namely on-site inspections and off-site monitoring. This new approach is based on the identification and monitoring of financial and non-financial risks that the soundness of the financial system, as well as the controls implemented by the institutions for their mitigation. In addition to the improvements made in the supervisory models of generic authorisation banks and insurers, the monitoring model for restricted authorisation banks was restructured in accordance with the improved assessment model developed by the International Monetary Fund. The Financial Stability Report has also been prepared and published, which has incorporated the results of stress tests carried out in the banking sector. It is intended that this reform of the legislation and regulation of the Financial System and the exercise of banking supervision should be in line with best practices at international level, in particular with the European Union, attentive to the agreement of technical and normative convergence existing between this community of European countries and Cape Verde. We are certain that we still have a long way to go in these uncertain times, especially since the Cape Verdean financial system, particularly banks, faces a number of challenges. These relate, above all, to the high level of undocumented credit, low profitability and low rates of credit growth to the economy. I am, however, convinced that with the engagement and collaboration of all stakeholders we will be able to overcome this demanding stage of the development process of our financial system. Generally speaking, it is the global framework that we wanted to share with you in terms of cape Verdean banking reality. We would also like to hear your experiences and key challenges you face. May we together as central banks of Portuguese-speaking countries work for what is our common goal, that is, the financial stability of our countries' banking system. May we bring to fruition the necessary reforms in order to have an increasingly strong, resilient banking sector and prepared to face possible systemic shocks of a different nature. Thank you very much and good work! I declare open the 4th Meeting of Banking Supervision of the Central Banks of portuguese-speaking countries. Beach, September 21, 2016 John Serra /Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde/

Para o efeito, a abordagem adoptada tem sido uma combinao de inspeces on site e monitoramento indirecto atravs de dados fornecidos pelas instituies supervisionadas, segundo um calendrio pr-estabelecido. Este processo de inspeco e acompanhamento das instituies financeiras tem por finalidade no s avaliar a sua capacidade de honrar os compromissos assumidos com os seus depositantes e aforadores, mas tambm o cumprimento de normas e regulamentos associados ao exerccio da actividade. A avaliao dessas instituies tem-se baseado nos sobejamente conhecidos parmetros CAMELS*. Embora esta abordagem tenha servido o sistema financeiro cabo-verdiano at ao momento, no devemos, contudo, darmo-nos por satisfeitos. Pois, uma das lies da recente crise financeira internacional  a de que muitas das instituies que colapsaram eram aparentemente bem capitalizadas, pelo menos, a crer nos dados que apresentavam. Outrossim, essas mesmas instituies tinham sido avaliadas como adequadamente capitalizadas e lquidas tambm pelos supervisores. Este facto indica que houve uma inapropriada avaliao dos riscos tanto presentes como dos que posteriormente emergiram, quer por parte das prprias instituies quer por parte dos reguladores e supervisores. ____________________________________________________________ *Capital Adequacy, Asset Quality, Management, Earnings, Liquidity and Sistems and Controls H, portanto, necessidade dos reguladores e supervisores fazerem uma avaliao mais realista dos riscos que os bancos enfrentam e terem uma maior disponibilidade para tomarem decises e agirem rapidamente sempre que se detectem situaes que possam perigar a instituio e/ou o sistema financeiro.  neste quadro que emerge o princpio da superviso baseada no risco, que reputamos ser o paradigma mais ajustado face ao novo contexto do sistema financeiro. O Comit de Basileia para a Superviso Bancria define a superviso baseada no risco como uma abordagem prospectiva. Atravs desta abordagem, o supervisor avalia as vrias linhas de negcio de uma instituio financeira, bem como a qualidade da gesto e os sistemas de controlo interno que  dedicado aos negcios em causa. Feito isso, passa a identificar as reas de maior risco e preocupao, de forma a direcionar a ateno dos supervisores para as mesmas. Por seu turno, a 14 Conferncia Internacional dos Supervisores Bancrios reteve como essncia da superviso baseada no risco o facto de o foco do supervisor ser o risco e os recursos disponveis serem alocados onde so mais necessrios. Em suma, a superviso baseada no risco apresenta a vantagem de permitir aos supervisores uma maior e melhor compreenso dos riscos incorridos numa instituio bancria e nas suas linhas de negcios. Ajuda a avaliar o risco sistmico que um banco encerra, assim como a probabilidade de contgio. Permite uma avaliao prospectiva, indicando o sentido do risco e fornece ao supervisor os inputs necessrios  tomada de medidas que se impem. Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, Nos ltimos anos, as autoridades de superviso vm sendo confrontadas, com um aumento contnuo de responsabilidades. Isto sem que os seus nveis de capacitao e os recursos disponibilizados acompanhem, a um patamar desejado, este acrscimo de atribuies. Esta situao  particularmente visvel nos pases em vias de desenvolvimento em que os recursos humanos e materiais so mais escassos. A isto acresce-se, ainda, um contexto em que a comunidade internacional no desenvolveu suficientemente as orientaes para uma superviso efectiva. Com efeito, reguladores e supervisores que at h pouco tempo tinham como atribuies apenas a superviso prudencial de alguns bancos passaram, num curto espao de tempo, a cuidar da sustentabilidade do sistema financeiro. Para alm disso, passaram tambm a supervisionar as instituies emissoras de moeda eletrnica, os chamados microbancos, bem como, um nmero crescente de empresas Tecnolgicas Financeiras. Tudo isso, a par da preocupao com a proteo dos consumidores de servios financeiros e com a educao financeira, a que se convencionou chamar de superviso comportamental. Neste quadro, a superviso baseada no risco ajuda os supervisores a alocarem e a usarem os seus escassos recursos numa perspectiva estratgica, bem como a priorizarem e a ajustarem as suas intervenes em funo dos riscos identificados e avaliados. Nos ltimos anos, Cabo Verde vem dando passos significativos tendo em vista a reforma e modernizao do quadro regulatrio e do processo de superviso das instituies financeiras, com o apoio de vrias entidades, nomeadamente do Banco de Portugal, do Banco Central do Brasil e das instituies de Bretton Woods. Neste contexto, foi j desenvolvido um conjunto de aces e actividades, das quais se destacam:  A publicao, em 2014, da Lei que Define os Princpios Orientadores e o Quadro Normativo de Referncia para o Sistema Financeiro;  A publicao, tambm em 2014, da Lei que Regula as Actividades das Instituies Financeiras;  A reestruturao do Departamento do Banco de Cabo Verde com a responsabilidade de superviso das instituies financeiras, adaptando a sua estrutura s responsabilidades e necessidades actuais da sua actividade;  O reforo e formao dos recursos humanos afectos a este Departamento; e  A regulamentao pelo Banco Central das vrias directivas constantes nos dois diplomas acima referidos, estando o processo ainda em curso. Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, Em 2015, o Banco de Cabo Verde adoptou a modalidade de superviso baseada no risco, a qual foi aplicada ao longo desse ano nos procedimentos de superviso, nomeadamente nas inspees on-site e acompanhamento off-site. Esta nova abordagem baseia-se na identificao e monitorizao de riscos financeiros e no financeiros que ameaam a solidez do sistema financeiro, bem como nos controlos implementados pelas instituies para a sua mitigao. A par das melhorias introduzidas nos modelos de superviso dos bancos de autorizao genrica e das seguradoras, procedeu-se  reestruturao do modelo de acompanhamento dos bancos de autorizao restrita, em conformidade com o aperfeioado modelo de avaliao desenvolvido pelo Fundo Monetrio Internacional. Tambm vem sendo elaborado e publicado o Relatrio de Estabilidade Financeira que tem incorporado os resultados de stress tests realizados no sector bancrio. Pretende-se que esta reforma da legislao e regulamentao do Sistema Financeiro e o exerccio da superviso bancria estejam em sintonia com as melhores prticas a nvel internacional, em particular com a Unio Europeia, atento ao acordo de convergncia tcnica e normativa existente entre esta comunidade de pases europeus e Cabo Verde. Estamos certos que ainda nos resta um longo caminho a percorrer nestes tempos de incerteza, tanto mais que o sistema financeiro cabo-verdiano, designadamente os bancos, enfrentam um conjunto de desafios. Estes prendem-se, sobretudo, com o elevado nvel de crdito em situao irregular, a fraca rentabilidade e as baixas taxas de crescimento de crdito  economia. Estou, porm, convicto que com o engajamento e a colaborao de todos os stakeholders conseguiremos vencer mais esta exigente etapa do processo de desenvolvimento do nosso sistema financeiro. Em linhas gerais  o quadro global que queramos partilhar convosco em termos da realidade bancria cabo-verdiana. Tambm gostaramos de ouvir as vossas experincias e principais desafios que enfrentam. Que possamos juntos enquanto bancos centrais dos pases de lngua portuguesa trabalhar para aquele que  o nosso objectivo comum, isto , a estabilidade financeira do sistema bancrio dos nossos pases. Que possamos levar a bom porto as reformas necessrias que se impem para termos um sector bancrio cada vez mais forte, resiliente e preparado para enfrentar eventuais choques sistmicos de diferente natureza. Muito obrigado e bom trabalho! Declaro aberto o 4 Encontro de Superviso Bancria dos Bancos Centrais dos Pases de Lngua Portuguesa. Praia, 21 de Setembro de 2016 Joo Serra /Governador do Banco de Cabo Verde/

Title: Intervention at the Meeting with the Insurance Sector, Praia
text: Intervention of the Governor, Dr. Joao Serra, at the Meeting with the Insurance Sector, Praia, May 23, 2017 Lecturers Professor Jose Figueiredo de Almaca and Dr. Mario Ribeiro, respectively, President and Director of the Insurance and Pension Funds Authority of Portugal, Mr. Administrators of the Bank of Cape Verde, Madam Auditor General of the Securities Market, Members of the Administrations of Insurers Guarantee and Impar, Brokers and Mediators, Directors and Advisors of the Bank of Cape Verde, Technical Gentlemen of the Bank of Cape Verde and the Insurers, Guest Gentlemen, Ladies and gentlemen, I would like to begin by expressing the sincere thanks of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Cape Verde to all those who have accepted our invitation to be with us at this very important event. As Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde, an institution that is also the Supervisory and Regulatory Authority of the Insurance Sector in Cape Verde, I welcome this meeting with the institutions of the Sector and i greet all those responsible and staff here. Let me highlight and greet in particular the distinguished Lecturers Professor Jose Figueiredo de Almaca, President of the Insurance and Pension Funds Authority of Portugal, and Dr. Mario Ribeiro, Director of Behavioral Supervision and Institutional Relations of this same institution. I thank you both deeply for your willingness to be here with us. I want you to know that your presence greatly honors us. We will begin our usual meeting, with an important Conference, where two relevant and relevant issues relating to the insurance sector will be addressed. First, risk-based supervision in the context of the insurance sector, a current theme that will be delivered by our guest, Professor Jose de Almaca. And a second, the current challenges for the insurance sector, no less important topic, to be presented by our also invited, Dr. Mario Ribeiro. Ladies and gentlemen, As we know, the concept of risk-based insurance supervision is a matter that had been debated since the late 1990s by insurance regulatory and supervisory agencies, and in particular by the International Association of Insurance Supervisors, IAIS, through the implementation of the Basic Insurance Principles. In the meantime, the new form of supervisory exercise would gain new momentum with the publication of the Solvency II Directive by the European Parliament in 2009, in principle aimed at the Member States of the European Union, but with a much wider geographical impact. Risk-based supervision, contrary to the traditional form of supervision exercise based on compliance analysis against established rules, is based on principles and best business practices and risk reduction. Thus, this new paradigm of supervision invites a profound change in the work processes of supervisors and supervised supervisors. In fact, its focus is preventive supervision, identified with the study of risks and trends and with timely intervention, in order to minimize the losses of policyholders and participants. But the essential pillars on which the new vision of supervision of insurance activity is based will certainly be developed by Professor Jose de Almaca who, in addition to being President of the Insurance and Pension Funds Authority of Portugal is also a Full Professor, therefore, a highly aresponsible personality to talk to us about these matters. In Cape Verde, assimilation and the necessary behavioral change to work on principles, and no longer by mere compliance with rules, are challenges for both the supervised market and the regulatory and supervisory body itself. In fact, if the institutions are required to develop an integrated management of the entire business and its risks, supervision requires an action that allows a good coordination between onsite and offsite analyses, that is, a face-to-face and distance analysis. This perspective enables market stability, consumer protection, as well as the application of best principles and practices, ultimately aiming at encouraging the raising of the risk management standard and providing a better quality service to both policymakers and beneficiaries. To meet the demands of risk-based supervision, the Banco de Cabo Verde Financial Institutions Supervision Department made a change in its work processes, redefined its priorities for insurance supervision, and redesigned the way information is monitored and processed. On the other hand, we are working on the continuous adaptation of the legislation applicable to the best principles and practices, in order to meet the requirements of insurance supervision, with a focus on risks. Ladies and gentlemen, Achieving goals from a risk-sensitive system consistent with the market is a certainly complex process. If this is for advanced economies, for a small economy like ours it represents an even greater challenge, and therefore deserves an unprecedented change in the work processes, both supervisor and supervised. The insurance sector in Cape Verde still has a marginal share in the production of national wealth, contributing less than 2% to GDP. Therefore, there is a wide growth space of the insurance business, both in terms of volume and in terms of the variety of products to offer. This growth must therefore be promoted with a view to encouraging long-term savings training, which is strategic for a country with a low level of internal savings as is our case. However, there are still strong constraints on the national insurance sector. On the one hand, the low income levels of a significant portion of our population, which prevents it from hiring insurance and forming savings with the acquisition of capitalization bonds and private pension plans. On the other hand, the low risk management culture of a large part of the population, the concentration of insurance in the "Automotive Sector", the weak growth of the "Life Branch" and the weak capacity to retain risks. If overcoming the first constraint will depend on the lasting movement of economic growth, the others, however, represent opportunities for growth for the insurance sector. Such opportunities are realised by increasing population literacy, a process in which the insurance sector should actively participate, investing in product innovation and creating risk retention conditions. Moreover, today there is a considerable set of changes on a global scale, which poses major risks to the business and requires a greater demand for harmonisation of the regulation applicable to the sector. There are numerous changes that currently impact the activity of the insurance sector, namely changes in the age composition of the population, in the way of thinking and acting of the client increasingly assertive, more informed and seeking more personalized products, technological changes with the integration of new technologies, natural disasters, among others. These situations condition the business of the sector, necessarily requiring the consequent change in the business management models of the institutions, as well as the design of new products and services, dealing with new types of risks and the creative search for new solutions. Dr. Mario Ribeiro with his vast and deep technical knowledge and experience in the field will certainly enlighten us much better about the current challenges facing the insurance sector. Despite the small size of our economy and the insurance sector in our financial market, the effects of major trends will be felt in Cape Verde sooner or later, even on a smaller scale, given the increasing globalisation of markets. In this way, the insurance sector is called upon to prepare for the major challenges ahead. Ladies and gentlemen, As we know, the financial guarantees to be presented by insurers are solvency margin and technical provisions. National insurance companies have a good solvency margin. They have never presented major problems in terms of capital solvency. They have always had a much higher degree of margin coverage than the legally required minimum. With regard to the coverage of technical provisions by assets affected, annually insurers have higher levels of coverage than legally required. National insurers thus have a relatively solid financial situation and have had highly positive results in recent years. The main challenge for our insurance sector is to ensure that future responsibilities to policyholders and beneficiaries are constantly maintained, thereby contributing to maintaining the stability of the national financial sector. The achievement of this challenge presupposes, on the one hand, the existence of a modern regulatory framework, complemented with new approaches to supervision at international level, more focused on the issue of risk analysis. On the other hand, it requires an efficient governance system that promotes the security and stability of companies in the sector. Continuously improving risk assessment is an essential requirement that the Bank of Cape Verde, as a supervisory body in the sector, should always take into account. In this context, the regulation on the submission of the internal control report by insurers is of particular importance, as it contributes to the objective of strengthening the financial soundness of the sector. Further legislation and adequacy will also contribute to an increase in production and, therefore, to further development of the sector. In this context, with the approval and publication in 2010 of a set of diplomas that defines the basic principles and the guiding regulatory framework for insurance and insurance mediation, our country has taken a decisive step towards reforming the reference framework for its insurance sector. Nevertheless, I think it is important to draw up a new legal framework for compulsory occupational accident insurance. The law regulating this insurance dates from 1978, a period immediately after national independence, and therefore no longer fits the current reality of the country, particularly with regard to the value of the reference salary for the calculation of premiums and compensation amounts, especially for disabilities and death. Likewise, important aspects of the legislation regulating compulsory motor liability insurance will have to be reviewed, in particular, those on compensation in the event of disabilities and death. Very recently it was assigned to the Automobile Guarantee Fund, under the management of the Bank of Cape Verde, responsibilities under maritime liability insurance. It is now necessary to regulate both the Government and the Bank of Cape Verde, considering, above all, its important social role. The insurance sector is by nature one of the institutional investors and is part of a very small financial market that presents few alternatives in terms of investments. In these circumstances, risk-based supervision should ensure the stability of capital in the sector and, therefore, a good analysis of investments, so that the sector presents sufficient financial guarantees in accordance with the established legal terms. This lack of alternatives has contributed to a high concentration of insurance investments, real estate and financial holdings in other financial institutions, which in our view is a major risk to the management of the asset portfolio of these companies. It is therefore questioned whether or not insurance undertakings should be allowed to apply their assets to technical provisions on products offered abroad. Another no less important challenge has to do with the development of bancassurance in the national financial sector in the near future. In other words, a greater interconnection between banking and insurance, with the possibility of selling insurance products in the balms of banks. Insurers must increasingly invest in greater diversification of their products, including those linked to health and disease, retirement, as well as supplementary insurance. Given the complexity of the existing challenges, they should also make a strong focus on the continuing training of their technicians. Ladies and gentlemen, The Bank of Cape Verde will adopt, within its legal powers, the measures that the development of the insurance sector requires, and as the Government's Financial Advisor will not fail to propose the necessary legal initiatives that are not within its competence. But he wants to do it in an articulate d'or with the sector, hence the reason for this event. In this context, the Conference, which is now starting, and the next Round Table are a unique opportunity that is offered to us for the exchange of experiences and concerns, sharing of lessons and proposals for solutions with regard to the adoption of new supervisory and regulatory approaches aimed at mitigating financial risks and the development of the insurance sector in Cape Verde. Let us hope that this meeting will share joint concerns and experiences and that the objectives pursued will be fully achieved in order to strengthen efficient supervision and consolidate the insurance sector in Cape Verde. Thank you very much and good wishes! Beach, 23 May 2017 John Serra /Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde/
text_original: Interveno do Governador, Doutor Joo Serra, no Encontro com o Setor Segurador, Praia, 23 de maio de 2017 Senhores Conferencistas Professor Doutor Jos Figueiredo de Almaa e Dr. Mrio Ribeiro, respetivamente, Presidente e Director da Autoridade de Seguros e Fundos de Penses de Portugal, Senhores Administradores do Banco de Cabo Verde, Senhora Auditora Geral do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios, Senhores Membros das Administraes das Seguradoras Garantia e Impar, Senhores Corretores e Mediadores, Senhores Diretores e Assessores do Banco de Cabo Verde, Senhores Tcnicos do Banco de Cabo Verde e das Seguradoras, Senhores Convidados, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Gostaria de comear por expressar o sincero agradecimento do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Cabo Verde a todos os que aceitaram o nosso convite, para estarem connosco neste evento to importante. Enquanto Governador do Banco de Cabo Verde, instituio que  tambm a Autoridade de Superviso e Regulao do Sector Segurador em Cabo Verde, congratulo-me com mais este encontro com as instituies do Sector e sado a todos os responsveis e quadros aqui presentes. Permitam-me destacar e saudar em particular os ilustres Conferencistas Professor Doutor Jos Figueiredo de Almaa, Presidente da Autoridade de Seguros e Fundos de Penses de Portugal, e Dr. Mrio Ribeiro, Director de Superviso Comportamental e Relaes Institucionais desta mesma instituio. A ambos agradeo profundamente a disponibilidade de estarem aqui connosco. Quero que saibam que a vossa presena muito nos honra. Vamos iniciar o nosso j habitual encontro, com uma importante Conferncia, onde dois relevantes e pertinentes temas relativos ao sector segurador sero abordados. Um primeiro, a superviso baseada no risco no contexto do sector segurador, um tema da atualidade e que ser proferido pelo nosso convidado, o Professor Jos de Almaa. E um segundo, os desafios atuais para o sector segurador, tema no menos importante, a ser apresentado pelo nosso tambm convidado, o Dr. Mrio Ribeiro. Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, Como sabemos, o conceito de superviso de seguros baseada em riscos  uma matria que j vinha sendo debatida desde o final da dcada de 90, pelas agncias de regulao e superviso dos mercados de seguros, e em especial pela Associao Internacional de Supervisores de Seguros, IAIS, na sigla inglesa, atravs da implementao dos Princpios Bsicos de Seguros. Entretanto, a nova forma de exerccio da superviso viria a ganhar novo flego com a publicao da Diretiva Solvncia II, pelo Parlamento Europeu, em 2009, em princpio voltada para os Estados-Membros da Unio Europeia, mas com impacto muito mais alargado em termos geogrficos. A superviso baseada em riscos, contrariamente  forma tradicional de exerccio de superviso baseada na anlise de compliance face s regras estabelecidas, assenta em princpios e melhores prticas de negcio e reduo dos riscos. Deste modo, este novo paradigma de superviso convida a uma alterao profunda nos processos de trabalho dos supervisores e supervisionados. Com efeito, o seu foco  a superviso preventiva, identificada com o estudo de riscos e tendncias e com a interveno tempestiva, de forma a minimizar as perdas dos segurados e participantes. Mas os pilares essenciais em que se assenta a nova viso da superviso da atividade seguradora sero, seguramente, desenvolvidos pelo Professor Jos de Almaa que, para alm de Presidente da Autoridade de Seguros e Fundos de Penses de Portugal  tambm Professor Catedrtico, portanto, uma personalidade altamente abalizada para nos falar dessas matrias. Em Cabo Verde, a assimilao e a necessria mudana comportamental para se trabalhar a partir de princpios, e no mais pelo mero cumprimento de regras, constituem desafios tanto para o mercado supervisionado como para o prprio rgo regulador e supervisor. Com efeito, se s instituies se exige o desenvolvimento de uma gesto integrada de todo o negcio e seus riscos,  Superviso requer-se uma atuao que permita uma boa coordenao entre as anlises onsite e offsite, ou seja, uma anlise presencial e  distncia. Esta perspetiva permite a estabilidade do mercado, a proteo do consumidor, bem como a aplicao de melhores princpios e prticas, visando, em ltima instncia, o incentivo  elevao do padro de gesto de riscos e a prestao de um servio de melhor qualidade, quer aos tomadores de seguro quer aos beneficirios. Para atender s demandas da superviso baseada no risco, o Departamento de Superviso das Instituies Financeiras do Banco de Cabo Verde procedeu a uma alterao nos seus processos de trabalho, redefiniu as suas prioridades em matria de superviso de seguros e redesenhou a forma de acompanhamento e tratamento da informao. Por outro lado, est-se a trabalhar na adaptao contnua da legislao aplicvel aos melhores princpios e prticas, de modo a atender s exigncias da superviso de seguros, com enfoque em riscos. Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, A consecuo de metas de um sistema sensvel aos riscos e consistente com o mercado  um processo seguramente complexo. Se o  para as economias avanadas, para uma economia pequena como a nossa representa um desafio ainda maior, merecendo, por isso, uma alterao sem precedentes nos processos de trabalho, quer do supervisor, quer do supervisionado. O sector de seguros em Cabo Verde tem uma participao ainda marginal na produo da riqueza nacional, contribuindo com menos de 2% para o PIB. Portanto, h um largo espao de crescimento do negcio segurador, quer em termos de volume, quer em termos de variedade de produtos a oferecer. Importa, por conseguinte, promover este crescimento com vista a incentivar a formao de poupana de longo prazo, o que  estratgico para um pas com baixo nvel de poupana interna como  o nosso caso. No entanto, colocam-se ainda fortes constrangimentos ao sector segurador nacional. Por um lado, os baixos nveis de rendimentos de uma parcela significativa da nossa populao, que a impede de contratar seguros e formar poupanas com a aquisio de ttulos de capitalizao e planos de previdncia privada. Por outro lado, a baixa cultura de gesto de riscos de grande parte da populao, a concentrao do seguro no Ramo Automvel, a dbil dinamizao do Ramo Vida e a fraca capacidade de reteno dos riscos. Se a superao do primeiro constrangimento depender de movimento duradouro de crescimento econmico, os outros, porm, representam oportunidades de crescimento para o setor segurador. Tais oportunidades concretizam-se com o aumento da literacia da populao, processo no qual o sector segurador dever ativamente participar, investindo na inovao de produtos e criando condies de reteno de riscos. Outrossim, assiste-se hoje,  escala mundial, a um conjunto considervel de alteraes, que representa grandes riscos ao negcio e requer uma exigncia maior de harmonizao da regulao aplicvel ao sector. So inmeras as mudanas que impactam, atualmente, a atividade do sector segurador, nomeadamente alteraes na composio etria da populao, na forma de pensar e atuar do cliente cada vez mais assertivo, mais informado e que busca produtos mais personalizados, alteraes tecnolgicas com a integrao de novas tecnologias, catstrofes naturais, entre outras. Estas situaes condicionam os negcios do sector, requerendo necessariamente a consequente alterao nos modelos de gesto dos negcios das instituies, bem como o desenho de novos produtos e servios, o lidar com novas tipologias de riscos e a busca criativa de novas solues. O Dr. Mrio Ribeiro com os seus vastos e profundos conhecimentos tcnicos e experincia na matria ir, certamente, nos elucidar muito melhor sobre os desafios atuais com os quais o sector segurador  confrontado. No obstante a reduzida dimenso da nossa economia e do sector segurador no nosso mercado financeiro, os efeitos das grandes tendncias far-se-o sentir em Cabo Verde, mais cedo ou mais tarde, ainda que em menor escala, dada a crescente globalizao dos mercados. Deste modo, o sector segurador  chamado a preparar-se para os grandes desafios que se avizinham. Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, Como se sabe, as garantias financeiras a apresentar pelas seguradoras so a margem de solvncia e as provises tcnicas. As empresas seguradoras nacionais tm uma boa margem de solvncia. Nunca apresentaram grandes problemas em termos de solvabilidade dos capitais. Sempre tiveram um grau de cobertura da margem bastante superior ao mnimo exigido legalmente. No que diz respeito  cobertura das provises tcnicas por ativos afetos, anualmente as seguradoras apresentam nveis de cobertura superiores aos legalmente exigidos. As seguradoras nacionais apresentam, desse modo, uma situao financeira relativamente slida e tm tido resultados altamente positivos nos ltimos anos. O principal desafio para o nosso sector segurador  o de garantir, em permanncia, o cumprimento das responsabilidades futuras para com os tomadores de seguros e beneficirios, contribuindo, assim, para a manuteno da estabilidade do sector financeiro nacional. A concretizao desse desafio pressupe, por um lado, a existncia de um quadro regulatrio moderno, complementado com as novas abordagens da superviso a nvel internacional, mais focadas na questo da anlise do risco. Por outro lado, requer a existncia de um sistema de governao eficiente que promova a segurana e a estabilidade das empresas do sector. Aperfeioar continuamente a avaliao de risco  um requisito essencial que o Banco de Cabo Verde, enquanto entidade supervisora do sector, deve sempre ter em conta. Neste contexto, assume particular importncia a regulamentao sobre a apresentao do relatrio de controlo interno por parte das seguradoras, na medida em que concorre para o objetivo de reforo da solidez financeira do sector. Igualmente, a melhoria da legislao e a sua adequao vo contribuir para um aumento da produo e, por conseguinte, para um maior desenvolvimento do sector. Neste quadro, com a aprovao e publicao, em 2010, de um conjunto de diplomas que define os princpios bsicos e o quadro normativo orientador da atividade seguradora e de mediao de seguros, o nosso pas deu um passo decisivo no sentido da reforma do quadro de referncia para o seu sector segurador. Apesar disso, julgo ser importante elaborar um novo quadro legal para o seguro obrigatrio de acidentes de trabalho. O diploma que regulamenta este seguro data de 1978, perodo logo aps a independncia nacional, pelo que j no se adequa  realidade atual do pas, particularmente no que diz respeito ao valor do salrio de referncia para o clculo dos prmios e dos valores das indemnizaes, sobretudo por incapacidades e morte. Do mesmo modo, aspetos importantes do diploma que regula o seguro obrigatrio de responsabilidade civil automvel tero que ser revistos, nomeadamente, os que se debruam sobre as indemnizaes em caso de incapacidades e morte. Muito recentemente foi atribudo ao Fundo de Garantia Automvel, sob gesto do Banco de Cabo Verde, responsabilidades no mbito de seguro martimo de responsabilidade civil. Impe-se, agora, a sua regulamentao tanto pelo Governo como pelo Banco de Cabo Verde, considerando, sobretudo, o seu importante papel social. O sector segurador  por natureza um dos investidores institucionais e insere-se num mercado financeiro bastante exguo e que apresenta poucas alternativas em termos de investimentos. Nestas circunstncias, a superviso baseada no risco dever garantir a estabilidade dos capitais do sector e, por isso, uma boa anlise dos investimentos, por forma a que o sector apresente garantias financeiras suficientes de acordo com os termos legais estabelecidos. Esta falta de alternativas contribuiu para uma elevada concentrao dos investimentos das seguradoras, em imveis e em participaes financeiras em outras instituies financeiras, o que a nosso ver  um risco grande para a gesto da carteira de ativos dessas empresas. Questiona-se, por isso, se se deve, ou no, autorizar as empresas de seguros a aplicarem os seus ativos afetos s provises tcnicas em produtos oferecidos no exterior do pas. Um outro desafio no menos importante tem a ver com o desenvolvimento da bancassurance no sector financeiro nacional nos prximos tempos. Ou seja, uma maior interligao entre a banca e os seguros, com a possibilidade de venda de produtos de seguros nos bales dos bancos. As seguradoras devem apostar cada vez mais numa maior diversificao dos seus produtos, nomeadamente, os ligados  sade e doena,  reforma, bem como os seguros complementares. Face  complexidade dos desafios existentes, devero tambm fazer uma forte aposta na formao contnua dos seus tcnicos. Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, O Banco de Cabo Verde adotar, no quadro das suas competncias legais, as medidas que o desenvolvimento do sector segurador requer, e enquanto Conselheiro Financeiro do Governo no deixar de propor as necessrias iniciativas legais que no sejam da sua competncia. Mas quer faz-lo de forma articulada com o sector, da a razo deste evento. Neste contexto, a Conferncia, que ora se inicia, e a Mesa Redonda que lhe segue so uma oportunidade mpar que se nos oferece para a troca de experincias e preocupaes, partilha de ensinamentos e propostas de soluo no que toca  adoo de novas abordagens de superviso e de regulao voltadas para a mitigao de riscos financeiros e o desenvolvimento do sector segurador em Cabo Verde. Esperemos que neste encontro sejam partilhadas preocupaes e experincias conjuntas e que os objetivos preconizados sejam plenamente alcanados, em prol do reforo de uma superviso eficiente e da consolidao do sector dos seguros em Cabo Verde. Muito obrigado e votos de bom trabalho! Praia, 23 de Maio de 2017 Joo Serra /Governador do Banco de Cabo Verde/

Title: Speech in the context of the Press Conference on Monetary Stimulus Measures of the Bank of Cape Verde
text: PRESS RELEASE SUBJECT: MONETARY STIMULUS MEASURES OF THE BANK OF CAPE VERDE 1. The Bank of Cape Verde shall have as its main task or task the maintenance of price stability, and as a secondary objective, to promote, in the country, liquidity, solvency and the proper functioning of a financial system based on market stability. 2. Without prejudice to the main objective, it is also up to the Bank of Cape Verde to cooperate in the implementation of the government's overall economic policy. 3. In this context, the Monetary Policy of the Bank of Cape Verde is oriented to maintain a level of external reserves consistent with the imperative of ensuring the credibility of the unilateral peg exchange regime to the Euro, as a pillar of price stability, a necessary condition for the economic and financial stability of the country. 4. Given the intense economic and financial relationship between Cape Verde and the European continent, which is affecting the Euro area, the financial crisis that persists in that area has negatively affected national economic dynamics. 5. For its part, various internal constraints, in particular at the level of structural reforms which hinder greater dynamics of economic activity, have not facilitated the development of the financial market, secondary market for short-term public debt, and the interbank market. 6. Nevertheless, monetary policy has been oriented, on the one hand, towards price stability and, on the other hand, on maintaining an adequate level of external reserves to support the exchange rate regime, seeking that implemented measures have a positive impact on the real economy. 7. However, certain structural constraints already identified, together with the maintenance of the bank liquidity surplus, have not allowed a desired transmission of monetary policy effects to the real sector of the economy, despite a relative improvement observed after the last measures implemented by the central bank in 2015. 8. The internal environment, where price losses persist, unsatisfactory developments in credit to the economy and a relatively comfortable level of foreign exchange reserves, calls for more effective monetary policy measures to be considered. These are part of accommodative measures, with a view to improving monetary transmission and creating conditions for stimulating credit to the economy and economic growth, through the channel of expectations, credit and confidence. 9. Some inefficiencies in the implementation of monetary policy have also conditioned monetary transmission. In fact, the adoption in 2013 of an auction mechanism for TRM - securities of monetary regularization of the Central Bank at the variable rate and the abandonment of the key rate as a TRM issuing rate has hindered the objective of signaling monetary policy through this instrument, weakening the power of the BCV to direct market interest rates to its management rate. 10. As a result of this option, the transmission of monetary through the interest channel was relatively weakened and the primary mission of the BCV to signal monetary policy was somehow compromised. It is also noteworthy the excess of bank liquidity in the system and the incipience of interbank markets and public debt, as important constraints to monetary transmission through the interest channel. 11. In addition, contrary to what is set out in the monetary policy operational framework, developments in the bcv and ECB's key rates make it possible to conclude that the BCV rate has not, of course, accompanied due adjustments, the dynamics of the ECB's rate of evolution, which has progressively reduced its rate to ever lower levels, to reach zero (0.0%) in March 2016, aggravating the disparity in relation to the bcv reference rate. 12. Finally, there is a significant difference between the rate of the Permanent Liquidity Facility and the Rate of the Permanent Liquidity Absorption Facility, which entails a large corridor for the fluctuation of overnight interest rates. On the other hand, an analysis of the Taylor rule applied to Cape Verde, made in 2015, indicates that, in the current context, considering the product gap and the deviations of effective inflation in relation to the expected, the appropriate key interest rate of monetary policy should be around 1%. 13. In view of the above mentioned inefficiencies, significant adjustments are required in the tools of the monetary policy operational framework in order to make them more efficient, which will include the use of the key interest rate in monetary policy signalling operations, carried out through TRM emissions, and the sterilization of excess liquidity in the banking system. 14. The balance of payments has been progressing favourably, with external reserves reaching an unprecedented level in December 2016 (around EUR 530 million), which guarantees some comfort in the fundamental objective of maintaining the country's international reserves. 15. There are no inflationary pressures, and the consumer price index has shown negative values in recent years, as mentioned above. 16. There is no need for unconventional measures, since we are not faced with the so-called 'liquidity trap' phenomenon, which happens when the interest rate is so low that the monetary authority is prevented from developing the economy through traditional monetary policy methods, using quantitative easing measures. 17. Thus, in view of the still unfavourable economic and financial situation, the absence of imminent pressures on the balance of payments and price developments, as well as the need for the Central Bank to strengthen the signalling function of the orientation of its monetary policy and to improve the effectiveness of monetary transmission, the Board of Directors of the Bank of Cape Verde, meeting at an ordinary session on 2 June 2017, it decided to make the following changes to the BCV reference rates and the implementation of a package of monetary management measures with a view to improving the transmission mechanism: (a) the reduction of the key rate by a dimension of 200 basis points, from 3.5% to 1.5%, with simultaneous communication to the market of the BCV's monetary policy orientation and continuous monitoring of impacts, with a view to provoking a faster and deeper reaction in the bcv's response actions without compromising or causing insecurity in key segments of credit institution funding; b) The reduction of the rate of permanent liquidity absorption facility, from 0.25% to 0.1%; c) The reduction of the rates of the permanent liquidity and rediscount facility in the same dimension as the principal rate, since they are indexed to it, from 6.5% to 4.5% and from 7.5% to 5.5%; (d) the absorption of excess bank liquidity, at the value determined in the short- and medium-term liquidity forecast, with a view to improving monetary transmission, despite the controlled increase in monetary policy costs; (e) the implementation of TRM interventions through fixed-rate auctions, with placement at the bank's principal rate, with a view to restoring the design of the principal rate, the efficiency of the interest channel and the credibility of monetary policy; f) The elimination of the exemption to Banking Financial Institutions of one million contos on the Base of Incidence of the Minimum Reserves scheme; (g) the simultaneous adoption of an appropriate and efficient communication policy in relation to the orientation of the central bank's monetary policy for a given period of time, with a view to improving the channel of expectations, interest rates and credit, and achieving the desired objectives for the financial system and the real economy; and (h) the elimination of the ceiling set to the bank for the use of permanent liquidity-decommitment facilities. 18. The measures adopted here in essence are aimed at strengthening the conditions for stimulating the financing of viable investment projects and, consequently, economic activity. 19. With the implementation of these measures, the BCV expects an increase in credit to the economy and a reduction in active interest rates, taking into account the conditions now created for a better functioning of the interbank market. Increasing credit to the economy, in turn, will lead to an additional boost to GDP growth. Likewise, it is expected that these measures will contribute to the stability of the Consumer Price Index, countering the potential negative impact of the deflation scenario. 20. The BCV also expects its efforts to be monitored by banking in the same sense, and it is important to stimulate credit to the economy as a basis for productive investments, indispensable for economic growth, without neglecting the associated risks. The banking sector is expected to take a consistent action as a driving force for monetary transmission as well as economic growth. The expectation of the BCV is that there will be, therefore, greater proactivity in the selection of projects for credit, imposition of greater confidence in the market, greater innovation and competitiveness. 21. Furthermore, the desired impacts of these measures will be greater if they are combined with the effective implementation of other structural economic policy measures, with a view, on the one hand, to reducing the risks of economy and, on the other hand, strengthening the balance sheet of banks and reducing risks that threaten the country's financial stability. 22. The new rates enter into force on 6 June 2017. Beach, June 05, 2017 John Serra /Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde/ Table: Structure of the Reference Rates of the Bank of Cape Verde Rates Previous structure New Structure (a) Director Fee 3,5% 1,50% Permanent Liquidity-Decommitment Facility Fee 6, 5% 4,50% Permanent Liquidity Absorption Facility Fee 0,25% 0,1% Rediscount Rate 7,5% 5,50% (a) Effective June 7, 2017
text_original: NOTA DE IMPRENSA ASSUNTO: MEDIDAS DE ESTMULO MONETRIO DO BANCO DE CABO VERDE 1. O Banco de Cabo Verde tem por misso ou atribuio principal assegurar a manuteno da estabilidade dos preos, e como objetivo secundrio, promover, no pas, a liquidez, a solvncia e o funcionamento adequado de um sistema financeiro assente na estabilidade do mercado. 2. Sem prejuzo do objetivo principal, cabe ainda ao Banco de Cabo Verde colaborar na execuo da poltica econmica global do Governo. 3. Neste quadro, a poltica monetria do Banco de Cabo Verde orienta-se para a manuteno de um nvel de reservas externas consistente com o imperativo de garantir a credibilidade do regime cambial de peg unilateral ao Euro, enquanto pilar da estabilidade de preos, condio necessria para a estabilidade econmica e financeira do pas. 4. Dado  intensa relao econmico-financeira entre Cabo Verde e o continente europeu, mxime com a rea do Euro, a crise financeira que persiste naquela zona tem afetado negativamente a dinmica econmica nacional. 5. Por seu turno, constrangimentos internos vrios, designadamente ao nvel de reformas estruturais que dificultam uma maior dinmica da atividade econmica, no tm facilitado o desenvolvimento do mercado financeiro, sobretudo o mercado secundrio de dvida pblica de curto prazo, e o mercado interbancrio. 6. No obstante, a poltica monetria tem-se orientado, por um lado, no sentido da estabilidade de preos e, por outro, na manuteno de um nvel adequado de reservas externas de suporte ao regime cambial, procurando que medidas implementadas tenham reflexo positivo sobre a economia real. 7. Entretanto, determinadas condicionantes estruturais j identificadas, aliadas  manuteno do excedente de liquidez bancria, no tm permitido uma transmisso desejada dos efeitos da poltica monetria ao sector real da economia, apesar de uma relativa melhoria observada aps as ltimas medidas implementadas pelo banco central em 2015. 8. A envolvente interna, onde persistem a baixa de preos, uma evoluo insatisfatria do crdito  economia e um nvel relativamente confortvel de reservas cambiais, interpela-nos no sentido da ponderao de medidas mais eficazes ao nvel da poltica monetria. Estas enquadram-se em medidas acomodatcias, tendo em vista o aperfeioamento da transmisso monetria e a criao de condies de estmulo ao crdito  economia e ao crescimento econmico, por via do canal das expectativas, do crdito e de confiana. 9. Algumas ineficincias na implementao da poltica monetria tm, tambm, condicionado a transmisso monetria. Com efeito, a adoo, em 2013, de um mecanismo de leilo dos TRM - ttulos de regularizao monetria do Banco Central  taxa varivel e o abandono da taxa diretora como taxa de emisso de TRM vem dificultando o objetivo de sinalizao da poltica monetria por via desse instrumento, enfraquecendo o poder do BCV em direcionar as taxas de juro de mercado para a sua taxa diretora. 10. Como resultado desta opo, a transmisso monetria por via do canal de juros ficou relativamente enfraquecida e a misso primordial do BCV de sinalizar a poltica monetria ficou de alguma forma comprometida. De destacar, ainda, o excesso de liquidez bancria no sistema e a incipincia dos mercados interbancrio e da dvida publica, como condicionantes de relevo  transmisso monetria por via do canal de juros. 11. Outrossim, ao contrrio do estabelecido no quadro operacional de poltica monetria, a evoluo das taxas diretoras do BCV e do BCE permite concluir que a taxa do BCV no acompanhou, naturalmente com os devidos ajustamentos, a dinmica de evoluo da taxa do BCE, que reduziu a sua taxa progressivamente, para nveis cada vez mais baixos, at atingir zero (0,0%) em maro de 2016, agravando a disparidade face  taxa de referncia do BCV. 12. Finalmente, verifica-se uma significativa diferena entre a taxa da Facilidade Permanente de Liquidez e a Taxa da Facilidade Permanente de Absoro de Liquidez, o que acarreta um grande corredor para a flutuao das taxas de juros overnight. Por outro, uma anlise da regra de Taylor aplicada a Cabo Verde, feita em 2015, indica que, no atual contexto, considerando o hiato do produto e os desvios da inflao efetiva em relao  esperada, a taxa de juro diretora adequada de poltica monetria deveria situar-se em torno de 1%. 13. Face s ineficincias acima referidas, requerem-se ajustamentos significativos nas ferramentas do quadro operacional de poltica monetria, de modo a torn-las mais eficientes, o que passar pela utilizao da taxa de juro diretora nas operaes de sinalizao de poltica monetria, executadas por via das emisses de TRM, e pela esterilizao da liquidez em excesso no sistema bancrio. 14. A balana de pagamentos tem registado uma evoluo favorvel, com as reservas externas a atingirem um nvel sem precedentes em dezembro de 2016 (cerca de 530 milhes de euros), o que garante algum conforto quanto ao objetivo fundamental de manuteno das reservas internacionais do pas. 15. No existem presses inflacionistas, tendo o ndice de preo no consumidor apresentado valores negativos nos ltimos anos, conforme j referido. 16. No h necessidade de medidas no convencionais, uma vez que no estamos perante o chamado fenmeno da armadilha de liquidez, que acontece quando a taxa de juro  de tal forma baixa que a autoridade monetria se v impedida de desenvolver a economia atravs dos mtodos tradicionais de poltica monetria, recorrendo a medidas do tipo quantitative easing. 17. Assim, considerando a conjuntura econmica e financeira ainda pouco favorvel, a inexistncia de presses iminentes na balana de pagamentos e na evoluo dos preos, bem assim a necessidade do Banco Central reforar a funo de sinalizao da orientao da sua poltica monetria e de melhorar a eficcia de transmisso monetria, o Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Cabo Verde, reunido em sesso ordinria do dia 02 de junho de 2017, deliberou proceder as seguintes alteraes nas taxas de referncia do BCV e a implementao de um pacote de medidas de gesto monetria com vista  melhoria do mecanismo de transmisso: a) A reduo da taxa diretora numa dimenso de 200 pontos base, de 3,5% para 1,5%, com comunicao concomitante ao mercado da orientao da poltica monetria do BCV e acompanhamento contnuo dos impactos, com vista a provocar uma reao mais rpida e profunda nas aes de resposta da banca, sem comprometer ou causar insegurana em segmentos chaves do funding das instituies de crdito; b) A reduo da taxa de facilidade permanente de absoro de liquidez, de 0,25% para 0,1%; c) A diminuio das taxas da facilidade permanente de cedncia de liquidez e de redesconto na mesma dimenso que a taxa diretora, visto estarem indexadas a esta, passando, respetivamente, de 6,5% para 4,5% e de 7,5% para 5,5%; d) A absoro do excesso de liquidez bancria, pelo valor apurado na previso de liquidez de curto e mdio prazo, com vista ao aperfeioamento da transmisso monetria, no obstante o aumento controlado dos custos de poltica monetria; e) A implementao de intervenes de TRM por via de leiles de taxa fixa, com colocao  taxa diretora do Banco de Cabo Verde, com vista a restaurar o desgnio da taxa diretora, a eficincia do canal de juros e a credibilidade da poltica monetria; f) A eliminao da iseno s Instituies Financeiras Bancrias de um milho de contos sobre a Base de Incidncia do regime de Reservas Mnimas; g) A adoo simultnea de uma poltica de comunicao adequada e eficiente em relao  orientao da poltica monetria do banco central para um determinado perodo de tempo, com vista a aperfeioar o canal de expetativas, de taxas de juro e de crdito, e a alcanar os objetivos desejados para o sistema financeiro e a economia real; e h) A eliminao do limite mximo fixado  banca para o recurso s facilidades permanentes de cedncia de liquidez. 18. As medidas ora adotadas visam essencialmente reforar as condies para estimular o financiamento de projetos de investimento viveis e, consequentemente, a atividade econmica. 19. Com a implementao dessas medidas, o BCV espera um aumento do crdito  economia e a reduo das taxas de juro ativas, tendo em conta as condies ora criadas para um melhor funcionamento do mercado interbancrio. O aumento do crdito  economia, por sua vez, induzir um impulso adicional ao crescimento do PIB. Do mesmo modo, espera-se com essas medidas, contribuir para a estabilidade do ndice de Preos no Consumidor, combatendo o potencial impacto negativo do cenrio de deflao. 20. O BCV espera ainda que os seus esforos sejam acompanhados pela banca, no mesmo sentido, sendo importante o estmulo ao crdito  economia como base para investimentos produtivos, indispensveis para o crescimento econmico, sem descurar os riscos associados. Aguarda-se que o sector bancrio tenha uma ao consequente enquanto agente impulsionador da transmisso monetria, bem como do crescimento econmico. A expectativa do BCV  que haja, portanto, maior proactividade na seleo dos projetos para crdito, imposio de maior confiana no mercado, maior inovao e competitividade. 21. Outrossim, os impactos almejados destas medidas sero maiores se estas forem combinadas com a implementao eficaz de outras medidas de poltica econmica de carcter estrutural, visando, por um lado, a reduo dos riscos da economia e, por outro lado, o reforo do balano dos bancos e a reduo dos riscos que ameaam a estabilidade financeira do pas. 22. As novas taxas entram em vigor a 06 de junho de 2017. Praia, 05 de junho de 2017 Joo Serra /Governador do Banco de Cabo Verde/ Quadro: Estrutura das taxas de referncia do Banco de Cabo Verde Taxas Estrutura anterior Nova Estrutura (a) Taxa Diretora 3,5% 1,50% Taxa da Facilidade Permanente de Cedncia de Liquidez 6, 5% 4,50% Taxa da Facilidade Permanente de Absoro de Liquidez 0,25% 0,1% Taxa de Redesconto 7,5% 5,50% (a) A vigorar a partir de 07 de junho de 2017

Title: Intervention in the Consignment Act of the Construction Work of the New Bank of Cape Verde
text: Intervention of the Governor, Dr. Joao Serra, in the Consignment Act of the Construction Work of the New Bank of Cape Verde, July 4, 2017. Prime Minister, Excellency, Honourable Members of the Government, Your Excellere, Mayor of Praia, Mr Secretary General of the MPD, Representatives of the Diplomatic Corps, Madam Auditor General of the Securities Market, Mr President of the Supervisory Board of the Bank of Cape Verde, Representatives of financial institutions, Representatives of the Design Team of architect alvaro Siza Vieira, Representatives of the Consortium of Contractors, Representatives of the Inspection Team, Mr. Bastonarios of the Orders of Engineers and Architects, Parish Priest of the Parish of Our Lady of Socorro, Dear Fellow Members of the Board of Directors and Employees of the BCV, Guest Gentlemen, Ladies and gentlemen, I am pleased to greet you and welcome you to this important and historic act of launching the construction work of the New Bank of Cape Verde. Allow me to express the sincere thanks of the Bank's Board of Directors and employees to all those who have accepted our invitation to be with us on this very special day for our institution. Our special thanks go to His Excellency the Prime Minister, Dr. Ulisses Correia e Silva, whose presence greatly honors us and dignifies this event. Prime Minister, Ladies and gentlemen, Today, July 4, 2017 is a great day in the history of BCV! More than 25 years after the first steps to find solutions for the construction of a headquarters from scratch for the Central Bank of Cape Verde, here came the long-awaited day. In fact, the construction of the New Seesite represents an undeniable and decisive milestone for the institutional strengthening of the BCV, being the culmination of a long-aforegone dream. Let me therefore congratulate the Collaborators, as well as the successive Administrations of the institution, for all the efforts made to celebrate the birth of the New Bank of Cape Verde today. A happy coincidence that this act of launching the works happens on the eve of the day of the celebration of the 42nd Anniversary of National Independence. In benefit of the truth, the history of bcv is confused with the history of Cape Verde itself as an independent country. Created a few months after the historic date of 5 July 1975, over these four and a half decades, the BCV grew, developed and consolidated, following the transformations of various natures that were happening in the country, particularly in the economic, monetary and financial fields. Indeed, the widely recognized success of Cape Verde's development effort is also due to a large extent to the strong performance that the Bank of Cape Verde has had throughout its existence, ensuring the value of the national currency, stability and modernization of the monetary and financial system, as well as developing and running the country's payment systems. In a global context of increasing complexity and uncertainties, there are numerous challenges facing the country, particularly in relation to its economy, with the BCV having a fundamental role in modernizing the national monetary and financial system. In this context of permanent changes and paradigm shifts, particularly in the areas of monetary policy and the regulation and supervision of the financial system, the strengthening of institutional capacities, the capacity building of human resources and their commitment to the development of Cape Verde assume an indispensable role. Along the path of the BCV, with emphasis on its contribution in defending the value of the Cape Verdean shield, as well as the stability of the financial system, there are well-founded reasons to consider the Central Bank as a reference institution of the Republic, aligned with the strategic objectives of the country, in passing, as is usually the case with most central banks at international level. The construction of the New Seesite is an important milestone in this challenging and successful path, so we are convinced that together, stone by stone, we will build a solid building, up to the challenges that the monetary and financial system faces and that today, this dream so enlivered by all, will effectively begin to come true. Since the early 1990s, the BCV has been operating in a building that had been built in the 1970s for commercial and housing purposes. This building has been adapted, with various constraints, to the demanding operating conditions of a Central Bank. This building no longer supports interventions for the expansion of spaces, alterations in electrical and sanitary installations, as well as communication and air conditioning systems, concomitantly with its daily use by BCV Employees. In view of this situation, the Civil Engineering Laboratory has been not advising the permanence, for much longer, in the current facilities of the Bank, especially for security reasons, so it is urgent to build a new space. The New Headquarters is also essential, with a view to developing a modern financial system and an increasingly demanding role for the Central Bank, taking into account above all the safeguarding of the integrity and full functioning of payment systems, as basic requirements of any modern State, with a sound and credible monetary and financial system. Prime Minister, Ladies and gentlemen, The process aimed at the construction of the New Headquarters of the Central Bank began in the early days of 1992, with the acquisition, in the Municipality of Praia, of the plot of land where we are located. Little by little, he was gaining pace and overcoming embarrassments, having counted on the enthusiastic collaboration of all the edis of praia and the selfless involvement of all bcv administrations. Understanding the nature and specificity of the building to be built, the Government of Cape Verde, through the Resolution of the Council of Ministers, no. 69 of 1999, dispensed with the public tender, the concession of the project. The choice fell to the internationally recognized architect alvaro Siza Vieira who, unfortunately, by medical recommendations, could not be here with us today, as it was and is his wish. It is also worth noting the precious support of Banco de Portugal to which we deeply appreciate, which from the beginning provided a technical team of engineers dedicated in the field of banking security, to accompany the technical team of the BCV. In 2000, on the occasion of the celebrations of the 25th anniversary of the BCV, the FIRST STONE was symbolically launched, in an act presided over by the then President of the Republic, the late Antonio Mascarenhas Monteiro, being Governor of the Bank, Dr. Olavo Correia, now Minister of Finance. The typology of projects, architecture and specialties, was properly studied and adapted to our country, and the same were designed with all the analysis and evaluations of the field, were it not for the designer team led by so experienced and renowned Architect. The projects were updated in 2010 to adapt both to technological developments and to the most technically appropriate solutions at the moment. In 2011, the procedures of "International Public Tender for Prior Qualification" were followed, for the selection of the inspection company and the contractor of the work, and the concursal process was completed in 2012. In January 2014, the BCV informed all competitors in the competition of the competition the result of the competition, having joined the final ranking table. In addition, they were informed that until that time, they had not been able to award the work for which they were waiting for the express authorization of the Government. First came the consortium constituted by the Spanish company, CONSTRUCTORA SAN JOSe and the Cape Verdean company, SOCIEDADE DE CONSTRUcoES  SGL, two companies with evidence given in the field of civil construction in Cape Verde and worldwide, as is the case of CONSTRUCTORA SAN JOSe. Through Decree-Law No. 52/2016 of 10 October, the Government of the Republic authorized the Bank of Cape Verde to be the depositary of the closed Pension Fund constituted for the financing of the work. The beneficiaries of this Pension Fund are bcv employees, in the assets and in the retirement situation, who started their duties until September 1993. It will be the funds from the contributions of workers receiving the bcv's private social security scheme that will fully finance the New Office, so its construction will not have charges, either for the Bank of Cape Verde and for the public bank. This mechanism, normally used by Financial Institutions, is supported by the International Financial Reporting Standards, allowing to remove pressure from the Bank's Balance Sheet Accounts, monetizing these resources as recommended by international best practices. The New Sedee, owned by the much-mentioned Pension Fund, will be transferred to the Bank of Cape Verde under financial leasing. As a result, the BCV will assume, on bebysof the Fund, the monthly instalments of its beneficiaries until these responsibilities are extinguished, as it is a closed fund. It is in this context that, by government order of 22 October 2016, the BCV was authorized to start the construction of the New Office, which is why, from that date, the contract procedures were resumed, which led to the award of the work to the consortium that won the competition referred to above. At the same time, the remaining competitors were notified and their explanatory report was sent, which contains the grounds for the deprecation of the respective tenders, as well as the relative characteristics and advantages of the selected tender and the name of the consortium chosen. That is, everything was done in strict compliance with the law, as it could not fail to be, considering the increased responsibilities of the Central Bank in promoting and defending best practices in terms of governance, transparency and credibility. Prime Minister, Ladies and gentlemen, If the construction of the BCV's New BCV, for most reasons, this construction was justified in the 1990s, considering not only the size that our economy has gained over the years, but also the development and modernization of the national financial system. On the other hand, the need for the continuous strengthening of the institutional capacity of the BCV for the benefit of the country is not in line with the persistence of logistical and security constraints for the regulatory, supervisory authority, and ensures the proper functioning of compensation and payment systems. The cost of the New Headquarters, which amounts to just over 1.8 million contos, about 17 million euros, has to do with the size, specificity and complexity of the work, which includes particular security solutions today required of any Central Bank, in addition to other valences. Investment in the construction of the New Seesite will not have any negative consequences for the country's long-controlled inflation situation and is likely to continue to be so in the near future. It will also not impact the external reserves that have evolved in a sustained and very favorable way in recent times, reaching sufficient values for the financing of more than 6 months of imports of goods and services projected for 2017. The construction works that we are going to start will certainly contribute to the further development of economic activity in the capital of the country, with a positive impact on the employment of skilled labour and not only, both in terms of construction itself, as well as the various existing specialties and also in the context of inspection work. On the other hand, it should be recalled that the consortium of companies that will build the New BCV Headquarters consists of a Cape Verdean and a foreign company, in an adjusted proportion of the sharebetween the parties. It is also worth noting that it is a work designed by the internationally renowned Architect Siza Vieira, which, due to its characteristics, size and complexity, will value not only the Bank of Cape Verde, but also the City of Praia and the country. It will certainly be the architectural masterpiece of reference in Cape Verde and a tourist attraction. The construction term is about 2 years and three months. The BCV Administration will closely monitor the execution of the project and will do everything in its power to ensure that there is strict compliance with costs and the deadline. Finally, I would like to take the opportunity to reiterate once again that no beneficiary of the bcv's private social security scheme will no longer receive the social benefits due to it, because of the construction of the BCV's New Office with the resources of its Pension Fund. All will continue to receive, in time and time, what is owed to them and the BCV accounts will benefit from the transparency and monetization of these resources recorded in their balance sheet as provisions. May the work blessed by the Parish Priest, Father Constantina, of the Parish of Our Lady of Help, to which the future See will belong, be carried out successfully, so that in just over two years we may all be together again at the inauguration of the New Seat of the Bank of Cape Verde. Thank you so much for your attention! Beach, 04 July 2017 John Serra /Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde/
text_original: Interveno do Governador, Doutor Joo Serra, no Ato de Consignao da Obra de Construo da Nova Sede do Banco de Cabo Verde, 4 de julho de 2017.
