Nesse mesmo ms de Janeiro de 2016, o Conselho de Administrao do BCV deliberou determinar, nos termos do artigo 151 alnea 1) da LAIF, a realizao de uma ao de auditoria externa independente  atividade do Novo Banco, tendo em conta a necessidade de conhecer melhor a real situao por que passava esta instituio. Em Janeiro de 2016, foi nomeado pelos acionistas um novo Conselho de Administrao do Novo Banco, com a misso principal de restabelecimento da situao financeira do banco, devendo para o efeito elaborar um plano de recuperao. Em face dessa nova situao, o Conselho de Administrao do BCV deliberou afrouxar as medidas restritivas anteriormente impostas ao Novo Banco, de modo a permitir que a nova Administrao tivesse um mbito de atuao menos limitado. A 11 de Maro de 2016, o Novo Banco envia ao BCV um draft zero do Plano de Recuperao, o qual foi considerado pouco consistente. Foram enviados ao Novo Banco comentrios, visando a apresentao por este de um Plano de Recuperao mais detalhado e consistente, o que no chegou a acontecer. O BCV, atravs do Governador, manteve o novo Governo sado das eleies de Maro de 2016, ao corrente da situao financeira e prudencial do Novo Banco, nomeadamente aquando de uma visita realizada ao BCV, pelo Senhor Ministro das Finanas, em Maio de 2016. Entretanto, no ms de Abril de 2016, os acionistas do Novo Banco deliberaram, por unanimidade, em assembleia geral universal, aumentar o capital social do Novo Banco em 700.000 contos, a acontecer em dois momentos: numa primeira fase no valor de 500.000 contos, at finais de 2016, e numa segunda fase, no valor de 200.000 contos, em 2017. Estes aumentos visavam o reequilbrio da situao financeira e a recomposio dos rcios prudenciais do Novo Banco. O aumento, que era previsto ser feito em 2016, no foi efetuado, o que reduziu, ainda mais, a possibilidade do banco recompor os seus rcios e a sua situao econmico-financeira. Face ao cenrio de contnua degradao da situao financeira e prudencial do Novo Banco, a 29 de Julho de 2016, o BCV entendeu que se devia retomar na ntegra e de imediato as medidas corretivas adotadas em Janeiro de 2016. Tal deciso devia ser comunicada e explicitada ao Governo, por forma a que o BCV e o Estado, nos termos da Lei de Bases, pudessem articular e procurar a melhor soluo a dar ao Novo Banco. Isso, tendo em vista a salvaguarda da confiana dos depositantes e a estabilidade do sistema financeiro. Em sequncia, no dia 02 de Agosto de 2016, o Governador do Banco de Cabo Verde enviou ao Ministro das Finanas um documento intitulado Situao Financeira e Prudencial do Novo Banco e Posio do BCV, dando a conhecer as preocupaes do Banco Central relativamente  situao da instituio de crdito, bem como o posicionamento do regulador a respeito. Na mesma data, foi disponibilizado ao Governo, enquanto representante dos acionistas do Novo Banco, o Relatrio de Auditoria Independente feito pela Empresa Ernst & Young, por determinao do BCV, que apontava para a existncia de deficincias graves ao nvel do controlo interno e da conduta da Administrao do banco em funes at incio de Janeiro de 2016. No dia 09 de Agosto de 2016, o Governador do BCV rene-se com o Ministro das Finanas para analisarem a situao do Novo Banco. O Ministro das Finanas solicitou um prazo mximo de trs meses para apresentar uma proposta de soluo definitiva, tempo esse que foi concedido pelo BCV. Em decorrncia, o BCV decidiu adiar, por um perodo de 3 meses, a reintroduo, na plenitude, das medidas corretivas aplicadas ao Novo Banco em Janeiro de 2016, sem prejuzo do seguimento apertado da evoluo da situao financeira e prudencial desta instituio de crdito. Ao mesmo tempo, foi-se preparando um plano para a medida de resoluo a ser eventualmente aplicada ao Novo Banco, visando, essencialmente, a proteo dos seus depositantes e os menores custos possveis para os contribuintes. Ou seja, perante uma situao complexa e indita enfrentada pelo regulador e supervisor, este iniciaria o processo de preparao da aplicao de uma medida de resoluo ao Novo Banco, caso at l, os acionistas no recapitalizassem o seu banco, por forma a que cumprisse os rcios prudenciais regularmente estabelecidos pelo BCV. No ms de Novembro de 2016 terminou o prazo concedido ao Governo, sem que os acionistas tivessem proposto uma soluo para o Novo Banco, nomeadamente a sua recapitalizao e, concomitantemente, a alterao, num quadro sustentado, do seu modelo de negcios. No dia 23 de Dezembro de 2016, teve lugar no Ministrio das Finanas, contando com representantes, ao mais alto nvel, deste departamento governamental e do BCV, um encontro derradeiro e determinante para o apuramento da situao e a estruturao da eventual medida de resoluo a ser aplicada ao Novo Banco Nessa reunio, ficou patente que no havia condies objetivas para a recapitalizao do Novo Banco, numa base sustentada. Ficaram assim esgotados todos os mecanismos com vista  recomposio do normal funcionamento do Novo Banco,  luz dos normativos vigentes. O banco no cumpria os requisitos para a manuteno da autorizao para o exerccio da sua atividade, com o iminente cenrio de falncia. Decidiu-se, ento, pela aplicao de uma medida de resoluo ao Novo Banco, tendo em conta o interesse pblico subjacente. Em sequncia iniciou-se o processo de preparao dessa medida respeitando todos os trmites legalmente previstos para o efeito, tendo a medida sido aplicada no dia 08 de Maro de 2017, nos moldes e termos que constam da respetiva Deliberao do Conselho de Administrao. Perante a situao por que passava o Novo Banco e em face das alternativas disponveis, tal medida afigurou-se como a soluo mais ajustada e menos custosa, quer para o errio pblico como para o pas. Foi ao encontro do dever imperativo atribudo ao BCV de garantir a proteo dos depsitos das famlias, das empresas e outras entidades, por um lado. Por outro, assegurou a continuidade dos servios financeiros essenciais, tendo em vista a estabilidade do sistema financeiro, com os menores custos possveis para o errio pblico e o pas. Ou seja, os spillovers effects negativos foram controlados. Esta deciso do Banco de Cabo Verde foi tomada no mbito do enquadramento legal, que responsabiliza e faz suportar as perdas da atividade bancria nos acionistas e credores subordinados, mantendo-se o objetivo do reforo da estabilidade financeira. Neste quadro, acionistas e credores subordinados foram chamados a suportar as perdas decorrentes da atividade bancria, que no controlaram adequadamente. A operao de aplicao de uma medida de resoluo ao Novo Banco, ficou praticamente concluda no dia 13 de Julho, com a assinatura do contrato tripartido entre esta instituio, o INPS e a Caixa Econmica, para a gesto e recuperao da carteira de crdito no pretendida pela Caixa Econmica, no valor de cerca de 710 mil contos. Com esta operao, criativa e inovadora, o INPS poder recuperar, ainda que a prazo, pelo menos, uma grande parte dos depsitos que detinha junto do Novo Banco, depsitos esses no valor de cerca de 721 mil contos. Com efeito, ir receber no s os crditos recuperados pela Caixa Econmica como tambm os respetivos juros. A Caixa Econmica, por sua vez, ganhar uma comisso de gesto dessa carteira de crditos e ter, ainda, direito a uma percentagem dos juros sobre os crditos recuperados. Enfim, uma boa soluo para todas as partes envolvidas, minimizando, o mximo possvel, os prejuzos que o INPS incorreu com aplicao da medida de resoluo acima referida. Concluda a operao supra-referida, o BCV colocou, desde o dia 17 de Julho o Novo Banco em processo de liquidao, para efeitos de concluso da alienao de alguns bens mveis ainda existentes nesta instituio. Assim sendo, no obstante os prejuzos incorridos pelos acionistas, no valor de cerca de um milho e 250 mil contos, o processo - pela sua complexidade e carcter indito a nvel nacional - poder ser considerado um autntico sucesso, tanto mais por se tratar de um mecanismo relativamente recente e ainda pouco adotado em todo o mundo, sendo Cabo Verde o segundo pas da CPLP (depois de Portugal) a aplic-lo. Obrigado pela ateno! Assembleia Nacional, aos 03 de agosto de 2017 Joo Pinto Serra /Governador do Banco de Cabo Verde/

Title: Closing Speech at the Workshop on the Secondary Market of Public Debt
text: Closing Speech at the Secondary Market Workshop on Public Debt, September 11, 2017 Members of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Cape Verde, Mr Charge d'Affairs of the Luxembourg Embassy in Cape Verde, Members of the Board of Directors of The AGMVM, Directors, Advisors and Coordinators of the Bank of Cape Verde, Mr Director General of the Treasury, Members of the Board of Directors of the Cape Verde Stock Exchange, Mr Presidents of financial institutions, Mr. Consultant Dr. Jose Fazenda Martins, Dear Employees of bcv and financial institutions, Guest Gentlemen, Ladies and gentlemen, It is an honor and satisfaction for me to close this important Workshop on the financing of the secondary public debt market in Cape Verde. I would like to congratulate the Advisor of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Cape Verde, Dr. Encarnacao Rocha, for promoting the organization of this event, whose realization was supported by the Luxembourg Cooperation, which we also thank. Likewise, our thanks to all those who accepted the invitation of the organizers of this Workshop, as well as to the consultant Dr. Jose Fazenda Martins for the brilliant presentation made and sharing their relevant technical knowledge and experience. I am convinced that at this meeting they shared joint concerns and experiences and that the objectives pursued have been fully achieved for the sake of the much desired as necessary development of the secondary market for Cape Verdean public debt. The BCV will take due account of the subsidies coming out of this reflection. Ladies and gentlemen, Savings and investment are fundamental concepts for understanding the functioning of the financial system. More than that, they are very important to the economy of any country. It is mainly through investment and savings that a country can generate jobs, income and quality of life. And to do that, these resources need to be applied as efficiently as possible. It is not by chance that one of the objectives of economic theory is precisely to study the efficient allocation of resources in order to maximize their usefulness for all market participants and, consequently, of the country. The financial market presents itself as a means for the realization of these allocations of resources, in order to provide better conditions for economic operators to carry out their activities. With the globalization of markets and the growth of capital flows, there was the improvement of the entire financial system, creating conditions for more efficient allocations. This has been better structured with more security and transparency. It is interesting to note that technological and financial system development are mutually stimulating. On the other hand, the international financial crisis triggered in 2007 and its effects on the financial sector have given rise to important and profound reflection. It highlights the need to redefine regulatory standards, strengthen internal financing mechanisms, exploring new channels for capturing savings and channeling them to investment. It is also necessary to promote financial literacy and good corporate governance practices. As one of the segments of the financial market, the capital market plays an important role in promoting investment and growing savings. In fact, the capital market provides advantageous financing alternatives to companies, aiming at the realization of medium and long-term investment projects and taking into account a demand that the credit market is no longer able to sustain on its own. It is recalled that the emergence of the capital market was based on two principles. On the one hand, contribute to economic development, acting as a capital booster for investments, stimulating the formation of private savings. On the other hand, to allow and guide the structuring of a pluralistic society, based on the market economy, with collective participation in the wealth and results of the economy. Thus, the capital market can be seen as an alternative to traditional applications in products offered by banks and the state, with a lower cost of financing for companies and greater access to capital by the general public. Ladies and gentlemen, The Public Treasury issues government bonds in the primary market, through competitive public offerings, in the form of auctions. Once issued, the securities can be freely traded between the parties, thus forming the secondary market for government bonds. The proper functioning of the secondary market promotes the valuation of financial assets in a more efficient and transparent way, besides enabling better risk management, increasing liquidity and boosting the primary market. The high liquidity, in turn, makes the pricing process more efficient, allowing the public treasury to issue financial instruments at lower cost and, consequently, lower risk of refinancing. The Cape Verdean public debt market originated in the early 1990s, with the liberalization of the national economy, which became an economy based on market logic. In this context, in 1994 began to appear the first regulations for the issues of Treasury Bills (BTs) as well as Treasury Bonds (OTs), however, limited to the primary market, despite the continuous development of the legal framework. However, one of the main basic conditions for public financing to be efficient is the existence of a developed secondary market for public securities. It is in secondary market negotiations that the price references of the various assets are formed, which, in turn, will determine the cost of financing the Treasury. Similarly, the ease with which investors enter and depart from this market, i.e. liquidity, represents a relevant variable in determining the interest of the various classes of investors. Thus, among the tasks of debt management, it includes the development and the search for a continuous improvement of the secondary market. In this sense, in 2009 the process of reforming the public debt market begins, with the approval of Decree-Law No. 59 and 60 of 14 December on bt emissions and OTs respectively. It should be noted that the BCV has always been in the lead of these reforms. With the publication of these diplomas, the public debt issued by the Cape Verdean State became susceptible to trading on the secondary market, and may be of its own grossly admitted to the market managed by the Cape Verde Stock Exchange. However, it was only possible to put these two legal provisions into practice in May 2013, with the publication of Government Ordinance No. 30/2013, of May 27, which allowed the passage of the securities, which until that date were under the management of the BCV, for the custody of the Stock Exchange. This Ordinance was very important for the development of the public debt market, namely because it allowed the start of state emissions as securities. From 2009 to 2013, a background work was done between the different stakeholders  the Ministry of Finance, the Bank of Cape Verde/AGMVM and the Stock Exchange  culminating in the entry into operation of the state auction platform in 2013. The implementation of this platform allowed the expansion of the base and the reduction of the cost of financing. However, the secondary market being one of the pillars of the reform is still in a very incipient state. However, significant amounts in government bonds have been issued through the Stock Exchange in recent years. For example, in 2016 about 14.5 million contos were issued, corresponding to approximately 9% of the wealth produced in that year, that is, the GDP of Cape Verde. Of this value of 14.5 million contos, 11.8 were OTs and 2.8 BTs. Despite all the effort to introduce improved state financing mechanisms, we have not yet been able to develop the secondary market for public debt. It should be noted that of the 20 public debt auctions that took place between 2013 and 2016, only five transactions took place on the secondary market. On the other hand, the securities issued by the State of Cape Verde so far have been acquired by commercial banks, being in their portfolio, causing the phenomenon called "hoarding", because there is no particular interest in trading it in the secondary market. Ladies and gentlemen, Given the importance of an active and liquid secondary market for the development of the Cape Verde capital market, I think it makes perfect sense to reflect on a research carried out by the World Bank that presents the basic conditions as essential for the proper functioning of the secondary market and drivers of improvements in the management of public debt. These conditions can be summarised as follows. a) A standardized dealer system, with rights and obligations associated with meeting trading targets, in addition to giving greater credibility to the market, stimulates the growth of liquidity; b) The existence of alternatives that amplify the number of participants, even in times of higher volatility, enabling the exit of unfavorable positions in competitive conditions. This characteristic is fundamental to make the issuer's interest in elongate debt and investor demand for liquid markets; (c) a broad and diversified base of investors and financial agents, composed of financial institutions, institutional investors, brokers, companies and individuals and the various classes of funds; (d) the presence of non-resident investors, who generally have the ability to trade longer securities. However, the presence of this class of investors requires further liberalisation of the country's financial account and good economic fundamentals. In this regard, the country's high public debt, about 131% in 2016, is pointed out as an aspect that may negatively affect cape verde's debt interest. On the other hand, there is a need to obtain a lower risk weight for the holding of public debt of the Republic of Cape Verde by Portuguese and foreign financial institutions, taking into account the existing Exchange Cooperation Agreement, which allows the connection of the national currency to the Euro; (e) the standardization of government debt securities, introducing, for example, trading unit, time counting pattern and asset delivery; (f) the concentration of maturities and the repurchase system, which increase liquidity and facilitate long asset issues with prefixed profitability. This lengthening of the debt, added to the placement of prefixed securities, in turn, decreases the exposure to the risk of interest and refinancing of the Public Treasury; (g) the existence of a representative over-the-counter market, as this allows the personalisation of financial products, implying an increase in participants; (h) the use of electronic systems, which increase market efficiency, as they allow participants to view offers, which leads to greater transparency, minimising limitations and asymmetric information of the parameters required for the labelling of securities prices. These factors increase the number of investors and, consequently, the liquidity of the market; (i) the existence of clear rules of conduct, which prevent fraud and market manipulation. These rules may be established by the regulatory authority or via self-regulation by the associations of market participants. As will be seen, the basic conditions presented above are generally non-existent in Cape Verde and even existing or incipient conditions are discussed by financial system participants, class entities, investors and directly related government agencies. It is therefore important to look at them and consider their creation, naturally mutatis mutandi. For this project to take place, all market players will need to be involved. The BCV is always ahead of all these reforms and will continue to give its full support wherever it is needed. Thank you so much for your attention! September 11, 2017 John Serra /Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde/
text_original: Discurso de Encerramento no Workshop do Mercado Secundrio da Dvida Pblica, 11 de setembro de 2017 Senhores Membros do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Cabo Verde, Senhor Charg dAffairs da Embaixada de Luxemburgo em Cabo Verde, Senhores Membros do Conselho Diretivo da AGMVM, Diretores, Assessores e Coordenadores do Banco de Cabo Verde, Senhor Director Geral do Tesouro, Senhores Membros do Conselho de Administrao da Bolsa de Valores de Cabo Verde, Senhores Presidentes das Instituies Financeiras, Senhor Consultor Dr. Jos Fazenda Martins, Caros Colaboradores do BCV e das Instituies Financeiras, Senhores Convidados, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores,  para mim uma honra e satisfao encerrar este importante Workshop sobre a dinamizao do mercado secundrio de dvida pblica em Cabo Verde. Queria felicitar a Assessora do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Cabo Verde, Dr. Encarnaco Rocha, pela promoo da organizao deste evento, cuja realizao contou com o apoio financeiro da Cooperao Luxemburguesa, o qual tambm agradecemos. De igual modo, os nossos agradecimentos a todos os que aceitaram o convite dos organizadores deste Workshop, bem como ao consultor Dr. Jos Fazenda Martins pela brilhante apresentao feita e partilha dos seus conhecimentos tcnicos e experincia relevantes. Estou convicto que neste encontro tenham partilhado preocupaes e experincias conjuntas e que os objetivos preconizados foram plenamente alcanados, em prol do to almejado quanto necessrio desenvolvimento do mercado secundrio de dvida pblica cabo-verdiana. O BCV tomar em devida conta os subsdios sados dessa reflexo. Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Poupana e investimento so conceitos fundamentais para o entendimento do funcionamento do sistema financeiro. Mais do que isso, so muito importantes para a economia de qualquer pas.  principalmente atravs do investimento e da poupana que um pas consegue gerar empregos, rendimentos e qualidade de vida. E para isso,  preciso que esses recursos sejam aplicados da forma mais eficiente possvel. No  por acaso que um dos objetivos da teoria econmica , justamente, estudar a alocao eficiente dos recursos de modo a maximizar a sua utilidade para todos os participantes do mercado e, consequentemente, do pas. O mercado financeiro apresenta-se como um meio para a realizao dessas afetaes de recursos, com o intuito de proporcionar melhores condies aos operadores econmicos de realizarem as suas atividades. Com a globalizao dos mercados e crescimento dos fluxos de capitais, houve o aprimoramento de todo o sistema financeiro, criando condies para alocaes mais eficientes. Para tal procedeu-se a uma melhor estruturao das formas de transao, com mais segurana e transparncia.  interessante observar que o desenvolvimento tecnolgico e do sistema financeiro se estimulam reciprocamente. Por outro lado, a crise financeira internacional despoletada em 2007 e os seus efeitos no sector financeiro vm suscitando uma importante e profunda reflexo. Evidencia-se a necessidade de redefinio de padres regulatrios, de reforo dos mecanismos de financiamento interno, explorando novos canais de captao da poupana e a sua canalizao para o investimento.  tambm necessrio o fomento da literacia financeira e das boas prticas de governo societrio. Como um dos segmentos do mercado financeiro, o mercado de capitais tem um importante papel na promoo do investimento e no crescimento da poupana. Com efeito, o mercado de capitais proporciona alternativas vantajosas de financiamento s empresas, visando a realizao de projetos de investimentos, de mdio e longo prazo e atendendo a uma demanda que o mercado de crdito no  mais capaz de sustentar sozinho. Recorde-se que o surgimento do mercado de capitais foi baseado em dois princpios. Por um lado, contribuir para o desenvolvimento econmico, atuando como propulsor de capitais para os investimentos, estimulando a formao de poupana privada. Por outro, permitir e orientar a estruturao de uma sociedade pluralista, baseada na economia de mercado, com participao coletiva na riqueza e nos resultados da economia. Assim, o mercado de capitais pode ser visto como uma alternativa s aplicaes tradicionais em produtos oferecidos pelos bancos e pelo Estado, com um menor custo de financiamento para as empresas e maior acesso ao capital por parte do pblico em geral. Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, O Tesouro pblico emite ttulos da dvida pblica no mercado primrio, por meio de ofertas pblicas competitivas, na modalidade de leiles. Uma vez emitidos, os ttulos podem ser livremente negociados entre as partes, formando assim o mercado secundrio de ttulos pblicos. O bom funcionamento do mercado secundrio promove a avaliao dos ativos financeiros de forma mais eficiente e transparente, alm de possibilitar uma melhor gesto do risco, elevar a liquidez e potencializar o mercado primrio. A liquidez elevada, por seu turno, torna o processo de formao de preos mais eficiente, permitindo ao Tesouro pblico emitir instrumentos financeiros com menor custo e, consequentemente, menor risco de refinanciamento. O mercado de dvida pblica cabo-verdiana teve a sua origem nos primeiros anos da dcada de 90 do sculo passado, com a liberalizao da economia nacional, que passou a ser uma economia assente na lgica de mercado. Neste quadro, em 1994 comearam a aparecer os primeiros regulamentos para as emisses dos Bilhetes do Tesouro (BTs) bem como das Obrigaes do Tesouro (OTs), no entanto, limitadas ao mercado primrio, apesar do contnuo desenvolvimento do quadro legal. Todavia, uma das principais condies bsicas para o financiamento pblico ser eficiente  a existncia de um mercado secundrio desenvolvido de ttulos pblicos.  nas negociaes em mercado secundrio que se formam as referncias de preos dos diversos ativos, as quais, por sua vez, vo determinar o custo de financiamento do Tesouro. Da mesma forma, a facilidade com que os investidores entram e saem desse mercado, ou seja, a liquidez, representa uma varivel relevante na determinao do interesse das diversas classes de investidores. Assim, dentre as tarefas de gesto de dvida, inclui-se o desenvolvimento e a busca por um contnuo aperfeioamento do mercado secundrio. Neste sentido, em 2009 d-se incio ao processo de reforma do mercado de dvida pblica, com a aprovao dos Decretos-Lei n. 59 e 60, de 14 de Dezembro, sobre as Emisses de BTs e OTs respetivamente. Note-se que o BCV esteve sempre na liderana dessas reformas. Com a publicao desses diplomas a dvida pblica emitida pelo Estado cabo-verdiano passou a ser suscetvel de negociao no mercado secundrio, podendo ser oficiosamente admitida ao mercado gerido pela Bolsa de Valores de Cabo Verde. Contudo, s foi possvel colocar esses dois dispositivos legais na prtica em Maio de 2013, com a publicao da Portaria governamental n. 30/2013, de 27 de Maio, que permitiu a passagem dos ttulos, que at essa data se encontravam sob a gesto do BCV, para a custdia da Bolsa de Valores. A referida Portaria foi muito importante para o desenvolvimento do mercado da dvida pblica, nomeadamente por permitir o arranque das emisses do Estado como valores mobilirios. De 2009 a 2013 foi feito um trabalho de fundo entre os diferentes stakeholders  o Ministrio das Finanas, o Banco de Cabo Verde/AGMVM e a Bolsa de Valores  culminando com a entrada em funcionamento da plataforma dos leiles do Estado em 2013. A efetivao dessa plataforma permitiu o alargamento da base e a reduo de custo de financiamento. Porm, o mercado secundrio sendo um dos pilares da reforma encontra-se ainda em estado muito incipiente. Entretanto, atravs da Bolsa de Valores foram emitidos, nestes ltimos anos, valores expressivos em ttulos de dvida pblica. Por exemplo, em 2016 foram emitidos cerca de 14,5 milhes de contos, correspondendo a aproximadamente 9% da riqueza produzida nesse ano, ou seja, o PIB de Cabo Verde. Desse valor de 14,5 milhes de contos, 11,8 foram OTs e 2,8 BTs. Apesar de todo o esforo na introduo de mecanismos mais aperfeioados de financiamento do Estado ainda no conseguimos desenvolver o mercado secundrio da dvida pblica. Saliente-se que dos 20 leiles da dvida pblica ocorridos no perodo entre 2013 e 2016, apenas cinco transaes ocorreram em mercado secundrio. Por outro lado, os ttulos emitidos pelo Estado de Cabo Verde at este momento tm sido adquiridos pelos bancos comerciais, ficando em carteira dos mesmos, provocando o fenmeno chamado de entesouramento, pelo facto de no existir interesse particular em negoci-la em mercado secundrio. Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Atendendo a importncia de um mercado secundrio ativo e lquido, para o desenvolvimento do mercado de capitais de Cabo Verde, julgo que faz todo o sentido refletir-se sobre uma pesquisa feita pelo Banco Mundial que apresenta as condies bsicas como essenciais para um bom funcionamento do mercado secundrio e condutoras de melhorias na gesto da dvida pblica. Estas condies podem ser resumidas da seguinte forma. a) Um sistema de dealers normatizado, com direitos e obrigaes associados ao cumprimento de metas de negociao, alm de dar maior credibilidade ao mercado, estimula o crescimento da liquidez; b) A existncia de alternativas que amplifiquem o nmero de participantes, mesmo em momentos de maior volatilidade, possibilitando a sada de posies desfavorveis em condies competitivas. Tal caracterstica  fundamental para compatibilizar o interesse do emissor de alongar a dvida e a demanda dos investidores por mercados lquidos; c) Uma base ampla e diversificada de investidores e agentes financeiros, composta por instituies financeiras, investidores institucionais, corretoras, empresas e pessoas fsicas e pelas diversas classes de fundos; d) A presena de investidores no residentes, os quais, em geral, apresentam a capacidade de negociar ttulos mais longos. No entanto, a presena dessa classe de investidores necessita de maior liberalizao da conta financeira do pas e de bons fundamentos econmicos. Neste particular, aponta-se a elevada dvida pblica do pas, cerca de 131% em 2016, como aspeto que pode condicionar negativamente o interesse da dvida de Cabo Verde. Por outro, h necessidade de se procurar obter um ponderador de risco mais baixo para deteno de dvida pblica da Repblica de Cabo Verde por parte das instituies financeiras portuguesas e estrangeiras, tendo em conta o Acordo de Cooperao Cambial vigente, que permite a ligao da moeda nacional ao Euro; e) A padronizao dos ttulos da dvida pblica, introduzindo, por exemplo, unidade de negociao, padro de contagem de tempo e de entrega do ativo; f) A concentrao de vencimentos e o sistema de recompras, os quais aumentam a liquidez e facilitam emisses de ativos longos com rentabilidade prefixada. Esse alongamento da dvida, somado  colocao de ttulos prefixados, por sua vez, diminui a exposio ao risco de juros e de refinanciamento do Tesouro pblico; g) A existncia de um mercado de balco representativo, pois este permite a personalizao de produtos financeiros, implicando um aumento de participantes; h) O uso de sistemas eletrnicos, os quais aumentam a eficincia do mercado, na medida em que permitem aos participantes visualizar as ofertas, o que induz a uma maior transparncia, minimizando limitaes e informaes assimtricas dos parmetros necessrios para a rotulagem dos preos dos ttulos. Esses fatores aumentam o nmero de investidores e, consequentemente, a liquidez do mercado; i) A existncia de regras claras de conduta, as quais previnem a fraude e a manipulao de mercado. Essas regras podem ser estabelecidas pela autoridade reguladora ou via autorregulao pelas associaes dos participantes do mercado. Como se ver, as condies bsicas acima apresentadas so geralmente inexistentes em Cabo Verde e mesmo aquelas existentes ou incipientes so objeto de discusso pelos participantes do sistema financeiro, pelas entidades de classe, pelos investidores e pelos rgos governamentais diretamente relacionados. Importa, assim, debruar-se sobre elas e ponderar a sua criao, naturalmente mutatis mutandi. Para que esse projeto se concretize ser necessrio a envolvncia de todos os intervenientes do mercado. O BCV este sempre  frente de todas essas reformas e vai continuar a dar todo o seu apoio l onde for necessrio. Muito obrigado pela vossa ateno! 11 de setembro de 2017 Joo Serra /Governador do Banco de Cabo Verde/

Title: Speech at the Closing of the Seminar The Ongoing Reform of the Financial System in Cape Verde
text: Speech by the Governor, Joao Serra, at the Closing of the Seminar The Ongoing Reform of the Financial System in Cape Verde, February 26, 2018 Members of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Cape Verde, Ms Chargee d'Affaires of the Luxembourg Embassy in Cape Verde, Members of the Board of Directors of The AGMVM, Directors, Advisors and Coordinators of the Bank of Cape Verde, Mr Director General of the Treasury, Members of the Board of Directors of the Cape Verde Stock Exchange, Lady Bastonaria of the Bar Association, Mr Presidents of financial institutions, Mr. Consultant Dr. Paulo Camara, Dear Employees of bcv and financial institutions, Guest Gentlemen, Ladies and gentlemen, It is an honor and satisfaction for me to close this important Seminar on the ongoing reform of the financial system in Cape Verde. I would like to congratulate the Advisor of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Cape Verde, Dr. Encarnacao Rocha, for promoting the organization of this event, whose realization was supported by the Luxembourg Cooperation, which we also thank. Likewise, our thanks to all those who accepted the invitation of the organizers of this Seminar, as well as to the consultant Dr. Paulo Camara for the brilliant presentation made and sharing their relevant technical knowledge and experience. I am convinced that joint concerns and experiences have been shared at this meeting and that the objectives advocated have been fully achieved, for the sake of the much-desired as necessary development of the Cape Verdean financial system. The BCV will take due account of the subsidies coming out of this reflection. Ladies and gentlemen, The financial system is one of the major pillars of the development and efficient functioning of a country's economy. To this end, the development of financial products, services and markets and the creation of an appropriate regulatory framework is indispensable. Cape Verde could not and cannot be oblivious to the modernization of the financial system and the evolution of the regulatory framework worldwide. In fact, the country has sought to keep pace with the evolution of the international financial system, introducing important reforms in the national financial sector. The reforms already adopted have sought to reflect, in Cape Verdean domestic law, solutions that accompany international best practices, in order to enhance the contribution of the financial sector to the sustainable development of the country. On the other hand, they aim to ensure the competitiveness of the regulatory model of the banking, insurance and securities market, thus avoiding risks of regulatory arbitrage. The new package of draft diplomas that is in public consultation undoubtedly contributes to the modernization of the Cape Verdean financial system, with the creation of innovative financial products and a legal framework more conducive to the day to the day. It brings important news to the capital market such as Crowdfunding, the Social Entrepreneurship Investment Organization, The Guaranteed Collective Investment Organizations and the Infraction Reporting System. Also, changes to the Securities Market Code, in the parts relating to the activity of financial intermediation, as well as the disclosure of transactions of directors of listed companies, despite the point, are also extremely important for the sector and already felt its need. In the continuity of the ongoing reform process, it is worth stressing the importance and urgency of the reform to the Commercial Business Code, approved by Legislative Decree No. 3/99, as well as financial intermediation, approved by Law No. 53/V/98, because these standards are misaligned and out of line with the various reforms that have been made in the financial sector. In this seminar which is now completed we have been able to find out sufficiently the importance of each of the draft diplomas in public consultation, as well as of the underlying legislative options. Therefore, I would like to focus my particular attention on the regulation and supervision of the capital market, mindful of its enormous importance and timeliness for our financial system and considering the imminent adoption of the above-mentioned diplomas. Ladies and gentlemen, At the international level and with the financial crisis that began in the international markets, regulation has been a process of continuous evolution. In this context, "regulatory" administrative law or, in other words, the law of economic and sectoral public ordination has become a true "laboratory" of legal science. In particular, financial regulation has become a "cutting-edge sector" in this laboratory, both for the supremacy of financial reality over economic and legal, and for the situation created with the global financial and economic crisis that began in 2007. It is recalled that this is a crisis called a "third generation" crisis, because it associates a banking crisis and a systemic financial crisis. An appropriate, useful and simultaneously demanding, flexible and proportionate regulation aimed at the cross-cutting protection of investors and the market, in turn, assumes the prior definition of regulatory policies. Such policies should, on the one hand, incorporate the real needs of the market and, on the other hand, consider the negative impacts of the regulation itself, which are over-regulation, rigidity, bias and indirect or collateral impacts of regulation, usually not foreseen. In addition to financial regulation, efficient and rigorous prudential and behavioural supervision is also inescapable, with the aim of ensuring compliance with the rules, both ex ante and ex post. The assumed natural inability of any model and supervisory system to ensure the individual protection of each investor and to dispense with the same degree of protection to all investors makes it necessary to make a selection. This involves focusing on the most vulnerable investors and the most complex products and operations with higher levels of risk. Thus, it should not be surprising that regulation and supervision can be assumedly favoured, for example, by retail investors over the rest. Or, among them, those most vulnerable, depending on their literacy, risk profile or financial capacity. This protection should be provided from the outset through the financial education of investors with lower levels of financial literacy, loss absorption and the ability to understand products, and also elect them as a privileged target of the provision to be dispensed by regulation and supervision. In addition to the protection of investors, there is also a need for a clear accountability of financial intermediaries, which are responsible for compliance with rules of conduct, in their relationship with investors, with a view to protecting the interests of the latter, and it is up to the supervision to ensure compliance. In Cape Verde, the regulation and supervision of the national capital market is the responsibility of the General Audit of the Securities Market (AGMVM), and this institution is responsible for the legal exercise of the protection of investors and the trust they place in the system. To this end, the AGMVM should monitor and ensure the transparent, effective and competitive functioning of the securities market. Indeed, it is of particular importance, in capital markets, the concern to protect the psychological element and the inherent confidence of the agents and actors in those markets, ensuring the existence of liquidity in the market, the profitability of investments and the security, credibility and integrity of the financial system. It is also apparent directly from the law that investor protection, the efficiency and regularity of the functioning of financial instrument markets, information control, systemic risk prevention and the prevention and repression of illegal practices are the main public purposes for AGMVM to pursue, by establishing a balance between protecting investor position and competitiveness and efficiency of markets. Inherent to the idea of investor protection is effective risk prevention and protection. However, it is intended here that investors are no longer free ed from the risks associated with investment decisions, but rather to ensure that they are adequately documented and, as well, perceived and anticipated by the market. It should therefore ensure that the AGMVM, as an administrative authority, is met and the requirements for investors to be met from the risks considered normal and acceptable to the market concerned. This aims to eliminate abnormal and extraordinary risks and prevent the intensification of market risks. Ladies and gentlemen, The continuous formatting of the regulatory framework of the financial market in Cape Verde is indispensable to make the national financial sector modern, credible and with increasing utility. In fact, in addition to all the reforms already underway, particularly in the last decade, the Cape Verdean financial sector still needs greater vitality, which involves the creation of new regulatory mechanisms and, at the same time, other sources of funding. Here, it is important to highlight the use of the market as an alternative source of financing for companies. The difficulty of financing Cape Verdean companies, especially medium and small enterprises, is a reality and a challenge that demands instruments to overcome them, thus reducing important economic constraints. In this context, crowdfunding is of great importance, as an alternative form of funding, from the point of view of entrepreneurs and beneficiaries In the particular context of Cape Verde, and given the quantitative profile of investments in crowdfunding, it is still to be hoped that the emergence of crowdfunding platforms can play an important role in the financial inclusion of the population, granting it access to alternative forms of savings and investment. As we know, crowdfunding, or Crowdfunding as it is traditionally known, is the funding that can be obtained by anyone, singular or collective, to raise portions of investment by one or more individual investors, through electronic platforms accessible on the Internet. These platforms aim, therefore, to provide a mechanism for projects, development of ideas and specific activities to find investors and that investors can also find projects with the potential to invest. Those interested in receiving funding, i.e. beneficiaries register with the electronic platforms set up for this purpose, presenting the regulatory information that may be determined about the project they wish to be financed and on its feasibility. Potential investors also register similarly with the platform. These electronic platforms are associated with a number of advantages, such as reducing information asymmetries and thus constituting an obstacle to fraud and enabling a higher rate of success in the collection of funds. This source of funding is a very beneficial option for the implementation of new projects, for which their promoters could hardly use traditional forms of financing. It is thus based on the following brocardo: small investments x large community excellent projects! The implementation and development of crowdfunding fosters not only entrepreneurship, but also job creation, entrepreneurship, innovation and research, which are indispensable pillars for a country's economic growth. I will end by ensuring to all players in the financial market, especially in the subsector of the capital market, that bcv, through its Governor, as the body on which the functioning of the AGMVM depends, will continue to be the main promoter of all reforms, supporting everything necessary to this end, within the framework of a close articulation with the Government. Thank you so much for your attention! Beach, 26 February 2017 Joao Pinto /Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde/
text_original: Discurso do Governador, Joo Serra, no Encerramento do Seminrio A Reforma em Curso do Sistema Financeiro em Cabo Verde, 26 de fevereiro de 2018 Senhores Membros do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Cabo Verde, Senhora Charge dAffaires da Embaixada de Luxemburgo em Cabo Verde, Senhores Membros do Conselho Diretivo da AGMVM, Diretores, Assessores e Coordenadores do Banco de Cabo Verde, Senhor Director Geral do Tesouro, Senhores Membros do Conselho de Administrao da Bolsa de Valores de Cabo Verde, Senhora Bastonria da Ordem dos Advogados, Senhores Presidentes das Instituies Financeiras, Senhor Consultor Dr. Paulo Cmara, Caros Colaboradores do BCV e das Instituies Financeiras, Senhores Convidados, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores,  para mim uma honra e satisfao encerrar este importante Seminrio sobre a reforma em curso do sistema financeiro em Cabo Verde. Queria felicitar a Assessora do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Cabo Verde, Dr. Encarnaco Rocha, pela promoo da organizao deste evento, cuja realizao contou com o apoio financeiro da Cooperao Luxemburguesa, o qual tambm agradecemos. De igual modo, os nossos agradecimentos a todos os que aceitaram o convite dos organizadores deste Seminrio, bem como ao consultor Dr. Paulo Cmara pela brilhante apresentao feita e partilha dos seus conhecimentos tcnicos e experincia relevantes. Estou convicto que neste encontro tenham sido partilhadas preocupaes e experincias conjuntas e que os objetivos preconizados foram plenamente alcanados, em prol do to almejado quanto necessrio desenvolvimento do sistema financeiro cabo-verdiano. O BCV tomar em devida conta os subsdios sados dessa reflexo. Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, O sistema financeiro  um dos maiores pilares do desenvolvimento e funcionamento eficiente da economia de um pas. Para o efeito, torna-se indispensvel o desenvolvimento de produtos, servios e mercados financeiros, bem como a criao de um quadro regulamentar adequado. Cabo Verde no podia e nem poder ficar alheio  modernizao do sistema financeiro e  evoluo do quadro regulatrio, a nvel mundial. Na verdade, o pas tem procurado acompanhar a evoluo do sistema financeiro internacional, introduzindo importantes reformas no sector financeiro nacional. As reformas j adotadas procuraram refletir, no direito interno cabo-verdiano, solues que acompanhem as melhores prticas internacionais, por forma a potenciar o contributo do sector financeiro para o desenvolvimento sustentado do Pas. Por outro lado, visam assegurar a competitividade do modelo regulatrio do mercado bancrio, segurador e de valores mobilirios, evitando, assim, riscos de arbitragem regulatria. O novo pacote de projetos de diplomas que se encontra em consulta pblica vem, sem dvida, contribuir para a modernizao do sistema financeiro cabo-verdiano, com a criao de produtos financeiros inovadores e um quadro legal mais propcio aos dias de hoje. Traz importantes novidades para o mercado de capitais como o Financiamento Colaborativo, o Organismo de Investimento em Empreendedorismo Social, os Organismos de Investimento Coletivo Garantidos e o Sistema de Reporte de Infraes. Tambm, as alteraes ao Cdigo do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios, nas partes relativas  atividade de intermediao financeira, bem como  divulgao de transaes de dirigentes das sociedades cotadas, pese embora sejam pontuais, so tambm de extrema importncia para o sector e j se fazia sentir a sua necessidade. Na continuidade do processo de reforma em curso,  de frisar a importncia e urgncia da reforma ao Cdigo das Empresas Comerciais, aprovado pelo Decreto-Legislativo n3/99, bem assim, da Intermediao Financeira, aprovada pela Lei n 53/V/98, pois estas normas encontram-se desajustadas e desalinhadas com as vrias reformas que tm sido feitas no sector financeiro. Neste Seminrio que ora termina pudemos inteirar-nos suficientemente da importncia de cada um dos projetos de diplomas em consulta pblica, bem como das opes legislativas subjacentes. Assim sendo, gostaria de incidir a minha interveno particularmente sobre a regulao e superviso do mercado de capitais, atento  sua enorme importncia e atualidade para o nosso sistema financeiro e considerando a iminente aprovao dos diplomas supra-referidos. Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, A nvel internacional e com a crise financeira que teve incio nos mercados Internacionais, a regulamentao tem sido um processo de evoluo contnua. Neste mbito, o Direito Administrativo regulatrio ou, por outras palavras, o direito da ordenao pblica econmica e sectorial tornou-se um verdadeiro laboratrio da cincia jurdica. Em particular, a regulao financeira transformou-se num sector de ponta neste laboratrio, quer pela supremacia da realidade financeira sobre a econmica e jurdica, quer pela situao criada com a crise financeira e econmica global, iniciada em 2007. Recorde-se que se trata de uma crise denominada de crise de terceira gerao, porque associa uma crise bancria e uma crise financeira sistmica. Uma regulamentao adequada, til e simultaneamente exigente, flexvel e proporcional dirigida  proteo transversal dos investidores e mercado, supe, por sua vez, a definio prvia de polticas regulatrias. Tais polticas devem, por um lado, incorporar as reais necessidades do mercado e, por outro lado, ponderar os impactos negativos da prpria regulao, quais sejam sobre-regulao, rigidez, enviesamento e impactos indiretos ou colaterais da regulao, habitualmente no previstos. Para alm da regulamentao financeira,  tambm incontornvel uma superviso prudencial e comportamental eficiente e rigorosa, com o intuito de garantir o cumprimento das regras, tanto ex ante como ex post. Com efeito, a assumida incapacidade natural de qualquer modelo e sistema de superviso de assegurar a proteo individual de cada investidor e de dispensar o mesmo grau de proteo a todos os investidores, torna necessrio que seja feita uma seleo. Esta implica fazer incidir o foco de superviso sobre os investidores mais vulnerveis e sobre os produtos e operaes mais complexos e com nveis de risco mais elevados. Assim, no deve estranhar-se que a regulao e a superviso possam privilegiar assumidamente, por exemplo, os investidores no profissionais em detrimento dos restantes. Ou, de entre eles, aqueles mais vulnerveis, em funo da sua literacia, perfil de risco ou capacidade financeira. Essa proteo deve ser, desde logo, proporcionada atravs da educao financeira dos investidores que apresentam nveis mais reduzidos de literacia financeira, de absoro de perdas e de capacidade de compreenso dos produtos, elegendo-os tambm como alvo privilegiado da prestao a ser dispensada pela regulao e superviso. Para alm da proteo dos investidores, h tambm necessidade de uma ntida responsabilizao dos intermedirios financeiros, aos quais compete a observncia de regras de conduta, na sua relao com os investidores, com vista  proteo dos interesses destes ltimos, cabendo  superviso assegurar o seu cumprimento. Em Cabo Verde, a regulao e superviso do mercado de capitais nacional est a cargo da Auditoria Geral do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios (AGMVM), competindo a esta instituio o exerccio legal da tutela dos investidores e da confiana que estes depositam no sistema. Para o efeito, a AGMVM dever controlar e garantir o funcionamento transparente, eficaz e concorrencial do mercado de valores mobilirios. Efetivamente, reveste-se de particular importncia, nos mercados de capitais, a preocupao de tutelar o elemento psicolgico e a inerente confiana dos agentes e intervenientes naqueles mercados, garantindo a existncia de liquidez no mercado, a rentabilidade dos investimentos e a segurana, credibilidade e integridade do sistema financeiro. Resulta, de resto, diretamente da lei, que a proteo dos investidores, a eficincia e regularidade de funcionamento dos mercados de instrumentos financeiros, o controlo da informao, a preveno do risco sistmico e a preveno e represso de prticas ilegais so os principais fins pblicos que cabe  AGMVM prosseguir, atravs do estabelecimento de um equilbrio entre a tutela da posio dos investidores e a competitividade e eficincia dos mercados. Inerente  ideia de tutela do investidor  a preveno e proteo eficaz contra riscos. Todavia, pretende-se aqui no j libertar o investidor dos riscos associados s decises de investimento, mas antes garantir que os mesmos so adequadamente documentados e, bem assim, percebidos e antecipados pelo mercado. Dever, deste modo, a AGMVM, enquanto autoridade administrativa, assegurar que estejam cumpridas as condies e preenchidos os requisitos que permitam a assuno pelos investidores dos riscos considerados normais e aceitveis para o mercado em causa. Com isso, visa-se eliminar riscos anormais e extraordinrios e prevenir a intensificao dos riscos prprios do mercado. Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, A formatao contnua do quadro normativo regulatrio do mercado financeiro de Cabo Verde revela-se imprescindvel, para tornar o sector financeiro nacional moderno, credvel e com cada vez maior utilidade. Na realidade, para alm de todas as reformas j encetadas, particularmente na ltima dcada, o sector financeiro cabo-verdiano precisa ainda duma maior vitalidade, o que passa pela criao de novos mecanismos de regulao e, ao mesmo tempo, de outras fontes de financiamento. Aqui, convm salientar o recurso ao mercado como fonte alternativa de financiamento das empresas. A dificuldade de financiamento das empresas cabo-verdianas, sobretudo das empresas de mdia e pequena dimenso,  uma realidade e um desafio que demanda instrumentos para a sua superao, reduzindo, assim, constrangimentos econmicos importantes. Neste quadro, reveste-se de enorme importncia o Crowdfunding, enquanto uma forma alternativa de financiamento, do ponto de vista dos empreendedores e beneficirios No particular contexto de Cabo Verde, e atendendo ao perfil quantitativo dos investimentos em financiamento colaborativo,  ainda de esperar que o aparecimento de plataformas de financiamento colaborativo possa ter um papel importante na incluso financeira da populao, concedendo-lhe acesso a formas alternativas de poupana e investimento. Como se sabe, o financiamento colaborativo, ou Crowdfunding como  tradicionalmente conhecido,  o financiamento que pode ser obtido por qualquer pessoa, singular ou coletiva, para angariao de parcelas de investimento por parte de um ou mais investidores individuais, atravs de plataformas eletrnicas acessveis na Internet. Estas plataformas visam, portanto, fornecer um mecanismo para que projetos, desenvolvimento de ideias e atividades especficas encontrem investidores e que investidores possam, tambm, encontrar projetos com potencial para investir. Os interessados em receber financiamento, ou seja, os beneficirios registam-se junto das plataformas eletrnicas criadas para o efeito, apresentando a informao regulamentar que vier a ser determinada sobre o projeto que pretendem ver financiado e sobre a sua viabilidade. Tambm os potenciais investidores procedem a um registo similar junto da plataforma. A estas plataformas eletrnicas encontram-se associadas diversas vantagens, tais como o facto de reduzirem assimetrias de informao e, assim, constiturem um obstculo s fraudes e permitirem maior taxa de sucesso na recolha de fundos. Esta fonte de financiamento traduz-se numa opo muito benfica no que respeita  implementao de novos projetos, relativamente aos quais os seus promotores dificilmente poderiam recorrer s formas tradicionais de financiamento. Tem assim, por base, o seguinte brocardo: pequenos investimentos x grande comunidade = excelentes projetos! A implementao e desenvolvimento do financiamento colaborativo fomentam no s o esprito empresarial, como tambm a criao de postos de trabalho, o empreendedorismo, a inovao e investigao, pilares estes indispensveis ao crescimento econmico de um pas. Termino assegurando a todos os intervenientes no mercado financeiro, sobretudo no subsector do mercado de capitais, que o BCV, atravs do seu Governador, enquanto rgo do qual depende o funcionamento da AGMVM, continuar a ser o principal promotor de todas as reformas, apoiando em tudo o que for necessrio para o efeito, no quadro de uma estreita articulao com o Governo. Muito obrigado pela vossa ateno! Praia, 26 de Fevereiro de 2017 Joo Pinto Serra /Governador do Banco de Cabo Verde/

Title: Speech at the opening of the Seminar, The Circulation of Securities and Investor Protection
text: Speech by the Governor, Joao Serra, at the opening of the Seminar, The Circulation of Securities and Investor Protection, March 7, 2018 Members of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Cape Verde, Ms Chargee d'Affaires of the Luxembourg Embassy in Cape Verde, Members of the Board of Directors of The AGMVM, Directors, Advisors and Coordinators of the Bank of Cape Verde, Members of the Board of Directors of the Cape Verde Stock Exchange, Lady Bastonaria of the Bar Association, Mr Presidents of financial institutions, Mr. Consultores Drs. Jose Martins and Hugo Santos, Dear Employees of bcv and financial institutions, Guest Gentlemen, Ladies and gentlemen, Following the latest international financial crisis, a number of initiatives have been triggered to resolate the models of regulation, supervision and governance of the financial system. We highlight the supervisory models that have been undergoing significant changes, becoming more intrusive and, in parallel, starting to have a more transversal and prospective approach. On the other hand, at the global level, especially Europe, there has been greater interference in the content of contracts relating to financial activity, in particular in the duties of information, adequacy, loyalty in conflict of interest management and other fiduciary duties. There has also been a greater demand for the protection of investors, particularly those not qualified, in view of the recognition of the existence of an impactful information asymmetry. In the current financial markets framework, it is essential that Cape Verde appropriate and adapt international good practices on the regulation and supervision of the financial sector to the national reality. And he's been doing it, from a few years to the present, although of course he still has a lot to do. Likewise, it is essential that the entity that regulates and supervises the securities market, the General Audit of the Securities Market, AGMVM, has standards that go far beyond what one might think depending on the size of our country. That is the only way, AGMVM will fully fulfil its regulatory and supervisory tasks and become a credible and internationally respected entity. Ladies and gentlemen, Capital markets, as organised and structured systems for collecting and channeling savings directly into productive investment or risk redistribution, play an unavoidable role in a country's economic and social development. Indeed, the reduction in intermediation costs enhanced by direct financing is not only a factor in competitiveness but also makes an important contribution to economic growth. In general, capital market regulation and supervision authorities have sought an appropriate trade-off between investor protection desideratum and the adoption of regulatory measures that foster market dynamism and competitiveness. Also for our country, it is essential to regulate and supervise that, at the same time, guarantees a desired level of protection and is to be as much as possible a friend of the business. Efforts have been made in this direction, although there is still much room for evolution. In Cape Verde, the capital market is still at a very early stage, largely because of the development stage of the domestic economy. However, there has been a significant evolution over the last decade, with the stock market capitalization reaching 68.4 million contos in 2017, equivalent to 40.2% of GDP, placing the country in a favorable position compared to other countries of its income level. However, the sector with the greatest dynamism has been the bond market, especially public debt securities, unlike the shareholder market which has had very little expression and dynamics. The Investor's Guide to be presented at this Seminar is a publication of the General Securities Market Audit. It contains a brief explanation of the functioning of the securities and derivative financial instruments markets, as well as a brief description of its main players. It is intended for all persons who wish to acquire some knowledge about the functioning of capital markets and the rights and duties they have in order to invest their savings in securities or other financial instruments. It is therefore an important information document and I would therefore like to highlight the importance of information and regulation for the protection of investors in the securities market and its proper functioning. In fact, one of the major challenges facing the supervision of capital markets today is to keep economic agents and investors informed properly. This desiderato aligns with international good practice, in line with the principles emanating from IOSCO - International Organization for Securities of which Cape Verde has been an affiliated member since 2016. Effectively, due to our country's compliance with IOSCO, the formatting of the new regulatory framework for the securities market is becoming increasingly demanding due to the recommended standards issued by this organization. In this context, one of the areas of greatest densification is precisely the duties of information and financial literacy. It should be noted that information is a principle enshrined in the Securities Market Code approved by Legislative Decree No. 1/2012 of 27 January 2012. Thus, it is essential that, at every moment, the various agents intervene to adequately understand the mechanisms by which investment in securities is governed, on the one hand. On the other hand, so that the various agents can more consciously fulfill their duties and exercise their rights. With this, the issuers start to provide annual information on the corporate governance, thus inaugurating the dissemination of the theme in Cape Verde. The required information covers the essential elements of corporate governance, including decision-making mechanisms in each company, the statutory rules for the exercise of voting and the composition of the shareholder structure. Of the same step, it is envisaged the possibility of annual accountability documents being submitted in accordance with international accounting standards. This aims to align financial information with international standards, which will certainly serve as a basis for the internationalization of listed Cape Verdean companies. Information on financial instruments, organised forms of trading, financial intermediation activities, settlement and clearing of transactions, public offerings of securities and issuers shall be complete, true, current, clear, objective and lawful. Ladies and gentlemen, The AGMVM shall, in accordance with Article 32 of the existing Securities Market Code, publish annually the updated text of the legal and regulatory rules relating to matters governed by the Code and in supplementary legislation. The dynamism of the securities market requires frequent changes to the regulations governing them, whether legal or regulatory in nature. It is therefore essential that, at every moment, the various agents intervene to properly understand the mechanisms underlying investment in securities and thus be able to more consciously fulfil their duties and exercise their rights. The provision of full information on securities and their issuers, together with the adjacent rules of conduct, promotes the protection of investors identically. Moreover, such information represents an effective means of strengthening confidence in securities, thus contributing to the smooth functioning and development of capital markets. On the other hand, rules on information and transparency have been defined, in particular on preventing and combating market abuse. To this end, a number of measures have been adopted covering the deepening of the reporting duties of financial intermediaries, such as the regulation of the obligation to disclose inside information and the possibility of deferring the disclosure of information to listed companies. Market transparency is also based on the proper disclosure of legal rules concerning it. For this reason, it is wish that this publication of the new Investor's Guide will be of great use to all professionals and investors in the securities market. As a complement to the Securities Market Code, AGMVM Regulation No. 1/2015 on qualified and unqualified investors clarified the regime that this classification entails. This regulation is based on the differentiation of treatment between qualified and unqualified investors, reserving for them more intense protection and a collection of additional duties imposed on financial intermediaries in the provision of investment services. Unqualified investors with a lower degree of investment knowledge and experience in securities and derivatives and related securities are classified as non-qualified and are unable to carry out a correct assessment of the risks involved. At this time of reform and modernization of the models of regulation of the financial system, the Cape Verdean legal system clearly requires a clear delimitation of these two figures, as an indispensable precondition for effective protection of investors. With regard to financial intermediation, a focus has been given to issues related to the processes of registration of financial intermediation activities and organizational requirements to which the exercise of the activity is subject. This includes matters relating to human, material and technical resources required for the provision of each of the intermediation activities, as well as organisational measures on conflicts of interest, segregation and risk prevention. They are also aspects to be taken care of by the regulations, policies and internal procedures of financial intermediaries relating to the categorisation of investors and the circumstances that should be considered for the purpose of applying the duties relating to compliance control systems, risk management and internal auditing. Finally, we wanted to take advantage of the opportunity offered to us with the public presentation of the Investor's Guide, to discuss two important topics. One on the issue and circulation of securities, and the other on the different levels of protection and information conferred on investors in Cape Verdean law and European law. The topics to be discussed in this Seminar are therefore of great use and opportunity for the moment we are going through. His presentation is in charge of Drs. Jose Fazenda Martins and Hugo Moreno Santos, two prominent legal advisors, with extensive experience in the field and numerous reflections and written works related to the functioning of the financial system. Thank you to both of us for accepting our invitation. Good wishes for good work. Thank you so much for your attention! Beach, 07 March 2017 Joao Pinto /Governor of BCV/
