O processo de transformao exige mudanas de comportamentos, de processo, nas instituies, na legislao e na regulamentao. Tambm, comporta riscos, cria resistncia e desafios a vrios nveis, nomeadamente na estrutura de propriedade, na capitalizao, na estrutura legal e no modelo de governao. No obstante isso,  importante reconhecer que o fator fundamental, na maior parte das transformaes institucionais, foi a necessidade de ter acesso a maiores e mais flexveis fontes de captao de recursos. Temos noo de que  hoje fundamental o papel das microfinanas como uma importante ferramenta econmica e de incluso financeira. Na verdade, atravs do microcrdito e, mais recentemente, dos chamados microseguros,  possvel gerar rendimentos, criar emprego e transformar a vida das pessoas de baixos rendimentos, que doutro modo no seria possvel, devido  falta de garantias tradicionais sob a forma de bens ou rendimentos relevantes. Minhas Senhoras e meus Senhores, A Lei das Microfinanas estabelece que as associaes e outras instituies que praticam microfinanas devem promover a segregao das funes de cariz social das de microfinanas. Por outras palavras, a lei impe que as atividades dessas organizaes passem a ser exercidas por entidades jurdicas distintas. As instituies enquadradas nas categorias A, B e C devem adaptar-se s demais disposies dessa lei, bem como fazer o respetivo registo no Banco de Cabo Verde, at 31 de dezembro de 2018. Para o efeito,  fundamental que os agentes que operam na rea das microfinanas, particularmente os gestores estejam devidamente informados e capacitados, para o exerccio da sua atividade no estrito cumprimento do quadro legal e regulamentar. Neste contexto, o Frum que ora se inicia  uma oportunidade mpar que se nos oferece para esclarecimentos, troca de experincias e preocupaes, partilha de ensinamentos e propostas de solues. E isso no que toca  adoo de abordagens de superviso e de regulao adaptadas  realidade e voltadas para a mitigao de riscos financeiros da atividade do sector das microfinanas Termino, reiterando todo o interesse e empenhamento do BCV na implementao e criao das condies institucionais e regulatrias, para o desenvolvimento sustentvel e inclusivo das instituies de microfinanas em Cabo Verde. F-lo- em estreita articulao com o Governo e com a Organizao representativa do sector. Muito obrigado e votos de bom trabalho! Praia, 30 de julho de 2018 Joo Serra /Governador do Banco de Cabo Verde/

Title: Speech at the Conference commemorating the 20th anniversary of the Signing of the Exchange Cooperation Agreement
text: Speech by the Governor, Dr. Joao Serra, at the Conference commemorating the 20th anniversary of the Signing of the Exchange Cooperation Agreement Mr Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance, Mr Governor of Banco de Portugal, Distinguished Gentlemen Lecturers, Mr. COMACC members and UAM technicians, Mr. Administrators of the Bank of Cape Verde, Directors and Coordinators of the BCV, Mr. BCV Collaborators, Ladies and gentlemen, I am pleased to greet you and welcome you to Cape Verde and to the 20th anniversary meeting of the Exchange Cooperation Agreement, which materializes through this Conference, subject to the theme "Prospects for the Evolution of the Exchange Rate Regime in Cape Verde". Let me begin by expressing the sincere thanks of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Cape Verde to all those who have accepted our invitation to be with us at this event of paramount importance. Ladies and gentlemen Two decades after the signing of the Exchange Cooperation Agreement between the Republic of Cape Verde and the Republic of Portugal, I am pleased to say that the Cape Verdean shield has achieved the much-desired nominal stability and credibility that have led to the signing of the Agreement. Undoubtedly this achievement, as well as the deepening of economic and financial ties between Cape Verde and Europe, the current context of macro-financial development of the country, which differs from that in which the Agreement was signed, calls for a joint reflection on the current situation and the challenges that are exchange rate regime in Cape Verde, as well as the possible avenues for deepening this important strategic agreement. Ladies and gentlemen Let me go back a little bit in time. In 1998, the country was living in a context of very incipient development of its financial system, of severe macroeconomic imbalances and of exchange rate instability, which greatly persevered the country's external reserves. Bearing in mind the idiosyncratic characteristics of a small open, insular and African economy, the nominal stability of the Cape Verdean currency has been seen since the dawn of independence as a sine qua non condition to promote the balance of the fundamentals of the economy and sustain long-term progress and development. Thus, it is natural that the strategic orientation by a fixed exchange regime was the way found to enable the reorganisation of macroeconomic imbalances experienced at the time, promoting more discipline in the conduct of fiscal and monetary policies and creating space for the promotion of structural reforms leading to greater economic integration of the country in the global economy, in particular the European one. Based on these precepts and supported by strong ties of friendship and culture, the Exchange Cooperation Agreement between the Republic of Cape Verde and the Portuguese Republic was signed, which entered into force with Resolution No. 81/V/98 of May 11, determining that "the Cape Verdean national currency is now linked to the Portuguese national currency by a fixed parity relationship". Since then, monetary policy has been based on the objectives of price stability and strengthening of external reserves, with a view to defending the exchange rate regime.1 First, parity was fixed with the Portuguese shield and, in 1999, with Portugal's participation in the Euro Area, parity was fixed with the euro. 1 Until 1993, monetary policy was oriented towards the objective of economic stability, with a focus on price stability, balance of payments and financing economic growth. 2 COMACC's mission is to supervise the financial operations resulting from the Agreement, as well as to monitor the implementation of economic policies. The Commission for Exchange Cooperation Agreement (COMACC), which is part of representatives of the Portuguese and Cape Verdean governments, and the Macroeconomic Monitoring Unit (UAM), a unit under the commission and composed of expert technicians, have ensured compliance with the Agreement over the past 20 years.2 Allow me a brief interregnum to express, on behalf of the BCV Board of Directors, a particular thanks to the current and former members of COMACC and UAM for their high spirit of dedication and engagement in this regard. Ladies and gentlemen The gains achieved with the Agreement are important and significant: 1- the country managed to converge nominally, with today's long-term trend of national inflation aligned with the ECB's inflation target (2%); 2- the actual effective exchange rate of the shield, an indicator of the competitiveness-price of the economy, remained globally stable in this period, having recorded only slight depreciation in recent years; 3- the stability and credibility of exchange rate policy (in 20 years Cape Verde has never realigned parity!) enabled the increase of foreign direct investment in the country, with positive effects on the diversification of the economy and foreign trade of the country, increasing the degree of coverage of exports by imports; 4- there has been a greater symmetry of the economic cycles between Cape Verde and the Euro area, mitigating the effects of the loss of monetary policy autonomy due to the exchange rate policy adopted; 5- the country's external reserves grew in a sustained way, in global terms, being above 5 months of import of goods and services since 2014 and covering more than 100% of the monetary base for many years, ensuring without any embarrassment external payments; 6- the legal framework for macroeconomic policies has evolved towards greater regulatory technical convergence with the Euro area, seeking to promote greater macroeconomic discipline, an indispensable condition for the sustainability of the regime; Effectively, after 20 years on the signing of the Exchange Cooperation Agreement (ACC), profound transformations have taken place in the Economy of Cape Verde. The transformation, reflecting the strengthening of economic and financial links with Portugal and Europe, was particularly notable in the development of the national financial system, which reflected the effects of promoting an institutional, regulatory and regulatory framework more in line with international best practices. The challenges posed to the continuous development of the national financial system have guided the structural reforms in the country and the performance of the Bank of Cape Verde. Examples of this are the Law that Defines the Guiding Principles and the Normative Framework of Reference for the Financial System, the Law regulating the Activities of Financial Institutions, both of 2014, as well as several regulations published in recent years3 on the deepening of the securities market, supervision of the banking system and prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing. In turn, the new Organic Regulation of the BCV of July 2018 aimed to adapt to the new legal framework of the financial system, strengthening, in particular, the supervisory function of the country's financial system (which has been oriented to risk-based supervision since 2015). 3 2014 and 2015 Ladies and gentlemen Very recently, in June of this year, the Government of Cape Verde liberalized capital movements, looking to leverage the long-term potential for growth and economic development, of which the financial system is an integral part. It should be noted that, since 2004, international current account flows have been liberalised and that the stability and credibility of the Cape Verdean currency have in fact allowed capital movements to be virtually liberalised in recent years. The freedom of capital movements is an instrument of exchange rate stabilization, because it facilitates the entry of currencies associated with long-term productive investments financed with external savings. Therefore, this reform can be understood as a deepening or maturing of the exchange rate regime in force. The lifting of control of capital movements, however, has a price. It implies the loss of the role of lender of last resort to the Bank of Cape Verde and, in a context of macroeconomic indiscipline, may potentiate speculative attacks on the currency.4 4 It must also be taken into account that, even in a context of macroeconomic discipline, speculators can test the stability of the currency. 5 Enhanced financial supervision should be done to compensate for the bcv's loss of the function of lender of last resort. In this new context, there is a pressing need for continuous strengthening of the supervisory capacity of the financial system5, within a regulatory framework that is intended to be in line with international standards, as well as the increasingly rigorous management of the interest rate differential between Cape Verde and the Euro area. Also, 20 years after the signing of the Exchange Cooperation Agreement, this new reality calls for reflection on an important exchange stabilization instrument underlying the Agreement - the Credit Facility of the Exchange Cooperation Agreement - which performs, albeit to a lesser extent, a function of last resort lender at the disposal of the Bank of Cape Verde. Ladies and gentlemen These aspects, as well as other challenges for the exchange rate regime in Cape Verde and other ways of deepening the ACC, will be discussed today on this important day. We are sure that we still have a long way to go, especially in these times of still some uncertainty. I am convinced, however, that with the participation of the distinguished guests present here, we will be able to shed light on this journey of economic and financial development in the country. Beach, 14 September 2018 John Serra /Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde/
text_original: Interveno do Governador, Doutor Joo Serra, na Conferncia Comemorativa dos 20 anos da Assinatura do Acordo de Cooperao Cambial Senhor Vice-Primeiro Ministro e Ministro das Finanas, Senhor Governador do Banco de Portugal, Ilustres senhores Conferencistas, Senhores Membros da COMACC e tcnicos da UAM, Senhores Administradores do Banco de Cabo Verde, Senhores Diretores e Coordenadores do BCV, Senhores Colaboradores do BCV, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores,  com prazer que vos cumprimento e vos dou as boas vindas a Cabo Verde e ao encontro de celebrao dos 20 anos do Acordo de Cooperao Cambial, que se materializa atravs desta Conferncia, subordinada ao tema Perspetivas de Evoluo do Regime Cambial em Cabo Verde. Permitam-me comear por expressar o sincero agradecimento do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Cabo Verde a todos os que aceitaram o nosso convite, para estarem connosco neste evento de suma importncia. Minhas Senhoras e meus senhores Decorridas duas dcadas desde a assinatura do Acordo de Cooperao Cambial entre a Repblica de Cabo Verde e a Repblica de Portugal, apraz-me afirmar que o escudo cabo-verdiano conquistou as to almejadas estabilidade nominal e credibilidade que nortearam a assinatura do Acordo. Sendo indubitvel esta conquista, bem como o aprofundamento dos laos econmicos e financeiros entre Cabo Verde e a Europa, o atual contexto de desenvolvimento macrofinanceiro do pas, que se diferencia daquele em que o Acordo foi assinado, interpela-nos para uma reflexo conjunta sobre a situao atual e os desafios que se colocam ao regime cambial em Cabo Verde, bem como as possveis vias de aprofundamento deste importante acordo estratgico. Minhas senhoras e meus senhores Permitam-me retroceder um pouco no tempo. Em 1998, o pas vivia num contexto de desenvolvimento muito incipiente do seu sistema financeiro, de acentuados desequilbrios macroeconmicos e de instabilidade cambial, que perigavam sobremaneira as reservas externas do pas. Tendo presente as caractersticas idiossincrsicas de uma pequena economia aberta, insular e africana, a estabilidade nominal da moeda cabo-verdiana figurou-se desde os primrdios da independncia como uma condio sine qua non para promover o equilbrio dos fundamentais da economia e sustentar o progresso e o desenvolvimento a longo prazo. Assim,  natural que a orientao estratgica por um regime de cmbios fixos tenha sido o caminho encontrado para viabilizar o saneamento dos desequilbrios macroeconmicos vivenciados na altura, promovendo mais disciplina na conduo das polticas oramental e monetria e criando espao para a promoo de reformas estruturais conducentes a uma maior integrao econmica do pas na economia global, em particular a europeia. Assente nestes preceitos e sustentado por fortes laos de amizade e culturais, foi assinado o Acordo de Cooperao Cambial entre a Repblica de Cabo Verde e a Repblica Portuguesa, que entrou em vigor com a Resoluo n 81/V/98, de 11 de maio, determinando que a moeda nacional cabo-verdiana passa a estar ligada  moeda nacional portuguesa por uma relao de paridade fixa. Desde ento, a poltica monetria norteou-se pelos objetivos de estabilidade de preos e de reforo das reservas externas, com vista  defesa do regime cambial.1 Primeiramente, a paridade foi fixada com o escudo portugus e, em 1999, com a adeso de Portugal  rea do Euro, a paridade foi fixada com o euro. 1 At 1993, a poltica monetria foi orientada para o objetivo de estabilidade econmica, com enfoque na estabilidade de preos, defesa da balana de pagamentos e financiamento do crescimento econmico. 2 A COMACC tem por misso supervisionar as operaes financeiras resultantes do Acordo, assim como acompanhar a execuo das polticas econmicas. A Comisso de Acordo de Cooperao Cambial (COMACC), da qual fazem parte representantes dos governos portugus e cabo-verdiano, e a Unidade de Acompanhamento Macroeconmico (UAM), uma unidade tutelada pela comisso e composta por tcnicos especialistas, tm assegurado o cumprimento do Acordo ao longo destes ltimos 20 anos.2 Permitam-me um breve interregno para expressar, em nome do Conselho de Administrao do BCV, um particular agradecimento aos atuais e anteriores membros da COMACC e da UAM pelo elevado esprito de dedicao e engajamento a este propsito. Minhas senhoras e meus senhores So importantes e assinalveis os ganhos conquistados com o Acordo: 1- o pas conseguiu convergir nominalmente, estando hoje a tendncia de longo-prazo da inflao nacional alinhada ao inflation target do BCE (2%); 2- a taxa de cmbio efetiva real do escudo, indicador da competitividade-preo da economia, manteve-se globalmente estvel nesse perodo, tendo registado apenas ligeiras depreciaes nos ltimos anos; 3- a estabilidade e a credibilidade da poltica cambial (em 20 anos Cabo Verde nunca procedeu a qualquer realinhamento da paridade!) viabilizaram o aumento do investimento direto estrangeiro no pas, com efeitos positivos na diversificao da economia e no comrcio externo do pas, aumentando o grau de cobertura das exportaes pelas importaes; 4- assistiu-se a uma maior simetria dos ciclos econmicos entre Cabo Verde e a rea do Euro, mitigando os efeitos da perda de autonomia da poltica monetria em virtude da poltica cambial adotada; 5- as reservas externas do pas cresceram de forma sustentada, em termos globais, situando-se acima dos 5 meses de importao de bens e servios desde 2014 e cobrindo mais de 100% da base monetria h largos anos, assegurando sem qualquer constrangimento os pagamentos externos; 6- o enquadramento legal das polticas macroeconmicas tem evoludo no sentido de uma maior convergncia tcnica normativa com a rea do Euro, procurando promover uma maior disciplina macroeconmica, condio indispensvel para a sustentabilidade do regime; Efetivamente, passados 20 anos sobre a assinatura do Acordo de Cooperao Cambial (ACC), transformaes profundas se operaram na economia de Cabo Verde. A transformao, reflexo do reforo dos vnculos econmicos e financeiros com Portugal e a Europa, foi particularmente notvel a nvel do desenvolvimento do sistema financeiro nacional, que traduziu os efeitos da promoo de um quadro institucional, normativo e regulador mais consentneo com as melhores prticas internacionais. Os desafios que se colocam ao contnuo desenvolvimento do sistema financeiro nacional tm pautado as reformas estruturais no pas e a atuao do Banco de Cabo Verde. So exemplos disso a Lei que Define os Princpios Orientadores e o Quadro Normativo de Referncia para o Sistema Financeiro, a Lei que Regula as Atividades das Instituies Financeiras, ambas de 2014, bem como diversos normativos publicados nos ltimos anos3 em matria de aprofundamento do mercado de valores mobilirios, de superviso do sistema bancrio e de preveno  lavagem de capitais e financiamento do terrorismo. Por sua vez, o novo Regulamento Orgnico do BCV, de julho de 2018, visou adaptar-se ao novo enquadramento legal do sistema financeiro, reforando, em particular a funo de superviso do sistema financeiro do pas (que se orientou para uma superviso baseada no risco, desde 2015). 3 2014 e 2015 Minhas senhoras e meus senhores Muito recentemente, em junho do ano corrente, o Governo de Cabo Verde liberalizou de jure os movimentos de capitais, perspetivando alavancar o potencial de crescimento e desenvolvimento econmico no longo prazo, do qual o sistema financeiro  parte integrante. Importa referir que, desde 2004, os fluxos financeiros internacionais relativos  conta corrente esto liberalizados e que a estabilidade e a credibilidade da moeda cabo-verdiana permitiram que, de facto, os movimentos de capitais estivessem praticamente liberalizados nos ltimos anos. A liberdade dos movimentos de capitais constitui um instrumento de estabilizao cambial, por facilitar a entrada de divisas associadas a investimentos produtivos de longo prazo, financiados com poupana externa. Por isso, esta reforma pode ser entendida como um aprofundamento ou amadurecimento do regime cambial em vigor. O levantamento do controlo dos movimentos de capitais, contudo, tem um preo. Implica a perda da funo de prestamista de ltima instncia para o Banco de Cabo Verde e, num contexto de indisciplina macroeconmica, pode potenciar ataques especulativos  moeda.4 4  preciso ter tambm em conta que, mesmo num contexto de disciplina macroeconmica, os especuladores podem testar a estabilidade da moeda. 5 O reforo da superviso financeira dever ser feito para compensar a perda da funo de prestamista de ltima instncia por parte do BCV.  premente, neste novo contexto, a necessidade de contnuo reforo da capacidade de superviso do sistema financeiro5, dentro de um quadro regulatrio que se pretende consentneo com as normas internacionais, bem como de gesto cada vez mais rigorosa do diferencial de taxa de juro entre Cabo Verde e a rea do Euro. Igualmente, decorridos 20 anos desde a assinatura do Acordo de Cooperao Cambial, esta nova realidade nos interpela para uma reflexo sobre um importante instrumento de estabilizao cambial subjacente ao Acordo - a Facilidade de Crdito do Acordo de Cooperao Cambial  que desempenha, ainda que em menor medida, uma funo de prestamista de ltima instncia ao dispor do Banco de Cabo Verde. Minhas senhoras e meus senhores Estes aspetos, bem como outros desafios para o regime cambial em Cabo Verde e outras formas de aprofundamento do ACC, sero hoje debatidos neste importante dia. Estamos certos que ainda nos resta um longo caminho a percorrer, sobretudo nestes tempos de ainda alguma incerteza. Estou, porm, convicto de que, com a participao dos ilustres convidados aqui presentes, conseguiremos fazer luz sobre essa caminhada de desenvolvimento econmico e financeiro do pas. Praia, 14 de setembro de 2018 Joo Serra /Governador do Banco de Cabo Verde/

Title: Speech at the 1st Meeting for The Management of External Reserves of the Central Banks of the Language Countries
text: Intervention of the Governor, Dr. Joao Serra, at the 1st Meeting on The Management of External Reserves of the Central Banks of the Language Countries Mr Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance, Excellency Mr. Administrator of Banco de Portugal, Mr. Administrators of the Bank of Cape Verde, Representatives of the Central Banks of portuguese-speaking countries, Representatives of financial institutions, Dear BCV Employees, Guest Gentlemen, Ladies and gentlemen, I am particularly pleased that the I Meeting for the Management of External Reserves of the Central Banks of portuguese-speaking countries took place in Cape Verde. It is an event of paramount importance and timeliness for a country that has a fixed parity exchange rate regime, in addition to being a small open economy and very dependent on imports and external savings. Our sincere thanks to all the representatives of the Central Banks present here for the excellent sharing of knowledge and experience in the management of external reserves. Our congratulations to the distinguished speakers and speakers for the brilliant and fruitful communications made. Likewise, we congratulate the organization of the event, the Department of Markets and Reserve Management of the Bank of Cape Verde and its Administrator, for the quality printed in its realization. The BCV will take due account of the subsidies coming out of the Meeting. Ladies and gentlemen, Coins, as reserve assets, have existed for thousands of years, from the time of the Greek Drachma in the 5th century BC. Money is irreplaceable due to its inherent stability and its global importance as a means of exchange. Today, in an increasingly integrated and interconnected global economy, virtually no country can survive without foreign exchange reserves. As was evident in this event, the official external reserves have served, in addition to the most basic functions, to show the world the stability of a country's economy to cope with its external liabilities. On the other hand, they are a factor in the attraction of new investments by international investors. In addition, foreign exchange reserves mitigate the country's external vulnerabilities during times of crisis, raising the confidence of economic agents and non-speculative investors. For Cape Verde, external reserves are fundamental to its own survival, particularly for three reasons. First, because it is a price-taking country, that is, it imports almost everything it consumes and invests. Secondly, because it needs to make unavoidable use of external savings to finance its development process. Third, to ensure the fixed parity exchange regime in force in the country. In this context, the maintenance of an adequate level of foreign exchange reserves is relevant in that it allows, among other objectives, to support and credibility monetary and exchange rate policy. Since the global financial crisis of 2008, a context of much greater uncertainty has prevailed, which is expected to remain indefinitely. Since then, the increasingly unfavorable conditions of application of reserves in the financial markets have forced central banks, including the Bank of Cape Verde, to adjust their paradigm of their management. Before the crisis, the paradigm was the profitabilization of external assets, even if it is based on the principle of prudence. In this context of positive interest rates, the Bank of Cape Verde benefited greatly from the income generated, which contributed decisively to the balance of its accounts. With the introduction of negative interest rates, management began to prioritize the maintenance of the value of foreign exchange reserves, which greatly impacted the accounts of the country's Central Bank. Today, with the increase in the increase in the main rates in the Euro area and the reversal of the restrictive U.S. monetary policy, the paradigm is to minimize the losses of foreign exchange reserves. In this context, it is crucial that central banks have greater operational clarity in management objectives. They should analyse the portfolio of their reserves holistically, look at the acquisition of gold and invest in the diversification of the portfolio of reservation. Security should be understood as reduced volatility and not so much as investing in presumed risk-free assets in a permanent trade-off exercise as to the risk-to-return ratio. It seems that the paradigm of minimizing the losses of foreign exchange reserves should prevail over a broader horizon. This paradigm is particularly relevant in developing economies with fixed exchange regimes, such as Cape Verde. It challenges central banks and their external reserve managers to find creative solutions, within the conservative risk profile that characterizes this type of institution. The Bank of Cape Verde has been aware of these changes and has sought to act accordingly. In a very complex management context, it is extending its euro and dollar investment portfolios, with much longer maturities, in order to mitigate the effects of this uncertainty on international markets. Moreover, it has already begun to study alternatives to diversify its portfolio of reserve currencies, as well as the acquisition of gold, this as a refuge asset. Ladies and gentlemen, It is true that the hegemony of the US dollar remains to this day, but the global economic and financial context is changing. The demand for a currency as a reserve asset mainly reflects the economic position of the area where it is issued. Particularly for this reason, the Chinese currency, the renminbi began to conquer its space between the reserve currencies. In 2016, this currency was used as an international reserve currency, representing 1.1% of the total. In 2018, its weight 1.9%, making it the fifth international reserve currency. By 2030 it is expected to amount to 10-20% of global reserves. So what does the future have for us? In a multi-polarised global economic context, it is the opinion of many experts that using a national currency as an alternative to the US dollar, such as the euro or the renminbi, would not solve the current problems of the international monetary and financial system. The idea of a supranational reserve currency has been fuelled by many, inspired by Keynes' proposal, as part of the creation of the Bretton Woods System in 1944. The United Nations, for its part, has advocated a new global monetary order based on a supranational reserve currency. In 2016, the International Monetary Fund recognized the negligible role that the current framework of its special drawing rights has played in the international monetary system. As a result, it was proposed to re-analyze the said framework and to identify the reforms necessary for the extension of its role. The table described above challenges us, as central banks and external reserve managers, to continue the weighting exercise, adopting an increasingly critical and cautious stance in exploring new investment alternatives. Likewise we must be even more aware of the basic functions that foreign exchange reserves perform. I did not want to end without mentioning that in 2018 Cape Verde adopted the full liberalisation of capital movements, which represents a significant structural change in the country's economic and financial relations with abroad. To date, that measure has had no negative impact on the stock of external reserves. These have increased to a historically high level, reinforcing the credibility of the existing exchange rate regime in the country of fixed peg of the national currency against the euro. To finish, I recall the deepest thanks for the opportunity that the Bank of Cape Verde had to host the 1st Meeting of External Reserve Management of the Central Banks of portuguese-speaking countries. Many thanks to all, for the active participation and good wishes to return home for those who came to visit us. Beach, 01 October 2019 John Serra /Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde/
text_original: Interveno do Governador, Doutor Joo Serra, no I Encontro de Gesto de Reservas Externas dos Bancos Centrais dos Pases de Lngua Senhor Vice-Primeiro Ministro e Ministro das Finanas, Excelncia Senhor Administrador do Banco de Portugal, Senhores Administradores do Banco de Cabo Verde, Senhores Representantes dos Bancos Centrais dos Pases de Lngua Portuguesa, Senhores Representantes das Instituies Financeiras, Caros Colaboradores do BCV, Senhores Convidados, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Apraz-me, em particular, que o I Encontro de Gesto de Reservas Externas dos Bancos Centrais dos Pases de Lngua Portuguesa se tenha realizado em Cabo Verde. Pois, trata-se de um evento de suma importncia e actualidade para um pas que tem um regime cambial de paridade fixa, para alm de ser uma pequena economia aberta e muito dependente das importaes e da poupana externa. Os nossos sinceros agradecimentos a todos os representantes dos Bancos Centrais aqui presentes, pela excelente partilha de conhecimento e experincias em matria de gesto das reservas externas. As nossas felicitaes aos ilustres conferencistas e palestrantes pelas brilhantes e proveitosas comunicaes feitas. De igual modo, felicitamos a organizao do evento, o Departamento de Mercados e Gesto de Reservas do Banco de Cabo Verde e o respetivo Administrador, pela qualidade imprimida na sua realizao. O BCV tomar em devida conta os subsdios sados do Encontro. Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, As moedas, enquanto ativos de reserva, existem h milhares de anos, desde o tempo do Dracma grego no sculo V antes de Cristo. O dinheiro  insubstituvel devido  sua estabilidade inerente e  sua importncia global como meio de troca. Hoje, numa economia global cada vez mais integrada e interconectada, praticamente nenhum pas consegue sobreviver sem reservas cambiais. Conforme ficou bem patente neste evento, as reservas externas oficiais tm servido, para alm das funes mais bsicas, para mostrar ao mundo a estabilidade da economia de um pas para fazer face ao seu passivo externo. Por outro lado, constituem-se como um factor de atraco de novos investimentos por parte de investidores internacionais. Ademais, as reservas cambiais mitigam as vulnerabilidades externas do pas durante tempos de crise, elevando a confiana dos agentes econmicos e de investidores no especulativos. Para Cabo Verde, as reservas externas so fundamentais para a sua prpria sobrevivncia, particularmente por trs motivos. Primeiro, por ser um pas tomador de preos, ou seja, que importa quase tudo o que consome e investe. Segundo, porque necessita de recorrer, de forma incontornvel,  poupana externa para financiar o seu processo de desenvolvimento. Terceiro, para garantir o regime cambial de paridade fixa vigente no pas. Neste contexto, a manuteno dum nvel adequado de reservas cambiais  relevante, na medida em que permite, entre outros objectivos, suportar e credibilizar a poltica monetria e cambial. Desde a crise financeira global de 2008, prevalece um contexto de muito maior incerteza, que dever permanecer por tempo indeterminado. Desde ento, as condies cada vez mais desfavorveis de aplicao das reservas, nos mercados financeiros, tm obrigado os bancos centrais, entre os quais o Banco de Cabo Verde, a ajustar o seu paradigma de gesto das mesmas. Antes da crise, o paradigma era a rentabilizao dos activos externos, ainda que assente no princpio da prudncia. Naquele contexto de taxas de juro positivas, o Banco de Cabo Verde beneficiava grandemente com os rendimentos gerados, o que contribua de forma determinante para o equilbrio das suas contas. Com a introduo de taxas de juro negativas, a gesto passou a priorizar a manuteno do valor das reservas cambiais, o que impactou muito negativamente nas contas do Banco Central do pas. Hoje, com o maior agravamento das taxas diretoras na rea do Euro e a reverso da poltica monetria restritiva norte-americana, o paradigma  de minimizao das perdas das reservas cambiais. Neste quadro,  crucial que os bancos centrais tenham maior clareza operacional nos objetivos de gesto. Devem analisar o portflio das suas reservas de forma holstica, perspetivar a aquisio do ouro e apostar na diversificao da carteira de moedas de reserva. A segurana deve ser entendida como volatilidade reduzida e no tanto como investimento em presumveis ativos risk-free, num exerccio permanente de trade-off quanto  relao risco/retorno. Ao que tudo indica, o paradigma da minimizao das perdas das reservas cambiais dever prevalecer num horizonte alargado. Este paradigma  particularmente relevante nas economias em desenvolvimento com regimes de cmbios fixos, como  o caso de Cabo Verde. Desafia os bancos centrais e os respetivos gestores de reservas externas a encontrar solues criativas, dentro do perfil de risco conservador que carateriza este tipo de instituio. O Banco de Cabo Verde tem estado atento a estas mudanas e tem procurado agir em conformidade. Num contexto muito complexo de gesto, est a estender as suas carteiras de investimentos em euro e dlar, com maturidades muito mais longas, de forma a conseguir mitigar os efeitos dessa incerteza nos mercados internacionais. Outrossim, j comeou a estudar alternativas de diversificao da sua carteira de moedas de reserva, bem como a aquisio do ouro, este enquanto activo de refgio. Minhas senhoras e meus senhores,  facto que a hegemonia do dlar norte-americano mantm-se at hoje, mas o contexto econmico e financeiro mundial est a mudar. A demanda por uma moeda como ativo de reserva reflete principalmente a posio econmica da rea onde ela  emitida. Particularmente por esta razo, a moeda chinesa, o renminbi comeou a conquistar o seu espao entre as moedas de reserva. Em 2016, esta moeda passou a ser utilizada como moeda de reserva internacional, representando 1,1% do total. Em 2018, o seu peso ascendeu a 1,9%, tornando-se a quinta moeda de reserva internacional. Prev-se que at 2030 o seu peso ascenda a 10-20% das reservas globais. Ento, o que nos reserva o futuro? Num contexto econmico mundial multipolarizado,  opinio de muitos especialistas que o recurso a uma moeda nacional como alternativa ao dlar norte-americano, como o euro ou o renminbi, no resolveria os atuais problemas do sistema monetrio e financeiro internacional. A ideia de uma moeda de reserva supranacional tem sido alimentada por muitos, inspirada na proposta de Keynes, no mbito da criao do Sistema de Bretton Woods em 1944. As Naes Unidas, por sua vez, tm defendido uma nova ordem monetria global, assente numa moeda de reserva supranacional. Em 2016, o Fundo Monetrio Internacional reconheceu o papel insignificante que o atual framework dos seus direitos de saque especiais tem tido no sistema monetrio internacional. Em decorrncia, props-se a uma reanlise do referido framework e  identificao das reformas necessrias para a extenso do seu papel. O quadro acima descrito desafia-nos, enquanto bancos centrais e gestores de reservas externas, a continuar o exerccio de ponderao, adoptando uma postura cada vez mais crtica e cautelosa na explorao de novas alternativas de investimento. Outrossim, devemos ser ainda mais conscientes das funes bsicas que as reservas cambiais desempenham. No queria terminar sem deixar de referir que em 2018 Cabo Verde adoptou a plena liberalizao dos movimentos de capitais, o que representa uma mudana estrutural significativa nas relaes econmicas e financeira do pas com o exterior. At  presente data, a referida medida no teve qualquer impacto negativo no stock das reservas externas. Estas aumentaram para um nvel historicamente elevado, reforando a credibilidade do regime cambial existente no pas de peg fixo da moeda nacional face a euro. Para terminar, renovo o mais profundo agradecimento pela oportunidade que o Banco de Cabo Verde teve de acolher o I Encontro de Gesto de Reservas Externas dos Bancos Centrais dos Pases de Lngua Portuguesa. Muito obrigado a todos, pela ativa participao e votos de bom regresso  casa para aqueles que nos vieram visitar. Praia, 01 de Outubro de 2019 Joo Serra /Governador do Banco de Cabo Verde/

Title: Speech at the XXIX Lisbon Meeting, at the Governors Roundtable, Lisbon
text: Implications of Technological Innovation in Financial Activity Speech by the Governor, Dr Joao Serra, at the XXIX Lisbon Meeting, at the Governors Roundtable, Lisbon, 11 October 2019 Innovation is a critical and timeless valence for economic growth and development. In a brief and simple way, innovation can be understood as the introduction of new products, services and processes, which add value to the economy. It translates into the introduction of something new whose impact, from a cost/benefit perspective, represents a significant positive change. This is because, together with the advantages of innovation, emerging threats and risks also arise. The theme of this meeting refers, at present, directly to the problem of Fintech, Regtech and Suptech. Fintech or financial technologies refer to new technologies that seek to improve and automate the provision and use of financial services. Initially, the term referred to support technologies, i.e. back-end systems used in the functioning of financial institutions. Later, especially with the launch of smartphones, there was a shift towards a greater focus on the services provided to consumers, thus evolving into a more focused definition. Fintech currently includes different sectors and activities such as retail banking, fundraising, education, financial inclusion, among others. Today, in several countries, digital financial services cover products and services such as payments, transfers, savings, credit, insurance, securities and financial planning. They also include the development and use of crypto-currencies, and their impact is felt mainly in payment systems. Addressing the Fintech problem necessarily implies also addressing the theme of Regtech or regulatory technologies. This is the management of regulatory processes in the financial sector through technology, automation, the processing of large amounts of data and machine learning. It refers to a number of companies specialising in business support, with a view to regulatory compliance, efficiently and less costly, based on technology. After the financial crisis of 2008, with the subsequent strengthening of regulation and the rapid digitisation of the financial sector, the problem of Regtech began to take on a great deal of acuity. Financial services are one of the most regulated sectors in the world. Regulation has become a central concern for national and supranational authorities, with the emergence and expansion of Fintech companies. Just as Fintech supports banks in providing banking services through technology, Regtech helps banks meet regulatory requirements. As for Suptech, i.e. supervisory technologies, they refer to the use of innovative technology by supervisors to support supervision. They help supervisors digitize reporting processes and regulatory processes, which translates into more efficient and proactive monitoring of risk and compliance. Suptech has been increasingly used in risk-based supervision, and applications have focused primarily on data collection and analysis. Fintech is associated, among others, with the following potentialities: i) facilitate access to financial services, mainly in countries with a low rate of financial inclusion; (ii) reduce transaction costs; (iii) impact efficiency and competition; (iv) mitigate the risks and inefficiencies linked to information asymmetry; and (v) improve compliance processes in financial institutions. In view of the benefits, especially for those who do not have access to financial services, several international organisations have recommended that national competent authorities promote financial innovation. As mentioned above, however, it should be aware that the rapid advancement of technology also brings with it threats and risks. In fact, along with new opportunities, new risks arise, namely financial, operational, in addition to cyber-risk and compliance risk. Some Fintech applications bring new threats to the integrity of the financial system. Similarly, certain innovations can be diverted for criminal purposes, such as money laundering and terrorist financing. In view of opportunities, risks and challenges, it is important that the regulator and supervisor have the tools, capacity and resources to respond to new services, new distribution channels, new technologies and new players. Moreover, the new architecture and new business models followed by payment service providers require a multidisciplinary response from central banks and other regulators. They also require new approaches, resources and skills in order to maximise opportunities and minimise risks to society. As we know, Cape Verde is a small island country with a small and open economy. The challenges of financial inclusion are particularly relevant in the country. For Cape Verde, the existence of a modern, resilient and reliable payment system is fundamental to the development of its economy and the financial inclusion of its population. In the context of technological innovation in financial activity, banco de Cabo Verde attaches a high priority to the modernization of payment systems and financial inclusion. In Cape Verde, the banking rate is relatively high, 75.3%, according to the latest data from the 2018 Cape Verdean Payment System Report. Regarding the coverage of the national banking network, the data indicate that 18 of the 22 municipalities in the country are covered by the network of branches/branches, i.e. 81.8% of the national territory. The penetration rate of mobile phones is 74% and the internet 57.2%, according to data from the 2017 National Institute of Statistics. In the field of infrastructure, Cape Verde has therefore met the conditions to leverage financial innovation and inclusion, ensuring access to financial services through a mobile device or other technology. In view of the importance of payment systems and services for the Cape Verdean economy, for the financial inclusion of citizens and for the competitiveness, in particular of businesses, a profound reform of the existing legal framework has been necessary. Thus, in 2018, and at the initiative of the Bank of Cape Verde, the national legal system was endowed with three central legislations, with a view to regulating the three main matters in this regard, i.e. (i) payment systems; (ii) payment services; and (iii) institutions providing payment services and isit electronic money. These three diplomas manifest a transversal principle, which is the essentiality of the Bank of Cape Verde's intervention as a central bank, in the promotion, supervision and general supervision of the system as a whole, but also as an operator and participant of payment systems. The relevance of the Bank of Cape Verde's intervention as a participant in payment systems is determined by concerns about the stability and security of the systems. It aims, in particular, to reduce the risks inherent to them by using the central bank currency as a liquidation asset. Among other things, the new legal framework regulates and facilitates access to the exercise of the activity of providing payment services and issuing electronic money to new entities, regardless of technological characteristics. It gives consumers access to payment services where certain institutions are unable to provide. In other words, it allows non-bank financial institutions to provide financial payment services, thereby promoting the financial inclusion of citizens. As for virtual assets, the Bank of Cape Verde, like many other central banks, issued a statement to point out the risks that those who acquire, hold or trade virtual currencies, or crypto-currencies such as Bitcoin, may incur, considering the growing popularity they have been taking on worldwide. Cape Verde has benefited and will continue to benefit from its demographic profile. By 2050, it will have a relatively young population, with an average age of 28.9 years. The affinity of new generations for technology, combined with a high penetration rate of mobile phone and internet, are factors that enhance and enable the incorporation of digital technologies in the country's economy. Banco Cabo Verde, as a regulator, supervisor and promoter of the development of the financial sector, is aware of the opportunities that technological innovation brings with it, as well as the risks and challenges arising in particular from the emergence of new business models and new players. It thus committed itself to promoting financial innovation, without neglecting, however, its mandate to ensure the stability and integrity of the financial system. Overall, Cape Verde is still in an embryonic phase in terms of Fintech, Regtech and Suptech. Aware of this and in fulfilling its mission in this area, banco de Cabo Verde considers the creation of a multidisciplinary working group. It should study the issues related to financial technology, new business models and the implications they may bring to the Cape Verdean financial system, proposing the measures taken as relevant. In essence, the working group should identify the following: 1. Strategies to promote the development of innovative financial technologies that promote greater efficiency, reduced cost of operations and financial inclusion; 2. any initiatives relating to Fintech and Regtech on the market in order to characterise the market; 3. The innovation-facilitating initiatives recommended by benchmarks that fit the Cape Verdean context; 4. The risks associated with new technologies, new distribution channels and new business models; and 5. Any internal reorganization needs in terms of recruitment, training, Suptech, etc., focused on digital transformation. In summary, I would like to say that it is my strong belief that technological innovation in financial activity will have a positive net impact on the financial system, provided that the risks are adequately mitigated. At The Bank of Cape Verde, this is a consensual perspective and the institution has been working towards a secure, solid, inclusive financial system at the service of people. In this complex area, cooperation is essential, so we express our satisfaction with the approach to the theme at this 29th Lisbon Meeting. Finally, on behalf of the Bank of Cape Verde, thank the Governor of Banco de Portugal for the honorable invitation to participate in this privileged forum for sharing knowledge and experience, in the framework of cooperation between the central banks of the CPLP. Thank you all so much for your attention. Lisbon, 11 October 2019 The Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde, Joao Pinto
text_original: Implicaes da Inovao Tecnolgica na Atividade Financeira Interveno do Governador, Doutor Joo Serra, no XXIX Encontro de Lisboa, na Mesa Redonda de Governadores, Lisboa, 11 de outubro de 2019 A inovao constitui uma valncia crtica e intemporal para o crescimento econmico e o desenvolvimento. De uma forma breve e simples, a inovao pode ser entendida como a introduo de novos produtos, servios e processos, que acrescentam valor  economia. Traduz-se na introduo de algo novo cujo impacto, numa tica de custo/benefcio, representa uma significativa alterao positiva. Isto porque, juntamente com as vantagens decorrentes da inovao, surgem tambm ameaas e riscos emergentes. O tema deste encontro remete, na atualidade, diretamente para a problemtica das Fintech, Regtech e das Suptech. As Fintech ou tecnologias financeiras referem-se s novas tecnologias que procuram melhorar e automatizar a oferta e a utilizao de servios financeiros. Inicialmente o termo referia-se s tecnologias de suporte, isto , aos sistemas back-end utilizados no funcionamento das instituies financeiras. Posteriormente, sobretudo com o lanamento dos smartphones, houve uma mudana, no sentido de um maior enfoque nos servios prestados aos consumidores, evoluindo assim para uma definio mais centrada nestes. As Fintech atualmente incluem diferentes setores e atividades, como a banca de retalho, a captao de fundos, a educao, a incluso financeira, entre outros. Hoje, em vrios pases, os servios financeiros digitais cobrem produtos e servios como pagamentos, transferncias, poupana, crdito, seguros, valores mobilirios e planeamento financeiro. Compreendem tambm o desenvolvimento e a utilizao de cripto-moedas, sendo que o seu impacto se faz sentir sobretudo nos sistemas de pagamento. Abordar a problemtica das Fintech implica necessariamente abordar tambm o tema das Regtech ou tecnologias regulatrias. Trata-se da gesto dos processos regulatrios no setor financeiro atravs da tecnologia, da automatizao, do tratamento de grandes quantidades de dados e da aprendizagem de mquina. Refere-se a um conjunto de empresas especializadas no apoio aos negcios, com vista  conformidade da regulao, de forma eficiente e menos onerosa, com base na tecnologia. Aps a crise financeira de 2008, com o subsequente reforo da regulao e a rpida digitalizao do setor financeiro, a problemtica das Regtech passou a assumir uma grande acuidade. Com efeito, os servios financeiros constituem um dos setores mais regulados no mundo. Pelo que, a regulao passou a ser uma preocupao central para as autoridades nacionais e supranacionais, com a emergncia e a expanso das companhias Fintech. Assim como as Fintech apoiam os bancos na prestao de servios bancrios atravs da tecnologia, as Regtech ajudam os bancos no cumprimento das exigncias regulatrias. Quanto s Suptech, ou seja, tecnologias de superviso, referem-se  utilizao de tecnologia inovadora pelos supervisores para apoio  superviso. Ajudam as autoridades de superviso a digitalizar processos de reporte e processos regulatrios, o que se traduz numa monitorizao mais eficiente e proativa dos riscos e da conformidade. As Suptech vm sendo utilizadas de forma crescente ao nvel da superviso baseada no risco e os aplicativos tm-se concentrado sobretudo na recolha e na anlise de dados. s Fintech so associadas, entre outras, as seguintes potencialidades: i) facilitam o acesso aos servios financeiros, mormente nos pases com baixa taxa de incluso financeira; ii) reduzem os custos de transao; iii) impactam na eficincia e na concorrncia; iv) mitigam os riscos e as ineficincias ligadas  assimetria de informao; e v) melhoram os processos de conformidade nas instituies financeiras. Face aos benefcios, sobretudo para os que no tm acesso aos servios financeiros, vrias organizaes internacionais tm recomendado que as autoridades competentes nacionais promovam a inovao financeira. Conforme referido anteriormente, deve-se, no entanto, estar ciente que o avano rpido da tecnologia traz consigo tambm ameaas e riscos. Na verdade, junto com as novas oportunidades, surgem novos riscos, nomeadamente financeiro, operacional, para alm do cyber-risk e do risco de compliance. Algumas aplicaes de Fintech trazem novas ameaas  integridade do sistema financeiro. De igual modo, determinadas inovaes podem ser desviadas para fins criminais, como a lavagem de capitais e o financiamento do terrorismo. Face s oportunidades, aos riscos e aos desafios,  importante que o regulador e o supervisor tenham as ferramentas, a capacidade e os recursos para responder aos novos servios, aos novos canais de distribuio, s novas tecnologias e aos novos players. Outrossim, a nova arquitetura e os novos modelos de negcios seguidos pelos prestadores de servios de pagamento obrigam a uma resposta multidisciplinar dos Bancos Centrais e outros reguladores. Exigem, tambm, novas abordagens, recursos e competncias, de forma a maximizar as oportunidades e a minimizar os riscos para a sociedade. Como se sabe, Cabo Verde  um pequeno pas insular com uma economia de reduzida dimenso e aberta. Os desafios da incluso financeira assumem particular relevncia no pas. Para Cabo Verde, a existncia de um sistema de pagamentos moderno, resiliente e confivel  fundamental para o desenvolvimento da sua economia e a incluso financeira da sua populao. No mbito da inovao tecnolgica na atividade financeira, o Banco de Cabo Verde atribui uma grande prioridade  modernizao dos sistemas de pagamentos e  incluso financeira. Em Cabo Verde, o ndice de bancarizao  relativamente elevado, 75,3%, de acordo com os ltimos dados do Relatrio do Sistema de Pagamentos cabo-verdiano, de 2018. Relativamente  cobertura da rede bancria nacional, os dados indicam que 18 dos 22 concelhos do pas encontram-se abrangidos pela rede de agncias/balces, ou seja, 81,8% do territrio nacional. A taxa de penetrao dos telemveis  74% e da internet 57,2%, segundo os dados do Instituto Nacional de Estatsticas de 2017. No domnio das infraestruturas Cabo Verde tem, assim, reunidas as condies para alavancar a inovao e a incluso financeiras, garantindo-se o acesso aos servios financeiros atravs de um dispositivo mvel ou outra tecnologia. Face  importncia dos sistemas e servios de pagamento para a economia cabo-verdiana, para a incluso financeira dos cidados e para a competitividade, nomeadamente das empresas, revelou-se necessria uma profunda reforma do quadro jurdico existente. Assim, em 2018 e por iniciativa do Banco de Cabo Verde, o ordenamento jurdico nacional foi dotado de trs diplomas centrais, visando regular as trs principais matrias a este respeito, a saber: i) os sistemas de pagamentos; ii) os servios de pagamento; e iii) as instituies que prestam servios de pagamento e emitem moeda eletrnica. Esses trs diplomas manifestam um princpio transversal, que  o da essencialidade da interveno do Banco de Cabo Verde enquanto banco central, na promoo, superviso e superintendncia geral do sistema no seu todo, mas tambm enquanto operador e participante de sistemas de pagamentos. A relevncia da interveno do Banco de Cabo Verde, enquanto participante de sistemas de pagamentos,  determinada por preocupaes que se prendem com a estabilidade e segurana dos sistemas. Visa, nomeadamente, reduzir os riscos a eles inerentes, atravs da utilizao da moeda do banco central como ativo de liquidao. Entre outros aspetos, o novo quadro legal regula e facilita o acesso ao exerccio da atividade de prestao de servios de pagamento e de emisso de moeda eletrnica a novas entidades, independentemente das caratersticas tecnolgicas. Faz com que o consumidor tenha acesso aos servios de pagamentos l onde determinadas instituies no conseguem prestar. Ou seja, permite a entrada de instituies financeiras no bancrias para prestar servios financeiros de pagamentos, promovendo, assim, a incluso financeira dos cidados. Quanto aos ativos virtuais, o Banco de Cabo Verde,  semelhana de muitos outros bancos centrais, emitiu um comunicado para assinalar os riscos em que pode incorrer quem adquire, detm ou negoceia moedas virtuais, ou cripto-moedas, como o Bitcoin, considerando a popularidade crescente que vm assumindo a nvel mundial. Cabo Verde tem beneficiado e continuar a beneficiar do seu perfil demogrfico. At 2050, contar com uma populao relativamente jovem, com a mdia de idade de 28,9 anos. A afinidade das novas geraes por tecnologia, combinada com uma elevada taxa de penetrao de telemvel e internet, so fatores que potenciam e viabilizam a incorporao das tecnologias digitais na economia do pas. O Banco Cabo Verde, na qualidade de regulador, supervisor e promotor do desenvolvimento do setor financeiro, est ciente das oportunidades que a inovao tecnolgica traz consigo, bem como dos riscos e dos desafios, decorrentes nomeadamente da emergncia de novos modelos de negcio e de novos players. Assim, assumiu o compromisso de promover a inovao financeira, sem descurar, no entanto, do seu mandato de garantir a estabilidade e a integridade do sistema financeiro. De um modo geral, Cabo Verde est ainda numa fase embrionria em termos de Fintech, Regtech e de Suptech. Ciente disso e no cumprimento da sua misso nesta matria, o Banco de Cabo Verde pondera a criao de um grupo de trabalho multidisciplinar. Este dever estudar as questes relacionadas com a tecnologia financeira, os novos modelos de negcio e as implicaes que podero trazer para o sistema financeiro cabo-verdiano, propondo as medidas tidas por pertinentes. No essencial, o grupo de trabalho dever identificar o seguinte: 1. As estratgias para a promoo do desenvolvimento de tecnologias financeiras inovadoras que promovam maior eficincia, reduo de custo de operaes e incluso financeira; 2. As eventuais iniciativas relativas s Fintech e Regtech existentes no mercado, de modo a caracterizar o mercado; 3. As iniciativas facilitadoras da inovao recomendadas pelas benchmark que se adequam ao contexto cabo-verdiano; 4. Os riscos associados s novas tecnologias, aos novos canais de distribuio e aos novos modelos de negcio; e 5. As eventuais necessidades de reorganizao interna em termos de recrutamento, capacitao, Suptech, etc., focada na transformao digital. Em sntese, gostaria de dizer que  minha forte convico que a inovao tecnolgica na atividade financeira ter um impacto lquido positivo no sistema financeiro, desde que os riscos sejam adequadamente mitigados. No Banco de Cabo Verde trata-se de uma perspetiva consensual e a instituio tem vindo a trabalhar neste sentido, em prol de um sistema financeiro seguro, slido, inclusivo e ao servio das pessoas. Neste domnio complexo a cooperao  fundamental, pelo que manifestamos a nossa satisfao pela abordagem do tema neste XXIX Encontro de Lisboa. Permitam-me, por fim, em nome do Banco de Cabo de Verde, agradecer o Governador do Banco de Portugal pelo honroso convite para participar neste frum privilegiado de partilha de conhecimento e de experincia, no quadro da cooperao entre os bancos centrais da CPLP. Muito obrigado a todos pela vossa ateno. Lisboa, 11 de outubro de 2019 O Governador do Banco de Cabo Verde, Joo Pinto Serra

Title: Intervention at the inauguration act as Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde
text: Intervention in the inauguration act as Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde, January 8, 2021 Former Prime Minister Dr. Ulisses Correia e Silva Ex.mo Deputy Prime Minister, Dr. Olavo Correia Ex.mo Minister for The State of Parliamentary Affairs, Sport, Family and Social Inclusion Mr. State Secretary of Finance Former Governor of bcv Fellow Administrators Distinguished Guests Ladies and gentlemen First of all, I am very grateful for the confidence that you and the Government have placed in me, in assigning me so high and noble responsibility to hold the position of Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde. Believe me, you will not spare my efforts to carry out the mission entrusted to me. Life has put me several and important challenges and, by the way, I have never found responsibilities, of any nature, always moved from the same spirit, spirit of total delivery and permanent effort, always seeking to improve my ability to fulfill the obligations and requirements in the exercise of any position that has been assigned to me. If any immodesty is allowed to me on this solemn occasion, I will say that, looking in the rearview mirror, I must conclude that I have done everything I have done to the limit of my abilities physical and intellectual to perform with merit the positions that, throughout my life, were conferred on me, without other major concerns. I am not a person to be distracted by faits divers or even with facts and incidents without special relevance in the situation, being focused only on ensuring, with the support of all administrators, managers, technicians and employees, that the Bank of Cape Verde fulfills with high quality its mission, both the main, and secondary, namely to maintain price stability, promote liquidity, solvency and the functioning of a financial system based on market stability, collaborate in the definition of monetary policy and implement it autonomously, manage foreign exchange reserves and ultimately act as the government's financial adviser. In the country's situation, this is the real issue, that of ensuring the continuity of the Mission that had been carried out by my predecessor and the outgoing administrators, seeking to develop the guidelines and practices that maximize the effectiveness of the Intervention of the Central Bank, introducing the innovations that will prove necessary, as a result of the examination that should be done in full serenity. I take this opportunity to wish successes and happiness to Dr. Joao Antonio Pinto Serra, as well as to all the outgoing administrators who accompanied him. The country's financial institutions, public entities, businesses and citizens in general can count on me as Governor. In the same line of reasoning, they can also count on all the administrators and all the employees of the Bank of Cape Verde. Here is the guarantee  of this I am very sure  that we will do everything to help promote the economy and the country, making use of assertive procedures that facilitate business development, suppressing or mitigating situations and circuits causing embarrassment, without rationally understandable reasons. Everyone will still be required to have an attitude focused on the ends, better said, on the objectives, without disregarding procedures imposed by law or by regulations that are necessary to safeguard those purposes. We will be guided by achieving maximum efficiency and effectiveness, without loss of the security necessary to optimize the results of the mission entrusted. The Bank of Cape Verde must always be part of the solution and never be a part of the problem. This is what we can promise the Government, all authorities and society at large: strictly comply with the laws of the Republic, exercise the office with a high sense of public service and provide all necessary collaboration with the utmost smoothness, transparency and loyalty. I am here today, invested in this noble function to serve Cape Verde. Thank you very much. Oscar Santos

Sr. Primeiro Ministro Dr. Ulisses Correia e Silva Ex.mo Vice-Primeiro Ministro, Dr. Olavo Correia Ex.mo Sr. Ministro do Estado dos Assuntos Parlamentares, Desporto, Famlia e Incluso Social Sr. Secretrio de Estado das Finanas Ex. Aproveito esta oportunidade para desejar sucessos e felicidades ao Dr. Joo Antnio Pinto Serra, bem como a todos os administradores cessantes que o acompanharam. As instituies financeiras do pas, as entidades pblicas, as empresas e os cidados, em geral, podem contar comigo, enquanto Governador. Na mesma linha de raciocnio, podem, tambm, contar com todos os administradores e com todos os funcionrios do Banco de Cabo Verde. Fica aqui a garantia  disso estou muito seguro  de que tudo faremos para ajudar a promover a economia e o pas, fazendo uso de procedimentos assertivos que facilitem o desenvolvimento de negcios, suprimindo ou mitigando situaes e circuitos causadores de constrangimentos, sem motivos racionalmente compreensveis. A todos ainda ser exigida uma atitude focada nos fins, melhor dizendo, nos objetivos, sem desconsiderar procedimentos impostos por lei ou por regulamentos que so necessrios  salvaguarda daqueles fins. Pautar-nos-emos por atingir o mximo de eficincia e de eficcia, sem perda da segurana necessria para se otimizar os resultados da misso confiada. O Banco de Cabo Verde deve fazer parte sempre da soluo e nunca constituir-se numa parte do problema.  o que podemos prometer ao Governo, a todas as autoridades e  sociedade em geral: cumprir com rigor as leis da Repblica, exercer o cargo com elevado sentido de servio pblico e prestar toda a colaborao necessria com a maior lisura, transparncia e lealdade. Estou aqui, hoje, investido nesta nobre funo para servir Cabo Verde. Muito obrigado. scar Santos

Title: Speech by the Governor, Dr. scar Santos, at the conference "Fair and safe digital financial services", BCV 15 March 2022
text: Welcome message from the Governor, Dr. oscar Santos, at the conference "Fair and Secure Digital Financial Services", BCV, 15 March 2022 2 Very good morning! Deputy Prime Minister, Dear Speakers, Directors, Managers and Employees of Banco de Cabo Verde, Dear Guests, Dear Guests, On behalf of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Cape Verde, I would like to thank all those present who accepted our invitation for an analysis and reflection on the possibilities and challenges associated with financial services such a current and pertinent topic. The world economy, a reflection of recent events, is facing yet another situation of extension of the crisis. Still under the effects of the global health crisis, the escalation tensions and the outbreak of the Ukraine-Russia armed conflict have contributed to a acceleration of the increase in global inflation and a downward revision in international economic outlook. It is worth remembering that the external environment of the national economy had been evolving favorably in the fourth quarter of 2021, with the economies of the major partners to continue their recovery path, despite the persistent supply-side bottlenecks and rising inflation. Domestically, the available indicators point to a continued recovery of economic activity in the fourth quarter of 2021, although more modest compared to the third quarter of the same year. The pandemic context clearly represents an unprecedented opportunity to transform the state of digital finance in Cape Verde, giving a new impulse and power to unbanked citizens. However, the rapid advancement of technology applied to digital financial services brings with more responsibilities and new risks, as well as aggravating traditional risks that can lead to unfair outcomes for consumers and leave behind those that they are more vulnerable in a society where there is less and less movement of Cashless Society. Aware of the responsibility of the Bank of Cape Verde in this area, the purpose of the meeting today is to find synergies between the BCV and other partners to, in together, continue to outline paths that can contribute to the improvement of the inclusion and financial literacy of Cape Verdeans, in the digital context, as Technological innovations applied to the financial sector are a benefit because, "Consumers, by definition, are all of us". Title: Speech by the Governor, Dr. scar Santos, at the swearing-in of the Auditor General of AGMVM, BCV, March 8, 2022
text: Speech by the Governor, Dr. oscar Santos, at the inauguration of the Auditor General Securities Market General, BCV, March 18, 2022 2 Very good morning! Minister of Finance, Your Excellency, Members of the Board of Directors of Banco de Cabo Verde, Madam Auditor General of the Securities Market, Outgoing Auditor General of AGMVM and members of the AGMVM team, Directors, Advisors and Coordinators of the Bank of Cape Verde, Representatives of Financial Institutions, On behalf of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Cape Verde, I would like to congratulate the Auditor General of the Securities Market (AGMVM) for the new function. Dr. Ana Semedo, economist, senior staff of the BCV, will be the second woman to be at the forefront of the challenges of the AGMVM. As you know, the Auditor General of the Securities Market, despite the fact that operate under the Governor of the Bank of Cape Verde, enjoys autonomy functional and administrative and is, according to the law, the authority responsible for supervision and regulation of securities markets. It also has the following attributions: to promote the development of the securities market, instruments financial intermediation activities and other functions that are related to it assigned by law. The capital market plays a relevant role in the effective financing of the economic activity in general, providing investors with an effective alternative to diversify the use of their savings and encourage the retention of their in the national economy. The AGMVM has been actively contributing to these objectives, namely, promoting the modernization of the regulatory framework, which should continue to deserve all the attention of the new Auditor and her team, especially in an environment of increasing digitalisation of markets, taking into account financial innovation. Avenida OUA, n 02 Cod. P. n 7954 - 094 Cx. P. n 101 Praia - Cabo Verde Tel.: 238 2607000 / Fax: 238 2607197 3 The supervision and regulation exercised by the AGMVM consist, above all, of the permanent monitoring of the performance of the people or entities involved in the capital market, with the aim of detecting unlawful acts, namely in the trading on the stock exchange; the monitoring of compliance with the law and regulations; or control of the activity of the Stock Exchange and of all participants in the stock market securities, as well as the verification of compliance with the obligations of Information to the public on securities issuers admitted to trading on the Stock Exchange. In 2021, the AGMVM began work on the revision of the Consumer Market Code Securities. In the context of cooperation and promotion of the capital market had the support of the technical assistance of the Portuguese counterpart (Commission of the Securities Market, CMVM), with regard to the sharing of experiences, related to the procedures for action within the scope of inspection/inspection face-to-face with supervised entities and investigation of crimes against the market. In the Regulatory Plan, Regulations for the Issuance of Securities were published Greens and Social Bonds and in the Supervision Plan, there was a Circulars on the Duty of Categorization of Investors and Verification of Adequacy of the Products to the Client's Profile with Financial Intermediaries, This is in compliance with the principle of investor protection, as well as the realization of the a self-assessment questionnaire submitted to the entities subject to its supervision, in the field of preventing and combating Money Laundering, Terrorism and its Financing (LC/CFT) in the securities market. Currently, the AGMVM faces some challenges, namely, the establishment of a Master Plan with guidelines and policy measures for the capital market in Cape Verde and the establishment of a Strategic Plan for the horizon (2022 - 2025) aligned with the Master Plan. The Mater Plan 2022 -2025 and other actions to be defined will certainly contribute to a further consolidation of the AGMVM and the securities market in Cape Verde. Avenida OUA, n 02 Cod. P. n 7954 - 094 Cx. P. n 101 Praia - Cabo Verde Tel.: 238 2607000 / Fax: 238 2607197 4 I am sure that the two institutions, AGMVM and BCV, will continue to cooperate in the in order to promote the development of the national financial system. In conclusion, I would like to say, on behalf of the Administrative Board of the Banco de Cabo Verde our recognition to the outgoing Auditor General, Dr. Pedro Lima Rocha, for his contribution to AGMVM. The Auditor General of the Securities Market, Dr. Ana Cristina Semedo, Our sincere wishes for many successes and achievements in the new role. Thank you very much! Avenida OUA, n 02 Cod. P. n 7954 - 094 Cx. P. n 101 Praia - Cabo Verde Tel.: 238 2607000 / Fax: 238 2607197
text_original: Interveno do Governador, Dr. scar Santos, na tomada de posse da Auditora Geral do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios, BCV, 18 de maro de 2022 2 Muito bom dia! Title: Speech by the Governor, Dr. scar Santos, "From the Alternative Scenarios of the World Economy to the Future of Cabo Verde in the International Context", June 10, 2022
text: Welcome from the Governor, Dr. oscar Santos, at the international conference "On Alternative Economic Scenarios to the Future of Cape Verde in the International Context", June 10, 2022 Bank of Cape Verde Governor oscar Santos - From Alternative Scenarios of the World Economy to the Future of Cape Verde in the International Context 2 Your Excellency, Deputy Prime Minister, Professor Doutor Antonio Rebelo de Sousa, Mr. Chairman of the Board of Directors of Pro Empresa, Members of the Board of Directors, Dear Guests, Very good afternoon! Welcome to the international conference "On Alternative Scenarios of the World Economy to the Future of Cape Verde in the International Context" organized by the Office of the Vice-Prime Minister in partnership with Pro-Empresa and the Bank of Cape Verde. A special greeting to the economist and Professor Antonio Rebelo de r Sousa for having accepted the invitation. It is an honor and a pleasure to be able to welcome you to the Bank Central. The current environment is characterized by high levels of uncertainty arising from the military conflict in Ukraine and the effects of the Covid-19 pandemic. We live in a Scenario of disruptions in international supply chains, shortages of cereals and fertilizers, rising raw material prices, inflation, and reduction purchasing power. In short, the risks have amplified and tend sideways negative. Avenida OU A, n 02 Cod. P. n 7954 - 094 Cx. P. n 101 Praia - Cabo Verde Tel.: 238 2607000 / Fax: 238 2607197 Governor oscar Santos - From Alternative Scenarios of the World Economy to the Future of Cape Verde in the International Context 3 The performance of the national economy in the last two years reflected the conjuncture international. In 2020, there was the largest drop in GDP in the history of the national economy, in 14.8 percent. Gross tourism revenues fell from 24.4 percent to 8.9 percent of the GDP, tax revenues decreased by about 23 percent, and consequently there was an increase in the overall public deficit from 1.8 to 9.1 per cent of GDP, a worsening of the external deficit to 16.5 percent of GDP and an increase in the unemployment from 11.3 to 14.5 percent. In 2021, with the advance of the vaccination rate in the country, the consequent relief of the restrictions and containment measures related to Covid-19, with the exceptional monetary and fiscal policy policies to mitigate the effects of the crisis on income, with the tourist recovery that took place in the country, especially in the last quarter of the year, it was possible to reverse this macroeconomic picture, with the national economy grew by 7 percent. However, tourism revenues and national gross domestic product continued still far below pre-pandemic levels. In the first three months of 2022, information indicates that, in terms of Exports of goods (including re-exports) grew by 103.3 564 percent gross tourism revenues, remittances from emigrants 29.8 percent, foreign direct investment, 16.2 percent and stock reserves Net international sales increased by around 85 million euros, guaranteeing 7.1 months of imports of goods and services. Avenida OU A, n 02 Cod. P. n 7954 - 094 Cx. P. n 101 Praia - Cabo Verde Tel.: 238 2607000 / Fax: 238 2607197 Governor oscar Santos - From Alternative Scenarios of the World Economy to the Future of Cape Verde in the International Context 4 However, as a consequence of the loss of purchasing power induced by the escalation inflation and the downward revision of the growth of the economies of the main economic partners of the country, the Bank of Cape Verde foresees for this year a moderation of economic growth in the range [3.5 - 4.5] percent. Notwithstanding the overall trend towards normalisation of monetary policy, with a view to to encourage bank financing on less restrictive terms, the Bank Central maintained its markedly accommodative policy, which were also complemented by others of a prudential nature. We are, however, aware of the need for continuous monitoring of developments of economic activity and beyond. The levels of uncertainty overshadow the process of economic recovery, aggravated by the conflict in Ukraine therefore, We will continue to strengthen the mechanisms for monitoring and mitigating the its effects on the economy, necessary conditions for economic growth sustained country. To conclude, we would like to emphasize that the topic could not be more timely and to count on the contribution of Professor Antonio Rebelo de Sousa to sharing experiences, leaves us convinced that we will have an excellent conference and that we will all leave here richer. We urge everyone to actively participate in the conference. We emphasize that the international economic conjuncture poses important challenges to Cape Verde, as a small island country with an economy dependent on the outside. We are facing a paradigm shift regarding the way we perceive the process of globalization. What alternatives and how can Cape Verde take advantage of and transform constraints into opportunities through possible partnerships innovative, as the conference announcement rightly states. I will end with a question: What conditions are we creating and what future are we to build for the new generations, because each generation has the responsibility to let better conditions for future generations, and therefore the Professor, who also was behind the scenes of the Foreign Exchange Cooperation Agreement, came to help us with your experience.
